author: minsky-ai[bot]
body:
## Summary

Implements mt#4795: each option in the cockpit's "Filter by project" switcher now carries a muted one-line triage summary ("N need you · M working" / "clear"), so "which project needs me" is answerable at the point of choosing, without a dedicated landing page (per the /product-thinking derivation this task descends from). The "All projects" option shows the cross-project aggregate.

## Motivation & Context

From the mt#4757 audit + the 2026-08-30 /product-thinking pass: a project-aware landing page was explicitly rejected (entity-CRUD spine — a destination you must visit to learn whether anything needs you). The value instead routes into the affordance that already owns choosing a project: the switcher itself.

## Design/Approach

- **No new server endpoint.** A new hook, `useProjectTriageSummaries` (`src/cockpit/web/hooks/useProjectTriageSummaries.ts`), composes the SAME scoped widget endpoints already powering the shell's ask-pending pulse (`GET /api/widget/attention/data`, `totalPending`) and the home fleet strip (`GET /api/widget/agents/data`, counting `liveness === "healthy"`).
- **Per-project scoping vs. the aggregate.** Each project fetches with an explicit `?project=<slug>` (always wins over the shell's current selection, per `api-client.ts`'s `apiFetch` default-append). The "All projects" row fetches with `{ global: true }` so it reads the true cross-project total regardless of whichever project happens to be currently selected in the shell.
- **Fetch only while open.** Queries are gated on the switcher's `open` state (`onOpenChange`), so the per-project fan-out costs nothing while the dropdown is closed — and (per reviewer round 1) further gated on the same "2+ projects known" condition the component's own early return checks, so a selector about to render `null` never constructs live queries at all.
- **Honest degradation (SC2).** A failed fetch for a scope (attention OR agents) renders `{ status: "degraded" }` → "status unavailable" — never silently folded into a fabricated "clear".
- **Closed-state trigger unaffected (SC3).** Radix Select portals the SELECTED item's `ItemText` children verbatim into the trigger when `<SelectValue>` has no explicit children — which would otherwise leak the muted triage line into the closed combobox. `ProjectSelector` now passes explicit `<SelectValue>{currentLabel}</SelectValue>` children to decouple the two.
- **Accessible names unaffected.** Radix wires each option's `aria-labelledby` to its `ItemText` content (name-from-content). The new triage `<span>` is marked `aria-hidden="true"`, so the accname computation excludes it — each option's accessible name stays the plain label, matching pre-existing test assertions (`getByRole("option", { name: "Minsky" })`).

## Key Changes

- `src/cockpit/web/hooks/useProjectTriageSummaries.ts` (new) — per-project (+ aggregate) pending/working fetch pair via `useQueries`, plus `formatTriageLine` (pure, exported for testing) and the `TRIAGE_DEGRADED_LABEL` marker.
- `src/cockpit/web/components/ProjectSelector.tsx` — renders each option's muted triage line via a new `OptionBody` sub-component; overrides `<SelectValue>` with an explicit label to keep the closed trigger unchanged; wires `onOpenChange` to gate the new hook's queries.
- `src/cockpit/web/components/ProjectSelector.test.tsx` — extends the fetch mock to route by URL/`?project=` param (hardened against a `Request`-instance input); adds a two-project fixture covering counts + "clear" + a distinct aggregate, a degraded-fetch fixture (SC2), and an accessible-name-preservation check.
- `docs/cockpit-ui.md` — adds a "The project filter" subsection to §The rail. This control (mt#2418) had no dedicated documentation at all before this PR; this both fixes that pre-existing gap and documents the new triage-line/degraded-state behavior (reviewer round 1 finding).
- `docs/verification/mt-4795/*.png` — the two AT3 live-verification screenshots, committed so the evidence below points at a real artifact rather than only narrating it (reviewer round 1 finding).

## Testing

Execution evidence:

```
bun test --preload ./tests/dom-setup.ts --preload ./tests/setup.ts --timeout=15000 --path-ignore-patterns='services/**' src/cockpit/web/components/ProjectSelector.test.tsx
7 pass, 0 fail, 15 expect() calls
```

AT1 (two-project fixture, counts + aggregate): `"renders per-project counts, a 'clear' project, and a distinct All-projects aggregate"`.
AT2 (fetch-failure fixture, degraded marker): `"a failed per-project fetch renders a degraded marker, never a fabricated 'clear' (SC2)"`.

[negative-control-deferred: n/a] — this PR is purely additive UI (new hook + new render branch); `ProjectSelector.test.tsx`'s pre-existing tests were only extended with a defensive `Request`-instance check in the fetch mock (a test-harness robustness fix, not a behavior fix), so there is no prior "buggy" behavior to revert and observe failing.

### Live verification (AT3, per src/cockpit/CLAUDE.md §Visual verification)

The shared `:9222` dev canary was reachable, but per an in-flight coordinator correction (mt#4798 tracks the underlying guidance fix — a Chrome launched via `session_exec` gets its sensitive-permission prompts attributed to the tray app on macOS) I instead launched a scratch headless Chrome from the harness's own Bash tool (`--remote-debugging-port=9333`, scratch `--user-data-dir`) and drove it with the chrome-devtools MCP tools, against a prod bundle of this branch (`bun run cockpit:build && bun src/cli.ts cockpit start --port=3738`) served from the session workspace, sharing the same Postgres project data as the operator's real two-project daemon (`edobry/minsky`, `edobry/peezombie.me`).

**Open dropdown** — "All projects" shows "43 need you · 4 working", "Minsky" shows "32 need you · 4 working", "Peezombie.me" shows "clear" — three distinct, independently-fetched values, matching the spec's worked example format:

![Open project switcher dropdown showing per-option triage summaries against the real two-project daemon](https://github.com/edobry/minsky/blob/task/mt-4795/docs/verification/mt-4795/switcher-open.png?raw=true)

**Closed-state trigger after selecting Minsky** — confirms SC3 (the trigger shows only "Minsky", no leaked triage text) and that the rest of the shell (Needs-you count, Fleet strip) re-scoped correctly:

![Closed project switcher trigger reading only "Minsky" after selection](https://github.com/edobry/minsky/blob/task/mt-4795/docs/verification/mt-4795/switcher-closed-minsky.png?raw=true)

No console errors during the interaction. Scratch Chrome and scratch daemon were torn down after verification.

## Deploy verification

This PR touches `src/cockpit/web/**` (deploy surface for the cockpit service). Per `src/cockpit/CLAUDE.md`, the operator's cockpit is tray-supervised and auto-rebuilds `dist/` from source on a `src/cockpit/web` change (no manual deploy step) — I will confirm post-merge that `dist/index.html` / `dist/assets/*` restamp shortly after the merge lands (mirroring the mem#1291 pattern), and separately confirm the `Cold-Start Cockpit Web Smoke` CI workflow is green on the merge commit.

## Scope

Per spec: changes are confined to the switcher component, its new hook, and (per reviewer round 1) the doc section documenting it. The rail Attention badge and home Needs-you leak (sibling mt#4794, in-flight in parallel) were not touched. The two deferred scale-up notes (an aggregation endpoint past ~5 projects; a per-project home strip once a 3rd project onboards) are recorded in the spec and were deliberately not built here.

author: tsukasai
body:
## Summary
- Closes #354. `resolve_tar_dash_c` previously only modeled tar's `-C`/`--directory` when it appeared EXACTLY ONCE per invocation (a deliberate scope cut from issue #209): two or more occurrences skipped composition entirely.
- Live-verified (bsdtar 3.5.3) that the issue's own premise was wrong: `tar -cf out.tar -C a sub/f1 -C b f2` against a real `a/b` tree archives from `a/b`, not a fresh `b` under the original cwd — tar's `-C` occurrences compose CUMULATIVELY via real sequential `chdir(2)` calls, exactly like git/make's own repeated `-C`.
- Fix: `resolve_tar_dash_c` now threads the same `CwdContext`/`resolve_cwd_outcome`/`classify_cd_target` cumulative chain `chain_dash_c_targets` (git/make) already uses, but applies each occurrence's own resolved anchor only to the operand range between it and the next occurrence (tar's `-C` stays positional, unlike git/make's single-final-anchor model). An unresolvable occurrence poisons the chain forward from that point only — an earlier, already-resolved range's composition survives.
- Follow-up fixup (this branch, second commit): the pre-existing doubled-`C`-within-one-dashless-cluster guard (issue #356) failed the whole cluster closed rather than compose — now an unjustified asymmetry with the dashed spelling this PR just made cumulative. Folded the same cumulative chain into `tar_dashless_leading_cluster_directory` so `tar cCCf a b ...` composes the same way `tar -C a -C b ...` now does.
- Also rewrote a stale doc block that still described the pre-fix "two or more occurrences returns None" premise, and disclosed a new (non-regressing) under-composition interaction: an unrecognized value-taking flag whose own value happens to look like a `-C` cluster can now truncate an earlier occurrence's operand range, since multiple occurrences are modeled at all now.

**GNU tar note**: cumulative behavior was verified live against bsdtar 3.5.3 only (no `gtar` available on this machine). Untested against GNU tar, but this can't regress: main composed *nothing* for the multi-occurrence case, so every multi-occurrence outcome on this branch is monotonically ≥ main's own detection even in a hypothetical GNU-tar divergence, and single-occurrence behavior is unchanged.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo build`
- [x] `cargo test` (1330 unit tests + all integration suites pass)
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] New/updated tests cover: cumulative dashed composition (absolute override, relative chaining, range boundaries, unresolvable-occurrence non-poisoning of earlier ranges, three-occurrence recovery after a poisoned middle occurrence, poisoned-range non-composition), and the doubled-C dashless cluster case (cumulative compose, unresolvable-middle-C poisoning)

author: rolyntrotter
body:
The skill only ran from a Claude Code plugin install, so the north star — ask in chat, get a puzzle — was out of reach for anyone not working from a checkout. This ships it both ways from one source, at v0.1.0, on the same release flow as [score-proofreading](https://github.com/RolynTrotter/score-proofreading).

## Releases happen on merge

Merging to `main` reads the version the manifests agree on and, if no `v<version>` tag exists yet, runs the checks, builds the archive, tags, and publishes. A merge that leaves the version alone republishes nothing, so ordinary changes are silent and a failed run can just be re-run. **The version bump is the release** — no separate tagging step.

Because a release now rides on a merge, everything a release needs is checked *before* the merge: a `release-ready` CI job fails any pull request that bumps the version without adding that version's `CHANGELOG.md` section, so a missing section is caught on the PR instead of reddening `main` afterwards.

The version lives in `plugin.json` and must agree with `marketplace.json` — those are what a plugin install reads, so they stay the source of truth here rather than `SKILL.md` frontmatter, which a plugin skill has no version field in.

## The archive

`cryptic-setter-<version>.skill` — a zip whose root holds one directory:

```
cryptic-setter/
  SKILL.md          VERSION      LICENSE
  schema/           scripts/     ui/      fixtures/
```

The plugin keeps `SKILL.md` a level deeper under `skills/`, so `tools/build_skill_bundle.py` hoists it. `SKILL.md` now resolves paths against `$ROOT` in a way that means the same directory in either install — `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` in the plugin, the folder holding `SKILL.md` in a `.skill` install — so neither shape needs its own copy of the instructions. Its publish step also covers having no Artifact tool that takes a file: build the standalone page and hand that over instead.

Only `PAYLOAD` ships, so repository furniture cannot leak into a published skill. **Verification runs on the built archive, not the tree it came from**: the packager unpacks the `.skill` and runs the validator, calibration tests and page build from inside it. Verified by dropping `ui/` from the payload list — the build fails on the missing `solver.html` rather than shipping a broken archive. The archive is reproducible (sorted entries, fixed timestamps).

## CI

Matrix across Python 3.10–3.13 — a skill lands in whatever interpreter its host provides — byte-compiling the scripts, then calibration tests, fixture validation, and the build-and-verify. All four interpreters produce a byte-identical archive. No pip step: the no-dependencies house rule means there is nothing to install.

## Also in here

- `CHANGELOG.md`, whose 0.1.0 section becomes the release notes, with the commits since the previous tag appended.
- `RELEASING.md` — what a release is, that merging cuts it, how to verify the asset afterwards.
- `LICENSE` — MIT, which `plugin.json` already declared but no file backed. It ships inside the archive.
- `make bundle` and `make release-check`; README install instructions for both routes; AGENTS.md rules on keeping the two install shapes from drifting.

## Testing

`make release-check` passes on 3.10, 3.12 and 3.13 as well as 3.11, all producing the same SHA-256. The `.skill` was unpacked outside the repo and exercised as an installed skill: fixtures validate, all 11 planted defects caught, standalone page and artifact body both build. Both branches of the `release-ready` gate were run by hand — unchanged version passes, bump to an undocumented version fails with the reason. Both workflow files parse.

## Why 0.1.0

Delivery works end to end; generation is still the model's job with the validator as the backstop, and the full pipeline has not been run start to finish on a complete grid. `CHANGELOG.md` says so under "Not yet".

Merging this publishes v0.1.0, since `main` has no `v0.1.0` tag.

author: lanabretterebner
body:
Fixes the v0.1.9 release failure ([run 33349462885](https://github.com/lanabretterebner/StemLab/actions/runs/33349462885)). All three Windows jobs — cpu, cuda, xpu — failed at **Install dependencies and run the tests**, before any installer build.

## What broke

```
Program 'installer-hook.sh' failed to run: An error occurred trying to start process
'...\installer-hook.sh' ... The specified module could not be found.
```

Entirely my test, not the script. `STEMLAB_SETUP_INSTALLER` is a pre-existing hook the setup script invokes as a program, and the stub I put behind it in [#111](https://github.com/lanabretterebner/StemLab/pull/111) was a bash script. Windows cannot execute one, so the six tests that reach the install step failed while the same file passed on Linux.

The script itself came through fine on Windows: staging, checksum verification and both refusal paths are among the tests that passed there.

## The fix

The stub is native on each platform — a `.cmd` on Windows, a shell script elsewhere.

**Not a `.ps1`**, which would have been the tidier-looking answer: the setup script reads `$LASTEXITCODE` after invoking the hook, and PowerShell sets that for external processes but *not* for scripts it invokes itself, so a `.ps1` stub would report no exit code at all and the script would treat every run as a failure.

## Two more things the same failure exposed

| | |
| --- | --- |
| The subprocess environment was built from scratch | On Windows that hands the child no `SystemRoot`, and how much still works is luck rather than design. It copies `os.environ` and overrides now. |
| The staging directory is now explicit for every run | So the two tests that set it themselves fold into one, and where the default points is pinned by a text assertion in `test_installer_definition.py` — the test it replaces could only assert a return code. |

## Verification

524 passed, 5 skipped; `ruff check src/ tests/` clean. The Linux branch of the stub is exercised here; the Windows branch is three lines of `cmd` and can only be proven by the Windows job.

## What is still unproven

The Windows jobs never reached **Build the portable payload and the installer**, so ISCC has still never compiled the new `StemLab.iss`. That is the next thing that can fail, and this change is what lets it be found out. Re-tag v0.1.9 once this is in.

author: fahad90fa
body:
## What this does

Closes out the production-hardening roadmap (all eleven code items across Tiers 1–3, plus Tier 4 reproducible builds), adds an on-host flood/DoS layer, and cuts the whole thing as a reproducible **0.1.2** package the website actually serves.

The governing rule throughout: **never fake a green.** Where a guarantee needs a kernel this environment doesn't have or a key that must not live in the tree, the code builds the real mechanism and gates the unprovable half behind an env flag or a `--features` opt-in that says so — rather than asserting a property it didn't check.

## Roadmap items (built, wired, tested)

**Tier 1 — correctness**
- **Real-packet enforcement conformance** — emitted nftables is loaded into a throwaway netns and a real loopback packet is fired per probe; the `allow-inspect` bypass is pinned to a packet. CI runs it as root with `UFW_NFT_REQUIRE=1`/`UFW_NETNS_REQUIRE=1` so "didn't run" is a hard failure.
- **Fuzz the hostile-byte surface** — the IPC wire protocol, the policy compiler, and the console HTTP head are driven with random/mutated bytes; any bytes in, a result out, no unwind.
- **Every advertised layer runs** — one test makes each advertised capability produce a concrete effect, so a layer going no-op is a named red.

**Tier 2 — fail-safe & resilience**
- **Explicit fail-safe posture** (`daemon.fail_mode`, default `closed`) with an emergency default-deny nftables barrier that keeps loopback/established/management ports in; every outcome is a fault-injection unit test, and the barrier loads into a live kernel.
- **Boot-time gap closed** — the restore oneshot runs `Before=network-pre.target`, ordering pinned by a test.
- **Privilege reduction** — every systemd unit sandboxed and capability-bounded (WAF exposure 9.x → 1.6), asserted by a test.

**Tier 3 — operational maturity**
- **Tamper-evident, hash-chained audit log** (`ufwd --verify-audit`), verified at startup.
- **Self-monitoring** for the faults that leave the daemon *looking* healthy (stopped worker, failing sink, policy drift), with de-duplication.
- **Ed25519-signed fleet bundles** (`--features tls`, `ring`) replacing the shared-secret HMAC weakness; the shipped `.deb` builds the daemon **with** tls so this is active in the artifact, not dormant.
- **IPv6 enforcement parity** (model parity + kernel loadability; real v6 packet enforcement is environment-gated and says so).

**Tier 4**
- **Reproducible builds** — `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` + path remap; `verify-reproducible.sh` builds twice and asserts identical SHA-256.

## On-host flood / DoS layer (new)

Addresses the honest limitation "it can't absorb a DDoS" by building the part a host firewall genuinely can:

- `daemon/src/edge_hardening.rs` installs a standalone `table inet ufw_edge` at hook priority **-150**, ahead of the policy table, dropping connection-rate/state floods in the kernel conntrack path: `ct state invalid`, a SYN-flood rate cap, a per-source `ct count` cap (v4+v6), and an ICMP/ICMPv6 echo cap. Every rule is drop-what-exceeds; the only `accept` is loopback, so it can never widen what the policy permits. Opt-in via `edge.flood_protection`, installed over `nft -f -`.
- Proven to load into a live kernel (`nft --check`) under `UFW_NFT_REQUIRE=1`; 4 unit tests pin the shape; startup is audited as a config change with a log line stating it mitigates connection-rate floods but a volumetric DDoS still needs upstream scrubbing.
- `docs/design/ddos-posture.md` states all three boundaries plainly: volumetric DDoS is an upstream job (physics, not a missing feature); there *is* a host-side WAF (signature detection on decrypted HTTP) but it's not a full edge WAF and a CDN can't live on the origin; patching and backups are separate controls this complements and never replaces.

## Release 0.1.2

- Workspace bumped to 0.1.2; the packaged `daemon.toml` ships the `[edge]` config (opt-in, default off) with the same honest note.
- Rebuilt the reproducible `.deb` (cli + daemon with `--features tls`) and refreshed the site's served copy under `website/public/downloads`, dropping the old 0.1.1 artifacts; `website/src/lib/content.ts` points at the new file, size, and SHA-256.
- **Verified byte-reproducible:** two independent builds yield the identical `845b1a96…1929b`, matching the served `.deb`, its `.sha256` sidecar, and `content.ts`.

## Verification
- Full workspace: build, clippy (default + `--features tls`), and tests green.
- Kernel conformance (fail-closed barrier + edge flood layer + emitted policy) loads into the live kernel via `nft --check`.
- Website typecheck + build green.

## Honestly still open (not code — time / people / an outside party)
- **Zero sustained runtime hours** on live kernels under real traffic (the dominant gap; a real 6-minute bounded soak ran, but not the 30-day run).
- **No independent audit** (made cheaper/smaller by Tier 1; the reviewer package is ready).
- **Staffed disclosure inbox** (the policy and `security.txt` ship; the staffing is operational).

author: davidschonert
body:
## What this adds

LanguageTool checking in the built-in markdown editor: underlines on flagged text, a correction card on click or hover, and click-to-apply replacements. Two backends, local and cloud, with local as the default so document text stays on the machine unless cloud is explicitly chosen.

## Reviewing this

Three places do something unusual on purpose. Each works around host behaviour, and each looks like a mistake without the reason.

1. **Secrets do not use `ExtensionStorage`** (`src/core/secrets.ts`). Two separate reasons. A contributed Lexical extension receives `ExtensionServices`, which carries no storage, so the runtime cannot read the token when it loads (nimbalyst/nimbalyst#1407). And `ExtensionStorage` scopes secrets as `nimbalyst:<id>:<key>`, and colons are illegal in Windows filenames, so it fails there regardless (nimbalyst/nimbalyst#1408). The IPC call reaches the same encrypted store in the same location.

2. **`contributions.configuration` declares an empty `properties` object** (`manifest.json`). The host renders its own field UI for every declared property, and those inputs are disabled on each save, which drops focus on every keystroke in a text field. Empty leaves this extension's own panel as the only settings UI, and config still persists because it is stored as a plain per-extension key/value bag. The key must still be present: omitting it makes the host reject the entire extension. `scripts/validate.mjs` fails the build on exactly that, because the SDK's own validator does not check contribution shapes.

3. **Repositioning and re-checking are on separate paths** (`src/lexical/CheckerExtension.ts`). Lexical has no decoration API, so underlines are painted into an overlay rather than by mutating the document. Sharing one debounce between repositioning and re-checking left underlines visibly stale for about half a second after each keystroke.

## Verified

38 tests cover the parts that run without the editor, including the property the whole design rests on: a markup item contributes its raw length to the offset space, not the length of its `interpretAs`, so a reported offset indexes the original document. The tree walk runs against a headless Lexical editor, so GitBook `{% ... %}` suppression and inline-code substitution are checked against a real node tree.

Checked against a live LanguageTool 6.6 server during development: `level=picky` adds matches, `disabledRules` and `disabledCategories` each suppress, and the service rejects a username sent without an apiKey. The overlay holds position through typing, scrolling and reflow in the running app.

## Not done

- No personal dictionary. This is the next thing worth doing, since product names are reported as misspellings on real documents.
- No inline suppression comments.
- **No rate limiting.** The service allows 20 requests and 75,000 characters per minute on the free tier, and 80 and 300,000 on premium. Every check sends the whole document, so characters per minute binds before requests per minute: a 20,000 character document allows a check every 16 seconds on free and every 4 seconds on premium. The cloud debounce is currently one hardcoded value, which is both too slow for premium and too fast for free.
- **No handling of the per-request character cap**, which is 20,000 free and 60,000 premium. A document over the cap is rejected outright, so the underlines disappear with only an HTTP error to explain it. Chunking the document by block would fix that, return results for the start of a long document sooner, and allow re-checking only the chunk being edited.
- No coverage of the overlay or the settings panel, which need the Electron host and are verified by running the app.

author: greninjam26
body:
The upload queue was created with a bare file name, which Path.of resolves
against the working directory. Running from Maven that is the project root, so
it worked. An installed application does not choose its working directory:
launched from the Finder or the Start menu it inherits the launcher's, often
the root of the disk.

Verified rather than assumed. With the working directory set to /, as a Finder
launch gives, writing the old path fails:

    /pending-game-results.jsonl: Read-only file system

so every result a player finished while the server was unreachable would have
been lost, silently, on exactly the builds phase 07 produces.

ApplicationDirectory resolves each system's own location:

    macOS     ~/Library/Application Support/Guess Who
    Windows   %APPDATA%\Guess Who, else ~\AppData\Roaming\Guess Who
    otherwise $XDG_DATA_HOME/guess-who, else ~/.local/share/guess-who

Files then land where a user would look for them and where an uninstaller
would think to remove them. If the directory cannot be created the working
directory is used, which is no worse than the current behaviour and will not
stop the game starting.

FilePendingGameResultStore now takes a Path rather than a String. That is the
part that stops this recurring: a bare file name can no longer be handed in and
quietly resolved against wherever the process happened to start.

The platform logic takes the environment as arguments, so all four cases are
tested on any machine without touching the disk or the real environment.

No migration. The only existing queue file holds five test results and is
gitignored, so carrying permanent migration code for it is not worth it.

Nine new tests, 311 in total, all passing.

Establishes the design of record for `lockstep` and the implementation plan for phase 1 (manual switching).

## What's here

- `docs/design/2026-08-30-repo-design.md` — the approved design. What the repo is, what ships, the technical findings that constrain everything downstream, and the decision-log format.

## Findings this design rests on

All verified on macOS 26.6.2 against a Cambridge Audio DacMagic 200M:

- Apple Music reports the true sample rate for **streamed** catalog tracks (`class: URL track`) via the public ScriptingBridge `sample rate` property — no log scraping needed.

- Nothing in macOS 26 auto-corrects the rate: forced to 192 kHz under 44.1 kHz playback, it held for the full 8 seconds.

body:
**Pixee Scan:** [10398972-fef4-4c4b-89b3-306d25b57cd8](https://app.pixee.ai/scans/10398972-fef4-4c4b-89b3-306d25b57cd8?fix-finding-id=AaBVl9TeVskNNOoGf_CR)
Confidence: HIGH Fix confidence is a rating derived from an internal benchmark and includes High, Medium, and Low confidence fixes. It comprises three weighted scores reflecting the safety, effectiveness and cleanliness of Pixee's code changes within a fix. [View Details in Pixee.](https://app.pixee.ai/scans/10398972-fef4-4c4b-89b3-306d25b57cd8?fix-finding-id=AaBVl9TeVskNNOoGf_CR)
--- ## Remediation This change fixes finding AaBVl9TeVskNNOoGf_CR. ## Details Prevent Command Injection in introduction/other_views.py ## Summary Prevent Command Injection in `introduction/other_views.py`. ## Vulnerability Description Command Injection occurs when an application builds an operating system command from untrusted input and passes it to a shell or command interpreter. An attacker can abuse this pattern to run arbitrary commands with the privileges of the application, which can lead to data theft, system compromise, or lateral movement. This class of issue is especially dangerous when input is only lightly transformed or filtered before execution. ## Changes Made The `introduction/other_views.py` view previously interpolated `request.POST.get('domain')` directly into an `nslookup` or `dig` command string and executed it with `subprocess.Popen(..., shell=True)`, which allowed user-controlled data to influence the shell command. The fix added a domain validation check using a hostname-matching regular expression and returns `Invalid domain` when the input is missing or malformed. It also changed the command construction from a single formatted string to a fixed argument list, and removed `shell=True` so the DNS utility receives the domain as a normal argument instead of shell-parsed text. The change preserves the existing OS-specific command choice while preventing the submitted domain from being interpreted as part of an OS command. ## Guidance Adherence **Source**: Pixee Knowledge Base Applied the following guidance from the remediation instructions: - **Prevent command injection vulnerabilities by sanitizing inputs and/or validating user input**: The patch adds a strict domain validation check with `re.fullmatch(...)` and rejects empty/invalid domains with `"Invalid domain"`, which directly follows the guidance to validate user-controlled data before using it in a command. - **Change this code to not construct the OS command from user-controlled data**: The patch stops building a shell command string via `"nslookup {}".format(domain)` / `"dig {}".format(domain)` and instead passes `subprocess.Popen` an argument list like `['nslookup', domain]` or `['dig', domain]`, while also removing `shell=True`. This matches the secure approach of avoiding shell command construction from tainted input. - **Use sanitization/validation to ensure input does not contain malicious commands**: The updated code normalizes the domain (`replace("https://www.", '') if domain else ''`) and validates it against a domain-name regex before execution, reducing the risk of command injection from malicious payloads. No new libraries were introduced, so no dependency manifest update was required.

**One number differed.** Queue 1 said **194** gate self-tests; I count **197, 1 skipped**. Not a contradiction — Queue 1 counted before three parser tests were added in that same PR. Populations: Queue 1 counted the eight CI modules at that commit; I counted the same eight plus `test_check_control_invocation` at its final commit. The skip is now named rather than left as a number: `test_roadmap_split`, *"5512d82 is no longer reachable; the fixture is the record"* — pre-existing.

## 22 checks PROVEN by my own mutations

Different edits from the ones the report describes; each grep-confirmed on disk and confirmed to compile or parse **before** any test ran. **One mutation did not compile and is reported as proving nothing.**

#207: 5 · #208: 10 · #209: 1 · #210: 6. Full list in the report.

## 4 checks defended by nothing — this is the finding

1. **`credentials::is_bound` does not require the SLOT to match.** Removing the `slot_id` predicate leaves the suite green. Queue 1's sweep varied the **digest** and was caught by `a_binding_does_not_reach_a_different_build`; **no test varies the slot.** If it regressed, a value bound to slot `a` would satisfy a step requiring slot `b` on the same bundle.
2. **`Grant::for_egress`'s credential-slot refusal was never swept at all.** Deleting it leaves the suite green.
3. **`security::map_event` can drop the `source` mark entirely.** Proven by mutating the second of two identical mapper bodies to `source: None` — compiles, every test green.
4. **`Home.tsx` can stop counting seeded rows.** Replacing the filter with `0` type-checks and the frontend suite stays green. `activitySummary` is tested; the wiring that feeds it is not.

## And a check that cannot fail — in my own PR #210

`both_read_surfaces_carry_the_mark` is named for two surfaces and asserts one:

```rust
let summary = security::summary(&conn).unwrap();
let _ = &summary;                                   // computed, then discarded
let marked_anywhere = rows.iter().any(|e| e.source.is_some());
assert!(marked_anywhere);                           // re-checks line 1208
```

**No state of the world makes that last assertion red if the earlier one passed.** Finding 3 is the proof.

So **PR #210's headline — "the mark reaches the reader" — is half proven.** It reaches `activity::list`. Whether it reaches `security::summary` or the Home sparkline is asserted by nothing.

## The produced artifact, end to end

Verified on **both** #207 and #210: `git ls-files` shows **no store** (the one match is `config/produced-artifact-contract.json`, the contract); RED before producing — *"the store is declared and nothing has produced it"*; the binary goes `register` (disarmed) → `approve_confirmed` → `set_active` → `run_due` with **no `claim_and_run` call**; GREEN on all five after, `invoked_by` = `run_due`.

**One stale-artefact trap caught in passing:** the store survives a `git checkout` because it lives under `target/`, so the gate read GREEN on the #210 checkout before that code had produced anything. Deleted, re-produced, re-verified. A reader repeating this must delete the store first.

## Method caveats, stated

`CARGO_TARGET_DIR` was shared across the four checkouts because `/tmp` here is a **7.8 GB tmpfs that filled** — one cargo target alone was 6.7 GB. Cargo fingerprints by content, so this is not the hazard a shared *git object store* is; the one place a stale artefact did appear is called out above.

Not done: the Windows-only jobs (no runner here); a new measurement of #207's flagged conflict with migration 0022 (it stands on reading the same two files, and is the Owner's decision either way); any re-measurement of the frontend intermittent — it did not occur in this pass, which is one more absence, not evidence.

◑ This pass is also mine. It is a second measurement, not a second party. **Not merged.**

author: xiaoba-dev
body:
## What

The playground repo found and fixed a real bug (playground#302, #304): a fire-and-forget heartbeat request that a short-lived CLI process could outrun before the request finished. This server's own equivalent call (server.ts:717, recordHeartbeat) was analyzed as architecturally safe from that same bug, because this process is long-lived (StdioServerTransport keeps it running until the host closes the connection) rather than "runs one command and exits" the way a CLI invocation does.

That analysis had never been exercised end to end. This PR is that exercise — no production code changed, this is test-only.

## How

Spawns the real built server (dist/index.js) as its own OS process and talks to it over a real StdioClientTransport, not InMemoryTransport (which shares the test process and therefore can't say anything about process lifetime — the existing protocol/integration suites use InMemoryTransport correctly for protocol-shape assertions, but it's the wrong tool for this question). Calls run_gene for real against a real local gene, which shells out via the real, already-installed rotifer CLI on this machine.

Two cases:

1. **Ordinary case** — the heartbeat this server sends on run_gene arrives, with channel `mcp:<host>` derived from the client's declared name.
2. **The one way "long-lived" could still lose a request** — shellExec uses spawnSync (synchronous), so the tool handler is blocked until the spawned CLI child fully exits before this server's own recordHeartbeat() even runs — it starts late in the handler. If a host closes the stdio connection the instant callTool() resolves, with zero grace period, does that late-starting request still get out before the process tears down? Confirmed by hand first that closing stdin alone (no signal) ends this server's process in ~10ms, so this is a genuinely tight window, not a theoretical one — then verified the heartbeat still arrives.

## Verification

Verified by hand in both directions: passes with recordHeartbeat() correctly wired into server.ts, and with that one call site commented out both cases fail (case 1 times out waiting for the request; case 2 sees zero requests) — confirming the fixture actually exercises what it claims to.

- `npx tsc --noEmit` + lint: clean.
- Full suite: 28 files / 358 tests passed.

## Bottom line

MCP channel delivery was already correct — this closes the gap between "analyzed as safe" and "verified end to end."

author: muqsitnawaz
body:
## PHNX-3626 — native-first `agents sessions resume` with same-harness account rotation

Resume now continues the **same** session with the harness's own native resume on its recorded `agent@version` + device + account, instead of spinning up a fresh `/continue` transcript replay. `/continue` is the last-resort fallback only when there is no native path or no healthy same-harness account. Approved behavior spec: `.agents/artifacts/2026-08-30/agents-resume-behavior/plan.html`.

### What changed
- **Native-first + account rotation** (`cli/src/lib/session/recovery.ts`): when the origin login is rate/usage/session/revoked-limited but its version home is installed, native-capable, and still owns the transcript, recovery stays **native** in the origin home and rotates to a healthy **injectable provider account** of the same harness via the existing `--strategy balanced` picker (no second scheduler). A native login in a *different* home can't read the origin transcript (§11), so that case still uses `/continue`. `resolveSessionRecovery` now reads the provider-inclusive account pool.
- **Injection wiring** (`cli/src/commands/exec.ts`): a native resume with a rotated account injects the provider credential through the same `--account` path; an explicit `--account` always wins.
- **Record-forward the origin version** (`lib/exec.ts`, `session-tracker/src/hook.sh`, `actor-sidecar.ts`, `db.ts`, `discover.ts`): `buildExecEnv` exports `AGENTS_RUN_VERSION`; the SessionStart hook joins it to the harness's real session id in the durable sidecar; the scan joins it at row build and write-once COALESCEs it (like `mode`/`harness`/`actor`); codex's relocated `.codex-homes/<version>/` home is now read by `extractVersionFromManagedPath`. This fixes the "origin version was not recorded → /continue" fallback.
- **db.ts template-literal fix**: a backtick inside a SQL comment terminated the upsert template string (left broken on the branch).
- Docs: AGENTS.md §11, `docs/specifications.md` (SES recovery), CHANGELOG.

### Verification (dev build, real codex session — the exact harness from the bug)
```
$ agents-dev sessions resume 01a05499
[agents] session recovery → native codex@0.146.0 on zion · origin codex@0.146.0 is installed, healthy, and owns the indexed transcript
Resuming codex 01a05499 (native) @0.146.0 in /Users/.../agents
```
Before: `/continue` replay, "origin version was not recorded", ran on the wrong host. After: **native**, version `0.146.0` recorded, correct device `zion`.

### Tests
- `recovery.test.ts`: native-resume-on-rotated-provider-account when the origin login is limited; native sibling in another home → `/continue`; existing native/`/continue`/missing-version branches.
- `actor-sidecar.test.ts` + session-tracker `hook.test.ts`: origin version recorded forward and preserved across a version-less rescan.
- `incremental-scan-e2e.test.ts`: `version` moved out of the parity field set (now write-once launch metadata, like actor/harness/mode).
- Full suite offloaded to fleet workers; typecheck clean.

author: edimarlnx
body:
Adds a `router` edition as a sibling of `server`: the machine boots as a firewall/router with only SSH and WireGuard exposed and no web management port.

## What it does
- **Two NIC roles** `wan0` (uplink, DHCP client) and `lan0` (internal gateway + DHCP server), named by MAC via `/etc/omarchy/router/roles.conf` / `omarchy-router-nics` / an autoinstall `router-nics` hint — never by this host's interface names.
- **IP forwarding** via a sysctl drop-in.
- **nftables `inet tui` firewall** (tui-firewall's own table) in place of ufw: `input` drop except established/ICMP/loopback/LAN and, from the WAN, only `22/tcp` + the WireGuard UDP port; `forward` drop except established and LAN→WAN; masquerade out `wan0`. Written as a readable `/etc/nftables.conf` loaded by `nftables.service` and previewed/applied by `omarchy-router-firewall` — not a hidden apply.
- **Reuses the server base**: the router runtime ships inside `omarchy-server` (`install/router/`, which sources the server leaves), and `omarchy-apply-system` routes to it under `OMARCHY_PROFILE=router`.
- **tui-tools**: installs the released tools (tui-firewall, tui-network, ...); `tui-router` and `tui-vpn` are left as commented placeholders until released.
- **Identity**: keeps the Omarchy identity; the console/MOTD say "Router" and the ISO menu label renders "Omarchy Router".

## Exposed ports and default policy
- Exposed on the WAN: `22/tcp` and `51820/udp` (WireGuard, configurable) — nothing else, no web port.
- Default forward: drop, with LAN→WAN allowed (conntrack) and masqueraded out `wan0`.

## Static verification
- The full `iso/patches` stack (0001–0013) applies clean; the orchestrator compiles (`py_compile`); every router leaf and command parses (`bash -n`); the `omarchy-apply-system` overlay patch applies and routes correctly.
- No web listener in the router unit set.
- The router-1.0 acceptance on real NICs (items 1–7) is owed to the lab — see `reports/2026-08-30-router-profile.md`.

Companion PR: `omarchy-server-pkgs#router-profile` bumps `omarchy-server` to `pkgrel 16` to ship `install/router/`.

author: nish3451
body:
## What changed

is_quota_cap_error (lib/seat-lib.sh) stage 2b hard-cap keyword fallback now includes FreeUsageLimitError.

## Why

OpenCode free-tier providers return HTTP 429 with FreeUsageLimitError type and message "Rate limit exceeded. Please try again later." — no reset-window text. The detector's stage 1 matched "rate limit exceeded", but stage 2 required either a window signal or a hard-cap keyword (weekly/daily limit/INFERENCE_CAP_ERROR). FreeUsageLimitError was missing from both, so the seat was never benched.

This caused a spawn-die-respawn loop: worker died on 429, intake re-claimed the issue, pick_seat re-picked the same un-benched seat, worker died again. fleet-heartbeat.service tripped with undersat_rc=1 (full-wedge: work=24, running=0).

With the match, mark_seat_quota_bench fires and falls back to the provider default (quota_bench_default_s=900 for opencode), benching the seat for 15 min so the reactive seat-health ledger can land its 30min-fresh rate_limited marker.

## Verification

- FreeUsageLimitError (no window) now matches is_quota_cap_error (rc=0)
- Transient 429 without quota keywords still does NOT match (rc=1)
- Devin rate limit (has window) still matches (rc=0)
- ClinePass weekly cap still matches (rc=0)
- Out-of-credits (no window) still does NOT match (rc=1)

Tests: bash tests/seat-lib.test.sh ALL GREEN (including new scenario 9b-mimo, existing 9b transient-429 no-match, 9b-devin, 9f-mimo bench-writer).

Fixes fleet-ops#2463. Closes fleet-ops#2463.

author: trevormil
body:
## The leak

`x-internal: true` was a no-op for publishing.

`openapitypes-helpers/routes.yaml` is the source of the published spec.
`scripts/normalize_yml.ts` copies it wholesale (injecting generated schemas)
into `openapitypes/combined.yaml`; `spread_explodes.ts` turns that into
`combined_processed.yaml`; `.github/workflows/genapi.yml` then pushes
`./openapitypes` to Stoplight **and** commits `openapi-hosted/openapi.json` +
`.yaml` — the spec LLMs consume — via an auto-PR.

Nothing in that path ever read `x-internal`. The flag was honoured only by
`scripts/check_routes_consistency.ts`, a lint no publish step gates on.

Proof: `POST /collection/{collectionId}/refresh` carries `x-internal: true` in
`routes.yaml` **and** was present in the committed `openapi-hosted/openapi.json`
and `.yaml` on `main`.

## The fix

**1. A filter in the publish path.** `scripts/strip_internal_routes.ts` runs in
`gen_api_docs_ci.sh` immediately after `normalize_yml.ts` — the single choke
point, before `spread_explodes.ts`, before the Stoplight push, and before
`convert_openapi_to_json.ts` writes the hosted files. The pushed spec and the
hosted JSON do not contain the operations at all; we do not rely on Stoplight's
own `x-internal` handling. It also runs in the local `gen_api_docs.sh`.

The shared logic lives in `scripts/lib/internalRoutes.ts`:
- removes every operation marked `x-internal: true`
- removes a path once it has no operations left
- prunes tag declarations orphaned **by that removal** — the mirror of the
  used-vs-declared tag bug fixed in #279 / #282. A tag that was already unused
  before the strip is deliberately left alone; that is a different defect and
  not ours to silently rewrite.

**2. Path-level `x-internal`.** A path item marked `x-internal: true` now takes
every operation under it with it, so a whole path can be marked once.

**3. A guard that fails loudly.** `scripts/assert_no_internal_routes.ts` exits 1
(never warns) and is wired into `genapi.yml` as a step **before** the Stoplight
push:

- **Assertion A** — the assembled spec contains zero `x-internal` operations
  (operation-level or inherited from the path item). Always enforced, against
  both `combined_processed.yaml` and `openapi-hosted/openapi.json`.
- **Assertion B** — no route the indexer serves behind `websiteOnlyCors` appears
  as a public operation. This reuses `check_routes_consistency.ts`'s existing
  parser rather than reimplementing it: `parseExpressRoutes` /
  `parseOpenAPIRoutes` / `arePathsEquivalent` moved to
  `scripts/lib/routeAnalysis.ts`, and `check_routes_consistency.ts` now imports
  them (−87 lines, behaviour unchanged).

  Assertion B needs an indexer checkout. CI attempts one into `.indexer-checkout`
  (gitignored, `continue-on-error`, `INDEXER_READ_TOKEN` falling back to
  `GITHUB_TOKEN`); when it succeeds the assertion runs and a violation fails the
  job. Locally `gen_api_docs.sh` always runs it against
  `../../../bitbadges-indexer/src/indexer.ts`. **Caveat, flagged deliberately:**
  if the indexer checkout is unavailable in CI, assertion B is skipped with a
  `::warning::` and only A is enforced. Point `INDEXER_READ_TOKEN` at a token
  that can read the indexer to make B unconditional.

**4. Regenerated hosted artifacts.** The filter is applied to the committed
`openapi-hosted/openapi.json` and `.yaml`: **93 → 92 paths**, a pure deletion of
the `POST /collection/{collectionId}/refresh` block (−67 JSON lines, −55 YAML
lines, zero insertions). Its only tag (`Tokens`) is still used elsewhere, so no
tag declarations changed.

## On the 126 vs 93 path count

The premise that assembly drops paths turned out to be wrong, and it matters, so
recording it: `normalize_yml.ts` copies **all** of `routes.yaml`'s paths through
untouched, and neither `spread_explodes.ts` nor `convert_openapi_to_json.ts`
removes any. The gap is **staleness**, not filtering — the committed hosted spec
carries 16 paths that no longer exist in `routes.yaml` and is missing 49 that do.

So a true regeneration would be a ~65-path diff that buries this fix. The hosted
artifacts are therefore only filtered here, and the 93 → 92 delta is exactly the
one internal operation and nothing else. Refreshing them against current
`routes.yaml` is a separate change.

## Recommended markings — the user's call, nothing marked here

No route was newly marked `x-internal`. The consistency checker reports 11
Express routes absent from the OpenAPI spec. **None of them uses
`websiteOnlyCors`; all 11 use only `premiumOnlyHandler` (API-key tiering), and
none carries an auth scope.** So on the indexer's own middleware evidence, none
is website-only and none is a candidate for `x-internal`.

### Group A — legacy POST duplicates of routes already documented as GET (7)

`indexer.ts:860` labels this block *"For backwards compatibility and to be
deprecated (thus the explicit v0)"*. Each shares its handler with a documented
GET. `normalize_yml.ts`'s `postToGetRoutes` list already converts most of these
in the spec, which is why only the POST verb reads as drift.

| Route (`indexer.ts`) | Documented as | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/v0/collection/:collectionId/:tokenId/owners` (861) | `GET /collection/{collectionId}/{tokenId}/owners` | public, redundant |
| `POST /api/v0/collection/:collectionId/balance/:bitbadgesAddress` (862) | `GET /collection/{collectionId}/balance/{address}` | public, redundant |
| `POST /api/v0/collection/:collectionId/:tokenId/activity` (863) | `GET /collection/{collectionId}/{tokenId}/activity` | public, redundant |
| `POST /api/v0/collection/:collectionId/refreshStatus` (864) | `GET /collection/{collectionId}/refreshStatus` | public, redundant |
| `POST /api/v0/claims/status/:claimAttemptId` (895) | `GET /claims/status/{claimAttemptId}` | public, redundant |
| `POST /api/v0/status` (910, comment: *"Backwards compatibility"*) | `GET /status` | public, redundant |
| `POST /api/v0/codes` (917) | `GET /codes` (also `GET /api/:version/codes`, 820) | public, redundant |

**Recommendation: mark none of them internal, and do not add them to
`routes.yaml`.** They are public aliases the maintainers already intend to
deprecate. If the drift noise is unwanted, deprecate the Express side rather than
growing the documented surface.

### Group B — genuinely undocumented, no documented twin (4)

| Route | Handler | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/v0/depth` (876) | `getDepth` | Central order-book depth for token markets and intent denom pairs. Public market data; siblings `/collection/{id}/orderbook/{tokenId}`, `/allListings`, `/collectionOffers` are all documented. **Looks public → document.** |
| `GET /api/v0/intents/depth` (880) | `getIntentsDepth` | The code comments call it a thin shim over `/depth`. Public. **Public → document, or leave undocumented as a shim; not internal.** |
| `GET /api/v0/intents/fills` (881) | `getIntentFills` | Public fill history; `/intents` and `/intents/{address}` are both documented. **Looks public → document.** |
| `GET /api/v0/collection/:collectionId/:tokenId/approvalItems/:address` (872) | `getApprovalItemsForAddress` | Sits in the marketplace block whose every sibling is documented. **Looks public → document.** |

Group B reads as documentation lag on newer market/intent features, not as
hidden internal surface. Adding them is out of scope here — this PR exists to
stop routes leaking, not to grow `routes.yaml`.

## Verification

- `bun run test` — 152 suites, 3316 tests, green (31 of them new, under
  `scripts/`; `jest.config.cjs` roots extended, and `scripts` excluded from the
  build tsconfigs so tooling never lands in `dist`).
- `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json --noEmit` clean.
- TDD: `scripts/lib/publishedSpec.spec.ts` was written first and failed on `main`
  for the right reason — 4 failures, all
  `POST /collection/{collectionId}/refresh` present in the hosted JSON and YAML.
  It asserts, from `routes.yaml` as the source of truth, that no operation marked
  internal

author: haninaguib
body:
Closes #98

Skip `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s jobs while the triggering PR is a draft, and start
them at `ready_for_review` instead — so the whole work-in-progress window (draft PR
open, through however many fix and review passes) costs zero CI minutes, and the one
run that gates an actual merge starts when the PR is marked ready.

This moves when CI starts relative to `/t-ship`, which used to read CI status *before*
marking the PR ready — now the same step that starts CI. `/t-ship`'s Procedure is
corrected: it marks the PR ready, then watches CI to a concluded result (no timeout —
the human running `/t-ship` is present for the invocation), and only then reaches the
confirmation gate, so the gate can never show "green" evidence that actually means
"nothing ran yet." `/t-drive`'s Solo mode CI pre-check (ADR-007) is retired — it decided
whether to defer *before* invoking `/t-ship`, and has nothing left to decide once CI
cannot have settled at that point regardless of how long the run's own work took; the
wait now lives entirely inside `/t-ship`, for both a human-invoked ship and a driven
one. `docs/adr/008-attended-ci-wait-at-the-ship-gate.md` records this, narrowing
ADR-007 to the case it still fits rather than silently contradicting it.

`/t-work` and `/t-review` were checked for the same CI-timing assumption and carry
none — left untouched.

## Checks run
- `./.t-workflow/scripts/consistency-check.sh` — PASS — commit `eb876ec`
- `./.t-workflow/scripts/plumbing-test.sh` — PASS — commit `eb876ec`

## Verified live, on this PR's own head sha
- Pushing this PR's commit while draft triggered `CI` run 33354338614: all 6 jobs
  (`consistency`, `record`, `plan-gate`, `title-gate`, `blockers`, `plumbing-test`)
  completed with conclusion `skipped`, zero steps run, in ~1 second — zero billed
  Actions minutes.
- Marking the PR ready (`gh pr ready 110`) started a new run, 33354361328: 5 of 6 jobs
  completed `success` (real work, not skipped) before the PR was converted back to
  draft (`gh pr ready 110 --undo`) to leave it in the normal pre-`/t-ship` state.
- `review-gate`'s `cold-review` job failed on the freshly-opened draft PR — this is the
  pre-existing symptom issue #97 already tracks (out of scope here; `review-gate.yml`
  is untouched by this diff).

## What remains open
- ADR-008's revisit triggers 1–2 (the attended watch's practical wall-clock cost, for
  both an interactive `/t-ship` and a driven session) are worth a human glance once this
  has run for real a few times — nothing to fix now, just worth watching.

## Why

The corners were `&ime_kana LS(LEFT_COMMAND) KANA` / `&ime_eiji LC(LALT) EIJI`,
a shape copied from `combo_kana` / `combo_eiji` in #186. The combos need that
hold: they swallow the two thumb keys, whose own mod-tap holds sum to exactly
Shift+Cmd and Ctrl+Alt. A corner key swallows nothing, so its hold restored no
chord and only cost the plain key:

- `hold-preferred` resolves to HOLD on any other key pressed inside the 200 ms
  term. The left corner sits next to `&al_q`, so a "kana then Q" roll produced
  Cmd+Shift+Q.
- Holding either corner past 200 ms emitted nothing at all.
- The tap only fired on release, never on press.

## What is deliberately not changed

The thumb combos keep their hold-taps exactly as they were, by request. That
keeps `&ime_kana` / `&ime_eiji`, `HOLD_TAP_HP200` and the `kana` / `eiji`
wrapper macros in use, so nothing became dead code and nothing was deleted.

- `./scripts/build-zmk.sh` green for all three targets.
- Read back from the generated devicetree
  (`build/imprint_left/zephyr/zephyr.dts`): base position 0 = `&kp 0x70091`
  (LANG2/EIJI), position 11 = `&kp 0x70090` (LANG1/KANA); `combo_kana` =

- `gen-eiji-drawer-map.py --check` and `gen-vkey-aliases.py --check` both in sync.

author: xcoder-es
body:
Closes #219. Contract tests for `POST /clickouts`.

Based on `main`, independent of #375 and #376 — merge in any order.

## What was already there, and what was missing

The four cases the task names were all covered by the existing handler suite: 401 (`TestAnAnonymousClickIsNeverEvenAttempted`, `TestAFailedAuthenticationIsNotAVerdict`), 409 (`TestAnOfferNobodyPublishesRightNowIsAConflict`), 429 (`TestAClickRefusedByTheRuleIsA429ThatSaysWhenToComeBack`), and no click row after a deeplink failure (`TestARedirectThatCannotBeBuiltIsA502AndRecordsNothing`).

So rather than write those again, this adds the thing **no behaviour test can do**: assert the *set*.

A status added to the handler and not to the document is a client that cannot handle it. A status removed from the handler and left in the document is a client handling something that will never arrive. **Both drift silently, because every individual test still passes.**

The declared responses are read out of `api/openapi.json` at test time rather than restated in Go — a copy is exactly the drift this exists to catch — and compared in both directions.

## The seven cases

One per documented status: `201` created, `400` a body naming no offer, `401` no usable token, `409` a band nobody publishes now, `429` the click rule, `500` a click that could not be recorded, `502` a redirect that could not be built.

Each error case also asserts `application/problem+json` and that the body's own `status` agrees with the response's — a client that cannot parse the failure cannot report it either.

## Verification

Two commits, largest 210 lines, each checked out on its own and built, vetted and tested against a freshly created database — 2 for 2.

`golangci-lint` v2.12.2 clean; coverage 91.1% against the 90% gate; full suite green with `-race -shuffle=on`; ref-name and author lints clean.

**Mutation-tested in both drift directions**, by editing the contract document rather than the code:

- adding a `418` to `createClickOut` that nothing serves → red, naming the undelivered status;
- removing the `429` that the endpoint does serve → red, naming the undocumented one.

Both restored afterwards; `git diff` on `api/openapi.json` is empty in this branch.

Hai tài liệu tiếng Việt trong `docs/ideas/`, cùng chỉ mục trong `docs/README.md`.

**`market-analysis-servo-robots.md`** — khảo sát thị trường robot servo. Tách rõ `[REPO]`
(Open Duck Mini v2, microduck, MiniPlan-V6, có dẫn dòng cụ thể) khỏi `[NGOÀI REPO]`

**`microduck-vs-open-duck-mini-v2.md`** — vì sao chuyển động của microduck đọc ra như một
con vật trong khi ODM v2 đọc ra như một robot đi rất tốt, dù cả hai đều là MuJoCo → PPO →
ONNX. Bốn nguyên nhân, mỗi cái có bằng chứng mã nguồn:

- Hợp đồng quan sát chứa lệnh tư thế đầu: `obs[51..55] = neck_pitch, head_pitch, head_yaw,
  head_roll`, nên `robot.look(x,y,z)` → `HEAD_FK.look_at` chảy *vào* policy thay vì cộng
  lên trên nó. ODM v2 chỉ điều kiện hoá theo lệnh vận tốc và có cả cờ `--zero_head`.
- Thư viện 9 policy cùng hợp đồng `obs[1,61] → actions[1,14]` sau một scheduler ưu tiên
  (`roulade > kick > ground pick > sit/rise > stand > walk`), với `last_action` *raw* dùng
  chung nên đổi mạng không giật.
- IMU nằm trên bus Dynamixel, đọc trong **cùng** `sync_read` với 15 servo → trọng lực và vị
  trí khớp cùng một thời điểm.
- Hằng số thời gian ở mọi đường ranh: `head_lowpass 0.5` / `legs_lowpass 0.7` khớp training,
  `CHORALE_MOUTH_TAU_S 0.09`, `HOME_RAMP 2 s`, fall predictor mềm gain *trước* khi đáp,
  theremin lấy một biến `closeness` ra cả pitch/level/mouth.

phạm vi kiểm chứng, nên so sánh tầng runtime dựa trên `experiments/`; và phần sim/nhận dạng
động cơ (BAM) của ODM v2 mạnh hơn những gì repo này để lộ. Mọi suy luận của tôi được đánh
dấu `[SUY LUẬN]`, tách khỏi `[MD]` / `[ODM]`.

author: marianocappucci
body:
El corte sucio de energia pasa, y el initdb ahora lleva --data-checksums

Punto #3 del README, en la misma VM. Se escribieron ventas a ~1000 por segundo,
cada una con su fila de outbox EN LA MISMA TRANSACCION, y se apago la VM de
golpe --`Stop-VM -TurnOff`, que es tirar del cable-- en plena escritura.

Al volver: 27.840 ventas, 27.840 filas de outbox, CERO ventas sin su outbox y
CERO outbox sin su venta. La ultima es `corte-027840`, o sea sin huecos. La suma
de totales se calculo leyendo la tabla entera, sin errores de lectura, y
PostgreSQL se recupero solo.

La invariante a proposito NO usa un registro externo: un archivo con "iba por la
venta N" se habria perdido en el mismo corte. Lo que se verifica es que toda
venta tenga su outbox y todo outbox su venta; una transaccion partida al medio
deja una sin la otra.

LO QUE ESE RESULTADO NO PRUEBA

Que el WAL se recupere bien no dice nada sobre lo que el disco haya escrito mal.
Por eso el initdb ahora lleva `--data-checksums`. PostgreSQL 16 los deja
APAGADOS por defecto --medido en el cluster de la VM: `data_checksums = off`--
y sin ellos una pagina que el disco devuelve corrupta se lee como datos validos:
el error aparece meses despues, en un arqueo que no cierra. Con ellos la lectura
falla y dice que pagina esta rota.

Se decide en el initdb y no se puede cambiar despues, asi que para un nodo que
va a vivir en un salon con cortes de luz es ahora o nunca. Cuesta algo de CPU
por pagina leida, que en esa maquina no se nota.

Verificado aparte, porque el cluster de la VM es anterior al cambio: initdb con
la linea nueva sale con 0 y dice "Las sumas de verificacion en paginas de datos
han sido activadas", sin perder ICU.

Quedan los puntos #5 y #6 --desinstalacion y actualizacion--, que necesitan el
`.iss` compilado.

author: ivanwng97
body:
The one SURFACED item from #960's verification round (V-1), as its own PR.

## The blind spot

The per-hook check asserted an empty **string**, and a `seen` file never written reads identically to one written empty. So a hook that died before `exec` passed the clean check vacuously. Two measured instances, both green before this fix:

- an early `exit` anywhere before the `exec`
- an operator's exported `SKIP_PREFLIGHT=1` sending the hook down its documented bypass — which the harness's `env` did not clear — leaving the check green **against a hook with no scrub at all**

## The fix, per the verification lens's recommendation

- A missing `seen` is emitted as `hook-died-before-exec`, which the clean check treats as a leak. General: it catches every died-before-`exec` cause, including ones nobody has thought of yet.
- `SKIP_PREFLIGHT=` cleared in the injected env — defense-in-depth for the one known instance, not the fix.

The control keeps its own teeth: with the `just` stub removed entirely, the suite still reds through the per-hook check.

## Measured, all six classes

| mutation | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| normal | green | green |
| `exit 7` after `set` | **green (the hole)** | red |
| empty scrub + ambient `SKIP_PREFLIGHT=1` | **green (the hole)** | red |
| scrub narrowed to `unset GIT_DIR` | red | red |
| whole scrub block deleted | red | red |
| harness self-broken (stub removed) | red | red |

Falsifies none of #960's mutation evidence — every red reported there ran through a path that reached `exec`; this closes the class that did not.

author: bannaarr01
body:
## What

Builds the engineering journal's browse surface — the index, the four category archives, and the series reading-order page — plus the two components groups 05 and 06 import (`CoverArt`, `BlogCard`). Group 04 of the parallel build brief (`grouped/plans/04-journal-taxonomy.md`).

With the editorial serif removed (PLAN.md §9), the journal no longer separates itself from the portfolio typographically. Recreating that separation through layout is this group's stated design burden (PLAN.md §4.7).

## Scope

In scope:

- `site/src/components/journal/**` — 12 components and 1 helper module
- `site/src/pages/blog/index.astro`, `site/src/pages/blog/category/[category].astro`, `site/src/pages/blog/series/[series].astro`
- `site/src/styles/tokens.css` — adds the 11 `--cover-*` tokens PLAN.md §4.8 specifies but group 00 did not ship (see Risk Level)
- Replaces group 00's three stubs (`BlogCard`, `CoverArt`, `CategoryTabs`) with real implementations, prop signatures unchanged

Out of scope:

- `site/src/pages/blog/[...slug].astro` — the article template, owned by group 05
- `site/src/data/**` and `site/src/content/**` — owned by group 07; this branch renders group 00's placeholder content
- `site/src/pages/index.astro` — untouched; it currently fails to build on `develop` because it imports 11 modules from the not-yet-landed `src/data/` (see Test Evidence)
- OG image generation (`astro-og-canvas`) — group 06

## Changes

- `CoverArt.astro` — implements PLAN.md §4.8 exactly: a 118deg gradient, three concentric arcs struck from a `68% 106%` focal point, a 52px grid, centred category glyph, category name bottom-left. Gradient/arcs/grid sit on one filtered layer so the per-category `hue-rotate` (`go` 0°, `aws-cloud` −14°, `system-design` +18°, `backend-engineering` +32°) never touches the white type above it. Variants `card` 16:10, `lead` 16:15.5, `banner` 16:6.4. Zero image bytes.
- `BlogCard.astro` — cover, mono meta row, optional series line, title, dek, and a footer pinned with `margin-top: auto`. Exactly one `<a>` per card, stretched over the whole card via a pseudo-element; "Read article" is a `<span>`, so no interactive element is nested inside the link.
- `Masthead.astro` — 84px lockup with "Journal" in the cyan→teal gradient, a monospace dateline, and a faint 52px rule grid echoing the cover art.
- `CategoryTabs.astro` — Latest plus the four disciplines, `aria-current="page"` on the active tab, horizontal scroll with the scrollbar hidden below 700px.
- `FeatureStory.astro` — split lead layout; the cover repeats the title link as `tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true"` so it is a mouse target without duplicating a tab stop.
- `CardGrid.astro` / `RowGrid.astro` — ruled cell grids. Every cell carries a top and right hairline and the inner grid is offset 1px into a clipping frame, so ruling stays correct at 3, 2 and 1 columns without per-breakpoint `nth-child` arithmetic and a partial final row closes on its own.
- `EmptyState.astro` — replaces the original site's bare-heading-over-blank-space for the three empty categories; shows the discipline's cover art, its description, and links to the categories that do have posts.
- `SeriesShelf.astro` / `DisciplineGrid.astro` / `SectionRail.astro` — numbered shelf rows and the shared ruled section header.
- `taxonomy.ts` — per-category glyph and hue-rotate map, typed as a total `Record<CategorySlug, …>` so a fifth category is a compile error; category titles resolve from the `categories` collection with a design-side fallback.
- `src/pages/blog/category/[category].astro` — `getStaticPaths()` over all four categories including empty ones, since the tabs and discipline grid link to all four.
- `src/pages/blog/series/[series].astro` — grid ordered via `getSeriesParts()` by `part` ascending, never by date, with `showPart` on every card.
- Byline, cover credit and page title now read the site owner from group 01's existing `SITE_OWNER` constant (`components/layout/nav.ts`) instead of the name carried over from the mockups, matching how `Header`, `SiteFooter` and `JournalFooter` already source it. The feature byline avatar uses `BJA`, matching the initials engraved in `ui/Logo.astro`. The card cover credit drops the "· Engineering Journal" suffix because the longer name wraps to two lines in a ~250-280px card cover; `lead` and `banner` keep the full credit.
- Merge commit `9bd4705` rewires the slice onto the real foundation: `--r-card`/`--r-pill`/`--shadow-card-hover` → `--radius-card`/`--radius-pill`/`--glow-card-hover`, `../lib/content` → the `../lib` barrel, and deletes a local `reading-time.ts` in favour of group 00's `getMinutesRead()`.

## Risk Level

medium

Additive UI on new routes with no auth, data-mutation or schema surface — but it edits one shared file (`src/styles/tokens.css`, owned by group 00) and replaces three cross-group stubs that groups 05 and 06 import.

## Rollback Plan

1. `git revert 9bd4705 e1cadac` — removes the journal slice and its merge; no other group imports `components/journal/**` yet except through the stubs restored by the revert.
2. If only the shared-file edit needs reverting, drop the `--cover-*` block from `src/styles/tokens.css`; `CoverArt` is the sole consumer and will render an unstyled gradient rather than break the build.
3. Redeploy from the previous `develop` build artefact. No migrations, no cache keys, no env changes to unwind.

## Test Evidence

```text
npm run build         PASSED for the six journal routes (see caveat below)
npx astro check       PASSED — 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 hints
npm run no-hex        PASSED — no hex outside styles/tokens.css
npm run format:check  PASSED — prettier clean across the slice
npm run test          no test runner configured in this repo
npm run test:e2e      no e2e runner configured in this repo
```

Caveat, stated plainly: `npm run build` **fails on this branch and on `develop` itself**, at `src/pages/index.astro`, which imports 11 modules from `src/data/` — group 07's owned path, not yet landed. That breakage is pre-existing and unrelated to this diff. The six journal routes and the type check were verified with that one page temporarily set aside; it is committed unmodified.

Verified in a browser against the merged tree (Playwright, `dist/` served locally):

- Six routes render: `/blog/`, all four `/blog/category/<slug>/`, `/blog/series/placeholder-series/`
- Masthead holds one line 375 → 1440px (315px of text in a 335px container at 375px)
- Series page renders Part 1 then Part 2, although the placeholder publishes part 2 first — confirming `part` ordering, not date
- Draft placeholder absent from `dist/` and the sitemap
- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` holds every hover transform at `none`, while the same hovers animate without it
- Keyboard pass: skip-link first, one link per card, feature cover correctly skipped, visible focus ring on every stop

## Database Changes

none

## Environment Variables

none

## Test scenarios (for QA)

- [High] Journal index renders — Steps: visit `/blog/` → Expected: masthead with "Journal" in cyan→teal gradient, one featured story, the remaining posts in a ruled three-up grid, series shelf and discipline grid below.
- [High] Empty category shows a real empty state — Steps: visit `/blog/category/go/` → Expected: the Go cover art, "No Go articles have been published", and pills linking to the categories that do have posts — never a blank grid.
- [High] Series reads in part order — Steps: visit `/blog/series/placeholder-series/` → Expected: cards labelled Part 1 then Part 2, even though part 2 has the later publish date.

author: rihards-freimanis
body:
## Summary

Scoped-down delivery of #1691. Builds the switchable subprocess/library mechanism the issue asks for and ports one real, low-risk operation onto it end-to-end (typed spec → both executors → runtime switch → doctor reporting → tests), rather than attempting all six tools in one pass. See "Why scoped down" below for the concrete evidence that drove this.

## The three contracts, verified against current code first

- **Dry-run must still render the CLI command.** True today and preserved: `ResolveAWSIdentity`/`CheckAWSStatus` are never even called during `cloud init aws --dry-run` — the CLI (`erun-cli/cmd/cloud.go`'s `runCloudInitAWSCommand`) hand-renders the same trace lines independently. New test (`cloud/init_aws_dry_run_unaffected_by_library_execution_mode`) proves the golden is byte-identical whether `execution.modes.aws-sts` is `library` or unset.
- **The audit line must still show the CLI invocation.** Both the subprocess and library paths call `ctx.TraceCommand("", "aws", args...)` with the *same* argv, built by one shared function (`awsGetCallerIdentityArgs`) so the two paths structurally cannot drift apart — a test locks this (`TestLibraryResolveAWSIdentityMatchesSubprocessObservableResult`).
- **Subprocess stays a runtime-switchable fallback, switchable without a release.** New config key `execution.modes.<operation>` in `~/.config/erun/config.yaml` (e.g. `execution.modes.aws-sts: library`), read fresh on every call via `LoadERunConfig()` — no rebuild, no restart. Defaults to `subprocess` for every operation.

## What's ported, and why only this

**Ported:** `aws sts get-caller-identity` (`ResolveAWSIdentity`, `CheckAWSStatus` in `erun-common/cloud.go`) → `aws-sdk-go-v2`'s STS client (`erun-common/cloud_aws_sdk.go`). Read-only, single call shape, already-injected dependency seams (`CloudDependencies.ResolveAWSIdentity`/`CheckAWSStatus`), turns "aws CLI not installed" / stderr-substring matching into a typed SDK error path.

**Why I didn't go further, with the evidence:**

- **helm** — the issue's own ranking calls this "cleanest of all," but reading the actual deploy path (`erun-common/deploy.go`'s `HelmDeploySpec.command()` → `DeployHelmChart`) shows it isn't a bare `helm upgrade --install --wait`: `runHelmDeployWithPodWatch` streams and parses helm's live stdout for pod status, and `runHelmUpgradeWithSelectorRecovery`/`recreateDeploymentAndRetry` retry based on parsed stderr text. The Go SDK (`helm.sh/helm/v3/pkg/action`) returns typed release/error objects, not a stdout stream to scrape — reproducing this recovery behavior faithfully needs real design work, not a mechanical port, and `deploy` is explicitly root `AGENTS.md`'s highest-blast-radius command. Smaller helm sites (`dependency build`, `pull --untar`, `get metadata`) exist but are individually low-value and I chose not to spread this PR thin across several one-off ports.
- **kubectl** (122 sites) — the single largest surface; needs exact replication of server-side-apply field-manager semantics, `--force-conflicts`, and wait-condition polling. Multi-week effort on its own.
- **git** (84 sites) — the issue itself bans porting `merge --squash`/conflict handling (owned by the merge-queue gate). Read-only porting is plausible but still a large surface; not attempted this session.
- **docker** (49 sites) — registry ops via `go-containerregistry` are plausible, but even those touch the fingerprint/promote logic in `build_spec.go`, which must be preserved exactly; builds via BuildKit are a heavier lift the issue itself flags.
- **ssh** (16 sites) — lowest-ranked by the issue itself ("low value"); not attempted.
- **dtach** — left completely untouched per the issue and per instruction (concurrent work in #1697 owns this area). Verified: no file under the session-lifecycle/dtach contract appears in this diff.

**Also not ported within "aws":** `sso login`/`logout`, `configure set`, `configure export-credentials`, the erun-OIDC federation setup. These drive a real browser SSO device flow or write the shared `~/.aws` ini files — neither replaced by this switch. Named explicitly in code (`awsSTSIdentityExecutionOperation`'s doc comment) and in the new docs section so nobody assumes more coverage than exists.

## The switch

- `erun-common/execution_mode.go`: `ExecutionModeFor(config, operation)` resolves `subprocess` (default) or `library`; unrecognized values normalize to `subprocess`. `ExecutionModeReport(config)` lists every operation with a library alternative (today: `aws-sts`).
- `erun doctor` prints `== Execution modes ==` with each operation's resolved mode, right after the `Target:` line — root config, so it needs no runtime pod and runs even without one.
- Documented in `erun-docs/docs/reference/configuration.md` (new "Execution modes" section) and `erun-docs/docs/cli/doctor.md`.

## Verification

- `erun-common`: new unit tests for the library path (`cloud_aws_sdk_test.go` — httptest STS server driven via the SDK's own `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL` env var, no real AWS account or daemon) and the mode-resolution logic (`execution_mode_test.go`).
- `erun-integration`: three new scenarios — dry-run parity under library mode (reuses the existing subprocess golden byte-for-byte), a real `cloud login` run that completes via the library path with **no `aws` stub declared at all** (proving it genuinely never shells out), and `doctor` surfacing `aws-sts: library` when configured. Every existing `doctor` golden gained the same 3-line `== Execution modes ==` block (reviewed — no other output changed).
- `go vet`/`golangci-lint` clean across `erun-common`, `erun-cli`, `erun-mcp`, `erun-integration`.
- `make check` (blocked on in this run, job exited 0): lint clean across all 6 Go modules, `erun-ui` Go tests green, `erun-kit`/`erun-console` tsc+eslint+prettier+vite+vitest all green, all `erun-devops/k8s/*` chart tests green, integration suite green with **coverage 75.6% (>= 75.6%)** — threshold held, not lowered.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./...` in `erun-common`, `erun-cli`, `erun-mcp`, `erun-integration`
- [x] `golangci-lint run ./...` in all touched Go modules
- [x] `make check` full gate, green
- [x] Manually confirmed no file under the dtach/session-lifecycle contract is touched

Refs #1691 — kubectl, git, docker, ssh, and the helm deploy path remain on subprocess; see "Why I didn't go further" above for the order I'd tackle them in a follow-up (helm's non-deploy read-only calls first, then aws's remaining operations, then kubectl `get`/`apply`/`wait`).
