author: jerichomagallanes
body:
## What this changes

Development builds produce a plan locally instead of calling Gemini, and the `sit` flavour is gone.

## Why

The free allowance is 20 requests per day per model, and a day of building this app exhausts it long before a user would. It happened here: a feature shipped in #71 with its success path untested because the day's quota had gone into testing the app, and #72 could only be verified because it was written to survive exactly that.

Development is the glutton, not the client.

`sit` goes because the plan it was meant to serve does not work. Every Play track, internal, closed and production, is the same app with the same `applicationId`. A `com.jericx.trainr.sit` build is a different app to Google, so a closed test of it would not count toward the twelve-tester requirement for publishing `com.jericx.trainr`, and testers would later have to uninstall it and lose their training. Beta and production differ by track and versionCode, not by flavour, and the same artifact is promoted upward so the bits tested are the bits shipped.

## How it works

`CannedPlanGenerator` reads the request the way the model is asked to, rather than returning a fixture: exactly the number of days the profile asks for, spaced across the week, using exercise keys the video catalog knows so tutorials still render, and loads that step up when a previous week is passed in, so progression stays visible while building the screens that show it.

**The choice is made by the source set, not a flag.** `planGenerator()` is defined once in `src/dev` and once in `src/prod`, and `FirebaseAiClient` moved into `src/prod` beside it. The class that can reach the network is not compiled into a dev build at all, so no wiring mistake can spend the allowance. Verified by unpacking both APKs: `FirebaseAiClient` is absent from the dev dex and present in prod, `CannedPlanGenerator` the reverse.

`GeminiPlanGenerator` stays in `main`. It is the retry and model-walking logic, it holds no network code, and its tests run under the dev variant against a fake client.

## Out of scope

Dead code removed while here, since it was the same sweep: the `sit` source set (which held nothing but `.DS_Store` files), an unused `img_rectangle` drawable, and the leftovers of the in-app language picker, which has been unreachable since #43 pinned the app to English: `LanguageSelector`, `LocaleManager.setAppLocale` and `getAvailableLanguageCodes`. #43 chose to leave that infrastructure dormant rather than delete it, so this reverses that decision; git history holds it if the language switch comes back. `LanguagePreferences` stays, because the prompt still reads a language code from it.

## How to verify

1. Turn on airplane mode, open a dev build, and regenerate the week: a plan arrives in about four seconds with no network.
2. `unzip` the dev APK and search the dex for `FirebaseAiClient`: absent.
3. Same for the prod APK: present, and `CannedPlanGenerator` absent.
4. `./gradlew tasks` no longer lists any `Sit` variant.

## Self-review checklist

- [x] Read the whole diff in "Files changed"
- [x] Verified offline generation on a device with airplane mode on, not just by reading the wiring
- [x] Verified by dex inspection that neither generator reaches the wrong flavour
- [x] README updated: the flavours now describe what they actually do
- [x] 305 unit tests and 167 instrumentation tests pass

body:
Prepares statifier_oban 0.3.1: bumps `mix.exs` to `0.3.1` and assembles the
two `changelog.d/` fragments accumulated since 0.3.0 into a `[0.3.1]` section,
deleting the fragments in the same commit as `changelog.d/README.md` prescribes.

## What lands in 0.3.1

- **Fixed** (`sob-uon`) - `StatifierOban.Timer.cancel/3` no longer cancels a
  timer job that is already executing, so a fired timer whose delivery exits
  the state that armed it is no longer killed mid-step by its own `onexit`
  `<cancel>`. This is the reason the release exists.
- **Changed** (`sob-a8k`) - an undecodable invoke job reports
  `error.communication.invoke.<invoke_id>` through the delivery seam before
  cancelling, whenever its row still names a scope and an invoke id.

The README's downstream-host note that also landed since 0.3.0 is
documentation and carries no changelog entry, per `changelog.d/README.md`'s
"do not write a fragment for documentation" rule.

A second commit moves `.claude/wurk/commit.md`'s "Version bump: never"
section to `0.3.1`. That section names the version `mix.exs` holds and says
in its own text that a release bead updates the line with it; this is that
release bead. It keeps `0.3.0` named as the last version actually on Hex.

## Why a patch bump

Neither landing adds, alters or removes public API, and neither is breaking,
so SemVer puts 0.3.1 rather than 0.3.2-as-minor or 0.4.0. Verified by reading
both fragments' headings (`Changed`, `Fixed`, no `Added`/`Removed`) and the
diff of `lib/` since `v0.3.0`.

- Full gate green on this HEAD: format, compile, credo, dialyzer, deps,
  138/138 tests, 95.4% coverage; `mix quality.verify` attests scope `all`,
  no profile. Doctor / Gettext / Sobelow are declared permanently

  (`Version: 0.3.1`); the generated tarball was deleted.

- Every acceptance criterion on the bead was machine-checked against the tree,
  including the fragments' bodies appearing verbatim in the new section and
  the headings ordered `Changed` then `Fixed`.

## Not in this change

The **tag and the Hex publish are the operator's own act** and are
deliberately absent. Nothing here is pushed to Hex.

## Provenance

- Bead: `sob-eqx` (filed for this release prep; the repo's `wurk.json` has
  `release: null`, so the mechanical steps follow the precedent of
  the in-repo 0.3.0 release-prep commit on `main` rather than a recipe).
- No sibling PR was rebased over; this branch is cut from `origin/main` and
  lands alone.
- No `docs/adr/` path is in this change, so the direction-agent review gate

author: thecodedrift
body:
<!-- stack root=214 pr=214,215:214,216:215,217:216,219:217 -->
**Stack** (root → tip):

- ➡️ #214 (you are here)
  - #215
    - #216
      - #217
        - #219
<!-- /stack -->

Bottom of the stack for the **generator payload alignment** — the CLI's half of the rule-delivery contract agreed with the Cloud Generator team.

## Why this exists

The generator was days from switching on rule generation against a payload the CLI cannot consume. The gap is structural, not a field mismatch: `rules[].content` is one flat ast-grep rule, while `ENGINE_LAYOUTS` defines a rule as a **directory**, and for two of three engines the extra files are what make it run.

| Engine | Complete rule | Response can carry |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sg` | `<id>.yml`, `.tests/` | rule only |
| `vale` | `<id>.yml`, **`.vale.ini`**, `.tests/` | rule only |
| `runtime` | `check.ts`, `captures/*.yml`, `.tests/` | nothing |

Each omission fails identically and in the worst available way: the rule is written, the command succeeds, and `check` exits `0`. A rule that never ran is indistinguishable from one that passed.

The generator team confirmed it against their own code — the runtime build path computed `canonicalHash(rule.check)` and discarded the result, and never wrote to `rules[]`. Every generated runtime rule would have reconciled into `unknown` and silently never run.

## What this slice does

**Resolves the engine on delete.** `deleteRuleFiles` hardcoded `ruleDirectory(cwd, "sg", id)`. A rule id doesn't carry its engine, so the one operation taking a bare id has to find which of the three sibling trees holds it. Invisible while ast-grep was the only deliverable engine — and about to stop being invisible.

`findRuleEngine` lives beside `ENGINE_LAYOUTS` rather than in the caller that first needed it, because every operation taking a bare id has the same problem.

Worth noting this was **already specified correctly**: `cli-rules` says `.taskless/rules/<engine>/<id>/`. The implementation had drifted from its own spec, not merely from its comments.

**Corrects seven stale layout comments** describing the pre-`0005` `.taskless/<engine>/rules/`. Two further occurrences in the migrations are legitimately historical and stay. One of these had already cost something real: the first draft of the cross-team contract document carried the wrong layout, because `discover.ts` is where a reader goes to be sure.

**Opens the OpenSpec change** `generator-payload-alignment`, recording the contract (G1–G7, C1–C3, A1–A4, N1–N4) and the six-slice delivery order.

## Delivery shape

**Stacked, merging forward** — each unit is independently safe in production and leaves `check` green alone.

| | Slice | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Engine resolution on delete; stale layout corrected | **this PR** |
| 2 | `@taskless/cli/layout` published, build-enforced | next — unblocks the generator |
| 3 | The five silent discovery drops become stated reasons; versions read | |
| 4 | `check.ts` enforced as the only executable | |
| 5 | The file-set writer, with path safety | |
| 6 | Re-fetch on `unsafe` / `unknown` | |

The changeset is on this branch and grows as the stack grows.

## Verification

- `1002` tests pass (main's `998` plus four new), typecheck and lint clean
- `openspec validate generator-payload-alignment` passes
- The delete tests **bite**: reverting to hardcoded `sg` leaves the `sg` case passing and fails `vale` and `runtime`, so they detect the specific defect rather than the presence of a check

## Note for reviewers

`Validate` on `main` will go red once this merges and stay red until the final slice archives the change directory. That is expected for a forward-merging stack and blocks nothing — branch protection reads each PR's own check.

## 報告内容と判定

> 問題ID: 51（教育原理）／報告内容：心身の発達の助長も含まれるのではないか

**報告は妥当でした。** 選択肢2と選択肢3の**両方が学校教育法第22条の要件を満たしており、正解が一意になっていませんでした。**

条文（e-Gov法令検索で確認）：

> 第二十二条 幼稚園は、**義務教育及びその後の教育の基礎を培う**ものとして、幼児を保育し、幼児の健やかな成長のために適当な環境を与えて、その**心身の発達を助長する**ことを目的とする。

| 修正前の選択肢 | 条文に含まれるか |
|---|---|
| 1. 義務教育の基礎を培う | ❌ 「及びその後の教育」が欠落 |
| 2. 義務教育及びその後の教育の基礎を培う（正解） | ✅ |
| **3. 心身の発達を助長する** | ✅ **含まれる** |
| 4. 小学校教育への移行を準備する | ❌ |

文法上はむしろ「心身の発達を助長すること」が「〜を目的とする」に直接かかる述部であり、**報告者の指摘のとおり**でした。

## あわせて発見した2つ目の不備

解説の条文引用から**「幼児の健やかな成長のために適当な環境を与えて、」が欠落**していたにもかかわらず、`「」` で囲んで引用の体裁を取っていました。**法令の不正確な引用は、条文を覚える学習者の妨げになります。**

## 修正内容

```
Q: 学校教育法が定める幼稚園の目的として、正しいものはどれか？
   A: 義務教育の基礎を培うものとして、幼児を保育し、その心身の発達を助長する
 ★ B: 義務教育及びその後の教育の基礎を培うものとして、幼児を保育し、その心身の発達を助長する
   C: 小学校教育の内容を先取りして指導し、就学の準備を整える
   D: 保護者の就労等により保育を必要とする幼児を、日々保護者に代わって保育する
```

**「心身の発達を助長する」を独立した選択肢から外し、正解の中に含めました。** これにより「義務教育の基礎」と「義務教育及びその後の教育の基礎」の違いを問うという本来のねらいを維持したまま、正解が一意になります。

誤答は「小学校教育の先取り」と「保育所の説明」に差し替え、明確な誤りとしました。解説の条文引用も公式の文言と完全一致させています。

author: data8504
body:
## Problem

Robot-fired homing weapons begin with `track_goal` unset.  A later target scan can find a valid target, but the returned object was used only for that turn and was not stored, so the missile usually returned to an untracked state on the next homing tick.

Persisting targets also makes the existing object lifecycle checks important: a player can become `OBJ_GHOST`, a remote player can cloak, and the live parent object type can change after a player-fired missile is launched.

## Changes

- Select an eligible target when a robot directly fires a homing weapon, leaving `object_none` when no target is available.  Smart children keep their explicit target assignment path.
- Store later target updates in `track_goal`, so an acquired target remains available on subsequent homing ticks.
- Reject ghost and cloaked player targets, and use the recorded firing identity for cooperative and team filtering after the shooter dies.
- Extract the existing fixed-point turn kernel and add deterministic tests for target selection, initial acquisition, retained reacquisition, no-target behavior, player death/replacement, and D1/D2 trajectory calculations.

Potentially addresses #488, pending gameplay evidence from players familiar with the original behavior.

## Validation

- Clean GCC 15 SDL2 builds of D1X-Rebirth and D2X-Rebirth
- Complete common, D1, and D2 header-include matrix
- 10 focused Boost homing tests
- Independent adversarial review of the final three-commit series

The trajectory coverage is a deterministic functional model of the production fixed-point code; it is not a claim of complete DOS/gameplay parity.

> AI assistance disclosure: I prepared this change with assistance from OpenAI Codex, operating as a distinct coding agent. Codex researched the implementation history, developed the tests and patch series, ran the stated validation, and performed an independent adversarial review. Gameplay evaluation and maintainer review remain external to that work.

author: patrickcleeve2
body:
Stacked on #685. The control verbs from the live run's build list — during the demo the agent could watch and answer, but not stop the run, change supervision, or re-run a task. All three now exist, each riding a mechanism the GUI already uses rather than a new one.

## How it works (plain language)

**`POST /app/workflow/stop`** — the Stop button, over HTTP. It calls the window's own `stop_task_workflow()": the task manager's stop event, plus halting a running mill or spot burn (their stop events + the same hardware stop call the core server's `stop_milling` route already issues from this thread — every step is thread-safe, no GUI-thread entry needed).

The deliberate part is the scope: it sits on the **read** router, following the `stop_milling` precedent we set in the first server PR. Stopping is the *safety* action — any agent that can see the microscope must be able to stop it. Arming exists to gate the dangerous actions; the emergency brake must never be behind the same gate. It also skips the command lock: a stop that queues behind the thing it is stopping is not a stop.

**`POST /app/supervision`** (control scope) — flips `task.supervise` in the live protocol. This is the exact value the workflow re-reads at every prompt-or-proceed decision (it's a live predicate, never a snapshot), so the change takes effect at the next decision point mid-run — the same behaviour as the GUI's supervised/automated toggle. One honest limitation: the GUI's own card/checkbox indicators refresh on the next task transition, not instantly.

**`POST /app/queue/requeue`** (control scope) — queues a task for an item in the *running* workflow. The queue deliberately allows adding an already-completed (item, task) pair — that IS its re-run mechanism — so "run 03's fiducial again" is just an add, optionally `front: true` to run next. Inputs are validated against the experiment's items and the protocol's task names; refusals come back structured (`queued: false` + reason + the valid names), and the queue-changed signal keeps the GUI's queue view current. When no workflow is running there is no queue: a structured refusal, not an error — batch-then-review re-runs happen inside the run.

Sidecar grows `stop_workflow`, `set_task_supervision`, `requeue_task` — 30 tools.

## Tests

- Context level: stop only fires the stop path while running (and degrades cleanly on a host without one); supervision flips are visible through the same `get_supervision` read the workflow uses; re-queue against a real TaskManager/TaskQueue re-runs a completed pair, bumps the version, and refuses unknown items/tasks with the valid names attached.
- HTTP level: stop responds on an unarmed (read-only) server; supervision and requeue 403 without control, 422 with missing fields.
- 79 tests green across the context/prompt/server suites.

author: datnguyen998
body:
## Summary
Two changes bundled into one PR since they landed back-to-back on this branch:

1. **Static data snapshot ("database") instead of live client-side fetch**
2. **Animation engine swapped from hand-rolled CSS/JS to Anime.js**

## 1. Static data snapshot

`graveyard.py` and `graveyard.html` used to each independently fetch and parse the 3 upstream sources (Killed by Google/Microsoft/Apple), duplicating the parsing logic and hitting 3 external APIs on every page load. Now:

- `graveyard.py` is the only thing that talks to the upstream sources. Its output (`graveyard_all.json`, committed to the repo) is the single source of truth.
- `graveyard.html` reads that committed file instead of calling the sources itself — removed `SOURCES`/`parseKbg()`/`parseKba()`/`PARSERS` entirely.
- `graveyard.py` also writes `graveyard_all.meta.json` (generation timestamp, per-company counts) for the dashboard's "last updated" line.
- Added `.github/workflows/refresh-data.yml` — runs `graveyard.py` daily (+ on-demand + on pushes touching `graveyard.py`) and commits the refreshed snapshot. This is what keeps the data current without a server.
- Added `computeStatus()`: since "dead" vs "scheduled" depends on today's date, which drifts between snapshot refreshes, the dashboard recomputes it client-side from each row's own date instead of trusting the baked-in value.

**Note:** `graveyard_all.json` doesn't exist in the repo yet — it needs to be generated for real by either running `python3 graveyard.py` locally, or by triggering the new workflow (works automatically once merged, or manually via "Run workflow" now). Until then `graveyard.html` will show a "run graveyard.py" error message rather than data — this is intentional; no fabricated data was committed.

## 2. Anime.js animation engine

Replaced every hand-rolled animation (CSS `@keyframes` + manual `requestAnimationFrame` loops) with [Anime.js](https://animejs.com/) v3.2.1, loaded from cdnjs, across both `graveyard.html` and `changelog.html`:

- Stat count-up, table-row entrance, lifespan-bar growth, the "scheduled" badge pulse, and the loading spinner all now run through `anime()`.
- New: a FLIP-style reorder animation on sort/filter (rows animate to their new position instead of jumping), an `anime.timeline()` sequencing the initial page reveal, and a small "pop" on chip click.
- **Progressive enhancement:** if the CDN is blocked/unreachable, `HAS_ANIME` is `false`, `<html>` gets a `.no-anime` class, and both pages still work correctly — a small CSS fallback keeps the spinner/pulse going, everything else just skips straight to its final state.
- Fixed a subtle leak: the "scheduled" badge's DOM node is recreated every render, so its `loop:true` pulse animation is explicitly paused-and-replaced each time instead of accumulating orphaned infinite loops while typing in the search box.

## Testing
This sandbox's network policy blocks both `jsdelivr.net` and `cdnjs.cloudflare.com`, so I couldn't test against the real upstream data or the real Anime.js library directly. Verified instead with:
- A local mock `graveyard_all.json`/`.meta.json` snapshot server — confirmed load, filtering, sorting, chip toggling, status recompute, and the missing-file error path all work.
- A minimal functional stub replicating Anime.js's API surface (`anime()`, `.set()`, `.stagger()`, `.timeline()`) — confirmed no console errors, correct final states after count-up/sort/filter/chip-toggle, and no orphaned-animation accumulation from rapid search typing.

Both should get a quick visual check against the real library/data once merged, since the stub can't confirm the animations actually *look* good — only that the calling code is correct.

author: larkooo
body:
## The bug

`mimi update` runs `git reset --hard origin/master` against **whatever branch the deploy checkout happens to be on** — and that checkout is almost never `master`.

`mimi audit` creates `mimi/audit-YYYY-MM-DD`, commits, pushes, opens a PR, and never switches back. The deploy repo on the box is sitting on `mimi/audit-2026-08-30` as I write this:

```
$ git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD
mimi/audit-2026-08-30
```

So the next `mimi update` resets *that branch* to master.

### 1. It rewrites the audit branch and eats uncommitted work

`git reset --hard` moves the current branch ref. The pushed remote branch survives (so open PRs are safe), but the local branch is silently destroyed, and any hand-edit in the deploy tree is discarded with no prompt.

### 2. It computes the rebuild decision from the wrong baseline

This is the part that actually misbehaves in production. `before` is read from `HEAD` — the audit branch tip — so:

```rust
let dashboard_changed = git_files_changed(&repo, &before, &after)...
let rust_changed      = git_files_changed(&repo, &before, &after)...
```

...diffs *the audit branch* against `origin/master`, rather than the deployed master commit against `origin/master`. The diff therefore includes the audit's own changes **in reverse**.

Reproduced on a scratch repo — deployed master, an upstream **dashboard-only** push, and an audit branch that touched `src/`:

```
OLD (before = HEAD on audit branch):
   dashboard/app.tsx
   src/main.rs        <-- phantom: the audit's own commit being reverted
NEW (before = master):
   dashboard/app.tsx
```

That phantom `src/` entry triggers a pointless `cargo build --release` + `sudo install` of a binary identical to the one already deployed. The inverse also holds: the two error terms can cancel and hide a genuine upstream change, **skipping a rebuild that was needed** — an update that reports success while deploying nothing.

## The fix

- Abort if tracked files are dirty, printing the porcelain status, instead of letting `reset --hard` discard them. Untracked files are deliberately excluded (`--untracked-files=no`) since `reset --hard` leaves those alone anyway — aborting on a stray file would be needlessly strict.
- Fetch, then switch to `master` before reading `before`, so the comparison is deployed-master → origin/master.
- Fall back to `git checkout -B master origin/master` if there is no local `master` branch (detached HEAD, fresh single-branch clone).

Audit branches are now left untouched.

## Why this matters for Mimi

`mimi update` is how every other improvement reaches the running system. When it silently skips a rebuild, a merged fix never actually deploys and the failure is invisible — the command still prints `Update complete`. It also means the nightly audit and the nightly update stopped stepping on each other: audit leaves a branch behind, update no longer eats it.

## How to test

```sh
cargo build --release
```

Behaviour, verified on a throwaway repo:

```sh
# 1. Parked on an audit branch -> switches to master, branch ref preserved
git checkout -b mimi/audit-test && git commit --allow-empty -m "audit change"
TIP=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
mimi update
git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD          # master
git rev-parse mimi/audit-test            # still $TIP (previously rewritten to master)

# 2. Dirty tracked file -> aborts instead of discarding
echo mutated >> src/main.rs
mimi update                              # Error: ... has uncommitted changes — refusing to reset

# 3. Untracked file only -> proceeds (reset --hard would not have touched it)
git checkout src/main.rs && touch stray.txt
mimi update                              # runs normally

# 4. No local master -> recovers via checkout -B
git checkout --detach && git branch -D master
mimi update                              # lands on master
```

Checked against the open queue first per `CLAUDE.md` — the existing `mimi update` PRs cover service restarts (#110, #98) and bun-vs-npm (#101, #90); #103 makes `mimi audit` sync to `origin/master` before starting. None touch the branch/dirty-tree handling here.

author: kengos
body:
The two items the リレー3 review of #203 raised and could not fix there.

## The picker offered five locales that cannot render

`defaults.locale` is the render fallback the CLI, MCP and FFI hosts read —
an ENGINE axis. The picker was listing the Designer's CHROME languages,
five of which the engine has no data for:

- `canonical_id` matches case-insensitively, then on a unique **bare-language**
  prefix requiring `c.len() > id.len()`. `en-GB` and `en-US` are the same
  length, so it never fires.
- No `en-gb.yml` ships, so `load_locale_pack` returns `LocaleNotFound`.

A document set to English (UK) therefore failed to render anywhere outside
the Designer — while this panel described it confidently, because
`engineLocaleFor` swapped the tag to `en-US` before asking.

Now the picker offers the engine-resolvable set (the registry's
`engineLocale` values, deduped — five collapse onto `en-US` — plus
`ENGINE_ONLY_LOCALES`). `ComboField` keeps free entry, so a document that
already carries `en-GB` still opens and still shows it; only the offered
list narrowed.

Deleting the substitution has a second effect worth naming: the panel's own
rule — "a tag the engine cannot resolve leaves it explaining nothing" — is
true again, without the exception #204 had to write into three docs. Those
notes are reverted.

The engine *does* widen a bare `ja` → `ja-JP` (its only aliasing), and a
file may carry any string, so a new line names the pack when it is not the
tag on screen. One i18n key, all six catalogs. It is also the first consumer
of `LocaleFacts.id`, which #203 shipped unread.

## The amount could contradict the field above it

The freshness guard was `answer.tag === tag`. On a currency edit the tag is
unchanged, so the previous answer kept rendering — a JPY amount sitting
directly under a Currency field reading `USD`. The canvas's last-good
analogy does not hold when the control contradicting the value is beside it.

The guard now covers the currency inputs as well. Deliberately NOT the whole
catalog `key`: that is the entire `defaults:`/`formats:` slice, so gating on
it would blank the line on a font-size or line-height commit that cannot
change it. A test pins both directions.

## Gates

`gui:verify` green locally (no `.rs` in this diff). Not re-driven in a
browser: the change is a list shape and one string, both pinned at the DOM
by `DocumentDefaults.test.tsx`, over a surface #203's live pass already
exercised end to end.

author: ranquild
body:
The one-shot encryption backfills (e.g. `EncryptNotificationAndPulseChannelDetails`) get deterministically undone by a single boot of any pre-encryption build:

1. The old build's `seed-notification!` (every boot) reads the seeded recipients through its own `mi/transform-json`; the encrypted `details` string isn't JSON, so it comes back as a raw ciphertext string.
2. `serialize-notification existing ≠ serialize-notification desired`, so seeding decides `:replace`.
3. It deletes and re-creates the rows through the old plaintext transforms — plaintext `details` again, and the next boot of the current build fails its strict read.

author: yourmoln
body:
## 问题与实现说明

首页“位置/动态”标签栏原本作为 headerContent 分别注入 HorizontalPager 的两个页面，并成为各自 LazyColumn 的首项。左右拖动时，标签栏处在页面坐标系内，因此会跟随页面内容横向移动。

本 PR 将 HomeTabRow 提升为 HomeDestinationContent 中唯一的共享标签栏，HorizontalPager 只占据其下方剩余空间并仅承载页面内容。同时：

- 保留每页 SaveableStateProvider，位置页与动态页的页面状态仍独立保存。
- 保留基于 settledPage 的当前页判断，toPagerTop 只影响稳定选中的页面。
- 保留动态页稳定进入后再创建时间线的懒加载行为。
- 保留动态页底部导航 padding 与位置页 LocalSharedSuffixKey 作用域。
- 收紧位置页入口，首页不再向位置页注入横向分页标题。

## 验证命令

~~~text
.\gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileKotlinDesktop
.\gradlew.bat :composeApp:desktopTest --tests "io.github.vrcmteam.vrcm.presentation.screens.home.HomeShellStateTest" --tests "io.github.vrcmteam.vrcm.presentation.screens.home.HomeMeetupCardGestureTest"
git diff --check
~~~

验证结果：Desktop 编译成功；HomeShellStateTest 3 项与 HomeMeetupCardGestureTest 1 项全部通过；git diff --check 无空白错误。编译仅输出仓库既有弃用与 expect/actual 警告。

## 代码流程图

~~~mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[HomeDestinationContent] --> B[唯一共享 HomeTabRow]
    A --> C[HorizontalPager]
    B -->|点击标签| D[animateScrollToTab]
    B -->|重复点击| E[SharedFlowCentre.toPagerTop]
    C --> F[Location 页面内容]
    C --> G[Activity 页面内容]
    F -->|settledPage 为 Location| H[位置列表响应回顶]
    G -->|settledPage 为 Activity| I[动态列表响应回顶]
    C --> J[SaveableStateProvider 按页保存状态]
~~~

## 实现假设清单

- [x] “位置/动态”属于两个首页页面共用的导航标签，应只渲染一个实例。
- [x] 左右滑动仍切换页面，但共享标签栏不参与 HorizontalPager 的横向位移。
- [x] 当前页以 settledPage 为准，拖动未稳定时不应让非当前页响应回顶。
- [x] 动态时间线继续在首次稳定进入动态页后创建，避免恢复预加载开销。
- [x] 标签栏提升到 Pager 外后固定在首页内容顶部，页面内部继续各自管理纵向内容。

## 未验证风险

- 未在登录后的 Android、iOS 与 Desktop 实际数据页面进行手势视觉回归。
- 未执行 Android/iOS 平台打包；本次共享 Compose 布局以 Desktop 编译与相关现有测试验证。
- 纯视觉位移未添加像素级或 Compose UI 断言，窄窗口、大字体及快速往返拖动仍需人工确认。

Corrections after reading the OpenCode loader source (packages/opencode/src/plugin/):

- **Bare package spec** — `@khaosoigai/oc-context-grid`, not `…/tui`: the TUI loader reads `exports["./tui"]` from the installed package's manifest itself (`resolvePackageEntrypoint`), and a subpath spec parses as a directory-type npm spec (`npm-package-arg`) so it would fail to install.
- **No `bun add`** — TUI plugins named in `tui.json` are auto-installed on demand into opencode's cache (`~/.cache/opencode/packages/`), same as server plugins. Restores the global-config wording since resolution doesn't depend on project `node_modules`.

body:
## Contexte

En vérifiant en conditions réelles le correctif du 409 sur `watchlist_alerts` (PR #88, run manuel `scan_shopify.yml`) : le run a bien détecté 4 bonnes affaires et ne contient **plus** la ligne d'erreur 409 qui apparaissait avant le fix — mais impossible de confirmer directement la ligne de succès `[Supabase] N alerte(s) watchlist enregistrée(s)` dans les logs, alors que le code s'exécutait sans erreur.

## Le trou trouvé

Seul `main.py` appelait `logging.basicConfig()`. Les 6 autres orchestrateurs CLI (`scan_boutique.py`, `scan_boutique_prestashop.py`, `scan_boutique_woocommerce.py`, `scan_precommandes.py`, `scan_precommandes_generique.py`, `scan_precommandes_philibert.py`) ne configuraient jamais le logger racine — donc tous les `log.info()` émis par `connecteur_supabase.py` / `connecteur_supabase_precoms.py` / `notifications_saas.py` / `memoire_supabase.py` quand ils sont appelés depuis ces scripts restaient **invisibles** dans les logs GitHub Actions. Seuls les `log.warning()`/`log.error()` apparaissaient (via le handler de secours par défaut de Python). Ce trou touchait toutes les lignes de succès du système, pas seulement le cas qui l'a révélé.

body:
## Summary
- `isMinifyEnabled = true` was already set for `release`, but `app/proguard-rules.pro` had blanket `-keep` rules for `android.**`, `androidx.**`, and individually for `androidx.lifecycle`, `androidx.activity`, `androidx.compose.**`, `androidx.ui.**`, `androidx.material3`, `androidx.navigation`, `androidx.compose.animation` — these exempted almost all AndroidX/Compose bytecode (the largest chunk of a Compose app) from shrinking and obfuscation, making R8 mostly cosmetic.
- Those AndroidX/Compose/Firebase artifacts already ship their own `consumer-rules.pro` inside their AARs, which AGP merges automatically — the app-level overrides were pure redundancy, not a safety net.
- Same redundant pattern removed from `core/ui/consumer-rules.pro` (`androidx.compose.ui.**`, `androidx.compose.material3.**`).
- Dropped a dead rule referencing a `com.generativeai` package that isn't a project dependency, and `-overloadaggressively` (a legacy ProGuard flag R8 doesn't act on).
- Added `-keepattributes SourceFile,LineNumberTable` + `-renamesourcefileattribute SourceFile`: crash stack traces stay symbolicated via the uploaded `mapping.txt` (Crashlytics), but the real source file name is stripped from the shipped APK — standard R8 hardening for both perf (smaller mapping) and security (less info leakage).

## Scope / what's intentionally NOT in this PR
Every feature/core module's own `consumer-rules.pro` still has a blanket `-keep class br.com.brunocarvalhs.<module>.** { *; }`, so the app's own business-logic code is still fully exempt from shrinking/obfuscation. Untangling that is higher blast-radius (needs a per-module reflection audit — Hilt codegen, Room, custom multibinding, etc. — plus full manual QA on an installed obfuscated release build) and wasn't attempted here since this environment has no adb/emulator to verify runtime behavior after obfuscation. Flagging as a natural follow-up.

## Test plan
- [x] `./gradlew :app:assembleRelease` locally — `:app:minifyReleaseWithR8` completes successfully; build only fails afterward at `packageRelease` due to missing local signing secrets (`KEYSTORE_PASSWORD` etc. are CI-only secrets, expected in a local run).
- [ ] Install the CI-built, signed release APK on a device and run the full manual QA pass (nav flows, Compose animations, biometric, chat/Room, Firestore) to confirm nothing relied on the removed AndroidX/Compose keeps.
- [ ] Compare APK size before/after in the build artifacts.

author: windwang2
body:
# Goal

Complete Paleo Workbench P2 convergence on top of the latest main (`e1622496`): unified CPU/RAM/VRAM/IO resource governance, a stable capability Provider SDK, and a Geological Harness for AI/Agent integration. All three legs verified end-to-end on production paths.

> Note: this branch bumps the `geo-viz-engine` submodule to `feat/p2-l1-global-budget-setter` (one small commit: public `set_global_budget()`/`global_stats()` on the RamSliceCache shared ledger — pushed to that repo).

## P2-A — Global Resource Governance (ADR 0064)

- **One governor over the existing single authorities** (TaskScheduler stays the one heavy queue, ResourceBudget the one policy object): admission control (`try_admit` for the scheduler, `admit`+`ResourceExhausted` for direct callers), reservations/leases, pressure states (NORMAL/PRESSURE/CRITICAL via a rate-limited, non-blocking `MemoryPressureMonitor` with cache-relief evictables), pressure-scaled CPU/IO allowances.
- **TaskScheduler**: admission hook (lease protocol, released on every terminal path), bounded priority aging (+5/5s, cap +50 — background never starves, interactive never preempts), strict interactive lane (background I/O stays at concurrency 1 per #1081), atomic claims, cancel-window closure, budget-derived lane niceness.
- **The four parallelism knobs now ask the governor** (transcode workers, factor-prepare workers, ONNX intra-op threads, scanner pool); the transcode in-flight window derives from `streaming_buffer_bytes`; the L1 slice ledger budget is wired through the submodule setter.
- **Telemetry**: one `runtime.snapshot()` over scheduler/governor/pressure/caches (existing counters aggregated — no new observability platform). Cancellation adapters unify the three existing token dialects.
- Stable config path: `PALEO_BUDGET_RAM_GB` + new `PALEO_BUDGET_CORES` / `PALEO_IO_SLOTS` / `PALEO_BACKGROUND_NICE`, plus the runtime `configure_runtime_budget` API.

## P2-B — Provider SDK (ADR 0065, ADR 0055 track P.REG)

- `ProviderDescriptor` (structured metadata + JSON-schema parameters + typed input/output names + ResourceProfile + cancel/resume/deterministic/threading) with structural validation — never signature guessing.
- Typed refs (`WellRef`, `SeismicVolumeRef`, `MapDocumentRef`, `FactorDatasetRef`, `PathRef`, …) + catalog `DataVersionRef` reuse; no anonymous dicts.
- Registry with duplicate/version detection, quarantine isolation (one bad provider never blocks boot), opt-in entry-point discovery (`PALEO_PROVIDER_ENTRY_POINTS=1`) — no directory scanning.
- Guarded execution: schema validation → typed-input check → governor admission → DataRun provenance (begin/complete/fail) → `ProviderResult`.
- **Built-ins wrap production seams**: `interpolation.kriging` / `interpolation.idw`, `seismic.attribute.c3` (per `KERNELS` entry, banded resumable zarr), `inference.tiled_onnx` (delegates to the existing `TiledOnnxProvider` — model registry/promote gates untouched), `export.map_product` (canvas/export parity renderer), `viz.map_render.fallback|qgis` (executable, probe-honest).

## P2-C — Geological Agent Harness (ADR 0066)

- `ActionSpec` is the single source: runtime validation, agent tool schemas (OpenAI/Gemini shape) and docs all derive from it — no hand-written second schema anywhere.
- Guarded executor: lookup → schema validation → permission gate (READ/COMPUTE default; WRITE via `from_app` app sessions; DESTRUCTIVE refused at registration) → context gate → governor admission → handler/provider → **scientific + map verification** → `ActionResult` (fail-closed: verification FAIL never claims success).
- 25 coarse-grained actions across workspace(5)/well(5)/seismic(3)/map(8)/geology(3)/workflow(1). Agents never drive UI, never touch SQLite, never write raw paths: export/volume paths are workspace-confined (post-resolution containment — traversal-proof) and never overwrite.
- Provenance: data writes create DataRun + versions (factor maps validate the grid *before* committing and return the version identity; attribute stores register as DERIVED with lineage).
- Vendor-agnostic LLM seam: `ToolSource`/`ChatModel` protocols + `HarnessToolSource`; zero vendor clients.
- Map validation hook (layers/extent/CRS/composition/export-readiness) and scientific validation (all-NaN FAIL, coverage, axis monotonicity, extent/CRS) close the loop.

## Architecture

```
LLM / Agent (external, ToolSource/ChatModel protocols)
  → HarnessExecutor (validate → permissions → context → admission → execute → verify)
  → ActionRegistry (25 ActionSpec; tool schemas derived 1:1)
  → Domain services / Provider SDK (schema → typed inputs → admission → DataRun)
  → DataCatalogService (single write authority) / open_volume / engines / renderers
Shared: TaskScheduler (1 heavy + 1 interactive lane) · ResourceGovernor ·
        MemoryPressureMonitor · VramTextureCache · RamSliceCache ledger ·
        SelectionContext · LayerRegistry · Well Engine · QGIS Renderer · 3D Scene
```
No second authorities created (one scheduler, one budget, one catalog, one layer truth, one selection bus).

## Performance (measured, this host — `benchmarks/p2_resource_governance_benchmark.py`)

| scenario | measured | budget |
|---|---|---|
| 100k catalog search + background verify | interactive queue delay p99 **0.61 ms**; verify 120/120 done | <50 ms ✅ |
| transcode + interactive slice browsing | slice p95 0.05→0.19 ms (tiny volume, sub-ms) | no meaningful degradation ✅ |
| attribute compute + interactive render | render queue delay p99 **0.50 ms** | <50 ms ✅ |
| large export (200k rows) + queries | interactive dispatch p99 **30.29 ms** | <50 ms ✅ |
| RAM/VRAM pressure | shed/evict/bounded/recover/no-deadlock 8/8 | all ✅ |
| harness READ dispatch (incl. context snapshot) | p99 **0.137 ms** | <10 ms ✅ |
| registry lookup | 10k lookups <200 ms (~O(1)) | ✅ |

Known, documented: SQLite index reads show a 20–60 ms tail under heavy concurrent file IO — reproduces with no governance (pre-existing catalog behaviour, recorded as a catalog-domain follow-up).

## Tests

Local full suite (`QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen`, this worktree's geoviz submodule): **all green except 2 environment-limited files** (`test_native_backend::map_edit_core`, `test_welllog_engine_native_integration`) which require built optional C++ extensions and **fail identically on clean main** (pre-existing, verified by side-by-side runs). New P2 coverage: 100 tests across `test_resource_governance.py` (30), `test_provider_sdk.py` (31), `test_harness_core.py` (26+), `tests/e2e/test_harness_scenarios.py` (8) — including adversarial cases (duplicate ids, invalid schemas, quarantined providers, pressure shedding, path-traversal refusals, claim atomicity).

**Online CI/CD was intentionally not used or awaited as the completion gate** (local regression + benchmarks + review served as the gate), per this phase's requirements.

## Review

Matt code-review (fixed point `origin/main`), three rounds (two-axis parallel sub-agents + verification):
round 1 → 6 HIGH/9 MEDIUM fixed; round 2 → 1 HIGH (relative-path traversal)/2 MEDIUM fixed; round 3 → all VERIFIED.

**BLOCKER: 0 — HIGH: 0**

## End-to-End Scenarios

- [x] well location map (labels + legend/scale/north/title + validation PASS)
- [x] current well curves (W23 → GR/RT/AC display + template)
- [x] seismic coherence (open_volume → provider → DERIVED registered → lineage)
- [x] kriging factor map + composition (validate-before-commit, version identity returned)
- [x] map product export (validation gate → production renderer → catalog OUTPUT version)

## Known Limitations (honest)

- Interpretation-creation actions for wells/horizons (`well.create_interpretation`, `seismic.create_horizon/export_interpretation`) are not registered: their draft/version lifecycles are currently UI-adjacent; the harness exposes reads + the fault-draft write (`geology.create_interpretation`) until headless commit semantics are defined for those lifecycles.
- `workflow.run_step` not regist

author: caseyblaze
body:
## Problem

`cloud-sql-proxy` reads Application Default Credentials once at startup and holds the refresh token in memory for the life of the process. It never re-reads the file and has no reload signal.

So after `gcloud auth application-default login`, a proxy that is already running keeps using the old token — it has to be stopped and started by hand before the new credentials take effect. That was a daily chore.

Signing in still needs a human (Google opens a browser). What this removes is the `csql stop` / `csql start` afterwards.

## What's added

| Command | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `csql restart [--env ENV]` | stop then start |
| `csql login` | runs `gcloud auth application-default login`, then restarts exactly the environments that were running — ones deliberately left stopped stay stopped |
| `csql watch enable\|disable\|status` | launchd agent watching the credentials file; running proxies restart on their own within seconds, however you re-authenticated |

`csql status` gains an auth summary and flags an environment that started before the current credentials as `running (old auth)`, with the command to fix it:

```
Auth:  credentials updated 2026-08-31 11:06 (authorized_user, quota project my-project)
       ! dev started before that — run 'csql restart --env dev'
Watch: enabled (proxies restart automatically when credentials change)
```

The watcher acts only when the file's *contents* change (SHA-256 compare), so redundant writes and the fallback poll cost nothing, and it restarts only environments running at that moment.

## launchd details this depends on

- **`AbandonProcessGroup`** — without it launchd kills the `cloud-sql-proxy` processes `auth-sync` just started, the moment `auth-sync` itself exits.
- **`StartInterval` fallback poll** — a kqueue `WatchPaths` watch can be lost when the watched file is replaced by rename, which is exactly how gcloud writes it. `auth-sync` is a no-op when nothing changed, so polling is cheap insurance.
- **TCC guard** — macOS blocks launchd from executing anything inside `~/Documents`, `~/Desktop` or `~/Downloads`; the job dies with `Operation not permitted` on every wake-up, visible only in the watch log. `watch enable` refuses to install from those paths rather than let it fail quietly.
- **`CLOUDSDK_CONFIG` passthrough** — a launchd job inherits nothing from the shell, so the variable deciding which credentials file is watched is carried into the plist.

## Testing

Sandboxed `HOME` with a stub proxy:
- restarts only running environments (a stopped one stayed stopped)
- no-op when the credentials hash is unchanged
- half-written credentials file ignored, and the following complete write does restart

Real launchd, end to end: agent fired ~12s after the credentials file changed, restarted only the running environment, and the new proxy survived the job exiting (reparented to PID 1). Teardown left no agent, plist or stray process.

The first end-to-end run is what surfaced the TCC restriction — it failed from a `~/Documents` checkout before passing from an unprotected path.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Two commits: a debugging pass, then filling in the empty `agent/`, `computer/`, `voice/` modules and `config.py`.

### Bugs fixed

1. **"Open Notepad" / "Open Calculator" never worked.** `open_application` did `if path.endswith(".exe"): if os.path.exists(path)` — for bare names like `notepad.exe` that resolves relative to the CWD, so every candidate failed and it printed "Could not find notepad". `resolve_executable()` now checks `os.path.exists` only for absolute paths and falls back to `shutil.which` (plus `os.startfile` for protocol targets like `ms-settings:`).
2. **"Open Google" / "Open YouTube" tried to launch an app**, because `startswith("open ")` was tested before the website branch, making the `open google` entry unreachable. Websites are matched first.
3. **Whisper's trailing punctuation broke exact matches** — transcriptions arrive as `"Click."`, `"Press Enter."`, which matched none of the `command in [...]` branches. `normalize()` strips `.,!?;:`.
4. **`type` lost capitalization**: the text was lowercased before typing, so "Type Hello World" typed `hello world`.
5. **Hardcoded `MICROPHONE_DEVICE = 1`** crashed wherever device 1 isn't an input. Defaults to the system device, overridable via `VOICE_AI_MIC_DEVICE`; a `PortAudioError` now prints `sd.query_devices()` instead of killing the process.
6. **No `if __name__ == "__main__"` anywhere**: importing `main.py` loaded Whisper and started recording; `voice.py` built `OpenAI(api_key=None)` at import, which raises when the key is unset.

### Structure

```
main.py                    listen -> parse -> act loop
config.py                  env-overridable settings + app/website tables
agent/brain.py             parse_command(text) -> Intent(action, value)
agent/tools.py             action -> callable registry, execute(intent)
computer/{applications,keyboard,mouse}.py
voice/{speech_to_text,text_to_speech}.py
scripts/                   the old one-off scripts (mic check, OpenAI API check)
tests/test_brain.py        10 unit tests, stdlib unittest
```

The key design point: `agent/brain.py` imports nothing but `config`, so parsing is pure and testable without a microphone or a screen — `agent/tools.py` imports `computer.*` lazily inside `build_tools()`.

```python
parse_command("Open Google.")     # Intent("open_website", "https://www.google.com")
parse_command("Type Hello World") # Intent("type_text", "Hello World")
tools.execute(intent, registry)   # False only for Intent("exit")
```

author: emersonian
body:
Found while verifying the `v0.1.0` downloads: the shipped `.app` reported `CFBundleShortVersionString = 0.0.1` and the shipped `.deb` reported `Version: 0.0.1`.

Cause: `crates/zkv/tauri.conf.json` pinned `"version": "0.0.1"` and no version-bump commit has ever touched that file - it has read `0.0.1` since rc1. Artifact *filenames* were always correct (they come from the workflow's `VERSION`), so this only ever showed up inside the bundles. The `.deb` is the one that matters: every release declaring the same version means apt will not upgrade one package over another.

Removing the key makes Tauri fall back to the app crate's `Cargo.toml` version, which is already the value `setup` checks against the tag - so there is no second place to remember on the next bump.

Verified by a `workflow_dispatch` dry run on this branch (builds all nine jobs, publishes nothing): the resulting `.app` and `.deb` both report `0.1.0`.

Note for a future release-candidate tag: a prerelease suffix such as `0.1.1-rc1` flows into the bundlers now instead of being masked by the pinned `0.0.1`, so the first rc-versioned tag after this should be dry-run before tagging.

author: cirras
body:
This PR fixes an obscure bug related to the 2-pass semantic analysis we're doing where we build the symbol table in one pass, throw away ASTs as we go, and re-parse source files (reassociating symbol information) in a second pass.

For symbol reassociation purposes, we were registering declarations, occurences, and scopes against token indices as if they were unique at the node level. They're not.

This led to some tricky situations where scopes in particular would be incorrectly attributed to the wrong nodes. This bug was masked very well because most name resolution occurs during symbol table construction.

The problem came about after symbol reassociation. In the analysis phase, on-demand name resolution occurs during expression type resolution. Any analysis rule calling `ExpressionNode::getType` was potentially impacted.

author: lucasvil4r
body:
Duas falhas que só aparecem **quando outra pessoa usa os scripts**.

## 1. As pipelines do time podiam ser sequestradas em silêncio

Cada membro tem a sua conta do Learner Lab, logo o seu bucket de state — os ambientes são independentes e não se atrapalham. Mas os **quatro repositórios da organização são compartilhados**, e é neles que vive a variável `TF_STATE_BUCKET`.

O `sobe-tudo.sh` sobrescrevia essa variável sem perguntar. Se dois membros rodassem, **o segundo apontaria as pipelines dos quatro repositórios para a conta dele** — e os merges de todo o time passariam a aplicar no ambiente de uma pessoa só. Sem erro nenhum, e sem ninguém perceber.

Agora ele só sobrescreve quando o valor já é o mesmo ou quando não há valor. Se outra conta for a dona:

```text
As pipelines apontam para OUTRA conta.
  atual:  ...4331
  a sua:  ...6131
Nao mexi. Seu ambiente sobe normalmente, mas os merges do time
continuam aplicando na conta de quem configurou antes.
```

O ambiente da pessoa sobe do mesmo jeito. Para assumir de propósito, `--assumir-pipelines`.

O `renova-secrets.sh` **continua sobrescrevendo sempre** — é o comportamento certo para quem é dono das pipelines, e um tiro no pé para quem não é. A documentação passa a dizer isso com todas as letras.

## 2. A tabela de etapas descrevia a ordem antiga

Ela ainda mostrava **sete** etapas com a rede antes das Lambdas — exatamente a ordem que causou o `ResourceNotFoundException` e que foi corrigida em tech-challenge-grupo-160/tech-challenge-oficina-mecanica#101.

Quem lesse formaria o modelo mental errado sobre a dependência mais delicada do fluxo.

Agora são **oito**, na ordem real, e as duas posições que não são preferência estão explicadas: as funções antes da rede, e o banco depois dela.

## Tipo de mudanca

- [x] fix: correção de bug
- [x] docs: documentação

## Tabela de parametros

Some junto a tabela completa dos **dez** argumentos aceitos pelos dois scripts, que só existiam no cabeçalho de cada um. Verifiquei um a um contra o `case` de parsing — todos documentados, nenhum documentado a mais.

## Como testar

```bash
bash scripts/sobe-tudo.sh --help
```

```bash
bash scripts/derruba-tudo.sh --so-conferir
```

`bash -n` passa nos dois.

Refs tech-challenge-grupo-160/tech-challenge-oficina-mecanica#84

author: aryu-ru
body:
### PR Information

- Fixed CVE-2025-29927

The second http block (the `X-Middleware-Subrequest` bypass request) has two matchers, a negative
matcher for WAF block pages and a `status: 200` check. It sets no `matchers-condition`, so nuclei falls
back to `or`, and either matcher alone is enough to satisfy the block:

- On a **patched** host the bypass header is ignored and `/` still answers `307`. The status matcher is
  false, but the body has no WAF strings so the negative matcher is true → block matches.
- On a **WAF block page** the body *is* a block page so the negative matcher is false, but the page is
  served with `200` → block matches.

`base_check()` is `http(1) && http(2)`, so it returns true in both cases and the template reports
critical. The negative matcher added in #16870 never actually constrained anything, because the
`status: 200` matcher can satisfy the `or` on its own.

Block 5 of the same template already expresses these exact two conditions as a single dsl matcher with
`condition: and`, so the intended semantics are unambiguous:

```yaml
      - type: dsl
        dsl:
          - "status_code == 200"
          - "!contains_any(to_lower(body), 'request rejected', 'your support id', 'access denied', 'request blocked')"
        condition: and
```

This restores the pre-#16870 behaviour of block 2 while keeping the WAF negative matcher effective.
The change only tightens the matcher, so it cannot introduce false negatives on a host that was
previously detected through this block.

Closes #17019. Also fixes #16782, which was closed as completed but still reproduces on current main.

- References:
  - https://github.com/projectdiscovery/nuclei-templates/issues/17019
  - https://github.com/projectdiscovery/nuclei-templates/issues/16782
  - https://github.com/projectdiscovery/nuclei-templates/pull/16870
  - https://zhero-web-sec.github.io/research-and-things/nextjs-and-the-corrupt-middleware
  - https://github.com/vercel/next.js/security/advisories/GHSA-f82v-jwr5-mffw

### Template validation

- [x] Validated with a host running a vulnerable version and/or configuration (True Positive)
- [x] Validated with a host running a patched version and/or configuration (avoid False Positive)

#### Additional Details

Four local `http.server` targets on 127.0.0.1, nuclei v3.8.0. All four answer `/` with
`307` + `x-nextjs-redirect` so `http(1)` passes on every one of them:

| port | scenario | bypass request returns |
|--|--|--|
| 19401 | patched, middleware used for i18n locale redirect (#17019) | `307`, header ignored |
| 19402 | vulnerable, middleware used as an auth gate | `200` + admin page |
| 19403 | patched, behind a WAF returning a block page (#16782) | `200` + "Request Rejected" |
| 19404 | vulnerable, middleware used for i18n locale redirect | `200` + home page |

Current template on the patched i18n host. Note that the bypass request answers `307`, and the match
is attributed to `word-1`, the negative matcher, firing on its own:

```
$ nuclei -t http/cves/2025/CVE-2025-29927.yaml -u http://127.0.0.1:19401 -debug-resp -ms
[DBG] [CVE-2025-29927] Dumped HTTP response http://127.0.0.1:19401
HTTP/1.1 307 Temporary Redirect
Content-Type: text/html
Location: /en-US/
X-Nextjs-Redirect: /en-US/
Content-Length: 0

[CVE-2025-29927:word-1] [http] [critical] http://127.0.0.1:19401
[INF] Scan completed in 8.379558ms. 1 matches found.
```

Current template on the WAF host. This is the mirror image: `status-2` fires on its own even though
the body is the block page the negative matcher was added to catch:

```
$ nuclei -t http/cves/2025/CVE-2025-29927.yaml -u http://127.0.0.1:19403 -debug-resp -ms
[DBG] [CVE-2025-29927] Dumped HTTP response http://127.0.0.1:19403
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Length: 190
Content-Type: text/html

<html>
<head>
<title>Request Rejected</title>
</head>
<body>
The requested URL was rejected.
Please consult with your administrator.
Your support ID is: <redacted>
</body>
</html>

[CVE-2025-29927:status-2] [http] [critical] http://127.0.0.1:19403
[INF] Scan completed in 2.180756ms. 1 matches found.
```

Before and after, all four targets:

```
                                          before      after
patched, i18n redirect      (19401)       MATCH       no match
vulnerable, auth gate       (19402)       MATCH       MATCH
patched, WAF block page     (19403)       MATCH       no match
vulnerable, i18n redirect   (19404)       MATCH       MATCH
```

```
$ nuclei -t http/cves/2025/CVE-2025-29927.yaml -u http://127.0.0.1:19401
[INF] Scan completed in 5.714047ms. 0 matches found.

$ nuclei -t http/cves/2025/CVE-2025-29927.yaml -u http://127.0.0.1:19403
[INF] Scan completed in 5.889357ms. 0 matches found.

$ nuclei -t http/cves/2025/CVE-2025-29927.yaml -u http://127.0.0.1:19402
[CVE-2025-29927] [http] [critical] http://127.0.0.1:19402
[INF] Scan completed in 2.817774ms. 1 matches found.
```

Honeypot check, matching the CI weak-matcher job. No results before or after:

```
$ nuclei -duc -silent -u http://honey.scanme.sh -t http/cves/2025/CVE-2025-29927.yaml
$
```

`nuclei -validate` passes, and `yamllint -c .yamllint` on the changed file is clean.

One note on #17019: the reporter also suggested restricting `http(1)` to redirect targets matching
`login|signin|auth|unauthorized`. I deliberately did not do that. Target 19404 above is a genuinely
vulnerable host whose middleware only does locale routing. The bypass really works there, so it
should still be reported, and an auth-keyword filter would suppress it. The `or`/`and` bug is the part
that produces findings on hosts that are not vulnerable at all, and it is what this PR fixes.

The `# digest` line is dropped so the template is re-signed on merge.

author: lbartoszcze
body:
One defect shape, found nine times in nine subsystems in about twelve hours. Every instance is **a declaration checked against something narrower than the world**: the check passes, the declaration is self-consistent, and nothing compares it to what is actually there.

`docs/checks-that-measure-nothing.md` names each one with its file and PR, the property they share, what it cost, and what a check has to do to be worth having. Linked from the README nav so it is not a file only its author can find.

### The nine, in one line each

1. `FLEET_LABEL_PREFIX` — a label prefixed onto a name that already carried the prefix. The constant is also defined twice, in `src/deploy/service.rs:4538` and `src/deploy/local_install.rs:41`, which is the same disease.
2. Watermark read by `src/providers/local/disk_cleanup/mod.rs` and enforced against a different source than `src/deploy/host_gates.rs` reads.
3. `mirror_to_output_uri`, `src/providers/local/slots.rs:625` — qualified store path and bare key are both `String`, so callers guessed; 417 objects landed at `ecosystem/<ns>/ecosystem/<ns>/…` (#161, #169).
4. Replication "off" in config while a second, never-audited writer filled the replica to 48.5 GiB (#166, #168).
5. A publish loop that returned cleanly with one of six binaries stored (#163).
6. `src/cli/status.rs:96` — completed jobs printed under "extracted (awaiting upload)" (#175, still open).
7. `scripts/surface.py` + AutoVersion — the gate cannot see a tree change under an unchanged command surface. **Open, unfiled.**
8. `writer-transfer-check.yml` — the newest `stado-v*` tag taken as if it named published bytes (#173, #174).
9. `Presence`, `src/cli/storage.rs` — a failed `storage get` read as absence when it could equally have been a store that did not answer (#174).

### The price, concretely

- `stado/0.10.0/darwin-arm64` — 0 objects of 9
- `stado/0.11.0/darwin-arm64` — 4 of 9
- `stado/0.12.1/linux-amd64` — 2 of 9: `SHA256SUMS` and the manifest, no binaries

Immutable, so unrepairable — three version numbers gone. Separately, 55 pinned jobs refused for seven days by a process no report could name.

### Item 7 is left open on purpose

`dbb7e27e` and `375955a6` both legitimately declare `0.13.1`. They differ by a workflow fix and a chunked-upload change in `src/cli/storage.rs`, and both advertise the same 49 top-level commands, so autoversion reads the change as `internal` and the number stands for two different trees. A published `0.13.1` would name bytes that are not the bytes on `main`.

Fixing it changes the shared release rule (`lbartoszcze/AutoVersion`) and what every future PR must declare. That is a decision to take in daylight, not during an incident — so it is recorded as open rather than quietly patched.

### Verification

Docs and README only; no code paths touched. Every symbol and line number cited was checked present at this commit: `service.rs:4538`, `local_install.rs:41`, `slots.rs:625`, `status.rs:96` all match the quoted text, and `host_disk.rs`, `host_gates.rs` and `disk_cleanup/mod.rs` all exist. 763 words.

author: chitalian
body:
## Summary

Fixes the **Jawn TypeScript Check** failure on `main` (red since #5799, run [33325934013](https://github.com/Helicone/helicone/actions/runs/33325934013)).

```
AudioController.ts(110,23): error TS18047: 'inputMetadata' is possibly 'null'.
AudioController.ts(213,27): error TS2345: Argument of type 'string | null'
  is not assignable to parameter of type 'PathLike'.
```

## Root cause

Not a null-handling bug. Both flagged lines sit under correct guards — `if (inputMetadata)` and `if (pathToClean)`.

#5799 stubbed the endpoint by adding one line and leaving the old ~170-line implementation beneath it:

```ts
public async convertToWav(...): Promise<ConvertToWavResponse> {
  return { data: null, error: "dead endpoint" };   // added by #5799
  const { audioData } = body;                      // everything below is unreachable
  ...
}
```

**TypeScript does not apply control-flow narrowing inside unreachable code.** Once the early `return` made the body unreachable, every guard below it stopped narrowing, so the null checks failed. Minimal repro:

```ts
async function f(): Promise<number | undefined> {
  return undefined;                  // remove this line and it compiles
  let md: { streams: number[] } | null = null;
  try { md = await probe("x"); } catch {}
  if (md) { return md.streams.find(s => s > 1); }   // TS18047
}
```

Patching the null checks would have been treating the symptom — the dead code is the defect.

## Change

Remove the unreachable body, plus the imports and helpers only it used (`ffprobePromise`, `codecToInputFormat`, and the `ffmpeg`/`fs`/`os`/`path`/`stream`/`crypto`/`buffer` imports). The file goes 223 → 22 lines.

Route, decorators, request/response interfaces, and the stub's return value are all unchanged — **runtime behavior is identical**.

## Verification

- `yarn tsc` in `valhalla/jawn` — clean (was 2 errors)
- `yarn build` — succeeds, TSOA routes generate
- `convert-to-wav` still present in `src/tsoa-build/private/routes.ts`, so the endpoint stays registered and still returns the `dead endpoint` stub

## Note

`main` also has a failing **E2E Test Suite**, which is unrelated to this and not addressed here — it fails at "Health Check Workers" during infra setup, before any test runs:

```
✗ HELICONE_API worker failed to start on port 8788
ERROR failed inspecting image locally: No such image:
  cloudflare-dev/requestbodybuffercontainer:d3463440
```

That looks like a container-image/setup problem in the workflow rather than a code regression. Happy to dig in separately.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01LgqQ5FzR95gK4vSXC13smY

body:
## Summary

Port the no-padding grouped query-row work to PrimTS attention and MLA decode, covering both throughput-latency 1CTA and throughput 2CTA kernels.

## Features

- Flatten `(query token, query head)` into physical query rows without padding.
- Support fixed and packed Q layouts, including empty packed requests.
- Support non-power-of-two query-head counts such as H6, H12, H24, H48, and H96.
- Make context, FMHA decode, and MLA compiled callables batch-dynamic while keeping workspace sizing plan-specific.
- Reuse compiled topologies across batch sizes when their static scheduler/reducer topology is unchanged.

## Dispatch policy

- Select the 1CTA query tile from flat query geometry only.
- Derive split-KV from K-step work, resident capacity, and the shared 128-split implementation limit.
- Use 2CTA above the native M64 1CTA row boundary.
- Within M64, select 2CTA only when 1CTA requires split reduction and 2CTA can produce direct output.
- Remove dtype-, shape-, and measurement-specific crossover tables, power-of-two split rounding, and candidate scoring.

A few structural performance outliers are intentionally retained rather than adding case-specific dispatch exceptions.

## Correctness fixes

- Predicate partial flat-query tails and empty runtime tiles.
- Apply causal masking using logical query rows.
- Preserve scheduler progress for multiwave and empty-tile launches.
- Correct split-workspace addressing and runtime-K pruning.
- Keep producer and standalone-reducer topology/capacity consistent.
- Use the fixed qualified reference-reducer launch geometry.

author: suool
body:
Re-review of the PR #16/#17 optimizations surfaced one real reliability regression and one test gap. Both fixed here.

## 1. 🔴 Concurrent refresh reports false `source_failed` (the main fix)

**Verified root cause** (reproduced locally, not just inferred): the web refresh fans out **one IPC per project** (`AppShell.onRefresh` + the startup auto-refresh), so several `refresh_projects` tasks run at once on the async runtime. Every store write goes through `with_store_txn`, whose `store.lock` is taken **non-blockingly** (`try_lock_exclusive`) as a cross-process single-instance guard. Two overlapping in-process writers → the loser gets `StoreError::Io(WouldBlock)`, which `is_stale_race` does **not** classify as stale → `RefreshOutcome::SourceFailed` → the UI announces *'N projects could not be refreshed'* on a routine startup refresh of a multi-project store. A concurrent register/relink can hard-fail the same way.

A new regression test (8 synchronized `record_source_observation` writes) **fails 7/8 with `WouldBlock` without the fix**, and passes with it.

**Fix:** an in-process write gate (process-global `Mutex`); the app-level writers (`register_project`, `relink_primary_git_source`, `record_source_observation`, `apply_project_command`) route through a new `ensure_home_then_write` that holds the gate across both the `ensure_home` preamble and the write. This serializes only **this process's own** writers — the slow git observation still runs in parallel in the service layer, and the on-disk lock still fails fast for a genuine second process. The init/`ensure_home` path is untouched, so its fail-fast `WouldBlock` contract and single-instance test are unchanged; the gated functions never call one another, so the non-reentrant mutex cannot deadlock.

## 2. 🟡 Chinese-first default was untested through real components

Component tests render without an `I18nProvider`, so they only exercised the default context's **English fallback**. Added an integration test rendering `ProjectsIndex` under a live provider in each locale, asserting the visible copy switches — catches a component wrongly pinned to English.

## Verified locally this session
- Rust: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` all green (core lib now 91 with the new test).
- Web: `npm run build` + `vitest` green (138 tests, +2). No `dist/` change (only Rust + a test file).

author: sterlanyu
body:
Refs #1271. Found by testing on the onprem cluster — `case_7bad3d1ac083`.

## The symptom, after everything merged

> The submitted alert is currently marked `[FIRING:2]` for `FaultMavenSLABreached` … **The pasted alert does not include the firing timestamp**, affected request path, measured SLA value, threshold, or business impact…

Reporting the firing time as missing is precisely the outcome this line of work exists to prevent.

## The pipeline was not the problem

Everything upstream worked, verified for that exact turn:

```
Seeded coverage for file_d0827c12b4c6 from caller-declared
observed_at 2026-08-31T04:13:38.141609+00:00 (content had no parseable timestamps)
request_id 0d7a462c…   ← turn 1 of case_7bad3d1ac083
```

So provenance was `caller_declared` (vouched) and the prompt carried `observed_through` with `age="3m"`. The `title_link` fix was working too — the reply cites the Alertmanager link at "lines 1–2", which is content that did not reach the engine before.

The model even *used* the value: it called the alert "currently reporting an SLA breach". Then it listed the firing timestamp as missing anyway.

## The fault is in my wording from #1273

The block said:

> do not ask the user for a firing time or duration **the item already states**

An alert's **text** states no firing time. The observation time is a separate attribute. So the rule read as inapplicable, and judging currency with the value while reporting it absent were not contradictory under that phrasing.

## The change

The contract now says the question is **answered**, not open:

- content was observed no later than that instant, so what it reports happened **at or before** it — for a forwarded alert, that is the answer to "when did this fire", to within the forwarding delay;
- a timestamp, firing time, occurrence time, start time or duration must **not** appear in the missing-data list while `observed_through` is present, and the user must not be asked for one — they already supplied it by forwarding;
- asking for an exact `startsAt` remains available as a **refinement** when a precise duration matters. Never a gap, never a blocker.

One definition, so it reaches INQUIRY and INVESTIGATING alike — turn 1 of a forwarded alert is an INQUIRY turn, which is where this was observed.

## Tests

A regression test citing the case, asserting all three clauses reach both templates. `tests/unit/core/investigation/` 3295 passed, 3 skipped. black, isort, CI ruff selection clean.

## Note on verification

This is a prompt-wording change, so unit tests can only prove the text reaches the model — not that behaviour changes. Worth re-running the forwarded-alert case on the cluster after deploy; the failing phrasing is specific enough to check for directly.

author: vlannaai
body:
Closes #1277. Implements **option 2** of the three candidates, chosen by the maintainer after they were put with their consequences.

## What it adds

```ts
match: [{ from: 'clientId', to: 'entityId', via: { collection: 'clients', take: 'id', on: 'entityId' } }]
```

A relationship expressible where the two collections **share no field**: bills carry `entityId`, disbursements carry `clientId`, and the client record relates them. Before this, such a topology could not use composite `triggerBy` at all.

## Why option 2, and why the test file is the argument

The three candidates differed on one edit — **re-pointing the intermediate**, which writes to neither the trigger nor the source collection:

| edit | option 1 (resolve on trigger writes only) | **option 2 (shipped)** |
|---|---|---|
| disbursement moves cycle | ✅ old ∪ new | ✅ |
| **client re-pointed** | ❌ **stale, silently** | ✅ old ∪ new bills refresh |

**Mutation-checked against exactly that.** Disabling the intermediate indexing — which *is* option 1's behaviour — leaves three of four tests green and reds only EDIT B:

```
✓ EDIT A — a disbursement write reaches the bill THROUGH the client
× EDIT B — RE-POINTING THE CLIENT refreshes the bills it used to address
    → expected 'no-client' to be 'covered'
✓ a dangling hop matches nothing rather than throwing
✓ maxFanout caps the hop fan-out
```

That is the whole case for the more expensive design: option 1 fails only on the edit nobody repeats, and fails quietly.

**The EDIT B assertion is `'no-client'`, not `'uncovered'`, on purpose.** With the client moved to E2, entity E1 has no client *at all* — so that value proves the bill was **re-derived against the new world** rather than merely left alone. A stranded bill would still read `'covered'`.

## How it works

Hop resolution substitutes the intermediate's value into the pair tuple, so everything downstream — including the index-backed matcher — is unchanged. **One lookup per written record** (`take: 'id'` is a direct get), never one per candidate row: the same bound that made #1266 refuse virtual computed fields as match targets.

Intermediate writes reuse #1249's existing prior-capture — when the client is the *written* record, its old value is already threaded — so old ∪ new needed no new mechanism, just the same one pointed at a third collection.

Registering hop collections in `_bySource` also puts the hop edge into `validate()`'s cycle DFS, which would otherwise be blind to it.

## Behaviour at the edges

- **dangling hop** → matches nothing, does not throw. A missing reference addresses nothing, and throwing would turn a data condition into an exception on every write.
- **`maxFanout`** caps the hop fan-out with its own message, distinguishable from the direct form.
- **prior-less paths** (sync-applied waves, tiers restores) fan out on the new tuple only, matching `triggerBy` and rollups rather than adding a third degradation story.

## Verification

Full hub suite **5499 passed** (628 files) · typecheck · tests-typecheck · lint 0 errors · `check:architecture` · bundle floor **−0.4%**.

author: andrewd-github
body:
## Problem

Some newer robots return `outlineVer: "2"` in `getMapInfo_V2` responses. The shared `OnMapInfoV2` handler currently rejects this before publishing `MapInfoEvent`, so the map stays empty and Home Assistant's image endpoint returns HTTP 500.

Refs #1762. Also reproduced on an X8 PRO OMNI (`n0vyif`, firmware `1.133.0`).

## Change

Accept outline versions `"1"` and `"2"` in the shared handler. Version `"0"` still skips inactive maps, and unknown versions are still rejected. This covers both requested responses and pushed map messages.

The observed V2 payload uses outline, room and block-line layers already supported by the existing Rust renderer. No renderer, hardware profile, dependency or Home Assistant changes are included.

## Validation

- Expanded version-handling tests for both message and command paths.
- Added a synthetic compressed map test that passes through each handler into the real SVG renderer, checking geometry and bounds without legacy map tiles. The fixture contains no real floor-plan data.
- Confirmed the four new V2 cases fail on unmodified `dev` at `5453eba`, then pass with the one-line change.
- Focused map suite: **62 passed, four existing SVG snapshots passed**. One existing pytest generator-parametrization deprecation warning remains.
- Ruff check/format and changed-file mypy (`--follow-imports=silent`) pass.
- Local native tests used the released 18.5.1 extension; the Rust source is unchanged between that tag and the tested upstream base. No fresh native build or full test suite was run locally.

On Home Assistant 2026.8.3 / deebot-client 18.5.1, the equivalent gate change was deployed via a temporary compatibility wrapper. The X8 map endpoint changed from HTTP 500 to HTTP 200, with room geometry, cleaning trace and position visible. A T9+ map continued to render. The captured X8 payload also rendered locally through the direct library patch.

Raw device logs, identifiers and the household's map are deliberately not attached. The reported T50/X11 devices in #1762 were not available for physical testing.
