author: marcodejongh
body:
## Summary

2.4 makes the **Boardsesh** drawing the default board renderer. Rather than changing how
every climber's board looks without asking, the app now asks once — with a horizontal
carousel of live renders of **their own board**, so the choice is made on what it actually
looks like rather than on a label.

The picker is a step inside the existing `/onboarding` route, **not a new modal**. The app
already has three launch-time prompts (first-run tour, QA tester, offline nudge); a fourth
would be one too many. Climbers who already finished the tour get this step on its own.

The same carousel then replaces the flat preset chip row on **More → Board look**, so the
presets are visible there instead of being four bare words.

### What changed

- **Retired the `board-render-mode-default` flag.** It shipped at 0% and existed to roll the
  mode out; 2.4 makes Boardsesh the app default outright, so `requestedBoardRenderMode` now
  answers `boardsesh` for a stored `mode: 'default'` with no flag in the loop.
  `board-glow-falloff` (a live A/B) stays. An older binary that cannot draw the mode is still
  pinned to Classic by the capability probe — that check is now the only thing standing
  between a 2.3 build and a mode it cannot draw, so it is pinned by a test.
- **Fixed a live accessibility bug.** `applyCvdPalette('monochrome')` turns `roleGlyphs` on,
  because a colour-only cue is meaningless once every role is a shade of grey. Applying any
  preset rewrote all twelve fields verbatim and switched those glyphs back off — a colour-only
  board for the one climber who cannot use colour. Preset application now only ever *raises*
  accessibility-owned fields. Worth reviewing on its own: it is a bug on `main` today.
- **`renderSettingsOverride` on `useNativeClimbRender`**, so a preview card can draw a preset
  the climber is not on. Substituted above the mode/veil/signature chain so it reaches the
  cache key: each preset caches as its own PNG, and a card matching the climber's real
  settings *shares* the real PNG rather than displacing it. Hold colours still come from the
  global override store, so previews are always in the climber's own palette.
- **One shared carousel** (`BoardLookCarousel`) behind both surfaces, over one pure options
  module, so the two can never drift on what the options are or what picking one does.

### Notable decisions

- **Skipping is a real answer.** It marks the step seen, leaves `mode: 'default'` (the new
  default), and never asks again. Read `outcome: 'skipped'` as "accepted the default", not as
  a funnel drop.
- **Cards skeleton rather than lie.** While the capability probe is unanswered, a Boardsesh
  card would resolve to a *classic* render under a Boardsesh label. Those cards render a frame
  with no board image until the probe answers; if it answers `false` the step never shows, and
  the seen flag is deliberately **not** written, so the climber is asked after they update.
- **Fresh installs are asked after they pick a board.** There is no board to preview during
  the first-run tour — the tour's whole job is to get them to pick one. The step is held
  (`wait`, not `none`) until a board is bound, and the route guard keeps it off the picker.

Rejected, worth a line: moving `roleGlyphs` into the `holdColorOverrides` store is the right
long-term fix — preset writes structurally could not reach it — but it needs a two-key storage
migration plus a change to the render signature's token set. The one-directional merge is the
same behaviour with none of the migration risk.

## Release Notes

- Pick how your board looks — Boardsesh, Subtle, High contrast, or the classic markers — with a live preview of each on your own wall.
- Lit holds now glow in their own shape by default. Not for you? Switch back to the classic markers any time under More → Board look.
- Board look now previews every preset on your board, in your own hold colours.

## Test plan

1. Open the app. You see "Pick your board look".
2. Swipe the row. Each card shows your board.
3. Tap "Boardsesh Subtle", then "Use this look".
4. Reopen the app. The question does not return.
5. More → Board look. Same row, applies instantly.

## Risk

Risk: 3/5 — a launch-time interruption plus a change to the default renderer for everyone who
never chose. Bounded: the per-climber setting still wins, the capability probe still forces
Classic on a build that cannot draw the mode, and the step self-suppresses there.

The diff itself is JS/JSON only and touches no fingerprint input, but the branch is based on
`release/next`, whose native renderer artifacts already differ from `main` — so `ota-check`
correctly reports a native change and this ships with the 2.4 store build rather than by OTA.
That is the intent: the default flip, the flag retirement and the step that explains them all
land in the same binary.

Two behaviour changes beyond the step itself, both worth a look at review:

- Applying a preset no longer clears a colour-blind climber's role glyphs (a bug on `main`).
- `ensureBoardseshSupportProbed` now runs for every install rather than the 0% flag cohort —
  two renders once per JS lifetime. It also latches `false` when the native module loader has
  permanently given up, without which `Climb View Opened` would go silent for the session on a
  build with no renderer.

author: michaelayoade
body:
Dated **ADR-0072 amendment (2026-08-31)**, ratified by Michael. Two additions from ERP's census. No clause of the ratified text is withdrawn, `retired_total` stays **0**, and nothing is deleted, disabled or revoked. This defines how a retirement is proven; it performs none.

## Addition 1 — the eighth family is `runtime_reactivation`, not `restart_policy`

The naming is the ruling. Docker's `restart: unless-stopped` normally restarts **the same container**, which is not a deployment at all — a family named after the policy would describe the wrong thing and fire on every benign case, and a guard that fires on benign cases is one people learn to override.

The executor property is narrower: **it can reactivate a displaced executor after reboot.** That reframes what a retirement owes — not *the artifact is gone* but ***the executor cannot autonomously return***. A script deleted from a tree whose unit is still enabled comes back at the next reboot with nobody having invoked anything. That is a pause with a receipt.

- A row carries `reactivates`, naming the declared executors it can return. Checked in **both directions** — a row claiming to reactivate nothing is refused the moment another row names it, because a one-way check is satisfied by declining to fill in your own field. A name that resolves to nothing is refused outright: a mechanism pointing at a ghost can never be proven gone.
- Two dispositions with checked premises: `reactivation_capable` (backlog) and `reactivates_no_declared_executor` (reviewed). `not_an_executor` is refused over an artifact carrying a live directive; the weaker verdict is refused over one carrying none, so it cannot become the place everything lands.
- The receipt gains `no_autonomous_return`: typed method (`observed_reboot` / `supervisor_catalog` / `mechanism_absent`), observer, host, and the mechanisms with their disposition after. **Every inventory row naming the subject must be accounted for.** That cross-check — not the transition table — orders a mechanism's retirement against its subject's.

`restart: "no"` correctly does **not** fire. That is the right shape for a one-shot migration service, and a detector firing on it would refuse the verdict of the most carefully written file in the tree.

## Addition 2 — `DisplacementWindow.v1`: attribution, not absence

Two positive controller cycles never proved the negative. **A quiet window is the claim under test, not evidence for it** — so `poll`, `periodic_snapshot` and `quiet_window` are **named and refused** as event sources rather than merely absent, because someone will try each and deserves to be told why.

The window does not assert nothing happened. It enumerates everything that happened and attributes each change to a controller receipt or a typed non-deployment cause. **Zero unattributed** — a change nobody can account for is a third executor, and a zero-invocation guard passes straight over it.

| property | what it catches |
| --- | --- |
| bounded, exact start/end runtime identities | an open or inverted interval |
| **chained** — changes must meet, ends must match | a transition the source never saw; completeness is *tested*, not declared |
| a non-deployment cause must be **same-image** | a restart that actually changed what is running |
| `cannot_establish` → verdict `UNMONITORED` | a pass with a caveat; an `unmonitored` verdict cannot be committed |
| both cited cycles must appear inside the window | a cycle the window cannot vouch for |

The chain is what makes "a complete, named event source" mean something: a source that missed a transition leaves a **break**, so completeness is measured rather than asserted. And the same-image check is where Docker's benign case lives — `same_container_restart` is *proven* same-image, not believed.

## Sensitivity: both halves, same reach

Per the fleet rule:

- `test_the_planted_third_executor_change_is_refused` — strip one attribution from the conforming fixture; refused.
- `test_a_properly_attributed_window_is_not_refused` — the same fixture, unmodified, through the same code path; admissible.

A refusal test alone proves the validator can say no; only the pair proves it says no to the right thing. Thirteen new refusals each have a matching negative control, and the new family carries its own planted discovery case — which caught a gap in its own fixture name (`_planted-compose.yml` didn't match the pattern list) before CI did.

## A specificity repair the eighth family exposed

On its first run the verb detector read a **usage comment** in `docker-compose.dev.yml` (`docker compose -f … up`) as a deployment, and the edge resolver drew a call edge **backwards** from `docker-compose.yml` to `scripts/deploy.sh` because that path appears in a comment there — so the topology inherited the verbs of the executor that deploys it. A path mention is symmetric; invocation is not.

Whole-line comments are now stripped before both verb detection **and** edge resolution. Conservative by construction: only lines whose first non-blank character is `#`, so an inline trailing comment keeps its command. Over-stripping produces false negatives, and those hide executors. This is `credential_lifecycle_sweep.py`'s "calls, not mentions" applied where no AST exists. The real `uses:`/`run:` edge (`deployment-adopter.yml` → `deployment-conformance.yml`) is asserted to survive the change.

## Starter's own census

Five new `runtime_reactivation` rows — three carrying `restart: unless-stopped`, two carrying nothing. **All reactivate nothing**, and that is a finding rather than a formality: the Starter's one executor is operator-invoked and runs in no container, so no supervisor here can resurrect it. `retired_total` = 0, `unadopted` = `[dotmac_erp, dotmac_sub]`.

## Frozen candidate untouched

Ten files changed: `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, the ADR, three inventory docs, the module, and two test files. **Zero** matches against `packages/dotmac-deployment-foundation/`, `deploy/`, the `foundation-candidate-0.3.0a2` record, rehearsal fixtures or any workflow. `deploy/rendered/docker-compose.yml` is *observed* by the census (declared as a row) and not modified.

## Validation

- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean.
- `python scripts/executor_retirement.py --check` exits 0.
- Baseline regenerated by `make executor-retirement-baseline`, not hand-edited.
- A conforming receipt was generated and validated end-to-end through the shipped CLI (`--validate-receipt`), and all thirteen new refusals were smoked through the validator with their message regexes checked. **That is a validator smoke, not test evidence — CI is the acceptance owner and no test suite was run locally.**

author: daniel-frenkel
body:
## The question

A rotated board sat on the verify page showing **"Already verified. Sent back to your device."** Does that path re-derive against the current secret, or short-circuit on the enrolment record existing?

## The answer: it re-derives, so recovery works

`key` is computed from the current secret **before** the ledger read and returned on both branches. An `already_enrolled` response carries a freshly derived key, so a device recovers from a `DEVICE_KEY_SECRET` rotation through this page exactly as intended.

Not a bug — but **nothing said so, and nothing stopped it becoming one.** If the derivation ever moves below the ledger read, or `key` is dropped from the repeat branch as redundant, a rotated device is told it is fine while still 401ing.

Now pinned by a test that rotates the secret between two enrolments of the same id and requires the second key to **differ**, plus a control requiring it to be **unchanged** without a rotation — without which the first assertion also passes against an endpoint returning a random string, breaking the reflash case the idempotency test exists for.

Rehearsed by dropping `key` from the repeat branch: **3 of 22 fail**, including both new ones.

## The actual defect was the copy

> "This board was verified before - reflashing does not change its key."

True about reflashing, and misleading in the one case that matters. **A secret rotation does change the key, and a rotation is why the reader is on this page.** The sentence answers a question they are not asking with a fact irrelevant to the one they are.

> "This board has verified before. A fresh key was issued just now and is the one above - if this board was already working, nothing changes."

Same family as the stale-vs-unverified finding: a screen reporting a conclusion drawn from the wrong signal.

author: millw14
body:
## Two commits were never merged

PR #17 was merged when its branch held only the first commit. I pushed two more afterwards, the PR was already closed, and they've been stranded ever since — **while I reported both as shipped.** They weren't. Cherry-picked here.

What was missing from production:

- **The chain switch.** A new user on a faucet asked *"how to do leave testnet?"* — and the answer I built for him never deployed.
- **The expiry-banner bypass fix**, and with it the disabled-until-acknowledged guard. Harmless in production *only* because the chain-move checkbox it depended on was stranded in the same commit. The two are consistent with each other, which is the only reason this wasn't a live hole.
- **Gating "run `merrymen start`" on self-hosted.** Which is what the owner hit today: a hosted dashboard telling them to run a CLI they never installed, as the first instruction after sending real money.

One conflict, in the "what the chain itself enforces" sentence — I'd corrected it twice, once per panel, and the line numbers converged. Kept `main`'s phrasing; they say the same thing and that one is tighter.

## Step three had no way onward

The rail promises **CHOOSE → BACK UP → FUND → RIDE**, and RIDE wasn't somewhere you could get to. Funding is an external action with no completion event, so the wizard sat on step three indefinitely.

The only exit was "back to the band" at the very bottom of the page, below the fold, sharing a row with "switch to another wallet" and a red "discard & start over" — so the nearest thing to a next step looked like one of two ways to throw the wallet away.

Now there's a **"watch it trade →"** button in the funded panel, shown from the moment **gas** lands rather than waiting for capital: with no USDG the agent runs in practice mode, which is exactly what someone who's just funded gas wants to look at.

## Verification

`npm test` 1,468 passing · typecheck clean · build clean.

Post-merge, the three recovered behaviours should be checkable on app.merrymen.dev: the chain-move checkbox in the re-sign panel, the banner scrolling instead of signing, and no "merrymen start" anywhere in a hosted session.

author: b-eau
body:
Renames the product to **Learn Claude** and reworks the whole surface so it argues for what it is actually for: helping people get more out of Claude as it gets more capable, rather than ranking them.

## What changed

**Structure.** A shell on every page — wordmark home, People/Repositories nav, a search field that resolves `owner/name` or a login, breadcrumbs. No page is a dead end. People lead the listing, repositories follow, ordered by recency with no rank numbers and no points; the widest column carries what to reach for next. Both actions sit behind quiet buttons in their section headers and open dialogs.

**Colour.** Encodes how far along something is and nothing else — one hue, four steps, shared by rails, marks and card edges. Tier is typographic now. Tier gates are drawn on the rail rather than in a legend, and gates past a subject's ceiling aren't drawn.

## Two defects found on the way

- **Observations were public.** They're private coaching by contract, but `/u/[login]` is a public page and rendered them to any visitor. Now gated on the viewer being their subject.
- **Advice was ungrounded.** Someone who had only ever reported sessions was told to fix "your repositories" — never read, possibly nonexistent. `kindsWithEvidence` scopes advice to evidence actually held.

## Schema

`principal_progress` gains `previous_score_normalized` and `changed_at`, written only when a score really moves. Additive and nullable — **the migration is already applied to the Neon database**, so this deploys onto a schema that already has the columns. Existing rows report no history until they next move.

## Also

On-demand repository reading from the dashboard (`POST /api/analyze`, sign-in required — each one is a real model call on a repository the requester picks). Copy buttons on every code block, with a fallback for refused clipboard access. GitHub links on every reference. Origin derived from the request so pasted commands name the host actually reached. Medal emoji dropped from the badge for drawn steps.

## Worth a second look

- **Dark mode is my extrapolation**, not part of the reviewed design.
- **The denominator question is unresolved.** Tier thresholds are absolute points but rails are proportional, so a session-only person (45 available) can't reach Advanced at 60. The rail honestly omits the unreachable gate; the scoring model is untouched.

`npm test` 63/63, both typechecks clean, production build passes.

author: meziantou
body:
`Emitter` silently corrupted every non-BMP character — all emoji, CJK extension characters, and anything else outside the BMP.

## The defect

`Emitter.cs:1202`, in the double-quoted scalar escape path:

```csharp
short code = (short)character;
if (code <= 0xFF) { Write('x'); Write(code.ToString("X02", …)); }
else if (CharHelper.IsHighSurrogate(character)) { … Write('U'); … }   // unreachable
```

`char` is unsigned 16-bit, `short` is signed. Any character at or above U+8000 casts to a **negative** `short`, so `code <= 0xFF` is true and the surrogate branch is never reached. High surrogates are U+D800–U+DBFF, all ≥ U+8000, so that `else if` was dead code.

`(short)'\uD83D'` is `-10179`, and `(-10179).ToString("X02")` yields `D83D` — so the emitter wrote `\xD83D`. YAML's `\x` escape takes exactly two hex digits, so re-parsing reads `\xD8` (`Ø`) followed by a literal `3D`.

## Failure scenario

Round-trip through `YamlNode.ToString()` / `WriteTo()`, measured before this change:

| Input | Emitted | Read back |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"😀"` (U+1F600) | `"\xD83D\xDE00"` | `Ø3DÞ00` |
| `"𠀀"` (U+20000) | `"\xD840\xDC00"` | `Ø403DÜ00` |
| `"中"` (U+4E2D) | `中` | `中` ✓ |

No exception, no warning — silent data corruption, and the emitted document is not valid YAML 1.2, so other parsers disagree about it too.

The escape path is only entered for non-printable characters (`IsPrintable`, `Emitter.cs:1030`), and among those only surrogates exceed U+7FFF, so the blast radius is exactly *non-BMP characters emitted through `Emitter`*. This reaches users via `YamlNode.ToString()`, `YamlNode.WriteTo()`, and `YamlNode.ToObject()` (which routes through `ToString()`).

`YamlSerializer.Serialize` uses `YamlWriter`, not `Emitter`, and was **not** affected — verified emoji round-trip correctly there both before and after.

## The change

`short code = (short)character` → `int code = character`. That makes the `<= 0xFF` test mean what it reads as, and the existing (correct) `IsHighSurrogate` branch becomes reachable and emits `\U0001F600`.

## Tests

`EmitterTests.EmitUnicodeEscapes` previously asserted the corrupted output:

```csharp
Assert.Equal("\"Test\\xD802\\xDD05Yo♥\"", result);   // before
Assert.Equal("\"Test\\U00010905Yo♥\"", result);      // after
```

Because it asserted the exact broken bytes, it passed on the buggy code and would have kept passing after any correct fix was reverted — it could never catch this. Replaced with the correct expectation, and added tests that assert on behaviour rather than literal output:

- `EmitNonBmpCharacters_RoundTrips` — 6 cases (emoji, CJK ext-B, Phoenician, mixed BMP/non-BMP, adjacent pairs) asserting emit → parse → equals original.
- `EmitNonBmpCharacter_UsesEightDigitEscape` — pins the `\U` form.
- `EmitBmpCharacterAboveShortMaxValue_UsesFourDigitEscape` — covers U+FFFE, above `short.MaxValue` but not a surrogate, which must still use the 4-digit `\u` escape. This is the case that would catch an over-broad fix.

`dotnet test` on `Meziantou.Framework.Yaml.Tests`: **888 passed, 0 failed** (Release, net10.0). Confirmed the 6 new round-trip cases and the corrected assertion actually execute.

Found during a project review of `Meziantou.Framework.Yaml`.

author: mike-thompson-day8
body:
Discharges the AUDIT PR #8798 reopen on rf2-9hcyf: the act-flag restore in the UIx component-test recipe worked on the success path but was not failure-safe. `mount!` set the global before `flush-views!` and only returned cleanup ownership afterward — a render/act throw lost the prior flag and left the node on the page; `unmount!` restored only after `flush-views!` and `node.remove`, so an unmount or effect-cleanup throw skipped the restore and, in the async `.finally`, `done`. That contradicted the page's copy-complete, unconditional-teardown, exactly-as-found contract.

The correction is local and surgical, carrying the donor final-cleanup discipline (`react_shared_suite.cljs:3280-3351`):

- `mount!` wraps render in `try`/`catch`: a throw restores the flag and removes the node before rethrowing — a failed mount leaves nothing behind.
- `unmount!` removes the node and restores the flag through its own `finally`, so a throw out of React's unmount or an effect cleanup cannot skip either.
- The async test's teardown runs in `try`/`catch`/`finally`: a teardown throw is reported as a failure and `done` runs regardless.
- One sentinel pre-value regression test (`mount-unmount-hands-back-the-act-flag-it-found`) plants a value the runner would never set, runs one mount/unmount round trip, and demands it back — the restore check no longer depends on the ambient runner's flag being non-true.
- No shared fixture; no rf2-3t2nq consolidation. The `wait-for` false polling window and the unconditional unmount are preserved.

The pinned verbatim block in `docs/core/testing/views.md` §4 moves in the same PR (the adapter's `clojure -M:test` pin holds page and file byte-equal), and the two prose sentences about teardown and the flag restore are updated to stay truthful.

## Quality gates

All run from the worker worktree with its own lockfile-installed `node_modules`; every exit code captured to a log+exit file pair and quoted from those files.

- Pin negative control (test file edited, docs not yet): `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/adapters/uix` — **exit 1**, `Ran 1 tests containing 3 assertions. 1 failures, 0 errors.` (drift named).
- Pin after the paired docs edit: **exit 0**, `Ran 1 tests containing 3 assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors.`
- Sentinel negative control (restore property removed: `unmount!`'s restore planted to force `true`, the pre-#8798 behaviour; plant/restore verified by git blob hash against the committed object): `npm run test:browser` — **exit 1**, `Ran 751 tests containing 4098 assertions. 1 failures, 0 errors.`, the single failure being the sentinel test (`actual: (not (= "recipe-sentinel" true))`). The pre-existing in-test restore assertion stayed green under the plant — the runner's ambient flag is `true` — which is exactly the gap the sentinel closes.
- Official browser lane on final content: `npm run test:browser` — **exit 0**, `Ran 751 tests containing 4098 assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors.` (750/4097 on main plus the one new sentinel test/assertion).
- `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` — **exit 0**; gate verified against this worktree by a planted broken link (exit 1 naming `views.md`), restore blob-hash-verified.
- `python -m mkdocs build --strict` — **exit 0**; same planted-fault verification (exit 1 naming the planted link), restore blob-hash-verified.
- `sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` — **exit 0**, `PASS fast PR spine`, 0 FAIL lines.

Hand-verified (no gate covers these): the two edited §4 prose sentences add or change no links and no tables; the fenced recipe block's contents are code (fences are outside both link gates' vision) and are executed byte-identically by the browser lane via the pin.

author: shiroha-a
body:
## Summary

`pg_indexes` を schema 非限定で引くテストが 3 本あり、パッケージ並行実行で `could not open relation with OID (SQLSTATE XX000)` により不定期に落ちていた。**CI の required check (`test`) でも実際に赤くなった** (PR #2778 の `test-shards (1)`)。

## 害は 2 つあった

issue 本文は (b) だけを挙げていたが、調べたら (a) のほうが重い。

### (a) regression guard が空振りしていた

GORM は `*string` に対し**全行を走査して dest を上書きし続ける**ので、複数行が返ると**最後の 1 行**が残る。実測すると、`clip_favorite` / `note` の index は 17 schema に存在し、返っていたのは **17 番目 (`internal_repository_ts`) の定義**だった。

```
Scan(&string) over 3 rows -> "last"
unscoped -> CREATE INDEX "IDX_clip_favorite_clipId" ON internal_repository_ts.clip_favorite USING btree ("clipId")
current_schema = internal_repository   (17 件中 15 番目)
```

他 schema の定義でも `NotEmpty` / `Contains "USING gin"` / `Contains "IS NOT NULL"` を全部満たすので、**自分の schema に migration が適用されていなくてもテストは緑**だった。3 本とも検査になっていなかった。

### (b) パッケージ並行実行で落ちる

他パッケージの `ApplyMigrations` が DDL 中だと、view が定義を取りに行った relation が既に消えていて OID エラーになる。CI の shard は PostgreSQL を 1 つしか立てないので手元と同じ条件が揃う。

## 主な変更点

### 1. `indexDef` ヘルパに集約 (`internal/repository/index_lookup_test.go`)

`schemaname = current_schema()` で絞り、**slice で受けて件数と schema 名の両方を確かめる**。最初は `Scan(&string)` のままだったが、それだと絞りを外す変異が **0/10 で生き残った** (物理順の都合で値が正しく見える)。

### 2. 静的 gate (`internal/entitycompat/catalog_query_test.go`)

doc に書くだけだと再発する — schema が 17-19 ある条件は残ったままなので。`pg_indexes` と `information_schema.columns` / `.tables` を引くクエリが絞られていることを検査する。`make catalog-check` / `make gates` に入れた。

**この gate も 2 回作り直している。**

- 初版は backtick を機械的にペアリングして raw string を切り出していたが、コメントや rune literal の backtick でずれる。**gate 自身のファイルで既にずれており** (backtick 41 個 = 奇数)、`TestCatalogQueryGate_Predicates` の本体を飲み込んだ幻のチャンクができて、絞りの無いフィクスチャ 3 つを見逃していた。`checked == 0` の空振りガードもそのチャンクで埋まっていた。→ `go/parser` + `ast.BasicLit` に変更
- 判定が `strings.Contains(sql, "schemaname")` だったので `SELECT schemaname, indexdef FROM pg_indexes WHERE tablename = ?` が通っていた。→ WHERE 述語 (`schemaname|table_schema|nspname` + `=`/`IN`) を見る
- opt-out の理由チェックが `--\s*unscoped:\s*\S` で、`\s` が改行を含むため理由なしのマーカーを通していた。→ `[^\S\n]`

`information_schema.schemata` は schema の一覧そのものなので対象外 (`pluginstore` が plugin 用 schema の列挙に使う)。意図的に schema を跨ぐクエリは `-- unscoped: <理由>` を書く。

### 3. doc (`CLAUDE.md` / `docs/testing.md` / `docs/development.md`)

絞る列が catalog ごとに違うこと、`Scan(&string)` の罠を書いた。あわせて `docs/development.md` の「静的 parity ゲート 4 種」を直した (#2762 で 5 種になった時点で直し損ねており、今回 6 種になった)。

## テスト

| 項目 | 結果 |
|---|---|
| `go test ./...` (並行) | **4 回連続で緑** (修正前は 3 回中 2 回落ちた) |
| 絞りを外す変異 | **10/10** で落ちる |
| 絞り + 件数チェックを外す変異 | **10/10** (schema 名チェックが効く) |

gate の変異 (すべて KILLED):

| 変異 | |
|---|---|
| 実クエリの絞りを外す | KILLED |
| **backtick 奇数のファイルに違反クエリを置く** | KILLED (初版は見逃した) |
| **二重引用符で書いた違反クエリ** | KILLED (初版は見逃した) |
| `information_schema.columns` の絞りを外す | KILLED |
| gate の判定を初版 (`Contains`) に戻す | KILLED |
| opt-out の改行対策を戻す / 理由なしにする | KILLED |
| `\b` を外す (`pg_indexes_backup` の誤検知) | KILLED |
| gate の列挙を空にする | KILLED |
| `schemata` を対象に戻す (誤検知) | KILLED |

## その他

敵対的レビューは 2 巡で止めた。**2 巡目の High が 1 巡目の修正による回帰**だったため — 1 巡目のレビューが提案した gate を採用したが、その初版に上記の切り出しの欠陥があった。AST 化して機能させたうえで、3 巡目は回していない。

Closes #2777

author: davenompozolo-blip
body:
Implements `NEXUS_PROVIDER_LIFT_SPEC.md`. Enabling change for the tile-collapse model; ships on its own.

## Why

`NexusBoardSection`, `NexusEarningsTable` and `NexusCotTable` each took no props and fetched their own data on mount. A collapsed tile has to show a headline — score, count, verdict — *before* the panel mounts, and it cannot do that for data that only arrives *because* the panel mounted. Every panel that owns its own fetch is a panel that can't be collapsed.

## What changed

**`nexusLive.js`** — three loaders (`loadBoard`, `loadEarnings`, `loadCot`) mirroring `loadMacro()`: same-origin, `ok` check, `null` on any failure so each panel falls back to its own empty state rather than throwing.

The load-bearing detail is **where they sit**. `getNexusModel()` returns the baseline early in two places, and today all three panels render through both because they fetch independently of Supabase. Placed in the existing `Promise.all` — below those early returns — they would disappear whenever Supabase is unconfigured, erroring, or the book is empty: the exact state where macro context is most useful. None of the three endpoints touches Supabase, so they load **above** the guard and merge into the baseline on both fallback paths.

**`NexusBoard.js` / `NexusEarnings.js` / `NexusCot.js`** — hook deleted, prop taken. Each keeps its own loading and empty rendering; only the data source moved. They now separate:

| prop | meaning | renders |
|---|---|---|
| `undefined` | model has not resolved yet | loading |
| `null` | resolved, endpoint unavailable | that panel's empty state |

The board's `err` detail is dropped because the provider swallows it. If it turns out to matter, `loadBoard()` should return `{ ok: false, error }` rather than the hook coming back.

**`nexusModel.js`** — three optional top-level fields documented. **`nexusMock.js`** — explicit `null` for all three, so the mock stays honest about what it does not supply. **`NexusFlagship.js`** — `FlagshipPanel` passes the model fields down.

## Acceptance

All six criteria verified, plus a Supabase-error case the spec did not enumerate:

| # | case | result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Healthy | three panels render, live book assembled |
| 2 | **Supabase down (`sb` null)** | **all three still render** |
| 3 | Empty book / view error | all three still render |
| 4 | One endpoint down | only that panel is `null` |
| 5 | All endpoints down | three empty states, page otherwise normal |
| 6 | No double-fetch | exactly one request each per load |
| 7 | Existing suites | 19/19 pass, none modified |

Also `npx vite build` clean (191 modules).

## Tests added

Two new suites; no existing suite touched (the compute modules are unmodified, so any change there would be a signal something was edited that shouldn't have been).

- **`nexusLiveProvider.test.mjs`** pins the guard placement across every state above. Proven by **forcing the regression** — moving the loaders back under the guards — and confirming exactly the four guard checks fail. Worth recording that the first version of this suite *passed* against that broken provider: its config stub read the mode at module-eval time and is cached under one URL, so it evaluated once on the healthy case and every later case silently re-ran the healthy path. `sb` is an ESM live binding now, reassigned per case. A suite that has not been observed failing is not a test.
- **`nexusPanelProps.test.mjs`** pins the `undefined` / `null` / payload branches of all three panels — a distinction a single `if (!board)` would quietly collapse, and one the tile work depends on.
- **`nexusLive.stub.mjs`** is the loader hook standing in for `../config.js`, which reaches for `import.meta.env` and `@supabase/supabase-js` under plain node.

## Not touched

`nexusBoardCompute.js`, `nexusEarningsCompute.js`, `nexusCotCompute.js`, the API routes, and all rendering below each export.

## Note on latency

The three fetches are parallel with each other but now sit ahead of `loadHoldingRows()`, so first paint waits on the slowest. Per the spec, the simple version ships first — the mitigation (start without awaiting, pass promises down, let tiles resolve independently) should not be built until it measures badly.

author: baotran01
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes a macOS Electron test-harness flake where `scrollIntoView()` can be dropped before the session row is clicked. The helper now uses explicit, non-smooth centered scrolling, retries while waiting for a non-zero viewport-visible target, and clicks only after visibility is established. It also reads the nested value returned by Chrome DevTools Protocol `Runtime.evaluate`.

This keeps the change limited to the Electron test harness and adds deterministic regression coverage for the reported failure mode.

## Related Issue

Fixes #97982

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/scripts/click-session-helpers.mjs`
  - Extracts the browser-side click expression.
  - Uses `scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'auto', block: 'center' })`.
  - Reissues scrolling while polling for viewport visibility for up to 3 seconds.
  - Fails closed when the session is missing or remains invisible.

author: unional
body:
Org-owned copy of the secretless changesets release workflow that
`storybook-community/*` repos have been borrowing from `unional/.github`.

Publishes through npm trusted publishing (OIDC) — no `NPM_TOKEN`, no
`CI_GITHUB_TOKEN`. npm validates the **caller** workflow's filename, so each
repo keeps its own `release.yml` and registers a trusted publisher naming that
repo and `release.yml`; nothing about the trusted-publisher config changes when
a repo switches to this workflow.

Two changes from the `unional/.github@v2` original:

- `pnpm-version` is wired into `pnpm/action-setup` — upstream declares the input
  but never uses it.
- A comment recording why pnpm 11+ is required: on pnpm 10, `pnpm info --json`
  prints an array, and `@changesets/cli` 3 reads `.versions` off it and crashes
  with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'includes')`.

Once merged, please tag `v1` so callers can pin

Two commits, on top of the merged contact-form work.

## 1. Portfolio restructure (`5272802`)

Audited the page as a hiring manager for ML/AI engineer internships would, and rebuilt its information architecture. The design system is kept — Space Grotesk + Inter, the blue accent, square corners, the narrow measure. What changed is what the page leads with.

**The finding that drove the rest:** the only project with public, reproducible evidence — the search-ranking capstone in this repo, with a deployed paper, public code and out-of-fold metrics — was not on the portfolio at all. Four unverifiable projects were, and the page opened with a self-description. The capstone is now the first project and the source of every figure in a new evidence band under the hero.

| Area | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Positioning | "AI Engineer · AI Researcher · Scientific ML" | One target role: Machine Learning Engineer / AI Engineer Intern |
| Hero copy | Describes interests | Describes method: framing, leakage audit, baseline before model |
| Evidence | none | Band of four real figures + the leakage callout |
| Projects | four paragraph blurbs | five cards: problem → my contribution → approach → result → stack → links |
| Skills | eight comma-separated items | four capability groups, each tied to the project that demonstrates it |
| How I work | none | six-step workflow |
| Background | none | Mathematics + CS section |
| CTAs | four competing chips, one dead | primary "View projects", secondary GitHub |

Every metric on the page traces to `work/outputs/capstone_metrics.json`: 18,010 pages across 30 clients, precision@50 0.88 against a 0.74 rule baseline and a 0.62 base rate, 24 decision-time features with 20+ window-overlapping columns audited out, one script reproducing everything from seed 42. Nothing is invented, and the leaky variant that scored higher (PR-AUC 0.775) is reported as a leakage confession rather than a result.

The capstone card states plainly that it started from this starter repo, listing what was provided and what was the author's own work. The in-progress project is labelled as such and makes no performance claim.

**Also fixed**
- The dead `href="#"` CV link is gone — there was no URL to point it at.
- The empty "Writing — coming soon" block is gone.
- The font stack no longer falls back to monospace, which misplaced the tone mark in "Nguyễn". Inter now sits second in the chain because it has full Vietnamese coverage.

**New:** `work/scripts/audit_portfolio.py` checks dead links, unresolved anchors, unsafe `target="_blank"`, and WCAG AA contrast across all twelve colour pairs. Passes clean.

## 2. Explainer rewrite (`ef029bf`)

`work/portfolio/HOW-IT-WORKS.md` rewritten in plainer language: shorter sentences, the data flow as a numbered walkthrough plus a diagram instead of prose, and the addition of what actually went wrong during the build — the placeholder key appears twice in the page, once as the key and once as the constant that checks whether the key is set, and replacing both made the page declare itself unconfigured and fail every test.

- Portfolio audit: no dead links, no broken anchors, all contrast pairs pass AA.
- Rendered at 1000px and 390px in Chromium: no horizontal overflow, no overflowing elements, no JavaScript errors.

Outbound network is blocked in the build environment, so Google Fonts could not load during rendering — the screenshots used fallback faces. The live rendering of "Nguyễn" should be confirmed after deploy.

author: vansin
body:
两个缺陷,第二个是**跑出来才看见的**,#1635 正文里没有。

## ① 报错点的文件不是它真读的那个

    const confPath = env.ANET_DAEMON_PATH_CONF || trustRoot;
    pin = readPathConf(confPath);                            // 读 confPath
    throw ... `no ANET_BIN_ABS resolved from ${trustRoot}`   // 报 trustRoot ← 默认值

实测:传 `ANET_DAEMON_PATH_CONF=/nonexistent-xyz`,报错说
`from /etc/anet-daemon/path.conf`。**用户一旦用了这个变量,报错会把他指向一个
从没被读过的文件。** 改用 `confPath`。

## ② 只给了要 root 的修法

`ANET_DAEMON_PATH_CONF` 这条免 root、活得过重启的路一直在代码里,却从没出现在
任何面向用户的文案里(#1635)。两处 `anet_bin_source`(reason 不同:一处是设了
`ANET_BIN_ABS` 但没开 `ALLOW_ENV_BIN`,一处是什么都没配)现在都给出:

    Or keep the pin in a file you own (no /etc, no sudo): ANET_BIN_REAL="$(node -e …)" \
      && mkdir -p "$HOME/.anet" && printf 'ANET_BIN_ABS=%s\n' "$ANET_BIN_REAL" > "$HOME/.anet/path.conf" \
      && export ANET_DAEMON_PATH_CONF="$HOME/.anet/path.conf"
      (put ANET_DAEMON_PATH_CONF in the daemon environment so it survives a restart)

措辞避开 "no root",因为消息里**已经有**一句 `No-root alternative to try first`
(讲的是 `anet daemon start` 自动声明 pin,另一个机制) —— 两个「免 root」并排会
读成重复。这一点也是跑出来才看见的。

## 验证

- 🔴 `bash -n` 验的是**从真实报错消息里抠出来的那 262 字节**,不是源码里的字符串。
  这个文件自己记着一次翻车:上一版给的修法语法就不成立,用户粘贴只看到 syntax error
  ——「验源码里的字符串」当时正好会放过它。
- 新增 `daemon-bin-error-help.test.ts` 4 项,含一条反向见证
  (`not.toContain("resolved from /etc/anet-daemon/path.conf")`) —— 没有它,
  把 confPath 写回 trustRoot 也照样绿。
- **两向见证**:
  变异① confPath→trustRoot ⇒ 1 fail;变异② 拿掉免 root 那句 ⇒ 3 fail;还原 ⇒ 4 pass。
- 仓内门 5 道全绿:doc-symbol-pins / mutation-pins / home-path-baseline /
  test-file-coverage / test-suite-registration(跑之前先 `git add`,否则新文件对
  `git ls-files` 型的门隐身)。

消息前缀 `anet_bin_unsafe_path:` 未改动(全仓 10 个文件依赖它,含 6 条 toThrow)。

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

The first 15 minutes were only a gate (`tradeEvaluationAllowed=false`); the levels they produce were thrown away. This preserves them as a fixed intraday reference that regime and signal read as one more feature.

`buildOpeningRangeContext()` (new, in the session layer) selects candles by their Eastern opening minute and computes the levels once, inside `partitionSessionCandles`:

```ts
rangeCandles = currentSessionCandles.filter(c =>
  minutesOfDay(c) >= 09:30 && minutesOfDay(c) < 09:30 + windowMinutes)
postRangeCandles = currentSessionCandles.filter(c => minutesOfDay(c) >= windowEnd)
```

Its input is already completed-candle-only and already truncated at `now`, so nothing after the evaluation instant can leak in and the 09:45 candle can never widen the range — replaying 09:51 yields the same five candles live or historically. `status` is `FORMING` until the wall clock passes the window end on the session's own date, `COMPLETE` after, `UNAVAILABLE` when the window produced no candles; the high/low then stop moving while `currentSessionFeatures.high/low` keep updating, and premarket levels stay in their own context.

Breakouts require a completed **close** beyond the boundary plus a tolerance (`OPENING_RANGE_BREAKOUT_TOLERANCE_PERCENT`, default 0.05%), so a wick through ORH that closes back inside sets `failedBreakoutAbove` instead of `breakoutAbove`. `breakoutStrength` scales the excursion by the range width and is lifted one band by repeated confirming closes with participation. Volume is measured as post-range candle volume over the average opening-range candle rather than the indicator layer's RVOL, which is rolling and not time-of-day normalised — it supports the reading, never gates it.

Regime consumes it through the existing `SessionEvidence`, which gains a third bucket so an inside-range market can strengthen `RANGE_BOUND`:

```ts
-interface SessionEvidence { bullish; bearish; reasoning; riskFlags }
+interface SessionEvidence { bullish; bearish; rangeBound; reasoning; riskFlags }
```

A rejected break subtracts from the side that attempted it rather than adding to the other one — failed bullish breakout never becomes bearish evidence. Signal reads `regime.openingRange` in `signal-factors.ts`; it fetches nothing and recomputes no levels, and a direction contradicted by the range position (bearish regime while price holds above ORH) surfaces as a conflict.

Config: `OPENING_RANGE_MINUTES` (default 15) and `OPENING_RANGE_BREAKOUT_TOLERANCE_PERCENT`, both documented in `.env.example`.

## Verification

`npm run build`, `npm run lint`, `npx prettier --check`, 255 unit tests (31 new across opening-range window/levels/breakout/rejection/volume/no-look-ahead, regime evidence and signal factors) and e2e all pass.

## Summary

- Upgrade the application from Expo SDK 54 to Expo SDK 55.

author: paolochaparro
body:
Barrido de la vista móvil del Panel de Trabajo, hecho sobre pantalla con el usuario. Dos criterios de fondo, aplicados igual en todas las secciones y para todos los roles:

1. La primera pantalla del teléfono muestra **datos**, no herramientas. Todo lo que sirve para configurar la vista (pestañas secundarias, filtros, import/export, modo selección) queda solo en escritorio.
2. **No quedan colores sueltos**: el azul, el celeste, el lila y el verde que venían de defaults salen de la paleta de la marca.

## Qué cambió

### Seguimiento
- Las tarjetas de resumen suben y quedan pegadas a las pestañas.
- Se van la ayuda del círculo, los chips "Ver primero", "Expandir todo" y la caja que envolvía a los dos botones de alta.
- El (+) del header ya no aparece en esta sección: el alta vive en "Nuevo seguimiento".

### Tareas y Proyectos
- Los proyectos arrancan **cerrados** cada vez que se entra a la sección o se cambia de área, no solo en la primera carga de la página.
- La franja, la inicial y la barra de avance de cada proyecto pasan del azul a una **escala de naranjos**. El azul era el color con el que se guardaban todos los grupos por defecto, no una elección de nadie; los grupos nuevos ahora nacen naranjos.
- La tarjeta de tarea usa todo el ancho: los chips de estado bajan a su propia línea y los de hover ya no reservan espacio en celular.
- **Debajo del título va el último movimiento con su fecha** (último mensaje del chat o última actividad) en vez de la descripción. Si la tarea no tiene movimientos todavía, cae de vuelta a la descripción.
- El selector "¿Qué querés crear?" entra como panel lateral desde la izquierda, igual que los filtros del Dashboard, y espera a que cierre antes de abrir el formulario (los dos se pisaban y el paso siguiente no llegaba a aparecer).
- El formulario de Nueva Tarea ya no muestra "Equipo asignado": la tarea queda automáticamente para quien la crea, su supervisor y la administración. "Nuevo seguimiento" no cambia — ahí el asignado es el responsable y se sigue eligiendo a mano.

### CRM
- Se va el botón azul "Nuevo Cliente" cuando el CRM va embebido en el panel (arriba ya está el naranjo). Sigue existiendo si la pantalla se abre por su cuenta.
- Las tarjetas quedan dos por fila, más grandes, con el ícono en negro sin fondo.
- **El pipeline pierde los fondos de color por etapa**: columnas blancas y una escala de naranjos (línea superior, punto y contador) de prospecto a perdido.
- Tabla/Pipeline son dos botones sueltos (el activo naranjo, el otro negro) y, junto con la caja de filtros e Importar/Exportar, no se muestran en celular.

### Obras, Rutas y Estimación
- **Rutas**: ícono del título en naranjo y del mismo porte que el resto, sin el botón azul duplicado, y el pin de cada ruta sin el cuadro celeste.
- **Obras**: la barra de la cartera (pestañas, buscador a lo largo y botones) baja debajo del resumen; números en naranjo.
- **Estimación**: se van el (+) del header y la bajada del módulo; las cuatro tarjetas quedan con título negro e íconos naranjos sin fondo.
- Las tarjetas de resumen de Seguimiento, Obras y CRM comparten ahora un mismo molde: ícono en negro y suelto, número grande y el nombre debajo en gris.

## Backend

Un solo cambio, en `enrichSeguimientoTasks` (`server/storage.ts`): además de la **fecha** del último movimiento, ahora se trae su **texto**, para poder mostrarlo en la tarjeta.

- Son dos `SELECT DISTINCT ON` extra (último comentario y última actividad por tarea). **Solo lectura**: no escribe, no modifica ni borra nada.
- El bloque ya venía envuelto en try/catch: si el agregado falla, el panel sigue funcionando sin esos datos.
- Probado en local con 238 tareas (120 con movimiento) sin demoras perceptibles, pero **vale la pena mirar el costo de esas consultas antes de que salga al sitio en vivo**, que es lo principal a revisar de este PR.

## Qué conviene revisar

- El costo de las dos consultas nuevas con volumen real.
- **Un vendedor ya no puede crear un seguimiento** desde esa pantalla: el (+) de arriba se sacó para todos y la barra de abajo ("Nuevo seguimiento") solo se le muestra a supervisores, encargados y administración. Si hace falta que el vendedor también pueda, hay que mostrarle esa barra.
- En el pipeline, la etapa **"No le interesa / Perdido" quedó en naranjo quemado**, no en rojo: se pierde el aviso visual de que algo se perdió. Fue una decisión explícita del usuario.
- En celular no se puede buscar dentro del CRM ni alternar Tabla/Pipeline; la vista y los filtros quedan como se dejaron desde el computador (se guardan por navegador).

## Nota

Hay un error de tipos **preexistente** en `client/src/pages/seguimiento-clientes.tsx:486` (una etapa `despacho` que no está declarada en `ESTADOS`). No lo toqué porque es anterior a estos cambios, pero conviene resolverlo aparte.

author: rbanick
body:
## #166 fixed the smaller of the two deletes

`_finalize` runs two multi-terabyte deletes per landed cell. #166 moved the **mosaic** delete off the trailing-assembly thread. The **staging** delete runs inside `assemble_zone_year`, on that same thread, and it is the bigger one.

Measured in production, 34N-2018 on `glossy-python`:

| event | time |
|---|---|
| `Global assembly complete` | 02:27Z |
| `Deleting prefix: …/staging/34N/2018/34N-2018-eb3771ff` | 02:27Z |
| `Deleting prefix: …/mosaics/34N/2018` — the next step on that thread | **04:27Z** |

Two hours, on the thread the next cell's assembly needs. `_validate` between them dispatches without waiting, so the gap is the staging delete itself. Other cells agree: `tidy-gopher` published 50N-2018 at 01:39Z and reached its mosaic delete at 03:54Z.

**So the symptom #166 was meant to cure survives it.** Seven of nine clusters idle for 91–117 minutes with 22 fully-staged cells waiting — with #166 alone they would still wait, just on the other delete.

## The change

`assemble_zone_year` gains `defer_cleanup`. Given a callable, it hands the staging delete over instead of running it inline; omitted, behaviour is exactly as before, which is what every other caller wants.

**The pool is created in the flow, not the runner.** The staging delete is issued from inside `assemble`, which the runner cannot reach — so the flow owns creation and passes the same pool to the runner via a new optional `housekeeping` parameter. The runner is what drains, so it is what joins the pool. That keeps lifecycle ownership where the draining is and stops the flow returning with deletes outstanding.

Both of a landed cell's deletes now run on that pool, and the assembly thread is released as soon as the cell is marked and tagged.

## Tests

Three, and the first two were confirmed by breaking the source.

- **`test_staging_cleanup_is_handed_to_the_caller_rather_than_run_inline`** — the regression. The oracle is that `cleanup_staging` is *not* called during `assemble_zone_year` and *is* reachable afterwards through what the caller was handed, then invokes it and checks it deletes the right run. Asserting only that a deferral fired would pass even if the work never happened. Forcing the inline path fails it with `the staging delete ran inline despite a deferral`.
- **`test_staging_cleanup_still_runs_inline_without_a_deferral`** — the default is unchanged.
- **`test_the_flow_actually_defers_both_deletes`** — the wiring. A deferral that works and a flow that never passes it is a fix that cannot fire, and both tests above would still pass. Removing the flow's argument fails it.

## Gates

3,709 unit tests pass, ruff clean, mypy clean across 128 source files.

## Sequencing

Not in tonight's restart, which goes out on main as it stands (#165 and #166). With those two the campaign is better than it was but assemblies still will not run back-to-back — they will block on the staging delete instead. This is what closes it.

author: juan-co-dev
body:
Juan, 2026-08-29:

> "why haven't we added the prices to the SKUs if we have all the pricing already… pricing should update from what we are receiving. But we can and should seed it since we have it basically on tap with angel spend."

That is two questions. This PR answers both. **Nothing is written** — dry-run is the default, `--execute` is lead-gated, and no receiving code changes.

## The seed half

**140 of 169 active SKUs held zero price rows.** Wave 6 sweeps the tail:

| disposition | SKUs |
|---|---:|
| **WRITE** | **11** — coverage 29 → 40 of 169 (17.2% → **23.7%**) |
| REFUSED (adjudicated, arithmetic finished) | 47 |
| NO SOURCE | 82 (62 of them the supply-run class) |

`11 + 47 + 0 blocked + 82 = 140`, and the script **asserts** it — if a refusal ever names a SKU that is already priced or misspelled, the run aborts rather than printing a coverage number that is quietly wrong. That number is the one Juan reads.

The 11 writes are Duke's Mayo $18.50, Olive Oil $31.24, Balsamic Vin $17.26, Canola Oil $40.56, Arugula $20.67, Parmesan (Grated) $76.03, Watermelon Radish $24.02, Black peppercorn $51.53, Saratoga $24.86, Natalie's Lemonade $10.63, Cannoli Shell $42.67. Full table + every refusal in `docs/seed/source/angel-wave6-dryrun.md`.

The refusals are one question far more often than they look: **15 of the 47 are Delmar**, and all 15 need the same sentence — *is one Delmar unit one of our packs?* Three of those (Branded Water, Coke, Diet Coke) already have the count independently confirmed from two other sources.

## Finding 1 — the 2024 costing sheet is not a second source, it is our own echo

The brief named `inventory-costing.csv` as a co-equal price source. It cannot be one:

```ts
// scripts/seed/02-skus.ts:137
const rows = readCsv("inventory-costing.csv");
idx.set(key, { unitsPerPack: 1, eachSize: qty, eachMeasure: measure });   // qty = column 4
```

**Our SKUs' `each_size` was seeded from the same row whose column 3 is the price.** So "the 2024 row matches our pack exactly" is a tautology for ~20 of the priceless SKUs — one number counted twice — not corroboration. That is on top of what the repo already said: the reconciliation report rates the file *"historical, unversioned, internally inconsistent"* (§C.4: 9 agree, **16 conflict**), and wave 4 set the precedent by binding Mortadella's vendor and deliberately **not** writing that sheet's price.

Nothing is written from it. 9 SKUs are HELD under a named `COSTING_SHEET_ONLY_2024` code with finished arithmetic, for Juan to ratify or reject — the wave-3/4 pattern verbatim.

## Finding 2 — the receiving wire is not dead code. It fired once, and the door just never asks.

The brief said zero receiving-source rows exist. Not quite, and the correction is the good news.

**The wire is complete end-to-end.** The input renders (`IntakeLineRow.tsx:342-357`), the form submits it (`ReceivingForm.tsx:612`), the routes validate it (`receiving/route.ts:60`, `continue/route.ts:42-43`). Both inserts (`receiving.ts:505` in `recordDelivery`, `:1123` in `addDeliveryLines`) gate on one thing: a non-null `unitPrice` on a line.

**The gap is an affordance.** The price box's own comment states the condition: *"expanded only; collapsed path untouched"* (`IntakeLineRow.tsx:341`) — and `ReceivingForm.tsx:143` builds every line seeded from a PO or last-delivery template with `expanded: false`. **The ordinary door flow renders every line collapsed, and a collapsed line has no price field.**

Prod confirms it exactly — all 7 `delivery.received` rows are smoke tests:

| when | deliveries | `priced_lines` |
|---|---:|---|
| 2026-07-01 | 3 | **1 each** — someone deliberately expanded a line |
| 2026-08-09 → 08-10 | 4 | **0 across all four** |

And the ledger's one non-seed row — `Banana Peppers $20.00` — **was written by `recordDelivery`**: its `recorded_at` is 97 ms *before* its own `delivery.received` audit row, and the price insert precedes the audit call. The mechanism is proven in production.

Consequence for this seed: `vendor_price_history` is append-only and every reader takes the newest row, so **a real receipt silently outranks a wave-6 estimate the day it lands** — no migration, no backfill, no cleanup of these rows ever needed.

Stated as findings, not fixes — the remedy is a UI decision that deserves its own PR. Also filed there: neither receiving insert (nor `recordSkuPrice`) sets `source`/`source_note`, so a door-entered price is today indistinguishable by column from an admin-entered one.

## What's in the diff

- `lib/angel-wave6.ts` — pure. Reuses wave 1's `computePackUnitPrice` / `exactQuotient` / `parseAngelCatalog` / `rowKey` rather than re-deriving them. Adds `COUNT_AGREES` (a price with no oz basis — Cannoli Shell's per-shell weight is one seed 30 left honestly open, and when our pack *is* Angel's pack no denominator is needed) plus `PACK_CONFLICT`, `NO_OZ_BASIS`, `PACK_SHAPE_OPEN`; reuses waves 1–2's six codes verbatim, because an unchanged reason must keep its name.
- `scripts/seed/34-wave6-price-fill.ts` — I/O shell. Refuses to run on an inconsistent rule table; re-verifies every pack against the **live chain-aware** `contentOzForSku` and drops any SKU whose pack moved under its transcribed divisor; **fresh-authoring only** (skips any SKU already holding a price — supersede belongs to receiving/admin, not a seed), which also makes a re-run a no-op by construction.
- `docs/seed/source/angel-wave6-dryrun.md` — full disposition + § E wiring note.
- `tests/angel-wave6.test.ts` — 28 tests.

## Gates

`next build` ✅ · `tsc --noEmit` ✅ (only the 6 pre-existing leaflet asset-import errors; none in wave-6 files) · `npm test` ✅ **1825 passed / 92 files**.

**DO NOT MERGE, DO NOT `--execute`** — both are Juan's call on the dry-run table.

body:
First live Plane Finder search failed with `Unexpected token '<', "<!DOCTYPE"...` — the research call outlives Cloudflare's ~100-second response timeout, so the tunnel returned an HTML 524 error page and the client tried to parse it as JSON.

Fix: the route now **streams** the response. `PING` heartbeat lines go out every 8 seconds while the research runs (keeping bytes flowing so Cloudflare never times out), and the final line carries `RESULT {json}` or `ERROR {json}`. The client reads the stream and parses the last line. Fast failures (auth, rate limit, missing key) still return plain JSON with proper HTTP statuses before the stream starts. Guards handle client disconnects mid-stream.

Deploy stamp `2026-08-31 plane-finder-stream`.

### Source-address critical option not enforced for non-public-key auth callbacks in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh
[CVE-2026-56854](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-56854) / [GO-2026-6303](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6303)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
The source-address critical option in the Permissions returned by an authentication callback was only enforced for the PublicKeyCallback and VerifiedPublicKeyCallback paths, extending the fix for CVE-2026-46595. Permissions returned by the PasswordCallback, KeyboardInteractiveCallback, NoClientAuthCallback, and GSSAPIWithMICConfig.AllowLogin callbacks were not validated against the client's remote address, so a source-address restriction set by those callbacks was silently ignored. The check is now applied to the Permissions returned by any authentication callback.

Unknown

author: jimjamscott22
body:
## Summary

A senior-frontend-style pass over the current screens (Today, Insights, History/Settings placeholders, onboarding, shared components, theme tokens), focused on making the app optimal for iPhone. Two concrete, verifiable issues came out of it and are fixed here; other observations are lower-priority polish, listed below for visibility rather than acted on in this PR.

- **Accent color failed WCAG AA text contrast.** `colors.ts` already flagged the light palette as unverified. Checking it: the documented `accent` (`#C75D3A`) measured **3.75:1** as body text on `canvas` (used for the onboarding error message) and **4.09:1** as button text (primary button label, secondary/ghost button label, tab bar active label) — both below the 4.5:1 AA minimum for normal-size text. Darkened it to `#AB4F31` (same hue), which clears 4.5:1 in every direction it's used as text. Updated `docs/visual-design.md`'s token table and rationale to match, per AGENTS.md's requirement to keep the governing design doc in sync with a code-level decision change.
- **Loading-state flashes.** The Today screen returned `null` during its initial load (canvas-colored blank screen, no feedback) instead of an indicator, unlike the app's entry gate (`app/index.tsx`). The Insights screen was worse: because it didn't check its own `loading` flag, it briefly rendered "Nothing recorded yet" before the first query resolved, which reads as incorrect information rather than a loading state. Added a small shared `LoadingState` component and used it in the Today screen and the entry gate (removing the duplicated inline spinner there), and added an inline loading indicator to Insights in place of the false-empty flash.

## Other observations (not changed here)

- No pull-to-refresh on Today/Insights — reasonable to add later if returning-from-background staleness becomes a complaint.
- `EventRow`'s time column has a fixed 64pt width; at the largest Dynamic Type accessibility sizes a wrapped time string could crowd the entry text next to it. Worth a look during physical-device Dynamic Type testing (AGENTS.md already calls for this).
- History and Settings are intentionally-scoped placeholders per their own comments referencing `docs/ux-flows.md` — not treated as bugs.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx jest` (47 tests passed)
- [x] `npx expo export --platform ios` (production export succeeds)
- [ ] Physical-iPhone smoke test (Dynamic Type, safe areas, offline launch) — per AGENTS.md, still needed before release and not run here.

body:
Three deletion scopes, owner-decided 2026-08-31. No behaviour change to any live path. After this PR the debate society is the only generation route in the code, and the tree carries no dead agentic remnants.

**43 files changed, +438 / −4621.** backend +326/−4051 · ui +9/−407 · docs +97/−157.

Evidence first: every deletion below was caller-grep-proven *in this branch* before it happened, not inherited from an earlier audit.

---

## Scope 1 — dead agentic remnants (`f2ceabb6`, +95 / −1274)

### 1a. The tool-use loop in `agents/portfolio_agent.py` (930 → 400 lines)

Deleted: `AgentToolCall`, `AgentPortfolio.tool_calls` / `.iterations`, `_anthropic_client`, `propose_portfolio_with_tools`, `MAX_AGENT_ITERATIONS`, `_agent_tools`, `_tool_get_asset_stats`, `_tool_get_correlation`, `_tool_stress_test`, `_execute_tool`, `_summarize_tool_output`, `_build_tool_user_prompt`, `synth_for_display`, and the zero-caller `display_for_synth` alias.

**Caller proof** — whole tree, excluding the module itself:

```
$ grep -rn "propose_portfolio_with_tools\|AgentToolCall\|MAX_AGENT_ITERATIONS\|synth_for_display" \
    backend/ ui/src scripts/ | grep -v "agents/portfolio_agent.py"
(no code hits — only prose in docs/archive/ and point-in-time cost estimates)

$ grep -rn "display_for_synth\|tool_calls\|\.iterations\|AgentPortfolio\|AgentPick" \
    backend/ ui/src scripts/ | grep -v "agents/portfolio_agent.py"
(empty)
```

**Kept, because they have live callers:** `PortfolioAgent`, `get_portfolio_agent`, `propose_portfolio`, `_build_user_prompt`, `_format_strategies`. `agents/generation_pipeline.py` uses the first two behind `_llm_available()` / `_served_model_for()`; `evaluation/stockbench/adapter.py` calls `propose_portfolio`. The module docstring now says exactly that, instead of describing an agent loop that no longer exists.

`services/cost_meter.py` and `docs/generation-cost-instrumentation.md` both documented the deleted loop's `record_llm_call` as *"inert, dead code queued for the follow-up deletion PR."* This is that PR; both now record it as resolved.

`backend/tests/test_portfolio_agent_prompt.py` looped its status-map assertion over `(_build_user_prompt, _build_tool_user_prompt)`. It now asserts against the one surviving builder, with a docstring saying why it changed shape.

### 1b. `services/strategy_guardrail.py` + `services/construction_trace.py` (+ both test files)

**Caller proof** — the only non-test importer of either module was *the other one*:

```
$ grep -rn "strategy_guardrail\|construction_trace" backend/archimedes/
backend/archimedes/services/construction_trace.py:28:from archimedes.services.strategy_guardrail import GuardrailResult
(plus the two generation_json docstring lines)
```

**#1591 / `dbrowneup/1575-paper-trace-pipeline` checked, as asked — no conflict.** The only mention of `construction_trace` on that branch's code is a *prose comment* in `services/paper_trace.py`:

```
paper_trace.py:310:  # NOT construction_trace.UNBOUND_VAULT. That sentinel is a non-blank …
```

It defines its own convention and imports nothing from the deleted module. Every remote branch was swept for real imports; the only hits are the file itself.

### 1c. `ArchitectProposal` / `StrategySelection` in `agents/generation_json.py`

Their only consumers were the two modules deleted in 1b. `extract_json`, `ArchitectCannedBackend` and `default_backend` stay — live in `debate_engine.py`, `strategy_fusion.py` and `services/arxiv_pipeline.py`.

### Docs

`docs/adr/portfolio-constructor-decision-tree.md` describes `portfolio_agent.py` as a `MAX_AGENT_ITERATIONS=12` tool-calling constructor. It gets a **dated note**, not a rewrite: the decision it records (which constructor is the keeper) is unaffected and stands.

---

## Scope 2 — the bypass generation route dies (`87e3db0c`, +265 / −1179)

`docs/adr/debate-society-sole-generation-pipeline.md` has said since 2026-07-09 that the debate society is the only generation pipeline. **It wasn't.** A second live, account-gated, LLM-spending generation route survived the Phase-3 cutover, and its own docstring admitted it:

> "This is a second live, SIWE-gated, LLM-spending generation endpoint."

It was gated only on `ARCHIMEDES_FUSION_ENABLED`, which is `true` in `infra/ecs.tf` and both compose files — i.e. **enabled in every deployed environment.**

The debate path has its own poll route, `GET /api/generate/jobs/{job_id}` in `generate_routes.py`. It is documented as one pair with the POST in `docs/api/strategies-and-rigor.md`. ### The guard the ADR deserves — `backend/tests/test_sole_generation_route_guard.py` (+186)

author: copilot
body:
## Summary

Automated triggers and cron schedules in inactive workflows were causing unexpected run failures and generating noise notifications. This change makes all 36 repository workflows strictly manual, conserving runner resources and silencing automated failure alerts.

## Changes

### Workflow Triggers

- Removed all automatic triggers—including `push`, `pull_request`, `pull_request_target`, `merge_group`, and cron `schedule`—from all workflow files under `.github/workflows/`.
- Retained or introduced `workflow_dispatch` as the sole trigger, preserving any configured job `inputs` to allow on-demand manual execution.

### Concurrency Group Hardening

- Appended a `|| github.run_id` fallback to concurrency groups in modified workflows referencing `github.event.pull_request.number` to prevent queueing or cancellation issues when triggered manually.

## Example

```yaml
# Before:
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, stable]
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 5 * * 2,6'
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: spec-review-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}

# After:
on:
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: spec-review-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}
```

author: patrickcleeve2
body:
Stacked on #689. The GUI half of the who-answered design — [mockup](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/85c7658d-653f-47a0-879c-a104b8cbe067) on the project.

## How it works

A compact strip under the Yes/No buttons, one row per answered (or withdrawn) question, newest first, capped at 6, hidden until it has something to say:

```
agent · declined Run Milling · 14:22:31
you · answered point of interest · 14:21:04
```

Agent rows render in the agent purple (`BORDER_STATE_COLOURS["agent"]` — single source, no new literal). Wording follows the rule from the design thread: **who · what · when** — no wire vocabulary on screen, question types get human names ('confirmation', 'alignment area'), unknown types degrade to their type name rather than to silence.

**One API evolution from #689**: the responder's single observer callable becomes a small observer list — `add_question_observer(cb) -> dispose` — now that the feed has two consumers (the event buffer and this widget). Each observer is exception-isolated: a failing one can break neither the click that caused the event nor the other observers. A plain list rather than a Qt signal deliberately, for exactly that isolation. Hosting subscribes through the same API; its unsubscribe rides the existing disposer list.

The widget is a dumb render of the responder's feed — the same single code path that applies answers — so it can never show something that didn't happen, and there is no 'update the timeline' step to forget.

## Tests

Driven through the real window and both real answer paths: operator rows say 'you', agent rows say 'agent', withdrawn questions show as withdrawn, the strip stays hidden until the first answer and bounded after many. 104 tests green across the responder/prompt/hosting/timeline suites.

author: codys-wright
body:
fix(deps): repin editor and keyflow so task-server can be vendored again

task's deploy pipeline has been red since at least 2026-08-30. Every
`nix build .#task-server` died before compiling anything:

    error: invalid inclusion of reserved file name Cargo.toml.orig
           in package source

editor's crates/mermaid-rs-renderer was vendored by unpacking a published
.crate archive, and the artifacts cargo generates inside such archives
came along with it. Cargo refuses to vendor any package source
containing the reserved name Cargo.toml.orig, so the affected editor tags
cannot be vendored at all.

Fixing it needed the full cross-repo cascade, because task pulled editor
from TWO places at once:

  1. editor      — drop the leftovers, tag v0.0.3
  2. keyflow     — repin editor v0.1.1 -> v0.0.3, tag v0.0.3
                   (task takes editor-keyflow from here, so this repo
                   kept feeding the broken rev back in)
  3. task (here) — repin editor -> v0.0.3 and keyflow -> v0.0.3

Repinning only editor here was not enough: the transitive path through
keyflow still resolved the broken tag. That is the diamond the repo rules
warn about — every repo must pin the SAME tag of a shared dependency.

Verified: `nix build .#task-server` now exits 0.

Tags are 0.0.x on purpose. These are pre-release products and the tags
had climbed well ahead of the crate versions (which all still read
0.1.0), so the new ones deliberately sort below the superseded v0.1.x.

body:
## Summary

Resolves issues #270, #271, #272, and #273 in a single PR.

---

### #273 — Eliminate shared mutable singletons in walletconnect.ts

**Problem:** `_onPairingUri`, `_pendingReject`, and `_sessionProposalHandler` were module-level mutable singletons that caused race conditions under concurrent connect attempts.

**Fix:**
- All pairing state moved into per-connect `PairingContext` objects.
- **Latest-wins:** `connect()` cancels the previous context via `AbortController` before creating a fresh one.
- **Unmount cleanup:** `abortConnect()` scoped to active context only, no global side-effects.
- **`resetWcState()` scoped:** does NOT clear all `wc@2:*` IndexedDB stores.
- `setOnPairingUri` shim preserved for backward compatibility.
- `SignClient` remains intentionally module-level (one WebSocket per app).

Tests: `wc2-context.test.ts` — concurrent connects, abort/unmount, resetWcState scope, shim compatibility.

author: jumarti96
body:
A four-deck run cost ~2.2M tokens (~550k/deck). The skill's prose is only ~27k tokens/run — the cost was what the skill told agents to read, and how many agents read it. Six changes, none of which remove a checklist item, a gate, or a failure mode.

Phase 5B Step 0: three parallel lens sketchers + a shape judge become one skeleton critic. The race was justified by an archetype blind-spotting problem that pinning archetype_family solved two days later; once sketches were builds of ONE archetype it bought nothing. Measured: the judge picked the first-dispatched sketch 4/4 for ~120k tokens/deck. The useful output (weak keystones, harvests) came from adversarial oracle-reading, which one critic does at a quarter of the cost. The critic must return a strongest_alternative argued against the thesis; Challenger item 6 now treats an empty one with no false_choice as BLOCKING, so a rubber-stamping critic fails loudly instead of getting quietly cheaper and worse.

Phase 8: one 439 KB bundle becomes two, split by role. The Proposer never needs the pool or dossier — 77% of what it was reading. grill_proposer.json is 11-35 KB; the Challenger's is ~250 KB after projecting out four fields no checklist item reads. Two files rather than "one bundle you must not read", because a prohibition is a prompt-adherence gamble. Compact separators throughout; nothing parses these by line.

Ship 11 parameterised scripts. The previous generation was re-authored per deck (817 KB across 125 files, including rewrite-debug cycles) and hardcoded DECK_SIZE = 40, a cube slug, a pool-rules dict, a cube-specific land-name table and commander_cards=None. Every one passes a 40-card run and silently produces wrong output on any other format. Each script now reads run_config.json and takes --run/--deck. smoke_test.py drives all of them across all four formats and is the reason that claim is testable.

Seed sweep gains a fourth band. Engine/Outlet and Enabler/Fodder had no band and entered only by cluster accident, hiding Siege Zombie and Cobbled Wings — both wanted, both found later by the Challenger at higher cost. The four bands now cover all six structural roles; still-unreachable count on two live pipelines went to zero.

Artifact hygiene: readable pool dumps banned, export_meta built at Phase 11 for the deck's ~50 cards instead of Phase 0 for all 305, part_deckN merged into sweep.json, approval rounds send changed slots plus gate output rather than the whole list.

Bugs fixed, all verified against the run that produced them:

- structural.py read report["status"]; run_structural_checks emits overall_status at top level (status is the key on each SUB-check). The verdict printed as None and the exit code stuck at 0, so Phase 6b — a HARD gate — could never fail. The smoke test only asserted "no traceback", which cannot tell a working gate from one that never fails; it now requires the printed verdict and the exit code to agree, and runs a negative fixture (a coverage declaration naming a card not in the deck) that must exit 1.

- render_save.py read e["answers"] for the sideboard column; the canonical field is when_to_board, which every saved deck carries and no deck spells "answers". The column rendered empty. The fixture had been written to match the script instead of the spec, which is why four format runs missed it.

- grill deck rows carried no tags, so the Challenger's independent mana_audit re-run computed accel=0 where the builder got a nonzero value and reported a phantom discrepancy — recorded in one deck's permanent record as a tool defect.

- grill deck rows carried no usable_as, so the Proposer could not meet its contract to defend an off-identity card by naming the legalising mode.

- enriched.json leaves mana_cost null on DFCs, zeroing their pip demand and making best_mode reject them as unusable in every colour: 41 cards silently dropped out of the colour gate. build_pool.py now backfills from card_faces[0] permanently.

- the Phase 5C splash check keyed on raw color_identity and wrongly flagged core-castable cards such as Lingering Souls; it now requires best_mode to return None.

- dump_json creates the per-deck directory, which seed_sweep is the first to write into at Phase 5A. Requiring the orchestrator to mkdir it first is an instruction it can silently skip.

Verified: smoke test green on 40-card, 60-card, commander-60 and commander-100; pytest 96 passed; the full script chain re-run against all four saved Lifegain decks.
