author: syatsuzuka
body:
## Summary
- On Docker Desktop (notably macOS), the bind-mounted repo inside the container can appear
  owned by a different UID than the container user even with `--user "$(id -u):$(id -g)"`,
  triggering git's dubious-ownership safety check.
- Specmatic's git wrapper doesn't surface that real error — it reports a misleading
  `Unexpected error ... Could not access 'origin/main'` instead, which made this hard to
  diagnose from the console output alone.
- Add `-e GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 -e GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=safe.directory -e GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0='*'`
  to the documented `backward-compatibility-check` docker commands (Part B and Part D,
  Unix/Mac and Windows) so the mounted repo is trusted without needing a writable `$HOME`
  for `git config --global`.
- Additionally, run the check with `-w /workspace/backward-compatibility-testing` plus the
  new `--repo-dir /workspace` flag, so the generated `build/` HTML/CTRF report lands under
  `backward-compatibility-testing/build/` (matching other labs like `api-coverage`) instead
  of at the top of the `labs` repo, which is invisible if an editor only has the lab
  subfolder open.
- Document the symptom under "Common confusion points" so future users can self-diagnose.

## Test plan
- [x] Reproduced the original failure on macOS Docker Desktop (`Could not access 'origin/main'`)
- [x] Confirmed root cause via `git status` inside the container (`detected dubious ownership`)
- [x] Re-ran the updated Part B command and confirmed it produces the expected `(INCOMPATIBLE)` verdict
- [x] Re-ran the updated Part D command and confirmed `(COMPATIBLE)` verdict after the fix
- [x] Confirmed the HTML/CTRF report is now written to `backward-compatibility-testing/build/reports/...` instead of the repo root

body: Lane F1 of wave 17. Three issues, one commit each, plus one commit for the review-gate findings. ## An owner action can target a superseded scope root after a write rotation **Mechanism.** Every owner action named its target scope root by re-deriving `derive_write_name(cachedWriteScopeSeed, scopeId)`. A write wave moves the root and the cache lags the wave until an adopt re-deposits the fresh seed. In that window the derivation named the **superseded** root. The demoted party keeps the write-name key for that name, so a replayed owner-signed commitment answers there. A second `Revoke` or `RotateNow` then passed `authorize_cut`, drove a full cut at a name no survivor reads, returned `Ok(Done)` for a revocation that did not happen, and raised the durable read-epoch floor off that record. **What landed.** The engine holds `current_root_name`, the `ipnsName` the vault root scope publishes under. Cold start, a first-run mint, a pointer consult, and a wave over the root scope all move that cell, and the wave moves it before anything fallible runs. `vault_root_scope` proves the derivation against it and refuses with `ContentUnavailable { message: "held-write-seed-does-not-name-the-current-root" }` - the read-side twin of the deposit-time proof `deposit_write_seed` already makes. One `seed_names` predicate serves both sides. The cell is the tick loop's only source for the root it polls, so a pass after a local wave polls the moved root rather than the name cold start opened with. **Verdict class.** The refusal answers `ContentUnavailable`, not `MalformedInput`. The condition is a session-local lag that the next adopt clears, so it is retryable availability rather than a refusal of host-supplied bytes, and the absent-seed refusal one line above already answers the same class. Both review gates asked for this. It removes the verdict-label complaint the gates recorded against the second item of #1359; that item's own cases, the rotation classifier's `TrustViolation` and `Seam` mappings, stay open there. **Tests.** `an_owner_action_refuses_while_the_cached_seed_names_the_superseded_root` drives a real downgrade over the vault root scope, asserts the next owner action refuses, asserts nothing published at the superseded name, and asserts a tick that adopts at the moved root clears the refusal. `a_cut_whose_floor_raise_fails_still_refuses_the_next_owner_action` injects a floor-store failure after the wave published and asserts the refusal still stands. Both return `Ok(Done)` without the guard. ## Hand out this member's own contact code so an exchange can complete **Mechanism.** Contact exchange is symmetric, but only the inbound half existed. `ImportContact` takes a peer's code and nothing produced this member's own. A member who opened the share dialog could import a contact and could not give one, so no exchange completed unless the other party already held a CipherBox-minted code. **What landed.** `SharingView` gained `own_contact_code`, the self-authenticating `{identityPk, encSubkey, bindingSig}` bundle `SessionIdentity::contact_code` mints - the same one the invite-claim path already carries. It rides the sharing read the dialog already takes, so it costs no new channel. The value is public material and derives nothing outside the frozen KDF catalog. The field crosses `crates/wasm` as `ownContactCode` and `packages/client` as `SharingDescriptor.ownContactCode`. The web import step renders it as hex beside the paste field, with the existing copy control - the same encoding `sharing/contactCode.ts` parses, so an exchange round-trips. **Tests.** A wasm boundary test asserts the code crosses as a `Uint8Array` and imports cleanly as a contact. A `readSharing` test asserts the code survives a scope the read could not reach. A web test asserts the dialog shows the hex code and its copy control. ## Settle read-grant grantee write-epoch vs empty write-history-link semantics **Mechanism.** `mint_grantee_scope` minted the grantee scope root with the parent scope's write epoch and `WriteHistory::Carried(&[])`. `WriteBody` documents an empty `writeHistoryLink` as the state at write epoch 1, so a folder that had rotated advertised an epoch above 1 with no link to walk back to. **What landed.** The mint pins write epoch 1 and `GranteeScopePlan` no longer takes the parent's epoch. The chosen answer is the pin rather than a doc, because a write grant now draws a fresh `writeScopeSeed`: the granted scope genuinely leaves the parent's write plane. The durable write-epoch floor does not refute the pin. A node the parent index already names as a scope root is refused as a share target, so a fresh grantee scope id carries no floor of its own. The grant-time cut then advances that plane from 1 to 2, which no floor blocks. **Tests.** `a_granted_scope_mints_at_write_epoch_one_however_far_the_parent_has_rotated` mints under a parent at write epoch 2 and asserts the grantee root publishes at 1. ## Notes for review - `crates/engine/tests/owner_actions.rs` is the only suite with the seeded-vault plus grant-row harness a real root write wave needs, so both new integration tests live there rather than in `crates/engine/tests/facade.rs`. - The encode side does not yet refuse `WriteHistory::Carried(empty)` paired with a write epoch above 1. `ResealSeeds::check_history_descends` is that invariant's home and it covers `Cut` only. That file belongs to another lane this wave, so #1565 carries it. Closes #1358. Closes #1407. Closes #771. > [!NOTE] > ### Prove owner actions against current root name and expose member's contact code in `SharingView` > - `Engine` now tracks `current_root_name` in shared state across cold starts, mints, and rotations; the tick loop reads it each pass instead of receiving it as an argument. > - `vault_root_scope` refuses owner actions with `ContentUnavailable` (`HELD_SEED_NOT_AT_CURRENT_ROOT`) when the held write seed does not derive the current root name; on success it uses `current_root_name` directly rather than re-deriving from the seed. > - After a root rotation, `current_root_name` updates immediately before subsequent fallible steps so later operations reference the new name. > - `SharingView` gains `own_contact_code` populated via `SessionIdentity::contact_code()`, exposed through the WASM getter `ownContactCode`, threaded through `SharingDescriptor`, the sharing store (as hex or null), and rendered in `ContactImportForm`. > - `GranteeScopePlan` loses its `write_epoch` field; `mint_and_publish` hardcodes `write_epoch` to 1 for newly minted grantee scopes regardless of parent epoch. > - Risk: `vault_root_scope` behavior change means cached write seeds naming a superseded root will fail owner actions until a tick re-adopts the current root; reviewers should check `seed_names` in [facade.rs](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box/pull/1564/files#diff-76615117c8cac0cf4673ee8bdad7503af14a9f6988afc51f66d3f31b82325238) and the `HELD_SEED_NOT_AT_CURRENT_ROOT` refusal path. `GranteeScopePlan` struct change removes the `write_epoch` field; all in-tree call sites in [create.rs](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box/pull/1564/files#diff-970653ffd561e97cde3d6b2bc26670f3e274d43faed73fc8542fd6dc6d4717c0) and [invite_mint.rs](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box/pull/1564/files#diff-e65a9ec521a9cc36144a7d2746d82e50ba1ff01281a3dad4ce3595a383c9f920) are updated. > > > > Macroscope summarized bf02b0c. > >

author: deathcharge
body:
## Outcome
Signed-member moderation is now exercised through two real Uvicorn processes sharing PostgreSQL. Fix socket ownership races exposed by deterministic manager regressions.

## Implementation
- Detach before physical close; reject late sends and stale queued broadcast snapshots using the original registration lock.
- Unknown/detached send returns false, duplicate close is inert, duplicate active registration is rejected. Failed sends attempt bounded physical close (1013).
- Real-process tests cover freeze/unfreeze, mute/unmute, ban/unban, reconnect denial, archive/reopen/history, unaffected peers and same-subject unrelated-room isolation.
- Document embedding compatibility, asynchronous remote teardown, evidence, and named remaining release gates.

## Regression and verification evidence
- Six new manager cases failed on baseline (6 failed / 8 passed); strengthened failed-send assertion also failed before its fix.
- python -m ruff check .; python -m ruff format --check .; python -m mypy samsarix_chat_engine; git diff --check: pass.
- python -m pytest -q tests/test_connection_manager.py tests/test_conversation_controls.py tests/test_postgres_runtime.py --timeout=30: 32 passed.
- python -m pytest -q -m "not postgres" --timeout=60: 180 passed, 61 deselected.
- Implementation 92bc2c8: all ten CI jobs pass, 241 tests / 88.55% coverage; dedicated PostgreSQL job 61 passed. https://github.com/Deathcharge/samsarix-chat-engine/actions/runs/33383479399
- CI also verifies Python 3.10-3.14/Linux, Windows 3.12, dependency audit, package build/metadata/installed-wheel smoke, TypeScript client, and container smoke.
- Live PostgreSQL and Docker are unavailable locally; their evidence comes from CI. Final documentation follow-up must pass CI before merge.

## Boundaries and follow-up
A send already started can finish before close. Administrative HTTP success does not mean all remote sockets have physically closed. Initial-handshake failure/cancellation cleanup and archive versus lease-renewal ordering remain explicit P1 follow-ups, alongside the v0.13 lag, contention, failure, load/soak, and backup/rollback gates. PostgreSQL remains guarded/unreleased; supported v0.12 remains single-process SQLite. No schema/dependency/license change, publication, production deployment, or paid resource.

author: mgfv2r2mpv-hash
body:
Phase 1 shipped the whole server half of the login store and no way to reach it. This adds the browser half: a **sign-in screen**, a **set-a-new-password screen**, and a **people screen** for administrators.

## What is here

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `auth/portalAuth.ts` | The only place that talks to `/api/auth` and `/api/admin`. No React. |
| `auth/AuthGate.tsx` | Decides which screen stands in front of the app. |
| `auth/SignInScreen.tsx` | Sign in, plus the first-run panel that makes the first administrator. |
| `auth/ChangePasswordScreen.tsx` | Both modes: on a change ticket, and on a live session. |
| `auth/UserAdminScreen.tsx` | The people table: add, turn off, reissue a temporary password. |
| `auth/AccountMenu.tsx` | Replaces `LogoutLink.tsx`. |
| `auth/TempPasswordNotice.tsx` | The once-only password box. |
| `auth/auth.css` | Everything the three screens need that `portal.css` did not already provide. |

## Three decisions worth reading

**A deployment with no `PORTAL_DB` renders the app untouched.** `readSession` reports `unconfigured` for a 503, and the gate passes straight through to `<WebApp />`. Cloudflare Access stays the only gate wherever the binding is absent, exactly as before this PR. `AuthGate.test.tsx` pins it.

**The first-run panel is not a convenience.** `decideAdmin` admits an Access-authenticated caller to `POST /api/admin/users` only while `listUsers()` is empty, and demands an administrator *session* from then on, with no fallback to Access. Without a screen offering that creation, the first administrator could only be made by hand-writing an HTTP request, and the one person who has to do that is the one person who is not in yet.

**The client restates no server rule.** `ChangePasswordScreen` imports `checkNewPassword`, `describeRejection` and `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH` from `functions/lib/authPolicy.ts`, which is pure and imports nothing. Raising the minimum on the server moves the client and both sets of tests with it. Refusals carry the server's own sentence rather than a client-side paraphrase.

## The one layout defect, and its guard

The people table dragged the whole page **269px sideways at 390px** in Chromium. The `.sr-only` span naming the actions column is `position: absolute`; without a positioned ancestor it resolved against the initial containing block, escaped the scroll box's clip, and landed at the table's full width in page coordinates. `.auth-table-scroll` now declares `position: relative`.

No jsdom test can measure that, so `auth.layout.test.tsx` reads back the three facts that together cause it, and says plainly that it proves the ingredients and not the pixels. It fails against this branch with the one line removed.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run` - **634 passing, 60 files** (was 568/54; +66 tests, +6 files)
- [x] `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:test` in `webportal` - clean
- [x] `npm run build` in `webportal` - clean
- [x] Chromium against a stubbed server, five screens x 320/390/768/1024/1440/1920: zero page-level horizontal scroll everywhere; the people table scrolls inside its own box below 1024 and fits outright above
- [x] Light and dark read correctly on all five screens
- [ ] After merge and deploy: create the first administrator from the live site **while Access still signs you in**, then relax the Access application. That order, not the other one.

## Still open, and not in this PR

- Whether the login form should carry Turnstile.
- `dev.sassi-cal-webportal.pages.dev` is not inside the Access application and shares the production login store. That is a dashboard fix: add the branch alias to the Access application.

author: eldad-caura
body:
The gate checks that a statement is **bound** to a tenant. It never checked that the caller cannot **rewrite the column it is bound on**. Three defects went through it in a week on exactly that gap:

| | method | the filter it had |
|---|---|---|
| #1081 / #1119 | `entity_update` | `if hasattr(entity, key): setattr(…)` |
| #1118 / #1122 | `memory_update` | `if hasattr(Memory, key)` in a comprehension |
| #1121 / #1129 | `fleet_upsert_node` | `if k not in ("tenant_id", "node_name")` |

Each built an `UPDATE ... SET` from a caller-controlled dict and admitted `id`, so the statement became `SET id = <caller's choice> WHERE id = :id AND tenant_id = :tenant` — predicate satisfied, primary key moved. **The last two were correctly tenant-bound the whole time**, so checks 1–3 had nothing to object to. The defect lives one layer below where the gate was looking.

### Three parts, three different failures

They are not redundant — each catches a mode the others miss:

1. **AST discovery** names every method building an UPDATE from caller keys and requires it to be registered. This is what `entity_update` and `memory_update` failed: no filter at all.
2. **Reference check** requires the method to actually mention the constant it is registered for, so the registry stays a *reading* of the code rather than a claim about it. Without it, a method could revert to `hasattr` while the registry still named the right constant and both other parts would pass.
3. **Runtime check** resolves each constant and asserts it admits none of the model's primary key, tenant-scope, or database-maintained columns — read off the model, so a schema change moves them without anyone editing this file. This is what `fleet_upsert_node` failed, carrying a filter that looked deliberate.

### What is deliberately not a site

`INSERT` is excluded. Naming the id of a row you are *creating* collides rather than overwrites, so no existing row moves — the defect is an existing row's identity changing under it. That cut keeps `relation_add`, `agent_add` and `agent_activity_digest_upsert` off the list. A loop over written-out column names is also not a site, which keeps `agent_add`'s second write off it. Both boundaries are pinned by tests, because flagging safe methods is how a registry fills with lines nobody reads.

The heuristic is biased the way the route classifier already is, and for the reason its docstring gives: it would rather name a method that turns out to be safe — one registry line a reviewer can delete — than miss one that is not, which is invisible.

### No allowlist

The invariant has no exceptions today. One with none does not need a file to hold them, and the first should be argued in review rather than added by `--write`.

### Validation

**Replayed against history.** Run against `postgres_service.py` as it stood before each fix, the check flags exactly the methods still defective at that commit — three, then two, then one. It would have caught all three.

**Sabotage, one per failure mode**, each confirmed to flip the gate red and back:

- widen a constant to admit the primary key → *"may write FleetNode.id (primary key)"*
- point a method back at `hasattr` while leaving its registration → *"registered as guarded by … but does not mention it"*
- add a new unregistered caller-keyed UPDATE → *"builds an UPDATE from caller-supplied keys … no registered identity guard"*
- leave a registration behind after a method stops qualifying → *"registered … but no longer builds an UPDATE"*

11 new tests, all failing on the parent commit, covering those four modes plus the decision boundary of the AST pass.

### It does not fail anything in flight

author: unbraind
body: `github/codeql-action/init` and `github/codeql-action/analyze` must carry the **same** version within a workflow. Dependabot opens them as two separate pull requests, so each one alone leaves the pair mismatched and the `codeql` check fails on **both**. Neither can go green by itself — the pair is a standing deadlock that has to be broken by hand on every codeql-action release. Measured 2026-08-31 in [unbraind/pm-gantt-chart#87](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-gantt-chart/pull/87) and [#88](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-gantt-chart/pull/88): `codeql` is the only failing check on each, with every other check green. This adds a Dependabot group for `github/codeql-action*` so both bumps arrive in a single pull request and move together. Five repositories in the fleet already had this (`pm-beads`, `pm-brief`, `pm-context`, `pm-csv`, `pm-web`); the rest did not, which is why the deadlock keeps recurring. The change is scoped to this repository's own `.github/dependabot.yml` — the existing schedule, limits and npm entry are untouched. pm item: [pm-starter-55ul](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-starter/blob/main/.agents/pm/issues/pm-starter-55ul.toon) --- ## Summary by cubic Groups Dependabot bumps for `github/codeql-action` so the `init` and `analyze` steps update together, and adds a CodeQL workflow so the repository actually gets scanned. Previously Dependabot opened a separate PR for each action, and because both must carry the same version in a workflow, each PR alone left the pair mismatched and failed the `codeql` check on both. This repository also ran no CodeQL workflow at all, so the group alone would have been a no-op. The new group in `.github/dependabot.yml` makes both bumps arrive in one PR; the new `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` scans `javascript-typescript` on push, pull request, and a weekly cron unique to this repo. The existing schedule, open-PR limit, and npm entry are unchanged. Written for commit 0c1f1d7a9ef44bb81ad2bb807e6d391f271244e9. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by Sourcery Add CodeQL scanning and keep its action dependencies synchronized through grouped Dependabot updates. New Features: - Add a CodeQL workflow to perform scheduled and change-triggered JavaScript/TypeScript static analysis. Bug Fixes: - Ensure CodeQL action updates are grouped into a single Dependabot pull request so paired actions remain on the same version. CI: - Configure CodeQL scanning with repository permissions, concurrency controls, and weekly scheduled execution. Documentation: - Document the new CodeQL coverage and Dependabot grouping fixes in the unreleased changelog.

author: arena-ai-coding-agent[bot]
body:
Implements #153.

## Summary

EDU-081 — Builder Immutability Reflection — **frontend-only** implementation.

After a Course reaches `PUBLISHED`, the Course Builder is reachable in a state where its structural mutation controls are still presented as editable controls, while the backend already enforces Course immutability (`409 — Published or archived Course is read-only`). This PR adds the corresponding frontend reflection per `ARCHITECTURE.md §10 — Course Publication Immutability` and the owner-approved UX contract (Issue #153 comment).

**No backend files are touched.** No new endpoint, no new route, no new state-management mechanism, no new ADR, no `ARCHITECTURE.md` changes.

## Behaviour

- Course status is obtained exclusively from the existing `courseApi.get` / `courseKeys.detail` server state via TanStack Query — the same Course detail query already populated and invalidated by the CoursePage publish flow. No duplicated local Course status.
- **DRAFT** — existing behavior fully preserved: create/edit/save/delete and attach/detach work; `Load more` works.
- **PUBLISHED** — Builder stays readable and navigable; all Course-structure mutation controls remain visible but become `disabled` (create/update/delete, attach/detach, and the editable inputs); a visible `Published — read-only` indicator is shown (existing `.state` convention).
- **ARCHIVED** — same as PUBLISHED with `Archived — read-only`; permanently read-only, no reactivation UI.
- Disabled controls cannot initiate mutation requests: buttons/inputs are `disabled` **and** mutation handlers early-return when read-only.
- Remains available: navigation (`Back to Course/Sections/Learning Units`), `Open Units`, `Open Activities`, `Edit Content`, `Load more` (pagination is a read), and all list rendering.
- `TeacherAssessmentReviewEntry` is **not** changed (assessment review is not a Course-structure mutation per §10).

## Files changed (all under `apps/frontend/src/modules/education/`)

- `SectionPage.tsx` — course-status query, read-only disabling of create/update/delete, banner, handler guards.
- `LearningUnitPage.tsx` — same reflection for Learning Units.
- `ActivityPage.tsx` — same reflection for Activities; passes `readOnly` to `ActivityContentPanel`.
- `ActivityContentPanel.tsx` — new `readOnly` prop (default `false`); attach select/button and Remove disabled in read-only mode; `Edit Content` link and `Load more` stay enabled.
- `SectionPage.test.tsx`, `LearningUnitPage.test.tsx`, `ActivityPage.test.tsx`, `ActivityContentPanel.test.tsx` — extended with DRAFT/PUBLISHED/ARCHIVED coverage including assertions that **no POST/PATCH/DELETE requests are sent** in read-only modes, and that status comes from the existing Course detail query.

## Validation

- `npm test` — 181 passed (23 files)
- `npm run typecheck` — passed
- `npm run build` — passed
- `git diff --check` — clean
- `git diff -- apps/backend` — empty
- `git diff -- shared` / `apps/frontend/src/shared` — empty

Per the repo workflow the PR is **not** merged; merge authority remains with the Project Architect / Human Project Owner.

## Резюме от Sourcery

Сделано так, чтобы интерфейс конструктора курса точно отражал неизменяемость опубликованных курсов.

Новые возможности:
- Неизменяемость опубликованных и архивных курсов отражается во всём интерфейсе конструктора курса: отображаются заметные индикаторы режима «только для чтения», при этом сохраняются навигация и доступ к просмотру.

Исправления ошибок:
- Предотвращены запросы на изменение структуры разделов, учебных блоков, активностей и связанного контента, если курс опубликован или находится в архиве.

Улучшения:
- Для единообразного управления возможностью редактирования в конструкторе используется существующее серверное состояние сведений о курсе без дублирования статуса курса локально.

Тесты:
- Добавлено покрытие для поведения конструктора в режимах черновика, опубликованного и архивного курса, включая отключённые элементы управления, сохранённые навигацию и постраничную навигацию в режиме «только для чтения», а также отсутствие запросов на изменение.

<details>
<summary>Original summary in English</summary>

## Summary by Sourcery

Make the Course Builder accurately reflect Course publication immutability in the frontend.

New Features:
- Reflect published and archived Course immutability across the frontend Course Builder with visible read-only status indicators while preserving navigation and read access.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent structural mutation requests for sections, learning units, activities, and linked content when their Course is published or archived.

Enhancements:
- Use the existing Course detail server state to consistently control Builder editability without duplicating Course status locally.

Tests:
- Add coverage for draft, published, and archived Builder behavior, including disabled controls, preserved read-only navigation and pagination, and absence of mutation requests.

Adds a standing regression for low-level read-only browser/CDP calls whose result scope can escape the intended Ego task space/profile. Motivated by citrolabs/ego-lite#319, where Storage.getCookies from a secondary profile can expose the default profile cookie jar.

Safety: regression/validator only. No permission expansion, browser write actions, credential handling, relay, or architecture change.

Expected behavior: do not treat read-only as inherently safe; prefer page/origin-scoped helpers and fail closed before retrieving browser-global sensitive session data.

body:
## 무엇을 마무리했나

30일째 멈춰 있던 **정정 2건**과, 한 번도 채워진 적 없는 것처럼 보고되던 **원장 3건**을 해소했습니다. 둘 다 세션 중 경고로만 스쳐 지나갔던 항목입니다.

## 1. CORR-260801-001/002 — 원인은 원출처가 아니라 코드였습니다

두 정정은 2026-08-01부터 `pending`이었고 사유가 **"원출처 quote 재확인 필요"**였습니다. 확인 결과 **원출처는 문제가 아니었습니다.**

예측 파일은 `market_implied`를 **퍼센트**로 기록합니다 — TEMPLATE이 `market_implied: <시장내재확률 % | null>`로 명시합니다. 반면 `benchmark_ledger`의 `market_prob` 컬럼은 **정본 분수**입니다. 그런데 `resolver.py`는

```python
"llm_prob":    round(r["probability"] / 100.0, 4),   # 변환 O
"market_prob": round(float(mi), 4),                  # 변환 X  ← 버그
```

그래서 22가 `22.0`으로, 5가 `5.0`으로 기록됐고 ingest가 `[0,1]` 범위 밖이라 **Q1 격리**했으며 `market_brier`가 484.0·25.0이라는 불가능한 값이 됐습니다.

**근거는 저장소 안의 불변 기록입니다.**

| 근거 | 내용 |
|---|---|
| r1 본문 | "시장내재: 선물(FedWatch) 약 30% vs 예측시장 15% → **시장내재 블렌드 22%**" |
| r4 본문 | "**Polymarket 인상버킷 합산 5%**" |
| DB `market_implied` | polymarket **0.053** @ 2026-07-19T22:55 — r4를 독립 교차확인 |

→ 정정값 **0.22 / 0.05**, Brier **0.0484 / 0.0025** (outcome=0).

**과거 행은 그대로 둡니다.** `benchmark_ledger`는 E7 append-only, `corrections.csv`는 E9로 행 수정을 거부하므로, 정정은 `CORR-260831-005/006`으로 **append**했고 두 행은 격리 상태를 유지합니다 — 그게 올바른 안전장치입니다.

**중요한 건 재발 차단입니다.** 오늘 기록한 예측 2건(`fomc-2026-12-09-hike` 52, `fomc-2026-10-28-hike` 27)이 모두 퍼센트라 해소 시 같은 버그가 그대로 재현될 상태였습니다.

### 테스트가 버그를 통과시키고 있었습니다

`test_ws2_benchmark` 픽스처가 `probability=40`(퍼센트)에 `market_implied=0.2`(분수)를 넣고 있었습니다. 한 픽스처 안에서 단위가 엇갈려 있었고, 그래서 변환 누락이 통과했습니다. `20`으로 바로잡았고 단언은 그대로입니다.

## 2. 원장 3건 — 파일은 있는데 날짜를 못 읽고 있었습니다

`ipo_reference_batch_receipts`·`ipo_reference_batch_status`·`timeseries_shadow_forecasts`가 `latest_date=None`으로 **한 번도 채워진 적 없는 것처럼** 보고되고 있었습니다. 실제로는 파일이 존재하고 내용도 있었으며, 날짜 키 이름이 달랐을 뿐입니다(`checked_at`, `as_of`).

레지스트리는 이미 `timestamp_field`를 선언할 수 있는데 `_dates`가 **CSV에만** 적용하고 json/jsonl은 키를 하드코딩하고 있었습니다.

**덮어쓰기가 아니라 fallback으로 구현했습니다.** `realty_o_entry_cohort_archive`가 `generated_at`을 선언하면서 `asof`도 갖고 있어, 덮어쓰면 데이터 기준일(2026-07-30) 대신 생성 시각(2026-08-04)을 읽어 **신선도를 과대평가**합니다. 하드코딩 키가 있으면 그쪽이 우선하도록 해 기존 동작을 전혀 바꾸지 않았고, 해당 원장의 `latest_date`가 2026-07-30로 유지됨을 실측 확인했습니다.

| 원장 | 이전 | 이후 |
|---|---|---|
| `ipo_reference_batch_receipts` | None | 2026-08-19 |
| `ipo_reference_batch_status` | None | 2026-08-19 |
| `timeseries_shadow_forecasts` | None / stalled | 2026-08-28 / **accumulating** |
| `realty_o_entry_cohort_archive` | 2026-07-30 | **2026-07-30 (불변)** |

stalled 11 → **9**.

## 3. 부수 — 캘리브레이션 리포트

`reports/calibration.html`이 2026-07-20 이후 재생성되지 않고 있었습니다. 지금 갱신돼 **예측 21→51건, 해소 2→8건**을 반영합니다.

## 검증

`pytest src/tests` **942 passed, 7 skipped** · `verify_track_record.py` PASS(A급 30) · `sync --check` · `inventory --check` · `audit-ledgers --check` · `provider-guard` · `security-check` 전부 OK.

회귀 테스트 2종 추가: 단위 변환 고정(옛 표현이 되살아나면 실패), `timestamp_field` fallback 동작(덮어쓰기가 되면 실패).

## 남은 미완결 항목

| 항목 | 상태 |
|---|---|
| `codex/scenario-v4-pr3-remediation` | 706줄 충돌, 비활성 shadow 대상 — **사용자 결정** |
| `codex/work` | 미머지 예측 7건 보유(원장 편입 불가), 보존 중 |
| 블루프린트 Q1·Q3·Q5·Q6·Q7 | 표본·권리검토 조건 미충족 — 시간 필요 |
| P3 게이트 9/50 | 해소 표본 축적 필요 |

author: koojunhwi
body:
## 작업 내용

BE `docs/specs/44` — [참고안·근거의 언어 — 질의한 언어로 응답 내용이 표시된다](https://github.com/Cure-Agent/cure-agent-be/blob/main/docs/specs/44-guidance-evidence-language.md)의 **FE 범위(수용 기준 25~38)** 구현입니다. BE 쪽은 [`#391`](https://github.com/Cure-Agent/cure-agent-be/pull/391)에서 착지했고, 계약은 #89로 이미 동기화됐습니다.

**채팅 화면의 「내용물」이 UI 토글이 아니라 그 메시지의 `responseLang`을 따르게 합니다.** §42가 답변 언어를 입력 문장에서 유도해 놓고 FE는 표시를 토글로 갈랐기 때문에, 한국어 토글로 영문 질의를 하면 **영어 답변 옆에 한국어 인용이 서 있었습니다**(프로덕션 관측). 이 제품이 파는 것은 근거가 답을 지지하는지 확인할 수 있다는 **대조 가능성**인데, 답과 근거의 언어가 다르면 그 대조가 깨집니다 — 근거의 언어는 자기가 딛고 선 답변을 따라야 합니다.

§42의 FE 판단(「표시 언어는 화면이 아니라 사람의 설정」)을 이 스텝이 뒤집습니다.

## 변경 사항

**표시 언어의 축**
- `assistant/page.tsx`가 근거 패널의 콘텐츠 언어를 함께 들고, `chat-panel`이 메시지마다 `responseLang`을 내립니다. 스트림 중에는 방금 보낸 질의에서 유도한 값(`state.responseLang`), 재조회에서는 저장된 `message.responseLang`이 그 자리를 잇습니다.
- 한 대화에 ko·en이 섞이면 **각 블록이 자기 언어로** 섭니다. `responseLang`이 없는 과거 메시지는 `ko`로 읽습니다.
- **경계**: 「인용 근거」 패널 제목·검토 폼·입력창·예시 질의문·지침 탐색기는 **UI 토글을 유지**합니다. 한국어 UI 사용자가 영문 질의 한 번에 자기가 누를 버튼까지 영어가 되는 것은 과합니다. 반대로 근거에 밀착한 **「미번역」 배지는 콘텐츠 편**입니다 — 경계 선언은 그 콘텐츠의 것입니다.

**한국어가 남던 자리**
- 근거 전문에 `recommendationTextTranslated` 표시 — 권고문에 번역이 생겨 배지가 항목 단위로만 남습니다.
- 펼침 헤더의 `sectionPathTranslated`를 **세 경로 모두**(근거 패널·저장된 인용·참고안 인용)에 적용. 하나만 채우면 `Osteoporosis CPG · v1.0 · Ⅳ. 권고사항`처럼 한 줄에서 언어가 갈립니다.
- 지침 목록 제목의 `titleTranslated`.
- 권고등급·근거수준 라벨 문구표(`shared/i18n/rating-label.ts`) — 프로덕션 전량이 6종뿐인 닫힌 어휘입니다. **모르는 라벨은 원문 그대로** 남깁니다(`code`가 함께 보여 대조는 깨지지 않습니다).

**정본 도달 경로**
- 「한국어 원문 보기」 인라인 토글과 `showKoreanOriginal`·`hideKoreanOriginal` 키를 제거하고 **원문 링크(`sourceUrl`)로 대체**했습니다. 계약이 이미 `pageStart`·`pageEnd`까지 실어 정본에 더 정확히 닿고, 카드마다 상태와 문구를 하나씩 늘리지 않습니다. §42 기준 35의 **요구는 유지하고 충족 수단만** 옮긴 것입니다.

**캐시**
- `lang`을 react-query 키와 쿼리에 함께 싣습니다 — 키가 같으면 언어를 바꿔도 이전 응답이 남습니다.
- `useEvidenceDetail`·`useGuidelines`의 언어 인자를 **선택이 아니라 필수**로 뒀습니다. 안 넘기면 조용히 한국어가 되는 것이 BE 쪽 결함의 구조적 원인이었습니다.

**계약 변경 없음** — 소비만 늘었습니다(`openapi/`·`generated/` diff 0). 신규 엔드포인트 0.

## 수용 기준 ↔ 테스트 매핑

동결 커밋 `60ceda88` (작성: Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`/max, 5개 파일 **31건**). 스텁 상태에서 31건 전부 개별 RED임을 확인한 뒤 동결했고, 구현 후 동결 무결성 감사 **diff 0**입니다.

author: brunoofarias
body:
## Contexto e objetivo

- Demanda: tornar a configuração Hermes reproduzível compatível com QA assíncrono e com uma política canônica de pull requests.
- Problema: dependências de QA, agentes aninhados e retestes integrais criavam ociosidade e handoffs sem reduzir o risco proporcionalmente.

## Solução implementada

- DEV é liberado imediatamente para trabalho independente depois de entregar uma unidade ao QA.
- Contratos estáveis, mocks e adapters liberam implementação antecipada; gates upstream ficam no QA integrado, merge ou ativação.
- Cada perfil executa diretamente com seu modelo/provider, sem Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor ou outro agente aninhado.
- Defeitos reais criam correção e reteste proporcional; metadata do PR é corrigida diretamente pelo QA.
- QA de código não depende de deploy: smoke de ambiente fica em gate pós-review/merge e requer autorização humana.
- Arquitetura produz fatias verticais pequenas, verificáveis e empilháveis e simula a ocupação dos DEVs.
- Nova variável obrigatória `HWF_PR_POLICY` torna idioma, títulos e modelos configuráveis por organização.
- PRs públicos não expõem perfis, IDs internos, executores, modelos, fallback, quota ou detalhes da orquestração.
- Templates de PO, arquitetura, DEV, QA e orquestrador foram alinhados.

## Contratos e compatibilidade

- Manifestos existentes precisam preencher `HWF_PR_POLICY` no arquivo local antes da próxima instalação/atualização gerada.
- O schema principal permanece na versão 1; nenhuma credencial ou informação de empresa foi adicionada.
- Boards existentes não são alterados automaticamente pelo kit.

## Dados e migrações

Não se aplica — não há banco ou migração de dados. A atualização afeta somente renderização futura de perfis.

## Segurança e privacidade

- `HWF_PR_POLICY` contém apenas instruções ou referência documental, nunca tokens.
- O validador de credenciais continua ativo.
- Isolamento entre organizações e gates humanos foram preservados.

## Observabilidade e operação

- Changelog documenta a alteração.
- O reteste em novo card permanece para defeitos reais, com escopo proporcional ao impacto.

## Testes e evidências

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: 3/3 aprovados.
- Renderização confirma `HWF_PR_POLICY`, execução direta, fatias verticais, QA editorial e gate de ambiente pós-review.
- `python3 -m json.tool deployment.local.example.json`: aprovado.
- `git diff --check`: aprovado.

## Critérios de aceite

| Critério | Como foi atendido | Evidência |
|---|---|---|
| QA assíncrono | Regras nos cinco perfis | Teste de renderização |
| Reteste sem `active_pr` | Novo card `qa_retest` | Template de QA |
| Execução sem agentes aninhados | Modelo/provider do próprio perfil | Templates e teste de renderização |
| Implementação antecipada segura | Contratos/mocks movem gate para QA/integrado | Templates de arquitetura e orquestrador |
| Fast path editorial | QA corrige metadata no mesmo card | Template de QA |
| HML fora do QA de código | Gate pós-review/merge autorizado | Templates de arquitetura e QA |
| Política de PR portátil | `HWF_PR_POLICY` obrigatório | Distribuição gerada e exemplo local |
| Configuração agnóstica | Sem nomes, contas ou caminhos reais | Revisão do diff e testes |

## Deploy e reversão

- Não há deploy automático.
- Após merge, gerar novamente e instalar perfis explicitamente.
- Reversão: reverter o commit deste PR e regenerar as distribuições.

## Riscos e fora do escopo

- Risco: uma instalação atualizada sem `HWF_PR_POLICY` local ficará incompleta; o exemplo e o README documentam o campo.
- Fora do escopo: migrar boards existentes, executar QA ou alterar credenciais.

## Checklist

- [x] Compatibilidade e atualização local estão documentadas
- [x] Testes relevantes passaram
- [x] Diff completo foi revisado
- [x] Nenhum segredo ou dado corporativo foi incluído
- [x] PR está pronto para review, sem merge ou aprovação do autor

author: stevevanhooser
body:
Retires the last entry in `knownDivergences`, left open by #901.

## `whatVaries.m` contradicts itself today

`local_varyingFields` asks `vlt.data.eqlen` whether two parameter values are equal. `eqlen` bottoms out in a bare `==`, so `eqlen(NaN,NaN)` is **false** and a parameter that is `NaN` in every stimulus is reported **varying**.

Then `local_uniqueValues`, forty lines down *in the same file*, collapses those NaNs with `isequaln`. So the parameter comes back varying over exactly **one** distinct value — this is the real output, from the last symmetry run's artifact:

```
varies = angle = [NaN]
```

A parameter with one distinct value is the definition of constant. **This is wrong on its own terms**, before any question of matching the Python port.

The fix is one line:

```matlab
if ~vlt.data.eqlen(ref.(common{j}), params{i}.(common{j}))   % → ~isequaln(...)
```

## Why `isequaln`, and why not fix `eqlen`

`isequaln` agrees with `eqlen` on **every** non-NaN case in the battery, and is strictly more robust besides: `==` is undefined for the struct-valued parameters real stimulus data carries, where `isequaln` simply works.

Fixing `vlt.data.eqlen` itself was the alternative and is the wrong call — `eqlen` is used across VLT and NDI, and changing NaN equality there has a far larger blast radius than one line in one function.

**One judgment call worth your eye:** the header used to cite `vlt.data.structwhatvaries` as the semantics being matched, and this deliberately deviates from it on NaN. The header now says so explicitly, because the deviation is the point rather than an accident. Note the file *already* deviated — `local_uniqueValues` has always used `isequaln` — so this makes one consistent choice out of two contradictory ones.

## `knownDivergences` is now empty

That is the **goal state**, not a gap: every case in the `fun` battery is a hard assertion in both languages. Both auditors iterate the list, so an empty one asserts nothing extra.

`cases.m` and `FUN_CASES_SCHEMA.md` record why each of the two entries left, because they left for **opposite** reasons and the difference is the useful part of the history:

| case | outcome |
|---|---|
| `cellValuedConstantParameter` | **never diverged** — a source-read prediction the first real MATLAB run refuted |
| `allNaNParameter` | **really diverged, and is fixed here** |

A future reader deciding how much to trust the list should be able to tell those apart.

## The skipped assertion this also closes

`allNaNParameter`'s `whatVariesDefs` entry recorded the **old wrong behaviour** as expected (`expectedVaries = {'angle'}`, `expectedVariesValues = {'[NaN]'}`) and set `divergenceExpected = true` — which makes `verifyWhatVariesExpected` **skip** the case entirely:

```matlab
if d.divergenceExpected
    continue;
end
```

Both are corrected: `angle` and `contrast` constant, at `NaN` and `1`, and now actually asserted.

## Tests

`whatVariesTest` gains two methods:

- `testAllNaNParameterIsConstant` — the behaviour this PR changes.
- `testNaNVaryingAgainstNonNaNStillVaries` — the companion guard, so an equality that ignored the parameter altogether cannot leave the suite green.

The case's `mirrors` field said `'none'` before; it names a real test now.

## Sequencing — this pair IS atomic, unlike #901/#75

**Merge with Waltham-Data-Science/NDI-python's branch of the same name**, which empties the Python list.

The previous pair could be split because the divergence had already stopped on its own, so each side's list removal was independent. **Here the code change is what ends the divergence**, so either repo alone leaves NDI-python's symmetry run red:

- this side alone → Python's `test_audit_known_divergences` fails on a now-stale entry;
- that side alone → Python's `test_matlab_python_symmetry` fails on an unlisted mismatch.

The branches deliberately **share a name**, so the symmetry job's branch-matching checkout (`ref: github.head_ref`, falling back to `main`) tests the pair before either merges. Runs on the NDI-python PR therefore exercise *this branch*, not NDI-matlab `main` — which is the validation neither PR could get last time.

Merge back-to-back to keep the window where NDI-python runs are red down to minutes.

## Validation

**Authored without a MATLAB runtime.** The expected values written into `whatVariesDefs` are not guesses: they are the Python port's measured output for the same fixture, and the whole point of the fix is that MATLAB should now produce exactly that. The NDI-python PR's symmetry run is the check that matters, and it exercises this branch directly.

`vlt.data.eqemp` also has a genuine unrelated bug found while tracing this — filed separately against vhlab-toolbox-matlab.

author: paul80nd
body:
Items 14, 31 and 32 from the whole-repository review, re-verified against `d44d96c`. One commit each, plus the version
moves.

## A tool's `category` is now the folder it sits in

`d071c2d` moved `policies` and `standards` to `from: sub-path` and left `tools` behind. That left the one field of
three still written by hand, which was also the only field in the whole schema carrying no `description:`.

**Dropping `required: true` was not a judgement call.** `schema-shape` refuses that pair outright, which I confirmed by
putting it back:

    field 'category' declares both 'from: sub-path' and 'required: true'. A derived field is not the author's
    to write, so nothing can satisfy the requirement. Drop 'required'.

So this matches the other two exactly: a record filed straight into `tools/` has no category, and that is a normal
state rather than a gap.

### The probe is the part worth reviewing

`tools/` holds no records in any corpus here, so this rule had never run. A throwaway record at `tools/testing/`
proved the derivation end to end — the index headed a `## Testing` section, and the regenerated field table read
`derived from the record's sub-path` — and then found what the change breaks:

- every `tools/_template.md` carried the key, in `template/` and `examples/engineering/`
- eight fixture records and templates across three golden fixtures carried it too

None of that would have been reported until somebody wrote their first tool record. The probe was removed before
committing.

## An enum no type draws on

`_enums.yaml` holds enums used by more than one type, and its header says so. `review-cadence` was drawn on by none —
no `values: $enums.` named it anywhere — and its own note conceded it was "not itself a frontmatter field". Each of the
six types declaring `review-by` already carries its own guidance in that field's description.

## One threshold under two rule ids

`hub-not-specification` and `links-rather-than-restates` carry the byte-identical `words() <= links() * 40`, on two
types, for two genuinely different reasons.

A comment each rather than a shared construct: one declaration serving both would tie two arguments together that only
agree on a number today. `.schema/CLAUDE.md` asks that moving a threshold be visible, and now it is from both sides.

## Evidence

| Layer | Result |
|-------|--------|
| `dotnet test tooling/kac.tests` | 1360 passed |
| `dotnet test tooling/kac.features` | 61 passed |
| `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true dotnet run tooling/kac-tests.cs` | 27 scenarios, 87/88 checks covered |
| `validate` and `generate --check` | clean in all three corpora and `template/` |
| `update --check --from ../../` | in step in all three |
| `export`, `pack`, `restore` | engineering packs `0.7.1`, payments restores it |

The one golden that moved is a single line number, because deleting the `category:` line shifted `licence` up one. The
diff is that number and nothing else.

## What I did not do

**No docs change.** `docs/framework/metadata.md` and `docs/design/held-to.md` both explain derived fields using
policies and standards as the examples, and both stay accurate.

**No shared threshold construct**, for the reason above.

author: norberia
body: ## Summary Full rewrite of codex-gateway per the agreed research plan, in four commits. Source drops from ~4,400 to ~2,300 lines (excluding tests) while adding Langfuse tracing. ### 1. Remove dead surface `/api/brain/deployments` (Brain drives deployments through the generic sessions API with its own managed prompt — the endpoint has zero callers), the browser debug UI, legacy 410 routes, `/api/threads*`, per-session `thread/new` + `thread/resume` endpoints, and `package.json`. This also removes the GitHub-token-in-prompt code path entirely. ### 2. Core rewrite - Codex client on `tokio::process`: async reader + wait task instead of two OS threads polling `try_wait()` every 250 ms; child stderr is captured and logged with the owning session id. - JSON-RPC errors keep their structured code (no more string-matching error classification). - Session state slimmed to what clients consume: `{ ready, cwd, startedAt, selectedModel, threadId, currentTurnId, activeTurn, lastTurnStatus }`. Thread history stays in codex; the lossy in-memory transcript replica is gone. - **`POST /api/sessions` accepts `threadId` as an alias for `resumeThreadId`** — fixes the silently broken session-recovery contract with Brain (Brain sends `threadId`; the gateway ignored it and opened a fresh thread). - A dead app-server now fails the active turn immediately instead of leaving Brain polling into its own deadline. - All config parsed once in `AppConfig`; codex child env / config args derive from it. - `startedAt` serializes as UTC with `Z` suffix so Brain's timestamp validation accepts it. ### 3. Langfuse integration - OTLP (HTTP/protobuf) to `{LANGFUSE_HOST}/api/public/otel/v1/traces`, Basic auth, v4 real-time ingestion header. Batched export on a background thread — a Langfuse outage can only drop telemetry, never block requests. Off unless `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY`/`LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY` are set. - One trace per turn: root span input = prompt, output = final agent message, token usage from `thread/tokenUsage/updated` (previously ignored). Completed items become child observations (commands + output, file changes, MCP tool calls, agent messages as generations); errors, warnings, and auto-answered approvals become events. - Identity from the env Brain injects at Devbox creation: `langfuse.user.id` = `SEALAI_NAMESPACE`, `langfuse.session.id` = `SEALAI_DEPLOY_TASK_ID` (fallback codex thread id), `SEALAI_PROJECT_ID` in trace metadata — a failing deploy task is searchable in Langfuse by task id. - Known credential shapes (GitHub tokens, API keys, bearer tokens) are scrubbed from all exported payloads; payloads capped at 8 KiB. ### 4. Docs & image Both READMEs rewritten around the six remaining endpoints + Langfuse setup; web UI dropped from the Docker image; version bumped to 0.7.0. ## Testing - `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked` — all green (26 tests). - Integration tests run the real binary against a fake `codex app-server`: HTTP session/turn flow, `threadId`-alias recovery, turn-completion race, thread resume. - New Langfuse end-to-end test: runs a turn and asserts the OTLP request path, Basic auth header, ingestion-version header, exported span names, session/user ids, turn output, secret scrubbing (`ghp_…` redacted), and usage export against a fake Langfuse endpoint. - Release build verified (Dockerfile builder path with lto/opt-z, 4.4 MB binary); manual smoke of the release binary: health checks, JWT enforcement, structured 500 on missing codex, `x-request-id` header, structured logs. ## Follow-ups (outside this repo) - Brain: send `resumeThreadId` (the alias keeps `threadId` working meanwhile). - devbox-runtime / Brain: inject `LANGFUSE_HOST` / `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY` / `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY` into sandbox v1 Devboxes to enable tracing (`SEALAI_*` vars are already injected today).

author: kisielewski
body:
**`main` went red on `check:zawodyweb`**, on the assertion *"and it converts to
the same bundle, element for element"*. The cause is older than the failure and
has nothing to do with the change that happened to land on it.

**A ZIP entry carries a modification time, and `fflate` defaults it to the
current time** — its own documentation says so. So the same package built twice
was two different files with two different SHA-256, and the product is built on
the opposite assumption: the Server stores a file under the digest of its bytes,
the Client declares that digest before uploading, and the Runner verifies it
before evaluating.

What that cost, beyond a flaky check:

- two managers converting the same archive stored two copies of one package;
- *is this the same package?* had no answer, because the digest moved on its own;
- the check reddened `main` at random, more often on a slower machine, because
  it compares two conversions and only notices when they straddle a millisecond.

**Measured rather than inferred.** Reproduced once on `main` at the first
attempt, then 33 clean runs; so instead of running it again, a two-second gap was
forced between the two conversions and it failed every time, naming
`package.zip` and `examples.zip` as the files whose digests differed. With the
fix and the same forced gap, it passes.

`zipArchive` in `src/package/archive.ts` is now the one way this product builds
a ZIP, and it stamps the DOS epoch on every entry. **Nothing reads that date**:
`fflate`'s `Unzipped` is a path-to-bytes map with nowhere to put it, and the
Runner's reader takes only `name()` from an entry. When an archive was made is
`exportedAt` on the bundle, which is a field somebody can read.

Two checks in `check:package`, each shown to fail before it was trusted:

- **`zipSync` is called nowhere but the helper** — taking the fourth call site
  back out of it reports `zipSync is called outside src/package/archive.ts`;
- **the same package built a second later is the same bytes** — removing `mtime`
  from the helper reports `the same package built a second later is a different
  file`.

author: musicjapanllc
body:
Adds a coordination layer over the already-merged production loops without duplicating their implementation or touching PR #453's Security Proposal files.

WORLD runtime now:
- aggregates active discovery capability leases into one `owner_trust_root_id` / lineage checkpoint
- emits exact-target execution intents from existing capabilities, including write/mutation/credentialed intent only when the live owner-derived lease already contains it
- consumes persistent replica/network-policy evidence from the existing META network loop
- consumes Guard denial self-tuning pressure and recovery evidence from the existing Senju recovery loop
- consumes production deployment receipts from the existing META/X continuity loop
- consumes existing security runtime state read-only, so #453 can merge independently and feed the same checkpoint later
- persists one WORLD checkpoint, execution-intent set, and workflow handoff set
- monitors evidence freshness and reports stale/missing component handoffs while leaving execution to each component's existing native schedule/recovery
- does not duplicate-dispatch component workflows, so concurrent agents/workflows are not interrupted

The coordinator does not mint a new external trust root, credential, scope, or deployment authority. High-impact execution requires a current owner-derived capability lease plus an independently registered executor; raw credential material is never persisted by WORLD.

The WORLD workflow itself is non-privileged (`actions: read`) and intentionally avoids all 8 files modified by open PR #453.

author: gianlucako95
body:
## Summary

Root Cause endlich gefunden — durch direkten Code-Abgleich mit einer vom Nutzer bereitgestellten, nachweislich funktionierenden Referenz-PWA (Wizzo, gleiches Gerät, gleiche Installationsart "Zum Home-Bildschirm hinzufügen"): `position:fixed` auf `html`/`body` war der eigentliche Übeltäter der ganzen 852-vs-793px-Saga — **nicht** irgendeine falsche Höhenangabe an der Root-Shell selbst.

Fünf vorherige Fixes (`100dvh`, JS-gemessene Höhe, `position:fixed`/`bottom:0`, `top/bottom:0` auf `html`/`body`, `manifest.json` `display:fullscreen`) haben deshalb alle nichts an `shellBottom`/`navBottom` geändert — sie haben alle die Root-Shell behandelt, während das eigentliche Problem eine Ebene höher lag: `html`/`body` waren seit dem ursprünglichen Rubber-Band-Fix `position:fixed`, und das lässt WebKit für jedes verschachtelte `position:fixed`- oder `dvh`-Element in der installierten iOS-Standalone-PWA einen verkürzten Viewport berechnen.

Die Referenz-PWA hat `html`/`body` **nie** `position:fixed` gesetzt — nur `height:100%` plus `overscroll-behavior` (html: `none`, body: `overscroll-behavior-y: contain`). Ihre Vollbild-Screens nutzen ganz normal `height:"100dvh"` auf einem nicht-`position:fixed`-Element, und das funktioniert dort nachweislich pixelgenau.

- `theme.css`: `html`/`body` zurück auf `height:100%` (kein `position:fixed` mehr), Scroll-Eindämmung nur noch über `overscroll-behavior`. `margin:0` bleibt (unabhängig sinnvoller Fix aus #28).
- `App.jsx`: Root-Shell von `position:fixed;top:0/left:0/right:0/bottom:0` auf `height:"100dvh"; width:"100%"` umgestellt, exakt wie im Referenz-Vorbild.

Version auf `1.0.89` angehoben.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run build` completes without errors
- [ ] `shellBottom`/`navBottom` im Diagnose-Screenshot prüfen — sollten jetzt näher an 852 liegen
- [ ] Kein Streifen mehr unter der Bottom-Nav sichtbar
- [ ] Rubber-Band-Scroll weiterhin blockiert (Bottom-Nav nicht mehr wegziehbar)
- [ ] Vollbild-Modals (Aufgabenformular, Bautagebuch) funktionieren weiterhin korrekt

author: yaraslaut
body:
`scripts/scenario/scenario_coverage.py` measured a surface nothing filled. This fills it: the corpus goes from 4 files to 72, and the report now exits `0` on both axes.

| Rung | Files | Actions | Workflows (floor) |
|---|---|---|---|
| pastebin | 12 | 6/6 | 8/8 |
| polls | 10 | 9/9 | 10/10 |
| bookmarks | 14 | 17/17 | 12/12 |
| ledger | 15 | 17/17 | 15/15 |
| kanban | 21 | 22/22 | 20/20 |

**71/71 actions dispatched. 8/8 envelope kinds. 11/17 refusals asserted, the remaining 6 exempt with written reasons.**

Every journey is named after what it does and sourced from its rung's own README — pastebin's first file is the definition of done's *create → list → open → burn → delete* verbatim; polls' undo file is the A-votes-B-votes-A-undoes interleaving the README calls that rung's headline design record.

## Verification

Every file was run against a real `ladder_<rung>_server`, re-run against the database the first pass left behind, and mutation-tested. **71 files, zero surviving mutants.** `test_morph_scenario.py` passes 118 cases; `ladder_kanban_tests` passes 137.

```
python3 scripts/scenario/run_scenarios.py --twice     # exit 0
python3 scripts/scenario/run_scenarios.py --mutate    # exit 0, no survivors
python3 scripts/scenario/scenario_coverage.py         # exit 0
```

## `scripts/scenario/run_scenarios.py`

The server lifecycle `morph_scenario.py` deliberately does not own, and which the workflow-axis spec already anticipated as `run_all.sh`. One server per rung, on a fresh SQLite database in its own working directory with the port bound to `0`; runs the directory; tears the process group down. `--twice` proves every file is re-runnable, `--mutate` proves its assertions are load-bearing.

## The blocker: kanban could not be driven at all

`KanbanAuthorizer` inherited `SigningAuthorizer` without the anonymous carve-out `BookmarksAuthorizer` carries, so `authorize()` demanded a bearer token for `AuthModel`/`Login` — the only action that mints one. Every action a fresh remote client could send was answered `err "unauthorized"`, login included. `ladder_kanban_headless` says so in its own comment: it takes the token on its command line, because it cannot ask the server for one.

bookmarks documents this exact deadlock, and records that it was found by driving a real server from a client. kanban was written later and inherited the shape but not the fix. It gets the identical carve-out — one model type, one action type, compared exactly. `Login` still refuses the reserved `system:` namespace, so an anonymous caller can mint a token for a name it chooses and nothing more. All 137 kanban tests still pass.

Without this the rung's 22 actions and floor of 20 were unreachable.

## What the corpus found

Three defects, each **asserted as it behaves** so the gate stays green, each with its issue named in the file that pins it:

- **#367** — `StoreTransaction` posts legs onto another book's accounts. The journal files under the named ledger, the foreign balance moves, and every read stays scoped — so the two books disagree and neither says so. A leg naming no account at all *is* refused, which shows the lookup runs and simply does not check the book. `UndoTransaction` makes the equivalent check.
- **#368** — an unattached `BoardModel` replies `stoull`, the `what()` of `std::invalid_argument`. Two actions have a guard with exactly the right message that never fires, because the optional is engaged with an empty string.
- **#369** — `GetRules` requires a `projectId` and then queries the attached board instead.

Four defects in the test apparatus itself, fixed here:

- the driver never drained server stdout, so servers wedged in `write(2)` on a full pipe about sixty mutant reruns in — the corpus passed and `--mutate` died with "no data within 10.0s" on a server that was neither crashed nor refusing;
- kanban writes its action log to `current_path()`, so runs accumulated it in the caller's directory and `GetActivity` replayed a previous run's project 1 as this one's;
- the pre-existing `paste-lifecycle.scenario` asserted a new paste appears in a bare `ListPastes` — true only while the database holds fewer than twenty public pastes with larger ids. It was passing by luck, and failed about half the time under repetition;
- `morph_scenario.py` correlated strictly by `callId`, which made the decode-failure path unassertable: a frame the server cannot decode has no envelope to read a `callId` from, so it answers with `0`. `Client.rpc` now accepts that in exactly that shape and nowhere else.

## Deviations from the plan, and where they are recorded

The design spec said "no change to the example applications". Two boundaries were crossed deliberately — the kanban authorizer fix, and the `callId` rule above — and both are now written into the spec where it said otherwise, rather than left to be found in the diff. **Neither the coverage thresholds nor the workflow floors moved.**

`scenario_coverage.py`'s own canary test, which pinned exit 1 and said in its comment that authoring the corpus was later work, is flipped to 0 with that history recorded.

## Not filed, deliberately

`ImportLedgerChunk`'s per-row commit leaves earlier rows posted when a later row is malformed. That looked like a defect until the code was read: `execute(ImportLedgerChunk)` records it as a ruling and gives the reason — a `SqlTransaction` nested around the loop would have `storeJournalImpl`'s inner `Commit()` end the outer one, since `SqlTransaction` toggles `SQL_ATTR_AUTOCOMMIT` on the connection directly. The scenario pins it and now cites that ruling instead of implying a bug.

author: bradley-t-t
body:
The send window gated on the hour and read the weekday only to report it, so a Sunday delivered a full daily cap between eight and five like any other day.

`sendsOn` lives in `lib/outreach/schedule.js`, which already owns the local date and imports nothing, and both the send gate and the ramp read it there. A Sunday run composes its drafts and hands none of them to the transport, which puts the reviewed text at the front of Monday's queue.

The ramp holds through the day for the same reason it holds when sending is switched off: a day that sends nothing adds nothing to the bounce record, and a step taken on one would leave the cap at a level no clean day has been read at, with Monday free to step again on top of it.

`check-send-schedule` walks the real gate rather than a copy of the hours, and asserts a Saturday delivers its cap and a Sunday delivers nothing. `check-outreach-ramp` walks a Sunday hold and the Monday step behind it.

body:
… delete-cascade orphans

Three architecture gaps from the mess-accounting spec, plus a data-integrity bug found while auditing live charges:

- Custom expense allocation: wires up the existing but previously-inert customPercentages/customAmounts fields so "Percentage-Based" and "Per Member Custom" splits actually compute per-member shares instead of silently falling back to an equal split, in workflow-integration.ts, engine.ts, engine-v2.ts, and financial-engine.ts, with a new UI for entering per-member amounts/percentages in the Add Expense form.

- Personal expenses: Expense.personal flag for spending that belongs to one member only (toothpaste, snacks, ...) — createExpenseWithAccounting skips all allocation/charge/payment/advance side effects for these, and every settlement engine excludes them from charges and contributions.

- Rent proration: new admin-configurable Rent Policy (Full Month vs Prorate by Days) so a member's join/leave month can be billed by actual days stayed instead of always the full month. Required actually wiring up the Joining/Leaving date fields on the member form, which existed in the data model but were never rendered.

- Fix: deleting a bazar entry or shared expense only ever removed that one document — the payment/ledger/advance records it had fanned out to stayed behind forever as orphans, permanently overstating a member's contributions. deleteBazarWithAccounting/deleteExpenseWithAccounting now clean up everything a create*WithAccounting call created; the expense version refuses to delete if a charge was already paid or its advance already recovered, pointing to a credit note instead.

- Also fixed engine-v2.ts (used by Monthly Closing) and financial-engine.ts (used by the Who-Owes-Whom settlement view) to apply the same self-paid-share-excluded-from-charges fix already applied to engine.ts, and corrected two live expenses plus two orphaned payment/ledger records found while auditing why two of four members weren't showing shared expense charges.

author: vholik
body:
Fixes #1430

## Problem

Adding a value to an inline (product-scoped) variant-axis attribute — e.g. `Size: S, M` → add `L` — mirrored the new value onto the attribute's `ProductOption`, but never associated it with the product. No `product_product_option_value` row was written, so creating a variant with that value failed:

> Option value L does not exist for option Size

## Fix

`updateProductAttributesOnProductWorkflow` now attaches the mirrored option values to the product after creating them on the scoped-axis path, via a new `attachProductOptionValuesToProductStep` (with compensation). Medusa's stock `updateProductOptionValuesOnProductStep` can't be used here — its compensation reads `product.options.values`, which crashes MikroORM `expandDotPaths` on the options-preview build — so it mirrors the existing `detachProductOptionValuesFromProductStep`.

## Tests

Added a regression test in `integration-tests/http/product/admin/product.spec.ts`: create a product with an inline `Size` axis, batch-add value `L`, then create a variant bound to `Size: L`. It reproduces the reported error on `main` and passes with the fix.

`http/product/*`, `product-attribute`, and `product-edit` suites: 5 suites / 52 tests and 6 suites / 74 tests green.

author: jonndailey
body:
**Finding 1 (dailey-weekly, verified against source + reproduced):** `migrate.js` split migration files on `;` client-side, so a semicolon inside a string literal executed as two broken statements.

**Reproduced before fixing:** a migration with `INSERT ... VALUES ('foo; bar')` fails on origin/staging's code with `syntax ... near ''foo'` — exactly as the finding predicted.

**Smallest correct change:** delete the splitter; the dedicated, short-lived migration connection sets `multipleStatements: true` and runs the whole file via `query()` (prepared `execute()` can't batch), so the MySQL server's real parser handles quoted semicolons. The `_migrations` bookkeeping INSERT stays parameterized `execute()`.

**Verified on a fresh MySQL 8 container:** all 5 existing migrations + a quoted-semicolon test migration apply cleanly (6/6), and `foo; bar` is stored intact as one row.

## Source
Issue #6

## Purpose
Close the narrow baseline validator debt where a legacy File Library locator followed immediately by an explicit identity statement such as `历史迁移证据，不是当前 canonical` was still classified as `fail_ambiguous`.

## Boundary
This PR does **not** allow legacy files to become active authority and does not add a broad legacy allowlist.

The classifier only adds a narrow historical-identity semantic pattern for provenance statements that explicitly say the referenced legacy material is historical/migration evidence **and is not current canonical / authority / rule source**.

Existing strict behavior is preserved:
- machine-route references to legacy names remain `fail_active`;
- `must read/current basis/canonical/authoritative` language on the legacy-bearing line remains `fail_active` even if a nearby line says historical;
- vague `historical evidence` without an explicit non-current identity remains `fail_ambiguous`;
- prior historical migration/supersession cases remain unchanged.

## Changed files
- `11_验收/validate_canonical_cutover.ps1`

- real Issue #6 two-line shape -> `pass_historical`;
- English `historical migration evidence; not current canonical authority` -> `pass_historical`;
- active legacy-bearing instruction followed by historical identity -> remains `fail_active`;

Draft only. No main mutation, no self-review, no Ready transition and no merge without independent verification.

author: jitamb
body:
Ladder step 3.2 — "4 outputs, 4 different actions." `narrate.py`'s the third and final LLM touchpoint (S8b).

`narrate(case, persona, contract, provider) -> Narration` writes four sections (headline, explanation, action, outstanding) per persona, over an already-entitled case (§17: entitlement runs before narration, never after).

**How "the model never produces a number" stays checked, not hoped for.** §17 also says "nothing downstream ever parses free text" — extracting numbers back out of prose to verify them would be exactly that. Instead the model gets a fixed menu of named `{token}` strings (already formatted, already banded if this persona's `amount_net` is restricted) and writes around them, never inside them; a guardrail per section strips every recognised token and `[ev-xxx]` citation, and if a digit survives — or an unrecognised token, an invented citation, or a blank response — that section falls back to a fully-templated, still-correct sentence built from the same tokens. Per section, not all-or-nothing: a model that stays inside the menu gets its own differentiated prose, a model that doesn't still produces something safe.

**A real security path entitlement alone doesn't close.** `entitle.py`'s own docstring already explains why `Case`'s numeric fields stay exact floats even after entitlement — only the separate JSON payload gets banded, since a float can't hold `"₹1–5 Cr"`. Narration reads the typed `Case`, not the payload, so it's the one place those figures could actually leak into text a restricted persona reads — `narrate.py` re-checks `contract.access.column["amount_net"]` and bands with `entitle.py`'s own `band()` itself. Verified against real generated scenario A data for both an unrestricted persona (cfo, exact ₹) and a restricted one (support_lead, banded); also checks no restricted account name leaks into any of the four sections.

Three real bugs caught by tests failing on the first run, not shipped: `primary_share` used the wrong (one-decimal) percent format instead of the UI's own whole-percent share convention; the guardrail's subset checks were vacuously true on an empty string, letting a blank model response through unfallback'd; and the prompt in the first draft never told the model which persona it was writing for at all. All three fixed, all covered by a dedicated test.

7 tests, 5 mutations against the guardrail and the money-restriction check (all caught). `make check` green: 506 Python tests, ruff/mypy clean.

author: jirigrill
body:
Closes the three measured bookkeeping gaps in `docs/spec/` from [#756](https://github.com/jirigrill/eczema-helper/issues/756), plus two more the requested table audit turned up.

## catalog.md joins the README table

`catalog.md` appeared **zero** times in `README.md`. It is the largest section — **70 unique `CAT-*` rules, no OPEN rules** — and an agent starting from the index, as the repo's convention directs, would never reach it. Its row routes to the two groups a reader most needs: the **sign-off gate** (`CAT-SIGN-1`..`-6`) and the `CAT-DERIVE-*` **display prohibition**.

## Two terms join GLOSSARY.md

Both name decisions whose entire content is what the app *does not* do, which is exactly the kind of term that cannot be inferred from its uses:

- **Sync health** — failure-only. No screen ever reports that sync works (`SET-SYNC-1`), and this is not merely a preference: no API can report the store is synchronised. Durability gate, ended-events-only verdicts, two consequence-keyed messages ([#723](https://github.com/jirigrill/eczema-helper/issues/723)).
- **Tolerant read** — an unresolvable `foodId` is a recoverable display condition, never a crash or a deletion. **No fallback label**: `MealItem` carries `foodId` alone, so the item is hidden and the meal degrades to read-only, and the two halves must not be separated. Retirement-in-place (`CAT-VER-5`, `-6`) leaves **bundle-vs-store skew** as the only route to an unknown id ([#703](https://github.com/jirigrill/eczema-helper/issues/703), [#749](https://github.com/jirigrill/eczema-helper/issues/749)).

A short paragraph in the glossary preamble states why these two are here, so the across-sections rule is not misread as having been bent.

## What the table audit found

The ticket's last bullet asked for a whole-table check. Two rows were wrong:

- **`settings.md` was the only row silent about its own OPEN rule.** `SET-PRIVACY-14` was mentioned in the README, but attributed inside the *`first-run.md`* row. Now stated in its own row as the shared question it is.
- **The `day-view.md` row called #744 "still open elsewhere".** It is closed and settled in `persistence-model.md` §4.1 — the second breakfast opens the first in edit, so one slot holds one meal.

Two rows made no OPEN claim at all (`skin-observation.md`, `persistence-model.md`); both measure zero, now stated. The `consent.md` row's "five questions" was verified against §11 — five.

## Verification

- Every rule id cited in the new text grepped against its source file — all present.
- Every behavior-area `.md` in `docs/spec/` now appears in the table; `TEMPLATE.md`, `GLOSSARY.md` and `DECISIONS.md` are covered in README prose by design.
- Docs only. No code, no decisions reopened.
