author: steipete
body:
Closes #134224

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users switching a compacted OpenClaw conversation to Codex would lose access to facts retained only in the conversation summary. The summary remained stored, but the fresh Codex thread received only the recent tail. In the live reproduction, a recall request returned the old seed acknowledgement rather than the remembered project code.

## Why This Change Was Made

Render canonical compaction and branch summaries at the existing Codex projection boundary, and permit a fresh thread to inherit summary-only history when no earlier user messages remain. This is the shared boundary for ordinary fresh-thread continuity and active context-engine assembly; changing storage, rereading raw history downstream, or patching Codex would fix the wrong owner.

The existing quoted-context framing, current-request separation, mention neutralization, UTF-16-safe size bounds, tool-payload handling, and original assembled-message identities are preserved. Resumed-thread incremental replay and native Codex compaction ownership do not change. No schema, configuration, dependency, or SDK surface is added.

## User Impact

Fresh Codex threads can use saved compaction and branch summaries instead of silently omitting them, including summary-only conversations. Summaries remain subject to existing per-message and total context limits; this does not reconstruct context already omitted from an existing native thread.

Production LOC: **+13/-1 (net +12)**. Tests: **+293/-152 (net +141)**. Docs: **+8**. The production growth handles two omitted canonical message variants and the connected fresh-thread admission predicate; it introduces no alternate flow or new abstraction.

## Evidence

- **Baseline:** `c884d51b870b8c961385655168410b70ac2834f8`, tree `2076f4f2c904332fbcffde58858ef910d785cdc9`.
- **Verified head:** `6806f1a400b9caa533f993ba391caa8347367edd`, tree `fe1ea2c3f3398e090a385b74a677b7242db5a3ba`. The final live run used a clean checkout of this exact published commit.
- **Regression red/green:** the test-only patch against unchanged production yields 16 intended failures and 224 passes. With the repair, all **292 owner and sibling tests pass**, with no skips. This includes actual SQLite compaction/branch entries, fresh-thread `turn/start.input`, active context-engine assembly, summary-only and assistant-tail cuts, mention neutralization, bounds, and generic CLI history coverage.
- **Live before:** the built Gateway, public compaction and runtime-switch RPCs, and actual managed Codex app-server reproduced the omission twice on the baseline. Stored-summary marker: present; native input, native assistant, and outer reply marker: absent. Completed runtime/model identity was verified rather than inferred from requested settings.
- **Independent review:** Codex autoreview is scoped-clean at its default P0 threshold, with no findings. Static diff/format checks passed.
- **Live after:** both `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` and `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` pass the compact → OpenClaw-to-Codex switch → recall → cold Gateway restart → recall flow on the exact published head. In each case the identifier is present in the stored summary, actual native user input, native assistant output, and outer reply. Session/lifecycle identity stays stable and the compaction count advances exactly once. These two cases completed 10 live turns, two manual compactions, and two restarts; both real Control UI captures passed with no page errors.
- **Broader validation:** all changed-scope checks passed, including production/test extension typechecks, lint, formatting, import cycles, SDK boundary declarations, and five doctor declaration/closure tests. The full candidate build passed with no ineffective dynamic-import warnings; rebuilding the clean published head also passed.
- **Exact-head CI:** https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33414178443 passed on `6806f1a400b9caa533f993ba391caa8347367edd`; the repository watcher reported `state=SUCCESS pending=0` and `GREEN`. One close/reopen recovered the missing ready-event run; no checks were bypassed.

Remote proof uses an isolated Linux Blacksmith Testbox, Node 24.19.0, managed Codex 0.151.0, and API keys supplied by the supported Testbox hydration path. The [hosted environment run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33409099808) identifies the environment; its own success is not the exit status of individual remote commands. No operator Gateway or state was used.

Focused command (run on the isolated Testbox):

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/context-engine-projection.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.context-engine.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-history.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/session-history.test.ts
```

The first changed-gate invocation stopped because the independently fetched temporary clone lacked the `origin/main` tracking ref. The ref was then restored to the exact frozen baseline before rerunning; no check or baseline was weakened. The first browser capture hit Chromium's Unix socket path-length limit in the temporary fixture; a short isolated browser temp directory corrected that setup. The initial dirty candidate-tree run also hit the intentional UI/Gateway build-identity guard because source-CLI rebuilding refreshed the Gateway identity. The final proof instead rebuilt the clean published commit and passed both UI captures without bypassing that guard. All failed captures remain excluded from passing evidence.

The owned Testbox had zero live task processes or zombies at final inspection and was stopped after evidence collection. No operator Gateway, native Codex home, or runtime state was touched.

### Source and dependency contract

Canonical summary messages carry `summary`, not `content`. The old renderer filtered them out; its blob is identical in stable `v2026.8.1`, the earlier pre-refactor source, and the tested baseline. This is a pre-existing defect; the original introducing commit is not established.

The lead and implementation worker directly inspected pinned upstream Codex `rust-v0.151.0`: [turn input submission](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.151.0/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/turn_processor.rs#L584-L640), [unchanged text conversion](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.151.0/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs#L390-L445), [input cap](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.151.0/codex-rs/protocol/src/user_input.rs#L8-L24), and [literal mention scanning](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.151.0/codex-rs/skills/src/mentions.rs#L76-L145). The loss occurs before native submission, not inside Codex.

### ClawSweeper follow-through

The latest review and its rank-up move request direct pinned Codex source inspection and completed exact-head validation; it reports no mechanical or security finding. The acting lead personally completed the required sibling-source inspection before implementation and again checked the submitted-input contract, as cited above. The implementation worker independently inspected the same immutable source. The completed runtime proof now follows stored summary → native input → native assistant → visible reply, including restart. Exact-head CI is now green, completing that follow-through. No re-review is requested merely for these evidence updates.

### Before and after

These are inspected, synthetic-only captures of the actual Control UI served by the isolated Gateway, displaying the conversations produced by the live CLI/RPC flow. They are not mocked UI states.

**Before:** after compaction and switching to Codex, the reply incorrectly repeats the last seed acknowledgement.

![Before: Codex repeats the old acknowledgement after compaction and runtime switch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/82b5c58d-6f16-4876-ace0-e4afeef83d81)

author: jumplink
body:
`SINCE` exists so a consumer can tell **"this surface describes a newer library than the one installed"** from **"this surface is wrong"**. That test only works for the members it covers, and it covered properties only.

## Measured

Against the installed `gtk4-4.22.4` / `libadwaita-1.9.3`, while `@girs/*@4.4.0` describes 4.23.3 / 1.10.0 — walking `DECLS`/`OWN_PROPS`/`OWN_SIGNALS` against the running typelib:

| | count |
|---|---:|
| properties missing from the installed library, **explained by `SINCE`** | 14 |
| properties missing, **unexplained** | **0** |
| signals missing, **unexplained** | **18** |

All eighteen are `force-close`, on every `GtkWindow` descendant. A correct surface, reported as eighteen defects — because a property-only map has nothing to say about `GtkWindow::force-close`. The consumer's only remaining options were an allowlist or not checking signals at all, and both give up the thing `SINCE` is for.

This is not hypothetical: `@gjsify/gtk-host`'s `generated.spec.ts` asks the installed typelib whether every emitted name is real, and its signal arm is exactly where those eighteen would land.

## The change

Signal since-versions are collected alongside the property ones and keyed `Type::signal`. `Type.property` and `Type::signal` are GObject's own two spellings, so they cannot collide and a reader already knows which is which.

The gate asserts both: the signal key is present, and no key carries both spellings.

## One thing the fixture had to get right

`OWN_SIGNALS` carries a widget's **own** signals, so a since-version on the abstract base reaches nothing — my first attempt put it on `Widget` and the assertion failed for the right reason. It now sits on a concrete class's signal, which is what the real corpus looks like.

## Checks

- `tests/widget-surface` green; A/B verified — removing the collection loop turns it red
- `gjsify lint` exit 0, `gjsify run check:app` exit 0

author: tyler-r-kendrick
body:
Second of the ADR 0079 stack. **Stacked on #288** — one commit on top of it.

ADR 0074 is explicit that anything with a deadline is detected by the lifecycle scanner and published on the `lifecycle.*` feed, never by a subsystem's own private due-check, and that OpenSesame's own rotation subscribes to that same feed so a break in it breaks us too. A session grant is a thing with a deadline, so it becomes `SubjectKind::SessionGrant` rather than keeping a timer of its own.

That is mostly inheritance: the whole ladder (notice, warning, urgent, expired), the same watermarks and `evaluate` certificates use, delivery through the `webhook_endpoints` that already exist with retry. It also inherits the structural safety — `ExpirySubject` has no field able to carry a value and `LifecycleEvent::payload` builds its JSON key by key, so **an expiry notification for a grant cannot carry what was granted**, however carelessly a future subscriber is written.

## The one real decision: renewability belongs to the kind, not to a flag

`should_respond` used to read `subject.auto_respond` alone. That is right for a certificate — renewing itself overnight is the platform doing its job. It is wrong for a session grant: one human's reach into another's vault renewing itself overnight is the platform giving away what it was trusted to hold.

So `SubjectKind::renewable()` is consulted first, and `SessionGrant` is the one kind that answers false.

Putting it on the kind rather than the flag is the whole point. A subject built with `auto_respond: true` — by mistake, or because a row was copied from a certificate — still gets no automatic renewal. A test asserts exactly that: every event the ladder produces for such a subject is refused by `should_respond`, while a certificate on the same rung is still acted on.

**Refusing to act is not refusing to tell.** Every rung still fires for a session grant, because somebody whose access lapses in an hour is precisely who the ladder exists for.

## The closed set earned its keep

`responder_for` matches `SubjectKind` exhaustively, so adding a variant broke the gateway build until "what acts on this?" was answered in code. That is the design working — the set is closed because each kind implies a platform-owned responder with real authority (ADR 0065 Tier X).

The answer is nothing, and it is the *second* fence: `should_respond` already refuses the kind before the dispatcher is reached. A new test walks `SubjectKind::ALL` rather than a hand-kept list, so the lookup cannot silently fall behind the set.

## Verification

`scripts/clippy-gate.sh` **CLEAN** across the workspace (pedantic, all features, all targets) and `cargo +1.88.0 test --workspace --all-targets` green — **81 suites, 0 failures**.

Worth noting for the reviewer: I caught the exhaustive-match break with my own workspace gate rather than in CI, but only *after* committing — verifying the crate I touched is not the same as verifying the workspace, and a closed enum is exactly where that gap bites.

Still no routes, no schema, no transport. Those are PRs 3–6.

author: anudeepkolla16
body:
The archive's vendor folders have been renamed to match the app names in the spend sheet, but the folder→app mapping saved at the last import (`_sync-config.json`, saved 2026-08-27) is a snapshot of the old names. Seven apps were still routed by a folder that no longer exists:

| App | Stale mapping still files under | Folder that actually exists |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Anthropic(Api Console) | `Claude Api` | `Anthropic(Api Console)` |
| Mango technology(Clickup) | `click up invoices` | `Mango technology(Clickup)` |
| Cursor pro | `Cursor` | `Cursor pro` |
| ElevenLabs | `Eleven Labs` | `ElevenLabs` |
| Google Voice | `Google vol` | `Google Voice` |
| OPENAI | `Open AI` | `OPENAI` |
| Linkedin Sales Navigator(Factors ai) | `Factors ai (LinkedIn sales nav)` | `Linkedin Sales Navigator(Factors ai)` |

Filing under a name that is gone recreates the old folder beside the real one and totals only one of them — the split this archive has already been through with `Bubble` / `Bubble Starter` and `Luzmo` / `Cumul(Luzmo)`.

## What changed

`appToSourceFolder` now takes the sheet's app names, and a folder the archive spells like the app beats the mapping outright. The sheet's name is what the archive is being kept in step with, so where the archive already carries it, it wins.

- Matching uses the same normalized form the vendor resolver uses, so `apollo` reaches `Apollo` and `Google Cloud` reaches `Google cloud`; the folder's own spelling is what gets written, never the sheet's.
- An app with no folder of its own still resolves through the mapping — `Laptops Procurement` has been filed under `Laptop procurment` since before any of this, and the mapping is the only thing that knows the two are the same vendor.
- An app name matching no folder adds no entry, so filing still reports a genuinely new folder.
- The folder listing moved below `summary`, which it reports a failed listing through and which was not yet defined where the listing stood — a `ReferenceError` if the listing ever failed.

This makes the saved mapping's staleness harmless rather than requiring it to be regenerated.

## Coverage after the rename

60 of the sheet's 66 apps now have an archive folder. Six folders have no row (`Attention`, `Courier bills`, `Laptop Repair`, `Laptops sold`, `Vercel`, `Zapier`) and six rows have no folder (`Dovetail`, `DBT Cloud`, `Hex`, `Keepa`, `Antivirus,MDM`, `WINGMAN(Clari)`).

## Testing

`npm test` — 237 passing (was 233). Four new cases cover the rename beating the mapping, the archive's own spelling winning, the mapping surviving for an app with no folder of its own, and an unmatched app name adding nothing.

author: einar-lennelov-unique
body:
## Summary

- `BingAgentConfig` gained `market`, `set_lang` and `freshness` as `ExposableParam` knobs (#2330 / #2331 / #2332 / #2352), but we are not comfortable releasing them yet.
- Rather than reverting the stack, this hides all three from the admin form with `RJSFMetaTag.SpecialWidget.hidden()` — the same tag `PostProcessorConfig.max_tokens_for_sources` and every `engine` discriminator already use.
- The fields, the derived `request_model()` / `exposed_params_model()` and the whole runtime path are untouched. With no widget to render, no deployment can pin a value or expose a knob to the LLM, and dropping the tag is all it takes to release them later.

## Changes

- One `_hidden_until_released` tag applied through three annotated aliases (`HiddenExposableMarket` / `HiddenExposableSetLang` / `HiddenExposableFreshness`), so the `Field(...)` bodies stay byte-identical and the revert is a one-line change per knob.
- `market` keeps its `dynamic_enforced_by_infra` tag underneath; the two merge without a key collision (`ui:disabled` + `ui:help` vs `ui:widget`).
- Parametrised test asserting all three knobs carry `ui:widget: hidden`; `test_market_ui_schema_editable_when_not_enforced` renamed to `..._not_locked_...`, since the field is no longer editable.
- README lines in `unique_search_proxy_core` and `unique_web_search` that advertised the knobs as admin-configurable now say they are hidden pending release.

## Risk

None for existing deployments. The knobs default to `{expose: false, value: null}` and this lands ahead of the release that first carries them, so no stored config can already have one switched on. `BING_AGENT_MARKET` still pins the market from the environment, which is deliberate — it is infra-only and undocumented for customers.

This is the first use of the `hidden` tag on an object-typed field rather than a scalar, so the render path was checked against the admin's actual dependencies: `@rjsf/core` 6.2.4 `SchemaField` computes `hidden = uiOptions.widget === 'hidden'` before dispatching to `ObjectField`, and `@rjsf/shadcn`'s `FieldTemplate` early-returns `<div className="hidden">`. The admin overrides `ObjectFieldTemplate` but not `FieldTemplate`, so the whole `Collapsible` section for each knob is `display: none`.

## Test plan

- [x] Generated uiSchema carries `ui:widget: hidden` on all three knobs, both on `BingAgentConfig` directly and on the `BingSearchConfig` branch of `WebSearchConfig.search_engine_config` (checked with `ACTIVE_SEARCH_ENGINES='["google","bing"]'`, so the discriminated-union `oneOf` walk is covered).

- [x] Dependents unaffected: `unique_search_proxy_client` → 322 passed, `unique_web_search` → 682 passed.
- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean, `basedpyright` → 0 errors.

author: nhomyk
body:
Scheduling the Microsoft sync (#604) means **untested code meeting a Graph tenant at 07:00**. The dispatcher and its five workers had no tests and had never executed — and today's pattern is that built-and-never-run is where the defects live.

**The dispatcher's contract is pinned where it matters.** One worker failing must leave the others to finish, or a tenant with no Tasks licence or a revoked mail scope costs the whole night rather than one entity. Holds both ways: a worker *returning* an error, and a worker *throwing* — the case nobody writes on purpose and everybody eventually hits.

**The calendar worker is tested because it's the one switched on.** A first delta has failure modes a steady-state one doesn't:
- no cursor yet, so it must request a full delta rather than pass `undefined` into a URL
- the cursor must be saved, or every night silently re-reads the whole calendar
- a tenant reports removals in that first window alongside creations

Real calendars are messier than a fixture: an all-day event has a date and no `dateTime`, a cancelled one can arrive with no start at all, and an event can have no attendees. Any of those throwing would fail an entire sync over one odd row.

**Nothing was wrong with the product.** The dispatcher already wraps each worker defensively and the worker already converts a Graph refusal into a returned error, which is what the dispatcher depends on. The tests say so now rather than somebody hoping so at 07:00.

One defect was in the *test*: my first fake exported only `listCalendarEventsDelta` while `common.ts` imports `describeGraphError` from the same module, so the error path failed inside the fake and looked like a product fault. Worth recording — an incomplete fake failing in the one path it exists to exercise is a convincing way to be wrong.

21 sync tests pass. `scripts/verify.sh`: all 10 green.

author: stevehill1981
body:
My previous change marked the SNES specifications unverified because "the machine's shelf is magazines only". **Wrong for the same reason as the N64** — the SNESdev PPU and S-DSP references were held here and hidden from search by the page-break skip.

They're a community wiki rather than Nintendo documentation, so they're cited as such, by segment, with the tier stated. What they establish is that the entry's "sound chip" is closer to a second computer.

**Two Sony parts.** The **S-SMP** is a processor — "SPC-700 processor, clocked at 1.024MHz" — with three timers, its own IPL boot ROM, and its own RAM behind a bus arbiter. The **S-DSP** has "8 voice channels", decoding "BRR samples at a variable sample rate using 4-point Gaussian interpolation" through a "FIR filtered echo buffer".

**The two CPUs barely talk** — four bytes of I/O registers between the 65816 and the SPC700. A game uploads code and samples once; after that the audio processor runs its own program against its own data in its own address space. That's why the music doesn't stutter when the main CPU is busy, why the reverb costs the game nothing, and why SNES music lifts out cleanly as `.spc` files.

**One figure falls out of the others:** "clocked by a 24.576MHz ceramic resonator", generating "1 stereo sample every 768 resonator cycles" — 32,000 samples a second exactly. The SNES's 32 kHz rate is arithmetic, not a chosen number.

⚠ Kutaragi's authorship of the chip is marked unverified — widely repeated, but in this library it appears only in modern secondary accounts, and no period document held here names him.

author: joris974
body:
Ports the pattern from freckle/npm-package-template#178 to this repo.

## Summary

- yarn 1 classic → pnpm; Node pinned via `.nvmrc`.
- Adds ESLint, knip, `typecheck` (now covers test files), `format-check`, and coverage (v8, gated at 70%) — all wired into CI.
- Switches the package to ESM (**breaking**).
- Modernizes `tsconfig.json` (ES2023, `NodeNext`, stricter checks); adds `tsconfig.build.json` for the `dist/` build.
- Adds `src/index.test.ts`. The package had no tests at all before this.
- `typescript` 7.0.2 → `^6.0.3`.
- Replaces the hand-rolled `check-git-clean.sh` with `freckle/check-git-clean-action@v1`.
- Drops `@semantic-release/exec` and `@semantic-release/git` from `.releaserc.yaml`.

## Package manager

Removed `yarn.lock` and the `yarn@1.22.22` `packageManager` pin, added `pnpm-lock.yaml` and pinned `pnpm@11.24.0`. Added `.nvmrc` (`24.20.0`); `ci.yml` reads it via `node-version-file` and installs with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.

## ESM (breaking change)

`package.json` gets `"type": "module"`. `dist/index.js` now emits real `import`/`export` instead of `exports.exhaustive = ...`.

This breaks `require('@freckle/exhaustive')`. Checked the consumers first: every reference in `megarepo` (`frontend/educator/*`, `frontend/student/*`, `frontend/platform/console`) goes through Vitest or a bundler, both of which handle ESM natively. There are no CJS `require` call sites.

`dist/index.d.ts` is byte-identical before and after; only `dist/index.js` changed.

## typescript pinned below 7

`typescript-eslint` hard-errors on TS 7.x, so adding ESLint requires `typescript` at `^6.0.3`. This repo was already on 7.0.2 via #54, so this is a downgrade rather than a hold.

No Renovate rule added to block the bump from coming back — per direction, `package.json`'s `^6.0.3` range is the only guard. Confirmed `dist/` output is byte-identical between TS 6.0.3 and 7.0.2 for this package, so the pin costs nothing; if Renovate reopens #54, CI will catch it on the first `pnpm lint` rather than silently.

## check-git-clean

The repo already had a `check-git-clean` script pointing at `check-git-clean.sh`, predating `check-git-clean-action`. It is not equivalent: the script uses `git diff`, which only sees modifications to tracked files. `check-git-clean-action` uses `git status --porcelain`, which also catches untracked files — the case that matters when `pnpm build` emits a new file. Removed the script and the `package.json` entry, and added the action after `pnpm build` in CI.

## Flow removal (breaking)

This was the last repo in the org still shipping Flow types (`dist/index.js.flow`, generated by `flowgen`). Dropped: `gen-flow.cjs`, the `flowgen` devDependency, the `&& node gen-flow.cjs` step on `build`, and the generated file itself. `dist/` now ships only `index.js` and `index.d.ts`.

Checked before removing: no repo in the org (`gh search code --filename .flowconfig`) still has a `.flowconfig`, so there's no internal Flow consumer left. This is a real breaking change for any *external* Flow consumer, if one exists — none is known.

(An earlier revision of this PR kept Flow, reasoning it belonged in its own PR since it removes a published artifact. Removing it here instead, per direction.)

## Type-check test files

`tsconfig.json` previously excluded `src/**/*.test.ts`, and nothing else covered them. It now includes them; new `tsconfig.build.json` re-excludes them for the `dist/` build. Confirmed by putting a type error in the test file: `pnpm typecheck` fails, `pnpm build` still passes.

## Coverage

Added `@vitest/coverage-v8` and `vitest.config.ts` with `provider: 'v8'`, `reporter: ['text', 'lcov']`, gated at 70% on lines/branches/functions/statements. CI runs `pnpm coverage` instead of `pnpm test` so the suite doesn't run twice.

There were no tests before, so the gate needed a suite to pass at all. `src/index.test.ts` covers both exports plus every branch of the internal `saferStringify` — `undefined`, plain values, circular objects, `BigInt`, and the non-`TypeError` rethrow. Currently 100% on all four metrics. Verified the gate fails when the threshold is raised above actual coverage.

## Release config

Dropped `@semantic-release/exec` (`yarn install && yarn run build`, broken after the pnpm migration) and `@semantic-release/git`'s push-back to `main`. Per #178, `main`'s branch ruleset forbids the bot pushing back, and `dist/` freshness is enforced at PR time by `check-git-clean-action` instead.

This repo shows the exact symptom #178 describes: npm's latest is **1.1.0** while `main`'s `package.json` still says **1.0.1**. The push-back never landed.

`release.yml` also drops the now-unused `@semantic-release/exec` install and pins `conventional-changelog-conventionalcommits@9`, with the comment explaining why (v10 needs `conventional-changelog-writer@9`, which semantic-release@25 doesn't ship).

## Other

- `package.json` gets `"files": ["dist"]`. There was none, so `pnpm pack` shipped 25 files including `src/`, `.github/`, and every config. Verified with `pnpm pack --dry-run`: now 5 files (`dist/` plus npm's always-included `package.json` and `README.md`).
- README: added an **Install** section using `pnpm add`, a **Development** section listing each script, and a note that `dist/` is committed. Also fixed the usage examples, which imported from `@freckle/exhaustive-js` (the repo name) rather than `@freckle/exhaustive` (the package name).
- `LICENSE`: open-ended copyright year, `2022` → `2022-present`, and holder `Freckle` → `Renaissance Learning Inc`. `package.json`'s `author` field matches.
- `.gitignore`: added `coverage`.

## Divergences from npm-package-template

Every shared config is byte-identical to the template: `eslint.config.mjs`, `knip.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `tsconfig.build.json`, `.nvmrc`, `.releaserc.yaml`, `ci.yml`, `vitest.config.ts`, `.restyled.yaml`. What still differs, and why:

- **`package.json`** — identity fields only (`name`, `version`, `description`, `repository`). Key order, `repository` shape, `rm -r dist`, and all dependency ranges now match the template.
- **`release.yml`** — no `if: false` guard. That is a template placeholder ("remove this when you are ready to release"); this package actively publishes.
- **`.prettierrc`** — removed the deprecated `jsxBracketSameLine` key. Prettier 3.9.6 prints a deprecation warning for it on every run, which `format-check` would now surface in CI on every PR. The key is a no-op here (no JSX). The template should probably drop it too.
- **`.gitignore`** — keeps the pre-existing `.vscode` entry alongside the template's two lines.
- **`LICENSE`** — copyright holder changed from `Freckle` to `Renaissance Learning Inc`, and `package.json`'s `author` field to match, per direction. Now identical to the template.
- **`RELEASE.md`** — kept this repo's more detailed version, which documents the `rc/*` prerelease branches this repo actually configures; #178 didn't touch this file.
- **`.github/CODEOWNERS`** — changed from `@freckle/engineering` to `@freckle/team-student-activities`, per direction.

## Deliberately skipped

- `.github/commenter.yml` and `.github/workflows/checklist.yml` — not present in this repo.

## Verification

From a clean `rm -rf node_modules && pnpm install`:

```
pnpm format-check   pass
pnpm typecheck      pass
pnpm lint           pass
pnpm knip           pass
pnpm coverage       8 tests pass, 100% lines/branches/functions/statements
pnpm build          pass, dist/ regenerated
```

Negative checks:

- Coverage gate fails as designed when the threshold exceeds actual coverage.
- `pnpm typecheck` fails on a type error in `src/index.test.ts`; `pnpm build` still passes, confirming `tsconfig.build.json` excludes tests.
- `pnpm pack --dry-run` compared with and without `"files"`: 25 files → 5.
- Smoke-tested the built ESM output with `node --input-type=module`, importing both exports from `dist/index.js`.

## Version bump

Marked breaking (`feat!` plus a `BREAKING

author: damienlethiec
body:
## Contexte

L'API va bientôt accepter des écritures ; ses deux surfaces n'avaient aucun frein. Rate limiting natif Rails (`ActionController::RateLimiting`, inclus d'office dans `ActionController::API`), adossé au cache du controller — `solid_cache` en production — sans gem ni middleware.

## Changements

- Token endpoint (`POST /api/oauth/token`, seule surface non authentifiée) : 10/min **par IP**, via `API::TokensController`, sous-classe de `Doorkeeper::TokensController` vers laquelle la route pointe désormais. Un client légitime demande un jeton toutes les deux heures ; seul un brute-force de credentials approche la limite.
- Endpoints authentifiés (`/api/*`) : 300/min par jeton — limite généreuse à dessein, la volumétrie légitime ne l'approche jamais ; elle ne borne qu'un client emballé ou un jeton volé. La clé est l'empreinte SHA-256 de l'en-tête d'autorisation : en clair, elle déposerait des bearer tokens dans la table `solid_cache_entries` et contournerait `hash_token_secrets`.
- `429 {"error": "rate_limited"}`, documenté au RUNBOOK comme **réessayable** — à ne jamais avaler en silence côté client.

## Points d'attention

- Derrière le front, `request.remote_ip` vaut ce que vaut le `X-Forwarded-For` : mal configuré, le frein par IP devient collectif ou contournable. Question posée à l'exploitation, avec les scopes et la volumétrie.

## Tests

- [x] Specs request des deux freins, y compris la discrimination par clé — un appelant ne compte pas contre un autre, une adresse ne compte pas contre une autre (assertions prouvées par mutation)
- [x] Spec de routing : seule la délivrance de token est routée, désormais vers `api/tokens#create`
- [x] `bin/ci` complète verte

Ticket de suivi interne #693.

author: ammeek
body:
## What

`KVStoreService.checkAccessNamespaceIsAllowed` skips the **Allowed Namespaces** check when the calling namespace is a descendant of the target so that KV inheritance keeps working. However, the descendant test was a bare `startsWith` with no dot boundary:

```java
return !childNamespace.startsWith(parentNamespace);

```

Because `"prod2".startsWith("prod")` evaluates to `true`, a flow in `prod2` was incorrectly treated as a child of `prod`. The allow-list was never consulted, granting access to `prod`'s KV store. The same flaw applies to sibling namespaces like `company.team2` against `company.team`.

**Why It Matters**

* **EE Scope:** EE only. In OSS, namespaces are not an authorization boundary and `isAllowedNamespace` is documented as always returning `true`.
* **Impacted Entry Points:** Reachable from `KvFunction` (`kv('key', namespace=…)`) and `RunContext.namespaceKv` (which backs `kv.Set` and `kv.Put`), meaning prefix-sibling writes are in scope, not just reads. `kv.Get`, `kv.Delete`, and `kv.GetKeys` invoke `acl().allowNamespace(…).check()` first and are not bypassed by this path.
* **REST Controllers:** Unaffected, as both call `kvStore(namespace)` where `fromNamespace == namespace`, so the shortcut never triggers.

**Changes Made**

* **Hierarchy Rule Standardization:** Replaced `isNotParentNamespace` with `isDescendantOrSelf`, utilizing `parent + "."`. This aligns with `Namespace.isInHierarchy` in EE, ensuring the allow-list and descendant check agree on what constitutes a descendant.
* **Call Sites Updated:** Applied to both the allow-list skip and the namespace-existence skip.
* **Exception Handling:** Swapped `catch (IllegalArgumentException)` to `catch (ResourceAccessDeniedException)`. The original catch block was dead code because `checkAllowedNamespace` throws `ResourceAccessDeniedException`. Without this change, a denial escaped as a raw access-denied exception rather than the documented `KVStoreException`.
* **Same-Namespace Behavior:** Unchanged. `isDescendantOrSelf` returns `true` for equal strings, matching the previous `startsWith` behavior.

**Testing**

* **New Coverage:** Added `KVStoreServiceTest.shouldDenyKVStoreAccessWhenAccessingFromPrefixSiblingNamespace` (`prod2` → `prod` is denied). Fails before the change, passes after.
* **Mock Refactoring:** Updated class mocks from OSS's always-allow behavior to emulate an EE allow-list (where each namespace allows only itself).
* **Regression Protection:** The mock update turns `shouldGetKVStoreForAnyNamespaceWhenAccessingFromChildNamespace` into a positive control, ensuring a real dot-descendant still skips the allow-list.

author: mwbrooks
body:
### Summary

This pull request gives developers a production install path for the Slack plugin in Codex:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add slackapi/slack-skills-plugin
codex plugin add slack@slack
```

Codex installs plugins only from a marketplace, and the one this repo publishes was named `slack-dev` after the plugin team's own testing rather than the audience it actually serves. That left `slack@slack-dev` as the only install path available to a public developer: adding a marketplace labelled "dev" in order to get the production release.

Promoting it to `slack` gives up the dev listing, which turns out to cost nothing. Codex accepts a local path as a marketplace source, so maintainers can test from a checkout with `codex plugin marketplace add ./` and never needed a published dev marketplace of their own. The README and the public plugin page in `docs/` are part of the same change, because both still advertised the plugin as Claude Code and Cursor only, and an install path developers cannot find is not a shipped install path.

### Preview

The install command developers are given:

```sh
# before — the only available path, labelled as dev
codex plugin add slack@slack-dev

# after
codex plugin add slack@slack
```

### Testing

Verified end-to-end against Codex CLI 0.146.1, then restored the machine to its pre-test state.

1. `codex plugin marketplace add ./` — the checkout registers and Codex resolves the manifest name as `slack`.
2. `codex plugin add slack@slack` — installs; `codex plugin list` shows the plugin enabled at 1.3.0 with all 8 skills.
3. `codex plugin remove slack@slack` and `codex plugin marketplace remove slack` — both clean up, matching the updated maintainers guide.

One finding worth flagging, because it makes the upgrade note below required rather than advisory: with a pre-existing `slack@slack-dev` install, adding `slack@slack` leaves **both** marketplaces installed and enabled at 1.3.0, exposing the same 8 skills. Codex does not recognize them as the same plugin, so the old entry has to be removed explicitly.

Locally, `make lint` (ruff + rumdl, 19 files), `make typecheck` (16 files), and `make test-unit` (21 tests) all pass.

CI: lint, typecheck, unit tests, and the evaluation tests all pass.

### Notes

**Upgrade note.** Anyone who installed under the old name should clean up before re-adding:

```sh
codex plugin remove slack@slack-dev
codex plugin marketplace remove slack-dev
```

That set should be small, since the marketplace has not been announced as a public install path yet. Doing the promotion now rather than after an announcement is what keeps it small.

**Naming.** Three marketplace IDs were considered: `slack`, `slackapi`, or keeping `slack-dev` and documenting it. `slack` was chosen as the cleanest match to the plugin name, giving `slack@slack`.

The display name `Slack` follows the dominant convention. Across the ~20 public repositories that currently ship a Codex `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, the bare brand name is what most use, and the alternatives rank well behind it:

- `Slack` — bare brand, ~55% of manifests (Firebase, Lepton, Virtuoso, StackQL, Inline)
- `Slack Skills` — brand plus "Skills", ~20% (Azure Agent Skills, Chris Banes Skills)
- `Slack Official` — brand plus an official qualifier, ~10% (OpenAI's own `Codex official` and `ChatGPT Official`)
- `Slack Marketplace` — brand plus "Marketplace", ~5% (a single manifest, and a local plugin listing rather than a published one)

The Codex schema defines the field as the user-facing *marketplace* title, so the surrounding UI already supplies that context. Sharing a display name with the plugin is also normal for a single-plugin repository: `firebase/agent-skills` uses `Firebase` for both, and `inline-chat/inline` uses `Inline` for both.

**Why no separate dev manifest.** Codex resolves marketplace manifests from four hard-coded relative paths, so shipping a `marketplace.dev.json` alongside a production one is not possible. Local development is handled by pointing Codex at a checkout (`codex plugin marketplace add ./`), which the maintainers guide now documents.

### Requirements

- [x] I've read and understood the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/slackapi/slack-skills-plugin/blob/main/.github/contributing.md) and have done my best effort to follow them.
- [x] I've read and agree to the [Code of Conduct](https://slackhq.github.io/code-of-conduct).
- [x] I've run `make test` and the tests pass.

author: 27mariogomez
body:
Fixes the pyqtgraph overflow warnings reported in iplot-viz/mint#177.

The minimap plots X relative to an integer offset taken from the baseline start. The timestamps arrive as unsigned nanoseconds, so a sample earlier than the window start (typically the extremity kept by decimated replies) wrapped around in the subtraction and landed at ~1.8e19, flooding the ViewBox with numpy 'overflow encountered in cast' warnings on every range update. The subtraction is now done in int64, so such a sample becomes a small negative coordinate instead.

The regression test builds a real pyqtgraph canvas with a sample preceding the window, renders the minimap and asserts both that no overflow warnings are emitted and that the plotted coordinates stay in range; it fails on develop and passes with the fix.

author: anandsundaram-hash
body:
Two commits. Both render evidence that already ships in the bundle and never reached a page.

## 1 — The day-one briefing

The estate pages say what the technology *is*. Nothing answered what someone asks in their first week. All of this was in the packet already:

```
How this business makes money   business model, revenue split, segments, who pays — as declared
What it is trying to do         5 corporate priorities, verbatim, in the record's own order
What the leadership says        44 of 44 leaders raised value realisation · 2 minority views
                                127 of 996 responses contradict the system record
In their own words              5 quotes, each attributed by role and theme
Industry patterns               12 the record states apply to this enterprise
```

The CEO, on value realisation:

> *"We approved Actuarial & Underwriting Analytics Modernization with a benefit number and nobody has been back to check whether it landed."*

That is the 43 blocked value claims, said out loud by the person who approved them.

**The blind spots render at the same weight as everything else.** No intake family carries a competitor, a peer plan, or a market-share figure, and nothing benchmarks a target externally. The page names those questions rather than staying silent, because silence reads as "no issue here".

## 2 — Every chapter gets the record it already has

A chapter with no drafted narrative rendered **"This chapter is not drafted yet"** and nothing else. True about the prose, false about everything else — the estate rows ship in the same bundle:

```
application_system 306 · vendor_contract 72 · infrastructure_platform 66 · data_asset 540
```

That chapter now renders six tables and five findings, computed at render time. **No model call.** Every figure is a filter over rows a reader can open.

```
What does not reconcile — five today
  <exposure>    108 applications holding PHI authenticate on local accounts   [CISO]
  <exposure>    196 regulated data assets are not yet production-governed     [CDO]
  <absence>     53 applications carry a declared end-of-support date          [Transformation Office]
  <established> 64% of the estate is self-hosted                              [CIO]
  <established> SQL Server linked-server pull is the largest pattern, 79/540  [VP Data & AI]
```

The authentication crossing produces a population **no single column holds**.

## Findings are rules, not sentences

Each computes its own number into a stable template, so it cannot go stale — it fires with a new number, or stops firing and the block gets shorter. That is why the block states its own count, and why **no empty state exists anywhere in these components**.

## Gates observed failing

- Remove the condition a finding reports → it **stops firing**, not fires with zero.
- An empty packet renders **no sections**, never headings over nothing.
- A testimony signal with no quotable text is **dropped**, not rendered blank.
- A table showing fewer rows than its source **states its own bound** (8 of 22 functions).

## Validation

- `npx jest src/components/home/v4/__tests__` — **47/47**, seven suites, no regression
- `npx eslint` on all changed files · `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` clean · `npm run release:check` passed

## One packet gap worth fixing next

Industry patterns reach the page as **titles only**. Their recorded `business_context`, `applicability` and `caveats` exist in the intake and are dropped by the packet builder. One change there makes the richest strategic content in the intake citable.

**Verified by the jsdom render harness the repo already uses for Home proof — a signed-in browser check is still owed before this is called live-proven.**

Release record: `docs/releases/records/2026-08-31-home-deterministic-page-depth.md`

author: marshallofsound
body:
Fixes the stuck "Backport Approval Enforcement" check on electron/electron#53332.

That PR ended up with five approval check runs on the head SHA. The four from the labeled/unlabeled deliveries all concluded "Not Required" within a minute of the PR opening. The fifth was created at 15:59:41Z by the `opened` handler and never completed, because the `opened` handler is always the slow one for a manual backport (it runs `updateManualBackport` first, which is what writes the labels in the first place). By the time it got to the approval verdict, its check-run snapshot from the top of the handler was two minutes stale, still said `queued`, and so the #423 guard let `queueBackportApprovalCheck` supersede the already-concluded run with a fresh queued one. Nothing fires after that, so it sits there forever. This isn't the reordering edge case #423 was defending against, it's the normal ordering for a manual backport.

Two changes:

- `queueBackportApprovalCheck` takes `{ supersedeCompleted }`. Callers that just need a pending run to exist pass `false`, and if the live run concluded in the meantime it's left alone. The decision is made against the re-fetch right before the write instead of the caller's snapshot. Both the "ensure a run exists" call at the top of the handler and the `opened` stay-pending path use it; the `backport/requested` paths keep superseding, which is the #53035 fix.
- The stay-pending path on `opened` is now only for trop-authored PRs, where the labels really do arrive from a different delivery (`backportImpl`). A manually opened backport gets labeled by `updateManualBackport` in the same handler before the live labels are read, so the verdict is already settled and it concludes right there, no labeled event needed.

Tests: reworked the #423 `opened` specs for the trop-authored case, added the manual-backport case from #53332, and covered `supersedeCompleted: false` in `checks-util.spec.ts`.

author: dpp
body:
Catalog-driven audit (unvalidated allocations, unbounded decompression,
silent truncation, unchecked escapes, symlink write-through) + test-first
fixes, each pinned by named tests with documented revert-checks.

## Highlights

* **RPM header caps:** entry count (100k) and data-store size (64 MiB) are
  validated BEFORE allocation — a 4-byte hostile field previously drove up
  to 2 GiB allocations/OOM.
* **Per-format budgets:** deb/apk/freebsd/openbsd/pacman reads now have an
  injectable decompressed-byte cap (2 GiB default), entry-count caps, and
  10 MiB metadata-member caps — previously unbounded.
* **Strict truncation (behavior change):** truncated CPIO/tar/ar archives and
  truncated member content now throw (`InvalidFormatException`/
  `IOException`/`BaharatStreamException`) instead of silently ending or
  returning partial data.
* **Extractor write-through fix:** extraction now verifies every parent path
  component (NOFOLLOW) and re-checks realpath containment before writing or
  deleting — a payload ordering `[symlink "etc" -> /etc, file "etc/passwd"]`
  previously clobbered files outside the target. Blocked under any ordering.
* **Uniform symlink policy:** dangerous targets are skipped consistently in
  all five tar readers (Apk/Pacman previously stored empty targets silently);
  absolute targets remain valid metadata.
* **Stream exception boundary:** mid-stream corruption surfaces as the
  documented `BaharatStreamException` carrying the checked cause — no bare
  `RuntimeException` anywhere.
* **Header strictness:** int-offset overflow fixed (`Math.addExact` — was an
  unchecked IOBE escape); corrupt string arrays return empty, never partial
  lists; `getStringStrict`/`getIntStrict` added; RPMs missing NAME/VERSION/
  ARCH are rejected at open.
* **Misc:** SQLite magic check reads 16 bytes instead of the whole DB;
  negative ar sizes rejected; no-progress streams fail instead of spinning;
  sparse tar entries expose their real/delivered size; FreeBSD manifest JSON
  is depth-guarded (GSON `StackOverflowError`).

## Testing

* 1074 tests, 0 failures / 0 errors / 0 skips (clean build, `mvn verify`).
* +46 new tests: jqwik property tests (CPIO truncation sweep comparing
  content, entry-order canary property, PackageReader fuzzing with a
  checked-only exception whitelist) in a dedicated isolated fork.
* Real distro-package corpus (`src/test/resources/...`) stays green under
  default budgets.

## Docs

* First ADRs: `docs/adr/001..005` (budgets, stream exception boundary,
  truncation semantics, symlink policy, strict header accessors).
* `gen_pkg_corpus.sh` (Docker) reproduces the corpus with SHA-256 sidecars.

## Behavior changes to call out

* Corrupt/truncated packages that previously "parsed" with partial data now
  throw (per-format tests updated with approval).
* Streams throw `BaharatStreamException` (documented) instead of bare
  `RuntimeException` mid-stream.

author: marius-patrik
body:
## Summary

- Converts `@dsh-stack/dialect-gemini` from `stack.kind: "extension"` to `"library"`, removing the dead `name`/`inject`/`Config`/`apply` cordis-plugin wrapper. It never mounted as a real cordis row anywhere; only its serialization helpers (`geminiDialect`, `serializeContents`, `buildToolNameIndex`, `translateGemini`, `mapGeminiFinishReason`) are actually consumed, by `@dsh-stack/dialect-code-assist` at the source-import level, not through the dialects registry.
- Fixes `src/packages/providers/check-plugin.mjs`'s own contract test, which had the same wrong assumption baked in — its `DIALECT_IDS` list included `"gemini"` and called `.apply(ctx)` on it, which is not what any real deployment's dialect resolution does.

## Why

Confirmed via `grep -rn 'dialect: "' publish/extensions/provider-*/src/index.ts`: every provider route resolves to `claude`, `antigravity`, `code-assist`, or `openai` — none to `gemini`. `provider-gemini-api` uses `dialect: "openai"` (Google's OpenAI-compatible endpoint), `provider-gemini-sub` uses `dialect: "code-assist"` (a JSON wrapper that imports `dialect-gemini`'s serialization helpers directly, not through `ctx.dialects.get()`). This predates #135's split of the monolithic `dialects` plugin — the old registry registered the same unused entry.

The `geminiDialect` implementation itself is real, complete, working code (not a stub) — this PR does not touch it, only the packaging: it was masquerading as an independently-mountable extension when nothing ever mounts it.

## Verification

- `pnpm build`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm verify`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm run format` all clean.
- `dialect-gemini`'s own `test.mjs` (protocol-level serialization tests, untouched) still passes.
- `dialect-gemini`'s `verify.mjs` rewritten to match the library shape (no `Context`/registration, just asserts the exported helpers).
- `@dsh-stack/providers`' contract test (`check-plugin.mjs`) — which broke on this change until its own `DIALECT_IDS` list was corrected — now passes, exercising exactly the dialect ids real deployments resolve.

Fixes #194

author: romulosutil
body:
Fecha a #494 exceto **T24** (smoke no painel Easypanel — só o Rômulo tem acesso). São 14 commits atômicos, um por task, na ordem sugerida pela issue.

> **Contexto para quem revisa sem a conversa:** a #72 mergeou o backend/infra do ditado de voz (PR #490) e fechou com a UI nunca implementada — os 6 checks obrigatórios passaram verdes com a feature inutilizável. Esta PR entrega a UI que faltava, conserta os oito defeitos achados na revisão pós-merge, implementa a decisão C de R19 e fecha as lacunas de teste. `FEATURE_FLAG_ASR_ENABLED` continua `false` por padrão: nada disto entra no ar com o merge.

---

## ⚠️ Requisito de deploy — ler antes de mergear

`ASR_WORKER_DATABASE_URL` é **fail-closed, sem fallback** para `DATABASE_URL`. Antes de deployar, provisionar uma vez, como dono do banco:

```sql
CREATE ROLE iris_asr_worker_login LOGIN PASSWORD '<gerada>' IN ROLE iris_asr_worker;
```

e apontar a env para ela. Sem isso, a rota do worker recusa subir — por desenho. Um fallback silencioso faria o worker rodar como `app_role`, que **perdeu** o grant nesta PR, e o tick morreria com `42501` a cada passada; ou pior, voltaria a funcionar se alguém reconcedesse o `EXECUTE`, desfazendo o T18 sem nenhum diff. `.env.example` e `infra/asr/runbook.md` §1.2/§1.3 têm o passo a passo e as queries de conferência.

Migrações novas: **`0139`** (coluna `reversoes` + índice parcial), **`0140`** (role do worker), **`0141`** (teto de reversões + backstop de idade).

---

## Parte 1 — a UI que faltava (T11, T12, T25)

`DitadoVoz` é o componente novo; `AudioLocal` delega a ele quando `asrHabilitado` desce do server component (R21 — o booleano nunca é lido do env no cliente, onde não existe e cairia para "desligado" em silêncio). A aba Áudio de 1 clipe continua funcionando com a flag desligada.

Teto de 2 min com encerramento automático (R1) · sem teto de quantidade (R2) · lista revisável com descartar/regravar por item (R4) · envio só no clique explícito (R5) · ordem preservada (R6) · botão que desabilita cobrindo o **lote inteiro**, não um clipe (R24) · clipe enviado perde as ações de edição (R27).

Resultado: 1 clipe = 1 parágrafo na ordem, com selo **visível** "Transcrito pela IA" (R17, `StatusBadge` do design system — nada de cor chumbada). Clipe falho vira "Não transcrito" com reenvio do IndexedDB ou digitação à mão (R12/R13). O texto **nunca** vai direto para a nota: "Usar no diário" o entrega ao rascunho e salvar segue sendo ato separado (R18).

Falha de **leitura** do polling renderiza erro e mantém o último estado — trocá-lo por lista vazia seria afirmar clinicamente que nada foi transcrito. Estourado o teto de 10 min, a UI para de pedir, diz que o lote pode seguir processando e **oferece um botão** de verificar de novo, em vez de mandar recarregar a página (um F5 no meio do diário custa o que o terapeuta digitou e não salvou).

`useGravador` extrai a máquina de microfone porque `AudioLocal` e `DitadoVoz` precisam do mesmo comportamento em permissão negada, codec de Safari (R7) e encerramento das trilhas — duplicá-la faria os dois divergirem justamente onde a falha é silenciosa.

**T25 / decisão C de R19:** `aceitarTranscricaoLote` lê e apaga `transcricao_texto` no **mesmo statement**, e só devolve o que o `UPDATE` de fato tocou. Se a RLS barrar a escrita, ela afeta 0 linhas em silêncio — devolver o texto ali entregaria uma transcrição que continua no banco. O `JOIN upd` é o que torna isso impossível.

**Dois defeitos que os próprios testes acharam antes do merge**, ambos da classe "tela certa, dado errado": a `ordem` do clipe lida de dentro do updater de `setClipes` chegava sempre `0` (o blob ia para a chave errada com a lista correta na tela); e a renumeração dos blobs feita dentro do updater esvaziava o mapa na segunda invocação do StrictMode.

## Parte 2 — os defeitos da revisão pós-merge

| | O que acontecia |
|---|---|
| **T14** | Só 503 revertia a tentativa. `401`/`403`/`404`/`502`/`504`/abort/rede gastavam tentativa, e em 3 a linha ia a `falhou` com `objeto_ref = NULL` — o que fazia o `finally` da rota **apagar o áudio**. Uma rotação de `ASR_SERVICE_TOKEN` feita só de um lado destruía toda a fila em ~60s. |
| **T15** | Timeout padrão de 30s contra mediana **medida** de 43,31s na VPS: o clipe mediano abortava antes de responder. Agora 120s, e as duas envs entraram no `.env.example` e no runbook. |
| **T16** | `DrizzleQueryError.message` embute os params — a transcrição — e a rota devolvia isso no corpo, que o script de disparo logava literalmente. Nota clínica inteira num log de container servido em **HTTP puro**. Agora só categoria fechada. |
| **T18** | Três definers cross-tenant que **não** devolvem 1 bit tinham `EXECUTE` para `app_role`. Role dedicada + `REVOKE` escrito (não deduzido de `CREATE OR REPLACE`, que preserva a ACL). |
| **T19** | `app_asr_falhar(id, true)` devolvia o clipe à fila ignorando o teto, e `app_asr_objetos_em_uso` conta `na_fila` como em uso — linha e objeto presos para sempre. Teto de 10 reversões em contador **próprio** + backstop de idade da linha. |
| **T20** | Idempotência tratava "linha inserida" como "lote concluído": queda de conexão no meio do upload deixava linhas `nao_solicitado` órfãs para sempre. |
| **T21** | Sem índice em `objeto_ref`. Medido em 50k linhas: `Seq Scan` 3334 buffers / 9,416 ms → `Index Scan` 3 buffers / 0,066 ms. |
| **T23** | `__pycache__` rastreado, `--dry-run` reportando "N apagado(s)" sem apagar nada, e áudio clínico ficando no IndexedDB para sempre quando a sessão expirava ou a aba fechava. |

**A premissa de T19 na issue estava parcialmente errada**, e o comentário da `0141` corrige: o laço do agendador **é** serial. A sobreposição real vem do cliente do disparo abortar em 120s enquanto o tick do servidor segue até ~215s — lockfile nenhum alcança isso, e por isso o fechamento é de banco. O lockfile entrou mesmo assim, cobrindo só o que cobre de fato: um segundo agendador no mesmo container.

## Defeitos que a própria PR criou e fechou

**A mudança de T20 abriu uma corrida.** Com o predicado novo, o perdedor da corrida que chega depois do commit do vencedor e antes da promoção lê o lote como não resolvido e re-sobe os blobs. Medido antes de decidir: **o upload roda fora de qualquer transação**, então um `pg_advisory_xact_lock` no SELECT de idempotência não fecharia a janela — ele solta no commit do INSERT, com o vencedor ainda uploadando. A correção é **compare-and-swap em `nao_solicitado`** nos dois UPDATEs do laço, e isso conserta um defeito maior que a corrida: sem ele, um UPDATE atrasado reverte para a fila um clipe que o worker já reservou ou transcreveu — transcrição duplicada e sobrescrita da nota que o terapeuta tem na tela.

O oráculo de R24 mudou junto: a contagem exata de uploads deixou de ser oráculo (a retomada a torna legitimamente variável) e passou a ser o **conjunto** de chaves escritas mais o estado final das linhas. O re-upload restante é inofensivo, e isso é medido: chave pura `loteId:ordem`, `PutObject` por chave (overwrite total, nunca merge parcial), nenhum clipe terminal ressuscitado.

## Um vazamento de credencial que só apareceu porque o teste era vacuoso (T22)

`storage.test.ts` injetava `new Error("AccessDenied: bad signature")` — literal que não conteria credencial sob implementação nenhuma, então a assertiva era verdadeira para qualquer entrada. Com o erro **realista** do SDK v3, que embute o cabeçalho `Authorization` inteiro (`Credential=<ACCESS_KEY>/…`), os três caminhos de `storage.ts` vazavam a chave — para um log lido no painel Easypanel em HTTP puro.

Na mesma leva: a auth do worker comparava um token de 13 bytes contra um de 23, então a checagem de comprimento curto-circuitava e `return true` na comparação sobrevivia à suíte inteira (qualquer portador com o comprimento certo seria aceito); e os 4 testes de `main()` do sweeper rejeitavam dentro de `resolveConfig()` sem nunca alcançar `varrer`, deixando passar a mutação que faria o sweeper **apagar áudio `na_fila

author: thalesbarretto
body:
**What it buys.** Removal of a live trap, not dead code. `cluster.dht-xattr-name` is settable on every release today, and setting it silently breaks the volume: rebalance linkfile cleanup returns EBUSY on every linkfile unlink, geo-replication syncs linkfile stubs to the secondary as real files, and `extras/rebalance.py` reads xattrs DHT never writes — because posix, geo-rep and the tooling all hardcode the default name the option claims to change, and no error surfaces anywhere. Its only consumer was the tier xlator, removed in 2019–2020. After this patch the on-disk names are fixed in code the way they were always fixed in practice.

**What it costs.** Nothing, for any deployment that works today: the option is `NO_DOC`, and no working volume can carry a non-default value — setting one breaks it as above. Stale state is handled by mechanisms already in the tree: glusterd drops unknown persisted keys with a warning, volgen never emits them, and graph init tolerates stale volfiles — `dht_init` now warns and uses the default. The residual, stated plainly: a volume that actually set a custom name keeps its old xattrs as inert baggage and self-heals layouts under the default on access. Nothing working exists to migrate, so no migration is provided.

**The proof.** Each claim is tested, not argued:
- `tests/bugs/distribute/issue-4674.t` (replacing `bug-924265.t`, which asserted the broken contract) went red→green across the change: defaults and the derived linkto name hold, a stale volfile mounts and serves but is not honored, set/get are rejected.
- A live upgrade A/B on a test cluster: option set on the old build → binaries upgraded → warning logged, volume serves, volfiles regenerate clean, the persisted key disappears from the store.
- A 106-test base-vs-patched differential (all of `tests/bugs/glusterd`, both distribute dirs, the thin-arbiter suite, volume smoke): zero regressions.

## Upgrade behavior tested

| Scenario | Result |
|----------|--------|
| Persisted `cluster.dht-xattr-name` at glusterd restart | "Unknown key" warning, key dropped from the volume dict and (after the next store write) from the info file |
| Stale client volfile with `option xattr-name` | mounts and serves; `dht_init` logs a warning; layout xattrs under the default name |
| Volfile regeneration (any `volume set`, or packaging's `*.upgrade=on` run) | regenerated volfiles carry no `xattr-name` |
| Old on-disk xattrs under a custom name | inert; layouts self-heal under the default on access |
| `volume set` / `volume get cluster.dht-xattr-name` | rejected (option unknown) |

Differential detail: 105 joined tests — 62 pass-on-both, 42 fail-on-both (container-environment noise, identical on both sides), 1 base-PASS→patched-FAIL flip (`brick-mux-validation-in-cluster.t`, a `count_N/A_brick_pids` settle-timeout) which re-ran 3×/side and passed on both — an unrelated timing flake, not charged.

Tree sweep: no other reference to `xattr-name`/`dht-xattr-name` remains (docs, extras, templates checked; `tests/thin-arbiter.rc` drops its stale default-value line in this patch).

Suggested release-note line: *"The tiering-era option `cluster.dht-xattr-name` is removed. Persisted values are dropped with a warning at glusterd restart; stale volfiles carrying the option are tolerated and ignored; on-disk xattrs under a custom name (never supported in practice) become inert."*

Fixes: #4674

author: eyelock
body:
Thirty-four commands printed as one flat list.

The complaint that lands is *"a CLI with this many commands is hard to learn"* — but the count is the wrong thing to blame. `git` has over a hundred and is learnable, because `git help` groups them. ynh's didn't.

## The groups were already there

Nothing had to be renamed or removed to see them:

```
Getting a harness   install uninstall update fork search registry sources
Using one           run agent ls info installed vendors
Authoring one       focus profile hook mcp include delegate sensors
Gating              check baseline
Operating           init status paths doctor prune image backend migrate
                    quarantine schema version help
```

A first-time reader needs the first two and can ignore twenty commands that aren't for them yet.

**Presentation only** — no renames, no removals, no wire change, no capability bump. This is the safe half of what #170 was reaching for.

## Descriptions rewritten where they restated the name

"Manage harness registries" survives. "Add a Git delegate to a harness" / "Remove a Git delegate from a harness" / "Update a Git delegate's options" — three lines saying nothing — becomes one saying what a delegate *is for*.

The footer now points at `ynh <command> --help`, which has existed since #260 and was mentioned nowhere on the page, and at `ynh schema --all`.

## Also fixes the sensors usage line

`cmd/ynh/sensors.go:68` printed `usage: ynh sensors <ls|show>` while `run` was dispatched. `ynh sensors --help` already listed all three; the error path didn't. I said I'd fix this in #260 and didn't.

## The guard caught the reformat

`TestEveryDispatchedCommandAppearsInUsage` failed immediately on all 34 — its regex anchored to a two-space indent, and commands are now indented under a heading. Updated to two-or-more.

The property it guards is unchanged: the name must *begin a line* rather than appear mid-sentence. Verified it still bites — removing `doctor` from the page fails it.

## Summary

Full day of live ASC + Samsung + RC progress captured, plus the operating rules learned along the way.

## Apple 1.0.1

- Version now **READY_FOR_REVIEW**; build 41 attached; \`usesIdfa=false\`; age rating \`FOUR_PLUS\`
- Draft review-submission bundle prepared, NOT submitted
- **App Privacy republished**: Financial Info removed (over-declared per code); Other Diagnostic Data added (\`TAMPER_SIGNAL\` / \`KEK_UNWRAP_FAILED\` / \`CRYPTO_DIAGNOSTICS\`; Not Linked; Analytics + App Functionality; no tracking). Cross-referenced against \`src/api/trackEvent.js\` and veyrnox.com/privacy §9.

## AI Security Protection — restructured into own subscription group

**Root problem**: Old AI SP subs were in the Safety Plus group. Apple's model: one sub per group at a time — so bundling AI SP under Safety Plus meant users couldn't hold both. Broke the "AI SP sits on top of Safety Plus" additive model.

**Fix**:
- New group \`22348777\` "AI Security Protection"
- New subs \`ai_security_protection_{monthly,annual}_2\` with 175 territories, 175 prices ($19.99 / $159.99 base US equalized), en-US localization, review notes, paywall screenshot
- Old subs deleted from Safety Plus group (SP now clean at 2 APPROVED)
- **RevenueCat**: 6 AI SP offerings × 2 packages relinked from old → new Apple products. Old products archived.

## Apple API gotchas (documented for reruns)

- \`PATCH subscriptions/{id}/relationships/group\` returns 403 — group assignment locked at sub creation.
- Sub name unique per app (409 on reuse).
- Sub state stays \`MISSING_METADATA\` ~15+ min after everything's populated (Apple backend cache lag).
- \`POST subscriptionPrices\` needs availability set FIRST; per-territory equalization is 175 POSTs.
- \`subscriptionPromotionalOffers\` require 176 API calls each (attributes + 175 territory prices). 10 offers = 1,760+ calls. Deferred — do via UI or dedicated batch script.

## Samsung

- Corporate Commercial Distribution Seller request **SUBMITTED** 2026-08-31 (Type of Sales: In Progress)
- Banking on file: Tide Current Account (ClearBank Ltd underlying) — sort/account/IBAN/SWIFT in doc
- URL param \`isCorpCommReq\` is cosmetic on Corporate-registered accounts (both \`Y\` and \`N\` render the same Corporate form)
- Awaiting Samsung review (typically 3–10 business days)

## Standing rule added

**One subscription group per service, decided at product creation.** Applies to Apple, Play, Samsung (Galaxy Store IAP), and Huawei (HMS IAP). If two subscription services are intended as additive (user holds both), they MUST be separate groups.

## RC MCP scope caveats (new section)

- \`attach/detach-products-to-entitlement\` → 403 (needs \`project_configuration:entitlements:read_write\`)
- \`attach/detach-products-to-package\` and \`archive-product\` → work
- Consequence: package swaps and archives scriptable; entitlement attach/detach dashboard-only

## Nothing was submitted for review

Prep state only. Owner clicks Submit for Review on the 1.0.1 draft bundle when ready.

## Test plan

- [x] Doc renders in GitHub markdown
- [x] Every state re-verified via ASC API + RC MCP at time of writing
- [ ] AI SP state to reach READY_TO_SUBMIT (Apple backend catch-up, poll before submit)
- [ ] Promotional offers (referral tiers + retention) populated on new AI SP subs before referral flow works on iOS

## What does this do?

Two new things for prompts:

**Run & Compare** : you can finally test your prompt versions instead of just storing them. Pick any two versions (say v1 vs the current one), give them the same input, hit run, and see both outputs side by side with token counts and how long each took. So instead of "here are my four drafts," you can actually tell which draft wins.

**Share** : publish a single prompt to a clean, read-only public link (`/p/...`) and send it to anyone, no login needed. Turn it off anytime and the link stops working. Everything stays private by default; only what you publish is visible.

- [ ] Bug fix (something wasn't working, now it does)
- [x] New feature (adds something cool and useful)
- [ ] Documentation (README, guides, comments)
- [ ] UI improvement (makes things look better or easier to use)

- [x] I added comments to explain tricky parts (if needed)

- Run & Compare is bring-your-own-key: add an OpenAI or HuggingFace key in Settings. Runs go through OpenAI or HuggingFace, so pick a model your key supports (e.g. `gpt-4o-mini` for OpenAI).

author: wfabian31773
body:
**P1 on `main`.** Codex found this on #241's head in a review that completed at 16:00:51Z, nine minutes after that PR merged. It is a safety defect, not transcript fidelity, and it is mine.

## What breaks

`handleCallerSpeechStarted` used one flag to answer two unrelated questions.

A caller who speaks **before** the greeting starts playing records `callerUtteranceHeld = false` — correct, their words genuinely come first and should be written through. But that same flag then gated the barge-in path. So on a **second** speech-start, once the greeting *is* playing, the stale `false` skipped the lock's early return, reached `assistantAudioPlaying === true`, and ran the barge-in: `cancelResponse()` plus a Twilio `clear`.

The greeting is cut mid-sentence. On `no-ivr` that is the 911 direction or the recording disclosure — the two statements the lock was added to protect. **The lock is defeated by the exact interaction it exists to survive**: a caller who talks over the opening.

Not hypothetical as a call shape: "hello?" while the line connects, then "hello, are you there?" once the agent starts speaking, is ordinary caller behaviour.

## The fix

Two questions, answered separately:

| question | when | scope |
|---|---|---|
| Where does this utterance's transcript line belong? | once, at `speech_started` | the caller |
| May the greeting be interrupted right now? | live, every time | the greeting |

The second is a fact about the greeting, so it is read fresh from `greetingHoldsTranscript()` rather than inherited from whatever the caller's first utterance concluded.

## Verification

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `npx vitest run src/runtime/ src/services/` — 1097 passing, 10 skipped; `p0Hardening.test.ts` is the documented baseline failure (needs real `DATABASE_URL`/`OPENAI_API_KEY`). Lane smoke 10/10.

Mutation-checked against a scratch copy:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| barge-in gated on the per-utterance flag again (the P1) | **5 red** |
| transcript decision recomputed on every speech-start | 1 red |

Control 90/90.

**The second mutation reddened nothing at first**, which is worth recording: the per-utterance carry added in #241 had become untested the moment barge-in stopped depending on it, because every ordering test has only one `speech_started` and the two forms agree there. The regression test now drives a second speech-start **and** its completion, so it pins the lock and the carry together — which is also the shape of the real call rather than two half-scenarios.

That is the seventh test this session that passed for the wrong reason. The pattern has not varied: a scenario that never reaches the state the bug needs.

author: maximeg129
body:
## Ce que contient cette PR

Deux modules pour l'indice d'endurance (section 3.3) — livrables aujourd'hui malgré 2 constantes toujours pending (exposant Riegel cyclisme R12, reconstitution W′ R15), parce que leurs chemins **principaux** n'en dépendent pas.

### `endurance.ts` — fait évoluer `src/components/cycling/riegel-types.ts`

Même mathématique que l'existant (régression log-log `P = a·t^(−e)` sur les records personnels de l'athlète), désormais adossée explicitement aux règles sourcées :

- **`fitEnduranceCurve`** — calibration individuelle (`riegel-calibrate-individual-exponent`, R13) : le chemin **principal**, déjà pleinement disponible, aucune constante pending requise.
- **`checkRiegelValidityDomain` / `recordsOutsideValidityDomain`** — nouveau : domaine de validité ~3,5-230 min (`riegel-validity-domain`, R12) via une nouvelle constante sourcée `RIEGEL_VALIDITY_DOMAIN` (`evidence/constants.ts`). Le texte source dit "avertir" hors de cette plage, pas "refuser" — la valeur reste utilisable, accompagnée d'un indicateur explicite plutôt que masquée.
- **`fallbackFatigueExponent`** — le seul chemin qui dépend de `RIEGEL_CYCLING_FATIGUE_EXPONENT` (toujours pending) : lève systématiquement aujourd'hui, jamais de valeur inventée.

### `criticalPower.ts` — nouveau, R14/R15

- **`fitCriticalPower`** — régression linéaire Travail (P×t) vs Durée : la forme linéaire de l'hyperbole puissance-durée de R14 (`Travail = CP·t + W′`). Pure algèbre appliquée au modèle déjà sourcé — **aucune constante pending requise**.
- **`wPrimeDepletionRateWatts` / `computeWPrimeBalanceDepletionOnly`** — déplétion de W′ au-dessus de CP, `W = (P−CP)×t`. Résolution de **Q6** (`docs/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`, votre réponse du 31 août) : pas un nouveau coefficient inventé, une reformulation algébrique de R14/R15. Explicitement "déplétion seule" — jamais de reconstitution sous CP tant que R15 est pending : un solde pessimiste, pas le vrai W′ balance de Skiba complet.
- **`wPrimeReconstitutionRate`** — dépend de `W_PRIME_RECONSTITUTION_CONSTANT` (pending, R15) : lève systématiquement aujourd'hui.

Ne remplace pas encore `riegel-types.ts`/`PowerCurveCard` — même posture que tous les modules `metrics/*.ts` précédents : domaine pur, testé, pas encore branché (Phase 5/UI).

## Validation

30 nouveaux tests (16 `endurance.test.ts` + 12 `criticalPower.test.ts` + 2 `constants.test.ts` pour `RIEGEL_VALIDITY_DOMAIN`) : régressions vérifiées sur des courbes générées exactement (round-trip), cas dégénérés (< 2 records, durées identiques, CP/W′ non positifs), domaine de validité Riegel (avertit sans masquer), effet multiplicateur de la déplétion W′ au-dessus de CP, solde qui ne remonte jamais sous CP, épuisement réel détecté sur un effort prolongé, et les deux fonctions pending qui lèvent systématiquement en citant leur Rxx.

Suite complète : 530/530 tests, `tsc --noEmit` clean, ESLint clean (2 warnings pré-existants sur des paramètres `_`-préfixés intentionnellement inutilisés — même convention déjà tolérée ailleurs dans le projet), build production clean. PR 0 à 5 sont mergées — celle-ci part de `main` à jour.

## Constantes pending restantes

Ten-Haaf (R33) — bloque toujours PR 7. Reconstitution W′ (R15) et exposant Riegel cyclisme (R12) restent pending mais ne bloquent plus rien dans cette PR (voir ci-dessus) — elles ne gatent que les chemins de repli explicitement documentés.

## Questions ouvertes

Aucune nouvelle. Q6 est résolue (voir plus haut).

author: enorm
body:
## Summary

Closes #926

`ej-site-down` is the rule #271 asked for first and the one #285's fourth box is meant to prove. **It could not be created on production, and it has not been
able to fire on staging since 24 August.**

```
$ EJ_NODE=ops@10.10.0.1 ./apply.sh
ej-site-down   created  404  <-- {"code":404,"message":"Stream kube_deployment_status_replicas_available not found"}
```

The stream does not exist because the metric never arrives. The gateway's egress policy permits `kube-system` on **9153 only** — CoreDNS:

```
warn  Failed to scrape Prometheus endpoint
      instance="kube-state-metrics.kube-system.svc.cluster.local:8080", job="kube-state-metrics"
```

## The omission was argued from a false premise

The policy header said:

> No allowance for `kube-state-metrics`, which the collector chart references **and does not install**, so that scrape has failed every cycle since #271.

It does install it — as a subchart, running in `kube-system` on both clusters:

```
kube-system   kube-state-metrics-77577b9db5-zpwjd   1/1  Running   (production, started with the collectors)
kube-system   kube-state-metrics-77577b9db5-tfjbs   1/1  Running   (staging, 10d)
```

So the policy was blocking a target that exists. The comment is **corrected rather than deleted** — the reasoning was wrong, and a reader who finds only an
allowance will wonder why it needed one.

Third fault of the same family, after #923 and #924: the policy set was written from belief and never exercised from a cold start.

**`--diff` cannot catch this class.** It compares the cluster's rules to this repository, not whether a rule can match a series — so it reports `ej-site-down in
sync` while the rule is inert. That is a real gap in the tooling and is noted in #926 rather than fixed here.

## What stays red, deliberately

Traefik and the four `flux-system` controllers also fail to scrape. Both are `prometheus-autodiscovery`, which this policy bounds to `event-junkie` and this
namespace on purpose — the file says widening it is a decision naming the namespace. kube-state-metrics is a different job and a chart dependency rather than an
annotated pod, which is why it is the one allowance added.

## Testing

```
flux schema validate deploy/clusters          144 resources, Valid: 139, Invalid: 0, Skipped: 5
kubectl kustomize deploy/clusters/production  renders; namespaceSelector AND podSelector in one `to`, port 8080
scripts/cluster-assertions.sh                 all assertions passed
scripts/comment-lint.sh check                 no violations
```

The selector pairing is worth checking in the render rather than in the source: two entries under one `to:` are an AND, and splitting them into two would open
port 8080 to every pod in every namespace.

**Nothing applied by hand.** The proof is `apply.sh` creating `ej-site-down` without a 404, then `--check` reporting it returning data.
