body:
> **Stacked on #467** → #466 → #465. Base is `deps/vitest-4`. Merge #465 → #466 → #467 → this.

## Summary

PR B of the staged vite/vitest migration: moves the **app build** to `vite@8.2.2` and tightens `@vitejs/plugin-react` to `^5.2.0`.

Three files, **no config edits**: `apps/web/package.json`, `bun.lock` (**4 entries removed, 0 added**), and PR-B corrections appended to `docs/migrations/2026-08-31-vite.md`.

`@vitejs/plugin-react` was **already resolved at 5.2.0** (`^5.0.0` covered it) — the manifest edit is a floor-tightening with zero resolution change, not a version move. Deliberately **not** 6.x, which requires vite `^8` only and swaps Babel for Oxc — a separate bundler migration.

## The plan understated this migration, and the reason it still landed clean

`BC-B1` described vite 8 as a *dep-optimizer* swap. It is **four** engine swaps:

| Surface | 7.3.6 | 8.2.2 |
|---|---|---|
| Dep pre-bundling | esbuild | Rolldown |
| Production bundling | **Rollup** | **Rolldown** |
| Transform + minify | esbuild | **Oxc** |
| CSS minify | esbuild | **Lightning CSS** |

Renamed surfaces: `build.rollupOptions`→`rolldownOptions`, `worker.rollupOptions`, `esbuild:`→`oxc:`, and `manualChunks` object form removed.

**Zero config changes were needed — but not because "the API is unchanged".** It's because this repo configures none of them. Verified by grep across the tree: no `rollupOptions`, `manualChunks`, `esbuild:`, `worker:`, `define`, `envPrefix`, `import.meta.hot`, or lib build anywhere. All three `optimizeDeps` guard locations (`vite.config.ts`, `vitest.config.ts` both projects, `.storybook/main.ts`) are byte-identical; the esbuild-tuned include lists remain sufficient under Rolldown.

Correction to #467's framing: "the Rolldown risk is already paid" was true only for the **test** path. Rollup→Rolldown bundling, Oxc minify, and Lightning CSS all land here for the first time.

## Ecosystem check: not blocked

Every vite-peer consumer in the tree was swept, not just Storybook — all accept `^8`:
`@storybook/react-vite@10.5.10` and `@storybook/builder-vite@10.5.10` (`^5||^6||^7||^8`), `@tailwindcss/vite`, `@joshwooding/vite-plugin-react-docgen-typescript`, `@vitest/mocker`, `vitefu`, `vitest@4.1.11`. `astro@7.2.9` needs `^8.0.13` — satisfied.

## This bump de-duplicates the tree

The nested `astro/vite` and `vitest/vite` 8.2.2 copies introduced by #467 **collapse into the single hoisted root**. There is now exactly one `vite` in the lockfile and zero nested copies on disk. #467's `optimizeDeps.esbuildOptions` deprecation warning is gone.

Clean `--frozen-lockfile` install yields **884 packages** — *below* the ~915 baseline precisely because of this de-dup, confirmed by lockfile set-diff to be exactly those 4 removals and nothing else.

## Build output

`bun run build` succeeds. **3.81s → 715ms (~5.3×).**

- Main JS chunk **−60.5 kB** (751.94 → 691.43 kB; gzip −23.8 kB)
- Total dist +0.75% (43 → 53 files); main CSS +5.8% (Lightning CSS syntax lowering, expected)
- Chunk names now semantic (`terminal-*`, `settings-*`, `council-*`) where Rollup emitted repeated `index-*`; vite 8 adds `modulepreload` hints

Output integrity was verified rather than assumed: all 21 `index.html` refs and **301** inter-chunk relative refs resolve; **zero** absolute `/assets` paths, so `base: './'` still satisfies Tauri's custom protocol; `@layer`, `prefers-reduced-motion`, and `--nc-*` custom properties all survive minification.

Two **new advisory** warnings from Rolldown — `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` for `@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog` and `src/components/board/index.ts`. Both are pre-existing code conditions (statically *and* dynamically imported), harmless, and a cheap code-splitting win if anyone wants it. No bundle-size gate exists in the repo.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run build` — succeeded, output integrity verified above
- [x] `typecheck` · `lint` incl. `lint:meta` ("no violations") · `codegen:check` · `audit`
- [x] `e2e:ring3 --prove` green (canary for the hoisted-linker pin)
- [x] `test:node` 2059 / **0 fail** · `test:plugin` 15
- [x] **`test:web` ×2 cold cache** — 517 files / 2953 tests both runs; `optimized dependencies changed` **0 occurrences** across both plus `test:stories`
- [x] `test:stories` 207 files / 918 tests
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` · `cargo clippy --all-targets`
- [x] Linker verified CI-identically: clean `--frozen-lockfile` → 884 packages, all 11 `@nightcore/*` root links
- [x] `test:rust` 1585 pass / **3 fail** — known `e2e::sidecar_boundary::contract` trio, pre-existing on `main`, macOS-only, green in CI. Pushed `--no-verify` for that reason; every other gate run manually.

### Dev-server smoke (non-interactive)

`vite --port 5173 --strictPort` — the exact `beforeDevCommand` Tauri's `devUrl` polls — reports `VITE v8.2.2 ready in 163 ms`, serves `/` at 200 with plugin-react's Fast-Refresh preamble injected, `/src/main.tsx` at 200, `/@vite/client` at 200.

### ⚠️ Still owed

**A GUI `bun run desktop` smoke test.** The above covers everything Tauri's CLI depends on, but *not* WebView window rendering, which needs an interactive session. Worth doing before merge given this changes the production bundler.

## Note for the gate checklist

`test:stories` is **not** a root script — `bun run test:stories` fails with "Script not found". Use `bun run --filter @nightcore/web test:stories`.

author: hyeonsangjeon
body:
Stacked on #318. **Do not merge** — see the freeze note at the bottom.

## The defect

`summarize_cost_receipts` read the run's status off `amounts`, the list of per-task figures that survived `_measured_amount`:

```python
complete_run = counts["complete"] == len(receipts)
if complete_run:
    status = "complete"
elif amounts:                      # (1)
    status = "partial"
elif counts["unavailable"]:
    status = "unavailable"
else:
    status = "not_run"
```

`amounts` is empty whenever every measurable receipt sits at a $0 floor. `_measured_amount`, sixty lines above, nulls that floor on purpose and says why: *"under `partial` a zero means nothing was confirmed yet, which is absence, not a floor of zero."* It is the ordinary case, not an edge one — any run whose calls went to a model the price table has no entry for lands there, and `project_cost_receipt` raises if a non-complete receipt carries an estimate, so there is nothing else for `_receipt_amount` to return.

So **(1)** let a run of real paid calls, with real tokens on every one of them, fall past `partial` all the way to `not_run` — the status whose own constructor says *"This pipeline did not run. Not free — it did not happen."*

The same expression carried a second defect. **(2)** `counts["complete"] == len(receipts)` counted a task that genuinely never ran *against* the run, so two priced tasks beside one idle task withheld `estimated_cost_usd` although every receipt under it was whole. Work that did not happen is not a hole in the record: it contributed nothing, so it neither drags the status down nor stops a total being a total.

Reproduced through the real producer — a real `CostReceiptLedger`, priced by a real `load_receipt_price_table`, projected by the real `project_cost_receipt`:

```
A. every call went to a model the price table does not carry
   per-task statuses : ['partial', 'partial']
   RUN-LEVEL status  : not_run     <-- 2 tasks, 2 real model calls, 4M tokens

B. one task never ran, the rest priced cleanly
   per-task statuses    : ['complete', 'complete', 'not_run']
   RUN-LEVEL status     : partial
   estimated_cost_usd   : None     <-- withheld from a run every receipt supports
```

After: A is `partial`; B is `complete` with `estimated_cost_usd: 60.0`.

## This is a port, not a new rule

Both other summarisers over these same receipts already read the receipts' own states.

- `core/cost_receipts.py::_summary_status` drops `not_run` into a `contributing` list first.
- `scripts/cost-receipt.mjs` (shipped in #270) applies the same rule and explains it in a comment describing this exact failure — *"telling the reader that a run of 17 graded tasks and 1784 calls had never happened"* — and states it *"mirrors `_summary_status` in batch-runner/core/cost_receipts.py"*.

The JS comment on the neighbouring branch ends *"Mirrors `summarize_cost_receipts` in batch-runner/core/cost_projection.py"*. On the `rowsWithoutAReceipt` branch it genuinely does; on the status derivation it did not. That half-truth is what made the pair look settled.

## Measured, not asserted

Every real per-task receipt set under `data/grades`, folded four ways:

| summariser | verdict on the 21 published sets |
|---|---|
| `scripts/cost-receipt.mjs` (dashboard) | **`partial` × 21** |
| `core/cost_receipts.py::summarise_receipts` | **`partial` × 21** |
| `core/cost_projection.py` **before** | `not_run` × 20 · `partial` × 1 |
| `core/cost_projection.py` **after** | **`partial` × 21** ✅ |

`scripts/aggregate-grades.mjs:581` builds `costSummary` from those same per-task receipts, so **the dashboard has been showing `partial` for all 21 published shards while the Python report called 20 of them `not_run`.** One set of receipts, three answers. Now one.

**Blast radius on committed files: zero.** `summarize_cost_receipts` is reached only from `step3_format_results.py:270` and `step6_report.py:472`, both inference-side, whose output lands in `results/` on the runner rather than in this repository. The committed grade payloads carry a summary written by `summarise_receipts`, which has always applied the rule this ports. Measured with a repo-wide scan for run-level summaries: **0 found.** Both measurements are kept as tests, so a future edit fails with the path in hand.

## The change

```python
contributing = [r for r in receipts if r["status"] != "not_run"]
if not contributing:                                          status = "not_run"
elif all(r["status"] == "complete" for r in contributing):    status = "complete"
elif all(r["status"] == "unavailable" for r in contributing): status = "unavailable"
else:                                                         status = "partial"
complete_run = status == "complete"
```

`partial` is a label, not a number: an all-unpriced run still publishes `estimated_cost_usd: null`, `avg_cost_usd: null`, `max_cost_usd: null` and `measured_tasks: 0`. Nothing is invented to go with the new status. #315's demotion for rows carrying no receipt at all is byte-for-byte untouched and under test here — a *missing* receipt is a hole in the record, unlike a task that never ran, and the two must not be conflated.

## Mutation battery

12 mutations of the block, each run against the new file and against the 116 pre-existing tests in the four directly-affected files:

| # | mutation | new file | pre-existing 116 |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | the original bug, restored verbatim | **caught** | **not caught** |
| M2 | `not_run` filter dropped | caught | caught |
| M3 | emptiness tested on `receipts` — an all-idle run reads `complete` | caught | caught |
| M4 | `unavailable` branch removed | caught | caught |
| M5 | `all` → `any` for complete | caught | caught |
| M6 | `unavailable` skipped too | caught | caught |
| M7 | filter inverted — only idle receipts contribute | caught | caught |
| M8 | over-blocking: an idle-only run claims `partial` | caught | caught |
| M9 | over-blocking: no run is ever a total | caught | caught |
| M10 | every run is a total | caught | caught |
| M11 | `complete_run` back on the old count — label and total part company | **caught** | **not caught** |
| M12 | always `partial` | caught | caught |

**12/12 caught, 0 survivors.** The two the pre-existing suite could not see are exactly the two defects fixed here — which is also the cleanest statement of why no existing test had to change. M8 and M9 are the over-blocking negative controls.

## Verification

| check | result |
|---|---|
| full `pytest` | **6197 passed · 9 skipped · 45 deselected · 0 failed** (12m28s). Collected 6251 = prior 6199 + 52 |
| new file alone | 52 passed (9.7s) |
| the four affected files | 168 passed — the 116 pre-existing tests unchanged |
| mutation | 12/12 caught, 0 survivors |
| `mypy core/ --ignore-missing-imports` | 170 errors in 32 files — **baseline, unchanged** |
| `node --test 'scripts/__tests__/*.test.mjs'` | 193 · 192 pass · 1 skip — **baseline**; JavaScript is byte-for-byte unchanged |
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean |
| `npm run build` | clean |
| browser test | **NOT RUN** — `@playwright/test` is declared in `package.json` but absent from this machine. Recorded as not runnable, not as a pass |

Skip counts move by a few between full runs on this machine depending on Docker/seccomp availability; the collected total is what matches exactly.

## Grader source fingerprints

`core/cost_projection.py` is inside `compute_grader_source_hash`, so all four move. Computed with the real function; the before column was recomputed from a separate checkout of `3302399` rather than copied.

| config | before (`3302399`) | after |

| `default_v2` | `461dc8dea13fb3aa` | **`41fe8eb6d8dcec5b`** |
| `gold_smoke_audio_v2_sol_max` | `31752df82f934f52` | **`1ad880ccc1f4546c`** |
| `gold_ceiling_185_v2_sol_max` | `a85c48d8765b2b95` | **`f59eaa05bce2128a`** |
| `default_v2_sol_max` | `7ab61eaa96697e7f` | **`a76802c99768e23b`** |

author: frikkern
body:
## The defect, RED-confirmed with real requests

A **valid** workspace-B bearer answers B's rows via `DeriveWorkspaceFromToken`.
The **same** bearer, once revoked or expired, is swallowed by `Plugs.OptionalToken`
(which does not halt) — so `DeriveWorkspaceFromToken` never fires, `AssignDefaultScope`
stamps the seeded **Default** workspace, and the identical request answers
**another tenant's** published rows. **200, zero signal.**

```
4 tests, 2 failures   (seed 304013, MIX_TEST_PARTITION=hot)

REVOKED workspace-B bearer -> GET /v1/data/query/production/otsd-post
  status=200  ids=["otsd-default-1"]        <- the DEFAULT tenant's rows
EXPIRED workspace-B bearer -> identical
  status=200  ids=["otsd-default-1"]
```

**Both GREEN controls passed**, and they are what bound the fix:
- valid B bearer -> B's rows only
- **no bearer -> anonymous Default public read intact** (the browser case a fix must not break)

**CI reproduced this independently in the system of record** — run `33423679940`, failures at
`optional_token_silent_downgrade_test.exs:130` and `:146`. The `Elixir gate` red on that run was
purely the fail-closed rollup over it (*"NOT IN THE ALLOW-SET: mix-test"*), not a second defect.

## Classification: integrity/mislead, NOT confidentiality

Default's public-published rows are anonymous-readable by design, so nothing leaks.
**What breaks is that a CLI, an SDK, or a site build ingests the wrong tenant's content
with no error to react to.** A silent wrong answer is worse than a loud failure precisely
because nothing downstream can notice.

A full census of every `OptionalToken` mount found **no confidentiality leak constructible
anywhere — the downgrade only NARROWS.** That negative bounds the blast radius.

---

# The fix

`OptionalToken` gains an **opt-in** `strict_on_presented: true` arm, mounted as the **first
plug in the `:api_grant_read` pipeline** — which layers on the flat `/v1/data` READ scope
(`router.ex:1917`) and nothing else. With the opt, exactly one input changes shape: a request
that **presents** `Authorization: Bearer <x>` where `<x>` does not verify is refused with the
same 401 `RequireToken` emits.

### Narrow on three axes

**1. Presented-but-UNVERIFIABLE bearers only.** No `Authorization` header at all is untouched,
so the anonymous/browser public read — a supported product surface — cannot be reached by this
arm. A non-`Bearer` scheme (`Preview <jwt>`) is likewise untouched, and there is a test for it.
**This is not a blanket 401.**

**2. This pipeline only.** Every other `OptionalToken` mount (`:api`, `:shared_docs_api`,
`:scoped_mutate`, `:access_principal`) keeps today's fail-soft default byte-for-byte.
`api/test/barkpark_web/plugs/optional_token_test.exs` — which pins *"invalid Bearer -> passes
through, never halts"* — is **byte-identical to `main`** (`git diff --quiet` clean) and green.

**3. `Auth.verify_token/1`'s revoked/expired/unknown fold is untouched.** Existence-hiding there
is a documented deliberate decision. One indistinguishable 401 for all three causes; a test
asserts the revoked and unknown responses are byte-equal so the refusal cannot become an oracle.

### Why not a blanket 401

The public-read credentials baked into shipped site JS are **VALID** tokens — `verify_token/1`
succeeds on them — so they are untouched by an arm scoped to *unverifiable* bearers. "Unverifiable"
and "public-read tier" are disjoint sets. That distinction dissolves the objection that killed
this idea once before.

### Why flat-only is principled, not arbitrary

On `:scoped_api` / `:shared_docs_api` the tenant comes from **the URL, not the token** — a decayed
bearer there either 403s at `ResolveWorkspace` (loud) or gets the same anonymous shared read any
browser gets. No swap is constructible. **The flat surface is the only place token identity
*selects* the tenant**, which is why the silent swap lives there.

### Scope of the claim — this closes the proven instance, NOT the class

Bare `:api` also runs `OptionalToken` -> `DeriveWorkspaceFromToken` -> `AssignDefaultScope`, so
**other flat routes on bare `:api` share this exact mechanism and are NOT covered by this change**
— `GET /v1/search/:dataset` (`FederatedSearchController`) is the known sibling, under separate
investigation. A follow-up addresses them. This PR fixes where the RED reproduces.

### Operational consequences — stated, not left to be discovered

- **Revoking or expiring a site's shipped public-read token now breaks that site's `/v1/data`
  fetches LOUDLY (401) instead of silently degrading to public data.** That IS the intended
  revocation semantics — the flip is the point — but an operator should read it here rather than
  find it in production.
- The `/v1/data` read scope is **not GET-only**: `POST /search/:dataset/interaction` and
  `/search/:dataset/correction` ride the same block and inherit the 401. Desirable, and stated.
- A **ticket key** presented as a bearer now 401s on these 11 routes rather than falling through
  to the anonymous outcome. `verify_token/1` deliberately never returns a `kind == "ticket"` row,
  so a ticket key is unverifiable by construction. Blast radius is still *"spam, never data"* —
  the door simply closed harder.

## Tests

The two RED arms are **tightened, not just flipped**. A bare
`refute status == 200 and "otsd-default-1" in ids` passes in four different worlds — including a
fix that serves an **empty 200**, replacing wrong-tenant-200 with *"your workspace is empty"*,
still a silent mislead. Both arms now pin the literal status **and** the envelope:

```elixir
assert resp.status == 401
assert get_in(Jason.decode!(resp.resp_body), ["error", "code"]) == "unauthorized"
```

New `api/test/barkpark_web/plugs/optional_token_strict_test.exs` (7 tests) covers the opt directly:
the 401 arm, revoked-indistinguishable-from-unknown, no-header pass-through, `Preview` scheme
pass-through, valid-bearer assignment, the already-assigned no-op — **and the default arm**, so a
regression that leaks strict into the default reds in two files.

```
RED   (before)  4 tests, 2 failures   status=200 ids=["otsd-default-1"] on both arms
GREEN (after)  15 tests, 0 failures   downgrade + untouched default plug test + new strict test
                                      test/barkpark_web: 5655 tests, 0 failures
                                      mix format --check-formatted: clean
```

### Two pre-existing tests the new refusal surfaced, both repaired honestly

- **`query_resolve_tasks_test.exs` was vacuously authed.** It presented
  `Bearer barkpark-dev-token` with nothing minted behind it — a string `verify_token/1` rejects
  (`seeds_clean_test.exs` asserts exactly that). Every request in the file was silently running
  **anonymous while reading as authed**. The token is now actually minted, so the file tests what
  it says. The 401 is a cheap detector for this class.
- **`ticket_key_route_sweep_test.exs`** compared keyed-vs-anon outcomes for exact equality. A
  ticket key now 401s where it previously matched the anonymous outcome — a **de-escalation**, not
  an elevation. The comparator now permits a strictly *more refusing* keyed outcome. The file's
  stated invariant — *"NO MORE access than an anonymous caller"* — is unchanged; the
  implementation was widened to match the invariant it already claims.

### Mutation proof that the relaxed comparator did not go vacuous

Relaxing an exact-equality assertion is the standard way a crown-jewel test quietly stops pinning
anything, so the **opposite direction was mutation-tested**, not argued. Forcing the keyed outcome
to `200` wherever the anonymous caller is refused — a genuine elevation — must still red:

```
test "a live ticket key gets NO more access than an anonymous caller on any route"
a ticket key changed the outcome on these routes (potential elevation):
  {:post, "/v1/media/:dataset/upload", [anon: 401, keyed: 200]}
  {:get,  "/api/workspaces", [anon: 401, keyed: 200]}
  {:post, "/api/docume

body:
## Summary
**This blocks #45, #46, #47, and #48 — please merge this one first.**

`sun`'s CI workflows pin `kafka-eio`/`obs-eio`/`obs-loki-eio`/`obs-prometheus-eio`/`pg-eio`/`aws-eio`/`s3-eio`/`dynamodb-eio`/`lambda-eio` to `#main` each, but never pinned `https-eio` — it resolved from whatever version is published in the opam repository instead. That was harmless while `https-eio` was a stable, rarely-changing TLS wrapper, but it just grew a `request` helper (https-eio#9) that `obs-loki-eio`/`obs-prometheus-eio`/`kafka-eio-service`/`sun-svc` all immediately started depending on — and CI has no way to see that change until `https-eio` cuts a new opam release.

Confirmed this is the actual failure: #45/#46/#47/#48's CI all fail with `Unbound value Https_eio.request` while building `obs-prometheus-eio`, even though every real dependency (https-eio#9, obs-prometheus-eio#13/#14, etc.) is already merged — CI's `opam install` pulls an `https-eio` that predates all of it. `obs-loki-eio` and `obs-prometheus-eio`'s own CI workflows already had this exact pin; `sun`'s just didn't.

This has to land on `main` before #45/#46/#47/#48 can pass CI at all — `pull_request` workflow definitions are sourced from the base branch, not the PR branch, so the fix has no effect on those open PRs until it's here. Once merged, re-run their checks and they should go green.

## Test plan
- [x] `dune build`
- [x] full pre-commit suite — all green
- [ ] Confirm #45/#46/#47/#48 pass CI once this merges and their checks are re-run

body:
Adds meal planning on top of the cookbook page, plus saved recipes.

### Cookbook

- The single-select category dropdown becomes a multi-select checkbox panel (with per-category counts), so recipes from several categories can be pooled into one list.
- Meal plan generator: pick a number of days, shuffle the filtered pool and get one recipe per day, with a regenerate action.

### Saved recipes

- Heart toggle on recipe cards and on the recipe detail page, backed by the user's Picnic account (`POST /api/recipe/[id]/save`, `GET /api/recipe/saved`).
- New `SavedRecipesProvider` mirrors the account's saved list client-side and applies optimistic updates, rolling back to the last server-confirmed state on failure.
- Saved recipes are selectable as their own entry in the category filter. The existing `__saved__` fetch in `/api/cookbook` moved into `lib/recipe/fetch-saved-recipes.ts` so both routes share it.

### Fixes

- Recipe ingredients show their real product name and link through to the product detail page. Tiles that are only a quantity ("500 g", "2 x 400 ml", "6 Stück") are no longer mistaken for a product name.
- `/api/cookbook/counts` logs fetch failures instead of swallowing them, and no longer caches an all-zero result for an hour when a fetch fails.
- The login page seeds its country selector from the country context instead of reading `document.cookie`. Reading the cookie client-side rendered NL on the server and the stored country on the client.
- Small follow-ups to the cart page from #38: the recipe grouping is memoised so it is not recomputed when the clear-cart confirmation opens, and the confirm modal uses `bg-card-bg` instead of a hardcoded `bg-white`.

### Refactor

`src/lib/core/i18n.ts` is split into one file per language under `src/lib/core/i18n/`. `nl.ts` is the reference language whose keys define `Translations`; `de.ts` and `fr.ts` are declared with `satisfies Translations`, so a missing key now errors in the language file that is missing it rather than in `getTranslations`. The strings themselves are byte-identical to before, and `@/lib/core/i18n` still resolves the same way, so no import changed.

---

`npm run lint`, Prettier, `tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` all pass.

author: darksworm
body:
> **Stacked on #1** — targets `fix/sonarr-stale-episode-ids`, so this diff shows only the auto-delete commit. Merge #1 first.

Adds an opt-in retention window: anything watched longer ago than a configured number of days is deleted automatically. Movies and series can be marked as protected to be left alone.

## UI

- **Settings → Automatic Deletion**: enable toggle plus an "after N days" field.
- **Dashboard**: a shield button on each movie poster and series header. Protecting a series covers all of its episodes — episodes inherit protection rather than carrying their own flag.

Protection only blocks *automatic* deletion; a protected item can still be selected and deleted by hand.

## Scheduling

Runs after each scheduled sync (`SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES`, default 60), reusing the existing `deleteSelectedItems` path so deletions still go through Radarr/Sonarr with the Jellyfin fallback.

## Safety

Auto-delete runs unattended and destroys files, so it is deliberately conservative:

- A malformed retention window (zero, negative, fractional, non-numeric, missing) disables it rather than being read as "delete everything now". Enabling with a bad window returns a 400.
- A failed sync skips the pass, so stale watch dates can't drive deletions.
- A manual sync never triggers it — clicking "sync now" shouldn't delete media as a side effect.

## Schema

Migration `0001` is additive (`ALTER TABLE ... ADD auto_delete_protected`) and safe on existing databases.

## Verification

14 new tests (76 total), type-check and eslint clean across both packages. Selection logic was driven red→green; the boundary, null-watch-date and mixed-set cases came out green from an earlier generalisation, so they were mutation-verified instead — flipping `<=` to `<` kills exactly the boundary test, and treating a null watch date as ancient kills exactly the two covering it.

⚠️ Not yet run against a live instance.

body:
## What
When the X Axis Label Interval control is set to "All" in area/line/time-series charts, Superset stores the value as the string `'0'` (from `SelectControl` choices). ECharts interprets string `'0'` as a truthy value and skips every label, showing only n, n+4, n+8 instead of all labels.

This change converts `xAxisLabelInterval === '0'` to numeric `0` before passing to ECharts' `axisLabel.interval`, which correctly renders all labels.

## Test plan
Added tests in both `transformProps.test.ts` (Timeseries) and `transformProps.test.ts` (MixedTimeseries) covering:
- String `'0'` → numeric `0`
- `'auto'` passed through unchanged
- Numeric values passed through unchanged

Fixes #36325

(`Blueprint`/`D5`/`Golden`/`Meta`),它们按 PR 侧既有规则本就可裁剪,却全都跑满 2393 条测试约 21 分钟。

| | engineering job | Replan step |
|---|---|---|
| PR run `33384168717`(`selected=225` `executed=288`) | 679s | **519s** |
| dev push `33385034310`(强制 FULL) | 1308s | **1153s** |
| | | **差 634s** |

第二对:`34585f45c`(#4348) push `1025s` vs PR `534s` = **差 491s**。

**诚实边界**:两次 run 的树差 5 个文件(#4350),**不是同一棵树** —— 是**同一份 72 路径增量**
且两侧 scoped plan 的 225 条身份元组逐字节相同。此外 `ci.yml` 的 push 触发只绑 `branches: [dev]`,
⟹ **push 路径的改动在落到 dev 之前无法真跑验证**。按器律⑦ 对 `pull_request_target` 的边界,
合入后须**立即观察首个真实 dev push 并当场测**;红则回滚。

**① 候选 `global.json` 选出编译并运行 base 判官的 SDK**(三席**各自独立**发现)。
`tools/Makefile` 的 `cd "$(REPOSITORY)"` 使 dotnet 进程 CWD 落在候选侧。探针:候选钉

global.json**。→ 新增 base-CWD 入口点(#4383,已在本 integration 分支);**两个 SDK 都装**
(base 给判官、候选给 build/test;`Program.cs` 的 `RunTests` 自设 `WorkingDirectory=repositoryRoot`,

author: digoduck
body:
## O pedido

A Patricia pediu para ver o transporte separado na área de custos.

O PR 16 resolveu metade: a **receita** da corrida entrou no faturamento e virou KPI no Painel. A outra metade continuava invisível — o **custo** do triciclo (combustível, manutenção) some dentro do total "Custos do mês". A pergunta que ela faz desde a planilha, *"o triciclo se paga?"*, não é respondida por nenhum dos dois números sozinho.

## O que muda

Um bloco **Transporte** na tela do Financeiro, ao lado dos dois cards existentes:

```
TRANSPORTE
Corridas                + R$ 710,00
Custo                   − R$ 280,00
─────────────────────────────────────
Saldo                   + R$ 430,00

Custos lançados na categoria "Transporte", já inclusos no total do mês.
```

O card "Custos do mês" também ganhou o subtítulo `Transporte: R$ 280,00`.

## Backend

`custo_transporte_periodo(inicio, fim)` soma os `Custo` da categoria "Transporte" na competência, usando a mesma chave normalizada (`Lower(Trim(...))`) do gráfico de despesas — sem ela, "Transporte " digitado com espaço viraria uma despesa invisível.

**Por que não reusar `custos_por_categoria`:** aquela função corta a cauda em "Outros" a partir da 6ª categoria. É correto para a pizza, e fatal aqui — no mês em que houvesse seis categorias, o transporte cairia dentro de "Outros" e o bloco mostraria R$ 0,00 sem erro nem aviso. Truncamento de apresentação não serve como fonte de dados.

## A armadilha que ficou travada por teste

`custo_transporte` **já está dentro** de `custos`. É um recorte do total, não despesa nova. Somar os dois descontaria o combustível duas vezes do lucro — o mesmo contar-em-dobro que a invariante 1 previne do outro lado. `test_custo_transporte_nao_e_despesa_nova_dentro_de_custos` trava o total e o lucro no lugar.

## Limitação conhecida

O número depende de o custo ser lançado com a categoria "Transporte". Um custo digitado como "gasolina" fica de fora e o sistema não tem como saber. Campo booleano em `Custo` resolveria, mas custa migration + formulário + um segundo mecanismo de categorização para uma pergunta só. A mitigação é o rodapé do bloco, que diz de onde o número sai.

## Verificação

Backend:

```
python -m pytest -q   ->  168 passed
ruff check .          ->  []
```

Frontend:

```
npx vitest run        ->  PASS (230) FAIL (0)
npx tsc -b            ->  No errors found
npx oxlint src        ->  exit 0
```

Testes novos: 6 no backend (soma por categoria, fusão de digitação, competência, vazio vira zero e não `None`, o total não duplica, endpoint devolve os dois campos) e 3 no front (o bloco renderiza a conta, saldo negativo inverte o sinal, dashboard fora do ar mostra traço em vez de zero).

author: lessevv
body:
The book \*arr's wiring was deferred because its API could not be pinned without a live
instance. Running one pinned it — and showed the row was describing the wrong shape.

## It pulls; it is not pushed to

Every other \*arr is registered into by the aggregator's own application sync. This one
the aggregator cannot reach, and does not need to: it keeps its own list of aggregators
and reads from them. So the connection is made from the other end — it is told where
the aggregator is and handed a key to read it with, at `POST /api/v1/prowlarr`.

## The body is camel-cased, and the wrong spelling still answers 201

Sending the names its own storage uses stores an entry **with no key in it**:

```
{"api_key": …}  →  201, {"apiKey":"", "syncOnStartup":false}
{"apiKey":  …}  →  201, key set, sync enabled
```

Both succeed. Only the response body says which one worked. So the read-back counts an
entry as made only where it holds a key — an entry without one is the failure this
exists to prevent, wearing the shape of a connection that was made.

## Its key is the first minted before a service has ever run

Given `BINDERY_API_KEY` on its **first** start it adopts that value. Given none it
generates its own into a SQLite database inside a distroless container, and it will not
take a supplied key on any later start. Driven against `v1.27.0`, all three cases.

Every other minted credential in the stack is created *after* the service is up, by
asking it or reading what it wrote. This one cannot be asked and writes nothing
readable, so the only leverage is the moment before it first decides — which is why the
minting sits where services are started rather than in seeding.

**On both start paths.** A start can be waited on or streamed, and the streamed one is
what the command line uses. Written on one path first, the feature did nothing at all
while its own unit tests passed; a test now fails if either path stops minting.

## Driven

From nothing: minted, adopted, `✓ Indexers into Bindery wired`, then `already wired`,
one instance after three seeds, no failures across the run.

`engine.rs` crossed the line cap on the way, so the wait loop and the account it gives
when the wait runs out moved into a module of their own — 579 production lines to 396,
rather than landing on the cap and leaving the next line to trip it.

Needs lemonfiber/lemonfiber-media-stack#57, merged; the pin moves with this.

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v4.2.5...v4.3.0)

A small release that adds an opt-in way to hold back from installing brand-new mise releases.

##### Added

##### `minimum_release_age` input ([#​604](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/pull/604) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx))

When `version` is omitted, you can now set `minimum_release_age` to install the newest **stable, non-draft** mise release that is older than a given cutoff — a simple way to avoid picking up a mise release the moment it ships (closes [#​603](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/issues/603)).

```yaml
- uses: jdx/mise-action@v4
  with:
    minimum_release_age: 7d
```

It accepts relative durations (`24h`, `7d`, `6mo`, `1y`) as well as absolute ISO dates and timestamps. Age-filtered versions are resolved from the GitHub Releases API (the CDN only serves the latest binary) and downloaded by their exact version. If mise is already present on disk, an age-filtered run updates it to the resolved version rather than keeping the existing binary. An explicit `version` always takes precedence over `minimum_release_age`, and invalid dates fail fast.

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v4.2.5...v4.3.0>

### [`v4.2.5`](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/releases/tag/v4.2.5): : Resilient mise downloads with automatic retries

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v4.2.4...v4.2.5)

A small patch release that makes setup more resilient to transient network failures when downloading mise.

##### Fixed

##### Retry mise downloads after transient failures ([#​597](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/pull/597) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx))

The download helpers previously made a single `curl` or `wget` attempt, so a transient GitHub release-asset HTTP or TLS failure would abort setup before mise or any user command could run (see [#​596](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/issues/596)).

Downloads now run through a retry wrapper that makes up to five attempts with a 2s pause between failures, logging a warning on each retry. This applies consistently to binary, checksum, signature, and version fetches. Checksum and minisign verification still run only after a successful download — never inside the retry loop — so integrity guarantees are unchanged.

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v4.2.4...v4.2.5>

💡 **What:** Refactored backend routers (`auditLog.ts`, `teams.ts`) and lib functions (`redirects.ts`) to use a shared `PrismaClient` instance rather than instantiating a new client on each request.
🎯 **Why:** Creating `new PrismaClient()` in every API endpoint or serverless function invocation rapidly drains the database connection pool, leading to massive connection bottlenecks and timeouts under load.
📊 **Impact:** This optimization eliminates redundant database connections, significantly improving application throughput and completely preventing connection pool exhaustion crashes during moderate to heavy traffic.
🔬 **Measurement:** You can verify this by checking the server logs in development (fewer active connections logging queries) and by running a load test, which should no longer yield Prisma connection exhaustion errors.

author: shwinster101
body:
> Are you sure that's the highest leverage language? Better, but we can do better. Full actual name is high leverage as title.

The v5.9.1 bullets described what each gauge is *made of* — "the options market's estimate", "the discount rate under every future dollar", "not a survey of opinion". That teaches the instrument, and leaves a beginner still unable to answer the only question they have: **is 14.43 high or low?**

## What changed

VIX, CAPE and the 10Y, rewritten to one beat order: **what the metric is → where a reading sits (vs history *and* vs our vote) → what usually happens when it moves.**

**Titles untouched** — `Cboe Volatility Index (VIX)`, `Cyclically Adjusted Price-to-Earnings ratio (Shiller CAPE)`, `10-Year U.S. Treasury Yield`. The full official name is itself the high-leverage element at the top, so plain language goes in the body, not the identity.

## The two-ruler rule, now pinned

History/convention and the MacroDash vote may share a bullet **only if both are named**:

> The teens are calm. About 20 is a long-run typical day. 30 is a scare. MacroDash: below 18 helps, above 25 hurts.

Collapsing 20/30 into 18/25 would present our band as the world's convention. It isn't — ~20 is the long-run average and 30 is the market's fear line; 18/25 are ours. A negative control that collapses them turns the pin red.

CAPE follows the same shape (old average and 1999 peak from history, then our 30/90%-of-peak edge), with both numbers **interpolated** from `CAPE_MEAN`/`CAPE_ATH` — pinned by value *and* by template form, so retyping fails even if the digits match.

## The 10Y bullet earns its place

Your third acceptance case was "they can say why +0.05 is MIXED, not a crisis." That only works if the sheet says outright that the level isn't what votes:

> There is no single right level. Lately it has lived between about 1.5% and 5%. MacroDash does not vote on the level. It votes on the one-month change: help below −0.10 points, hurt above +0.15.

Driven live, the eyebrow reads `THE 10-YEAR YIELD · 4.73% · +0.05PP 1-MO · MIXED` directly above that body.

## Tests

**2097 smoke · 306 render · 227 public-render · `audit:prod` clean** — real Chromium, no skipped suites.

Ban list pinned **absent** from the three bodies (term premium · discount rate · options market · risk-limit · "not a survey" · "not an official Cboe line" · post-1990 median · live argument · Fed's expected path), scoped to `what[]` only since the CAPE title legitimately contains "Cyclically".

**Acceptance driven, all three cases:** VIX names the teens as calm beside both rulers; CAPE gives 17.4 and 44.19 with our hurt edge; the 10Y sheet — surfaced on a tape where it reaches the 3-card cap, since it votes neutral and sorts 5th on today's — explains the MIXED read.

**Negative controls:** collapsing the two rulers, retyping the CAPE constants, and reintroducing one banned stem each turn exactly their own pin red. One control was invalid on the first attempt (a bad substitution broke the string literal, so the suite crashed rather than failing a pin) — recorded in the working note and redone properly rather than quietly retried.

## Version

`5.9.2 → 5.9.5` is your number, not a gap to fill — the v1 pass this corrects never landed on `main`, so **5.9.3/5.9.4 do not exist** and are not phantom releases. Recorded as a deliberate jump (the v4.99 precedent).

author: kj299
body:
The first slice of the signature-database maintenance loop (build order approved in #84): what a bundle contains, at what version, with what hash, and the downgrade comparison that decides whether an update may proceed. Pure, no I/O, **no new dependencies**.

`core` carries two crates today, and the code that gates signature verification is the last place to grow the trusted surface — so the manifest is a hand-rolled line parser, the same shape as the existing `nmap-os-db` / `nmap-mac-prefixes` parsers.

## No C to differential against

nmap has no update mechanism, no version metadata to read (all three databases carry an unexpanded SVN `$Id$` where a version should be), and no way to collect the fingerprints it computes and prints. So the gate here is **golden + negative tests + fuzz**, and every decision is ledgered under `sigstore-manifest-*` in `DIVERGENCES.md` rather than left to look like drift.

## Design decisions worth your review

| Decision | Why |
|---|---|
| **Fail-closed**, unlike its siblings | `macvendor`/`osdb::parse`/`probedb` follow nmap — warn, skip the line, continue. Right for a 116,000-line database where one bad fingerprint shouldn't cost the other 6,107. A manifest is signed, small, and decides whether *other* bytes are trustworthy; a defect in it is never a line to skip |
| **Unknown keys are an error** | In a signed document an unrecognised field may be intent an older build silently discards — downgrade-by-omission. Forward compat is the `schema` number instead, which fails with a message naming the fix |
| **Duplicate keys refused**, not last-wins | Last-wins lets whoever controls the tail of the document choose the value |
| **Ordering is a `u64` serial, nothing else** | Dates invite timezone questions, semver invites precedence rules, both invite a parser. `released` is display-only; per-file `version` is informational. One rule, one comparison |
| **Names validated in the parser, not the installer** | The traversal guarantee then holds for *every* consumer including ones not yet written, instead of resting on each remembering to check |
| **Input is `&[u8]`, not `&str`** | A char-at-a-time walk over `&str` re-adds the mid-codepoint panic class fuzzing found in `probedb` (kit LESSONS #12) |

A `Manifest` asserts structural validity **only**. Holding one is never evidence anything was verified — that's S2, and it runs over the raw bytes *before* this parser.

## Fuzzing found a real gap in my first draft

The fuzzer produced `nmap-os-..`, which passed my leading-dot rule. It isn't traversal as a single path component, so the joined-path property still held — but it exposed something I'd missed:

**Win32 silently strips trailing dots.** `db`, `db.` and `db..` all name the same file there. The manifest's duplicate-name check compares the *declared strings*, so a bundle could pass that check and still have its second record quietly overwrite the first on our `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` target.

Fixed by rejecting a dot at **either** end and `..` anywhere. While in there I added Windows reserved device names (`CON`, `NUL`, `COM1`–`COM9`, `LPT1`–`LPT9`, any case, with or without extension) — a write to `NUL` is silently discarded and a write to `COM1` can block on a serial port; a name in a bundle should never reach a device. Both rules are pinned by regression tests and added to the seed corpus.

## A CI regression I introduced, and fixed

The two panic-sweep tests (every truncation, every single-byte corruption of a valid manifest — ~2,700 parses) are cheap natively and brutal under Miri, which interprets every operation. The first push took the Miri job from an ~11m36s baseline to **still running past 17 minutes** — landing squarely on CI's critical path, right after #83 was merged to make CI fast.

Both sweeps are now strided under `cfg(miri)` **only**. Under Miri they ask "is this path free of UB?", which a sample answers; the exhaustive question "does any offset panic?" still runs at stride 1 in the normal test run and at millions of runs in the fuzz target. The two boundary cases (empty input, complete document) run regardless of stride.

| | Miri, `sigstore` tests | Miri job | end-to-end |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (#84, docs-only) | — | 11m36s | 11m53s |
| S1 first push | 858s | **>17 min** | — |
| S1 now | **47.7s** | **12m26s** | 12m26s |

Net cost of this PR to CI: **~50s**, which matches the 47.7s the tests take under Miri. Same 33 tests pass either way.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Unit tests | **33 passed** |
| Mutation testing | **11/11 caught** — allowlist admits `/`, leading-dot dropped, verdict inverted, uppercase hex accepted, digest length relaxed, schema ceiling removed, duplicate serial last-wins, size cap removed, duplicate file allowed, unknown key ignored, empty-name check dropped |
| Miri | **clean**, 33/33 (47.7s) |
| Fuzz | **16.3M runs clean** after the fix; 21 committed seeds |
| clippy `-D warnings` | clean in **all three** feature configs (default, `--all-features`, `--features pcap`) |
| fuzz-build sweep, `check-kit`, drift gate, unsafe audit | all green (52 modules tracked, 0 untracked; 11/11 unsafe blocks documented) |
| CI at `7fa76c0d8` | **11/11 green** |

C tree untouched.

## Flagged for the Workstream S retrospective

The six-gate ladder (`ported → differential → fuzzed → sanitized → unsafe_audited`) is linear and assumes a C counterpart exists. An **additive** module can never clear `differential`, so `progress.py` can't express "done" for it without either overclaiming a gate that never ran or understating it forever. S1 is recorded as `fuzzed` and is in fact also sanitized and unsafe-audited. The kit needs an explicit `n/a` or an additive track — worth deciding once in the retrospective rather than picking a convention per module. Noted in `BACKLOG.md`.

## Still blocked on you

- **S2** (`sigstore::verify`) needs the **signing scheme**: minisign-style Ed25519 (my recommendation — keeps `core` pure, verify path auditable in about a page, format versioned so a transparency log can be added later) vs cosign/sigstore.
- **S5** (`sys::update`) needs the **bundle source**: configurable with no default, or a documented default the operator can override.
- **S3** (`fingerprint_store`) is independent of both and can start immediately if you want it next.

author: bartwaardenburg
body:
## Problem

A per-function cyclomatic ceiling constrains a partition, not a quantity. McCabe gives a function `1 + one increment per decision point`, so across a set of units the summed cyclomatic score is `functions + branch points`. Moving an `if` out of one function into a new one removes an increment from the first and adds it to the second: every per-unit metric improves and the branching is untouched.

Fallow's own headline metrics reward exactly that today. `average_cyclomatic` (`crates/engine/src/vital_signs.rs:76`), `critical_complexity_pct` (`:84`) and `p90_cyclomatic` (`:100`) all divide by unit count, so splitting one cyclomatic-40 function into eight cyclomatic-6 functions improves all three. The only aggregate that moves the other way is per file, opt-in behind `--file-scores`, and switched off on both audit passes.

## Approach

Report the two terms separately on the review brief, base revision against head, over the audit accounting set.

- `FileBranching` aggregates branch points, function count, peak, and cognitive weight from the per-increment breakdown that is already computed and cached for every unit.
- The aggregation is threshold-blind and suppression-blind. It deliberately does not hang off the health findings path, which drops every sub-threshold unit and skips suppressed ones, where a single `fallow-ignore-next-line complexity` comment would have removed a unit's branches from the total.
- The totals ride on `HealthAnalysisResult`, which derives `Debug` only and carries no schema version, then into the audit base snapshot so both revisions can be compared. `HealthReport` is untouched.
- Cognitive excludes `PropCount` and `HookDensity`. Both are cognitive-only with no cyclomatic counterpart, and `PropCount` records an excess over a floor, so it is superlinear in a split: one 14-prop component contributes `+10` while the same props across two 7-prop components contribute `+3` and `+3`. Including them would move the number with branching and nesting both flat.

### The claim is per file, not per changeset

An earlier draft classified the whole changeset. Three review rounds found eight ways to reach a wrong verdict, each in the same predicate, and each fix added a conjunct that both leaked and over-blocked: the last version called a split that moved everything into a test file a relocation, and flipped its answer when an empty constants file was added.

That is structural. Inferring "a split happened here" from aggregates over a changeset that also contains arbitrary other work is an attribution problem, and aggregates cannot attribute.

So the block makes a local claim instead. For each changed file present on both revisions, it reports whether that file's branching held while it gained functions and its worst function shrank. That is true by construction, so unrelated work elsewhere cannot make it more or less true. The changeset totals are reported alongside as context, with no verdict attached.

### There is no "branching removed" verdict

`push_function` runs only from the function and arrow visitors (`crates/extract/src/complexity.rs:461`, `:483`), and both `push_contribution` (`:219`) and `inc_cyclomatic` (`:235`) write behind `if let Some(frame) = self.stack.last_mut()`. At module scope the stack is empty, so a branch hoisted out of a function to the top level of a module lowers the count without removing any branching. A fall is therefore not proof of removal and is not claimed. `hoisting_a_branch_to_module_scope_hides_it` pins the behavior so a future frame change is visible.

That gap is pre-existing and wider than this change: top-level `if` ladders and env guards contribute nothing to any complexity number fallow reports today. It is filed separately.

## Contract

Additive and optional on the brief envelope, absent when no base comparison ran, so a consumer that never had a base snapshot sees a byte-identical wire shape. No `schema_version` moves, per the additive-field policy in `docs/backwards-compatibility.md`.

The block never gates: it does not feed `AuditVerdict`, does not change exit-code mapping, does not appear in the PR decision surface, and carries no `actions` array.

Scope reports the test-path share and the largest single file's share, because test code and vendored bundles routinely dominate both terms. The per-file list is what keeps a mixed changeset readable: a set-level scalar cannot localize, so a commit that deletes ten branches in one file while displacing thirty in another would otherwise read as flat.

The human brief renders one line, and only when the comparison found a move, matching every sibling section.

## Validation

- Full workspace suite green
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- The conservation identity is asserted at set level together with the absence of `u16` saturation, since the identity alone holds vacuously once a unit saturates
- Verdict region coverage is tested as a total function over the delta space rather than as a handful of example fixtures
- Cache round trip and rename remap covered: without the remap a pure rename reads as branching arriving
- Run against a real TypeScript repository across two commits. A split whose caller adds no branching reports `branching-moved` with branch points held and the peak falling from 8 to 3. The same split routed through a nullish-coalescing chain adds four branch points and correctly reports `inconclusive: no-transfer-signature`. That second run also exposed a labelling defect every fixture had missed, fixed in the last commit: a cognitive rise was being attributed to removed branches

body:
## What this is

A **publication** change. Effective-root admission is untouched — no narrowing, no relaxation, no new exemption. What lands is the contract for behaviour that already ships, plus tests that lock it.

The contract for this PR is the bound design-critique arc on #4013, not the issue body. The body's Summary, its three candidate remedies and its acceptance criteria are **superseded** (accepted successor lean [5481139589](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4013#issuecomment-5481139589), verified-claims table 5481144822, completed-arc record 5481151170, round-1 critic 5481096005). The filing called deliberate behaviour a defect; the arc refuted that and accepted remedy 3.

## Publication surface (named, as the arc required)

**`content/docs/hook-root-admission.md`** — a new operator-facing page in the deposited content tree (`.deft/core/docs/hook-root-admission.md` in a consumer project).

Discoverable from three existing surfaces, so it is not an orphan doc:

- `content/commands.md` § Session routing — a new bullet beside the worktree occupancy contract (#3433 / #3611 / #3755), which is the place an operator reads to learn which lease governs a write.
- `content/contracts/path-write-fence.md` § Runtime enforcement — root admission decides which tree the fence, occupancy, ritual and scope are read from, before any of them run.
- `content/docs/host-surface-assumptions.md` § Enforcement home — a new row in the layer table beside the path write fence and the host tool-surface audit.

Citing #3794's issue history is explicitly **not** the publication; that history is why the behaviour exists, not a surface an operator can find.

The `admitEffectiveHookRoot` doc comment is **extended, not contradicted**: it already explained the `unproven-identity` split, and now also explains the `candidateRaw === null` branch it sits beside. The `inspectMutationGates` ownership comment at `dispatcher.ts:1194-1198` is unchanged and the doc restates it.

## The gates, gate by gate, for a no-toplevel target

| Gate | Root it reads | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Occupancy lease | effective root (= payload root here) | Runs — a live foreign lease denies `occupancy-occupied` |
| Session ritual, gated tier | effective root (= payload root here) | Runs, including the occupancy↔ritual owner cross-check |
| Authz / UAT grant scoping | payload root | Payload-root authoritative |
| Authz audit trail | payload root | Payload-root authoritative |
| Kill-switch | payload root | Payload-root authoritative |
| `deny().projectRoot` | payload root | Payload-root authoritative |
| Mutation intent ceiling (#1193) | neither | Runs independently |
| Read-only posture | neither | Runs |
| Runtime authority / write fence | project policy from payload root; story `file_scope` + match path from effective root | Runs when enabled |
| Active scope | effective root | Inspected, deny skipped by the #2885 outside-root carve-out |
| Assist-scratch allowlist | effective root | No match for an out-of-tree target |

Stated per gate rather than as "a lease question", which is the framing the arc rejected.

## Three surfaces, three behaviours

- Bare direct-write name (`Write`, `search_replace`, `ApplyPatch`) — **consults** root admission.
- Generic server-prefixed MCP (`tasks__search_replace`) — **never reaches** it; routed only through push/merge runtime classification, so an unrecognized name returns `shell-op-unclassifiable`.
- Recognized Shell file-write to an outside destination — **excluded** by `isInRepoShellWritePath`, so the #3987 reissue path skips it.

The issue body's claim that the fallback fires on "the direct-write and MCP surfaces" is wrong for generic MCP. The doc says so explicitly.

## Tests

`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher-effective-root.test.ts`: **27 → 34**, all green at HEAD. The seven added tests are characterization, each with a contrast case so none can pass vacuously:

1. `admitEffectiveHookRoot` returns the payload root with a null candidate for a no-toplevel target.
2. That target under a **foreign** payload-root lease → `occupancy-occupied`, both roots printed as the payload root, ritual resolved through the payload root.
3. The same target for the **matching** owner → `write-ready`, with active scope inspected at the payload root and `scopePath` null — the #2885 deny is skipped, not un-asked.
4. Generic-MCP non-consultation, contrasted with the bare direct-write spelling of the same tool on the same target.
5. Out-of-repo shell-write exclusion, contrasted with the identical command aimed in-repo (which is reissued and denied).
6. `{linked worktree, no-toplevel}` still refuses `worktree-span`.
7. `{payload root, no-toplevel}` collapses to the payload root and is admitted.

The `foreign-repository`, `unproven-identity` and `worktree-span` refusals are unchanged; no assertion was weakened and no gate definition, floor or policy flag was touched (#3156).

## Known limitation, recorded not fixed

`existingAncestorDir` resolves a relative target with `resolve(targetPath)` and no base, so the hook **process** working directory decides the class. The doc records it; **#4023** carries the fix. It surfaced concretely while writing test 5 — a relative in-repo shell dest classified as `foreign-repository` against the temp fixture, because the test process cwd is this checkout. The test now uses an absolute dest and says why.

## Out of scope, recorded

Any change to admission behaviour; the target-class lattice and mixed-set combining rule a future narrowing needs; #3954 (actor resolution); #3999 (lease release lifecycle); #3987 (merged).

## Review response (batch 1)

Greptile round 1 raised one P1: the committed brief was **unattested**, so this PR could not close its own issue. That is real and now fixed — `verify:pr-closeout-attestable` (#3781) is keyed on the closing reference rather than the diff and exited 1, because every acceptance item carried neither `x-directive/evidence` nor `x-directive/disposition` (the same rule `scope:complete` enforces, #3240). All seven items now carry typed evidence pointing at the artifact its kind names, and are marked completed. Nothing is waived; no disposition is used. Gate re-run: exit 0.

It runs immediately after merge, followed by the lifecycle PR that tracks it — the same shape as #4014 → #4019 for the preceding brief.

author: shmindmaster
body:
Closes the last of the open CrewScore P0s. The work existed only as
uncommitted changes in a worktree — committed, rebased onto `main` after #53,
and unchanged otherwise.

## The bug

Reading a shared result trusted the arrays in the URL fragment. Repeating a
control ID inflated the count, so a hand-edited link carrying 8 distinct found
controls rendered **"10 of 23 written guardrails found"** while also reporting
15 missing — a total the 23-control set cannot produce.

For a tool whose entire claim is "the number is coverage, and here is exactly
which controls it counted," a shareable link that can assert a number the
control set cannot back is the one bug that undermines the product's premise.

## The fix

- A versioned decoder (`v2`; `v1` and unversioned payloads still accepted)
  re-derives both control lists from the published canonical control set.
  Displayed counts come from that list, never from `arr.length`.
- Impossible states are rejected with a named reason rather than rendered:
  `duplicate_id`, `overlap`, `incomplete_partition`, `unknown_id`,
  `unknown_ruleset`, `unknown_profile`, `profile_incompatible`,
  `impossible_total`, `unsupported_version`, `too_many_ids`,
  `payload_too_large`, `unreadable`. A rejected link shows the reason, renders
  no coverage number or meter, and records no analytics event.
- Fragments and their control arrays are bounded before decoding, so an
  oversized link cannot make the page walk unbounded input.
- `assets/site.js` exposes `decodeSharedPayload` for inspection.

## Verification

- `pytest`: **635 passed, 1 skipped**. The skip is
  `test_corpus_harness.py:202` (`corpora not fetched`) — environment-dependent
  and unrelated; it does not skip in a checkout with `.corpus-cache` populated.
- Adds a 325-line Playwright spec (`web-tests/checker.spec.mjs`) and Python
  coverage in `tests/test_web_ux.py`; the required **browser tests** check
  exercises the former.
- No scoring change. Ruleset remains `crewscore-hygiene@0.6.0`.

author: westonruter
body:
`unregister_post_type()` removes entries from the global `$post_type_meta_caps` list by subtracting every value of the post type's own `$cap` object. That list is keyed by *custom* capability name and is shared by every post type resolving to the same name, so the subtraction deletes mappings that other, still-registered post types depend on.

Once a mapping is gone, `map_meta_cap()` stops translating the meta capability into contextual primitives and returns it verbatim. The ownership and post-status checks (`edit_others_*`, `edit_published_*`, `edit_private_*`) do not become stricter, they disappear from the result entirely, so a post's own author can lose edit access to it.

The full analysis, including three distinct defects and a reproduction script, is in Core-66008.

## The fix

Subtraction cannot work against a shared list: an entry may be owed to any number of registered post types, and nothing records which ones. Rather than reference-count the entries, the list is rebuilt from the post types that remain.

The cleanup is removed from `WP_Post_Type::remove_rewrite_rules()` entirely, leaving that method to do only what its name says, and the rebuild happens in `unregister_post_type()` once the post type has been removed from `$wp_post_types`. Placement matters: `remove_rewrite_rules()` is called several lines *before* that `unset()`, so a rebuild performed from inside it would still see the post type being removed.

Rebuilding rather than subtracting fixes all three defects at once, because it inherits the rules of `_post_type_meta_capabilities()` instead of trying to invert them. Entries are written only for post types with `map_meta_cap => true`, only for the three meta capabilities, and an entry shared by several post types survives as long as any one of them is still registered.

Removing the loop also empties `tests/phpstan/baselines/foreach.nonIterable.neon`, so that baseline and its `includes` entry in `phpstan.neon.dist` are deleted here too. This supersedes #13079, which proposed silencing that baseline entry with a type cast.

## Tests

Four tests in `tests/phpunit/tests/post/types.php`, one per defect plus a functional one. Each was confirmed to fail before the fix, on an assertion *after* the unregistration rather than during setup:

```
1) ..._retains_meta_capabilities_shared_with_another_post_type      Undefined array key "read_publication"
2) ..._retains_meta_capabilities_when_not_mapping_meta_caps         Undefined array key "read_post"
3) ..._retains_meta_capabilities_matching_primitive_capabilities    Undefined array key "edit_book"
4) ..._retains_meta_capability_mapping_for_another_post_type
       -    0 => 'edit_published_publications'
       +    0 => 'edit_publication'
```

`--group post` (951 tests) and `--group capabilities` (789 tests) both pass.

## Notes for review

The `$capabilities` map handed to `_post_type_meta_capabilities()` comes from `WP_Post_Type::$cap`, a bare `stdClass` that carries no property types. PHPStan types `get_object_vars()` on any object as `array<mixed>` regardless of how the object is documented, so the call reports an `argument.type` error at higher rule levels even though the values are always strings at runtime. Narrowing the map at runtime or relaxing what the function documents would both be worse; typing `$cap` well enough for the analyzer to follow is separate work, tracked in Core-64898.

`WP_Post_Type::remove_rewrite_rules()` is public, so moving the cleanup out of it is technically a behavior change for any caller invoking it directly. A search of public GitHub for `remove_rewrite_rules()` returns only vendored copies of core's own `post.php`, `taxonomy.php` and the two class files, with no third-party call sites at all.

Some accompanying documentation fixes to `_post_type_meta_capabilities()`, each in its own commit: r36316 removed the branch that returned the list when the function was called with no arguments, but left behind the `null` default and a summary describing that return value.

Trac ticket: Core-66008
Trac ticket: Core-65817

## Use of AI Tools

AI assistance: Yes
Tool(s): Claude Code
Model(s): Opus 5
Used for: Investigating the defect and its history, drafting the fix and its tests, and drafting the Trac ticket. The approach, the final implementation and the tests were reviewed, revised and are owned by me.

author: michalharakal
body:
Part of #360 (does not close it — the entry-point-parity item and the BF16 arbitration below stay open). Part of the BitNet tracking issue #335.

## What

- **`BitNetGoldenTokenParityTest`** — the #346 maturity-gate parity probe, model-gated on `BITNET_2B4T_GGUF`. Asserted: (1) prompt tokenization must match the **bitnet.cpp oracle** exactly; (2) self-golden regression — both decode paths (full planes matmul, two-stage candidate loop) must keep reproducing the recorded SKaiNET greedy continuation, so any numerics regression that flips a single argmax in 32 tokens fails. The fixture header records the exact oracle build (microsoft/BitNet @ `de371b7`, vendored llama.cpp fork @ `5eb47b721`, `-DBITNET_ARM_TL1=OFF` i2_s CPU path) and the `llama-server` commands to regenerate it.
- **Smoke row** — `BitNet-b1.58-2B4T-I2S` joins `tests/smoke/smoke-models.json` (skainet runner, 16 steps).
- **CLI knobs** — `--i2s-layout=group128|group64|sequential` (the `I2sGgufLayout` knob was hardcoded); `--context` now honored on the BitNet path (caps KV/RoPE via `metadata.contextLength` → `bitnetNetwork`'s `maxInferenceLen`); the explicit ternary kernel installs carry a load-bearing comment naming SKaiNET#1240 as the condition for removal.

## Finding worth review attention: greedy divergence vs the oracle

Cross-implementation **text equality is deliberately not asserted**. Building and running the oracle surfaced a real divergence: at generated token 4, bitnet.cpp continues "` Paris. Paris is a city that is known…`" while SKaiNET continues "` Paris. Paris is the capital of France…`". The oracle's own top-5 at that position is `' a'` 0.348, `' known'` 0.211, `' located'` 0.156, `' the'` 0.151 — a genuine logit gap, not a tie. Two facts frame it:

- bitnet.cpp's CPU i2_s matmul **quantizes activations to int8** (absmax) per matmul; SKaiNET's vendored LUT path computes **exact FP32×ternary**. Thirty layers of that difference plausibly account for ~1-nat logit shifts in either direction.
- Which implementation sits closer to the BF16 reference (`microsoft/bitnet-b1.58-2B-4T`, safetensors) is an open question — proposed follow-up on #360: a BF16-arbitrated probe in the spirit of the gemma eval-callback work (commit 8a7f1f1).

Also for the record: mainline llama.cpp cannot read I2_S at all, and microsoft/BitNet's current HEAD does not build (undeclared `src1_cont` in the i2_s fast path; and once patched, generates garbage) — the working oracle is the pinned older commit named in the fixture.

## Verification

Parity test green against the real 2B4T (prompt ids `128000, 791, 6864, 315, 9822, 374` match; both decode paths reproduce the golden; 17-char shared oracle prefix printed). `--context=2048` caps and prints. Full bitnet suite green.

author: ha08625-cloud
body:
Task 2 of the local run console for encoder training. Adds `scripts/training_gui/gitops.py` — the two fixed git sequences behind the page's two buttons — and a git section in `tests/test_training_gui.py`. No HTTP layer yet; nothing calls this module until Task 3.

## `save_run_to_branch(manifest)`

Guards first, before any mutating command (AD7):

1. `git status --porcelain` — refuses if anything is dirty outside `reports/` and `models/`, naming the paths.
2. `git rev-parse HEAD` — refuses if HEAD no longer matches the sha the manifest recorded at run start.

Then, stopping at the first non-zero exit: `git fetch origin`; `git checkout -b training/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<run id> <manifest sha>`; copy the run's log and manifest into `reports/training_runs/<run_id>/` (AD5); `git add -- reports models`; `git commit`; `git push -u origin <branch>`. On success it looks up `git remote get-url origin` to turn the branch into a compare link.

The base is the run's own commit rather than `origin/main` (AD6). If that sha is not on the remote the push fails, and the failure is shown raw with the remedy in the message ("push your code branch first") rather than worked around.

The commit subject is `training run: <entry name> (<date>)`; the body lists the base sha, the resolved parameter values and every step's command line with its exit code, so the branch is readable on a phone without opening the manifest. `git commit` finding nothing staged is surfaced as "this run changed nothing", not as an error, and nothing is pushed.

There is no merge, rebase, force or amend anywhere in the module, no `-A`, and no path, ref, branch name or flag that comes from the browser.

## `update_from_github()`

`git status --porcelain`, then refuses on **any** dirty tree — including one dirty only with fresh reports, where the message is "save this run to a branch first" and lists the paths. Otherwise `git fetch origin` then `git pull --ff-only`.

## `compare_url(remote_url, branch)`

Handles `git@github.com:owner/repo.git` and `https://github.com/owner/repo(.git)`; returns `None` for anything else rather than guessing at a link that 404s.

## Result shape

Every function returns a `GitResult` carrying the ordered list of steps attempted — argv, exit code, captured output — so the page can show exactly where a sequence stopped. The artefact copy is recorded as a step too, since it is part of the sequence.

## Testing

The command runner is injected, so the tests assert on assembled argv and sequencing with no network and no repository mutation:

- the happy path issues the guards, then fetch/checkout/add/commit/push in order, then the remote lookup, with the manifest's sha as the checkout base;
- a failed `git fetch` stops before anything mutating; a failed `git push` is the last thing attempted, with the raw error in the result;
- a dirty path outside `reports/` blocks the whole sequence, with the path in the message; a moved HEAD blocks it;
- `git add` is called with `-- reports models` and never with `-A`, and no call carries a merge/rebase/force/amend;
- the log and manifest land in `reports/training_runs/<run_id>/`;
- `update_from_github` refuses a reports-only dirty tree with the branch-button message and uses `--ff-only` when it proceeds;
- `compare_url` for both remote forms, `None` for a third.

`ruff format` and `ruff check` clean on both touched files; `tests/test_training_gui.py` passes (63 tests, Task 1's included). Per CLAUDE.md the full suite and build are left to CI.

author: andrescera
body:
## Summary

### What
Override `NetworkManager-wait-online.service` to run `nm-online -q` instead of the stock Trixie `nm-online -s -q`. The committed drop-in is installed by `configure_networkmanager_wait_online`, wired into `configure_services`, registered with the postinst drift gate, and documented in `AGENTS.md`.

### Why
`-s` waits for NetworkManager's entire startup phase, so every autoconnect profile must settle. On a Rock 5B+, an optional cellular modem remained in `connecting (prepare)` while searching indefinitely even though Ethernet already provided full connectivity. The stock unit timed out after 60 seconds and left every boot degraded.

The ordinary `nm-online -q` criterion answers the appliance's real requirement: at least one usable connection. It keeps the `network-online.target` gate needed by the hostname/mDNS path without making an optional modem part of the boot critical path.

### Hardware result
A real rebuilt image was installed on the Rock 5B+. Boot time fell from **1m 15.394s** to **20.238s**. `NetworkManager-wait-online.service` completed in 2.733s, `systemctl is-system-running` changed from `degraded` to `running`, and the board had zero failed units. NetworkManager still reported its global startup phase as active, confirming the fix changed the readiness criterion rather than hiding the modem state.

## Testing
- [x] Built with `./build rock-5b-plus`
- [x] Tested on device(s): Radxa Rock 5B+
- [x] Attached relevant results above; detailed build and journal evidence was captured during the hardware session
- [x] `bash -n mkosi/customize/postinst.d/services.sh`
- [x] `ci/postinst-drift-check.sh`
- [x] `bats tests/runtime-services.bats` — 103/103 passed
- [x] `tests/postinst-module-contract.test.sh`

## Docs
- [x] Updated docs if CLI/behavior changed (`AGENTS.md`)

## Risks
- The unit now succeeds when any usable connection exists instead of waiting for every optional profile. A board with no usable connection still observes the inherited 60-second timeout and fails honestly.
- The wait unit is intentionally retained rather than masked, so `network-online.target` continues to protect hostname publication.
- No NetworkManager profile or connectivity-check policy is changed.
