author: andrej-rabek
body:
The `-202` runtime module catalog epic, six tickets' worth, from the integration
branch to `main`. 16 commits, 10 files.

**This is the merge that changes what customers get**, because production
generates from `main` with `INFRA_TEMPLATES_BRANCH` unpinned.

## What is in it

| Ticket | What |
|---|---|
| `-205` | Strict extraction gate in CI, legacy-paths allowlist, explicit types |
| `-206` | 15 `@module` + 146 enriched `@param` tails on the AWS templates |
| `-227` | RDS engine version reaches Terraform; CI fixtures derived from `aws.js` |
| `-208` | `@section` labels/defaults and `available=false`, the templates half |

Almost all of it is **comment metadata**. Of the ten files, five `.tf` files
change by a single line each and four of those five are decorator text with no
Terraform semantics.

## The one exception, and it wants a decision

`26954c9` changes three RDS defaults, and the commit carries no body explaining
why:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `rds_instance_class` | `db.t3.micro` | `db.t3.small` |
| `rds_max_allocated_storage` | 50 | 100 |
| **`rds_multi_az`** | **true** | **false** |

This is the only change here that alters what AWS actually provisions. It raises
cost on two axes and **lowers availability on the third** — and `-206` had
flagged `rds.multiAz` as one of three divergences where "the template is the
safer value", which this reverses. `-206`'s own acceptance criteria ask for owner
sign-off on the default-divergence list; this is that item and it is not
recorded anywhere.

**Please confirm this is intended before merging.** Everything else in the PR is
metadata and could land without it.

## Preconditions, both checked rather than assumed

- **The decorator trim is live.** `-206` noted that enriched decorators are
  copied into the customer's repo, so the trim must be on before this reaches
  `main`. `TRIM_DECORATOR_ATTRS: "true"` is in the **running** Deployment
  (`ghcr.io/devopsgroupeu/injecto:0.10.0`), not merely in GitOps values, and the
  effect is measured: longest generated line **714 chars with the trim off, 92
  with it on**.
- **Production Injecto understands this grammar.** `0.10.0` is deployed. `0.8.0`
  would have served `available` as the string `"false"`, which the wizard's
  `available !== false` test passes — Lambda back on offer with every gate green.

## Verified on the merged tree

`6b80389` merges `main` in, so this is `main` plus the epic, with the pinned
`INJECTO_REF: v0.10.0`:

- generation gate **PASS**
- strict catalog extraction: **15 services, 0 errors**
- `rds.version` present, `engineVersion` gone — `-227`'s fix survived the merge
- `lambda.available` is a real boolean, not the string
- `terraform fmt -check -recursive` clean; `terraform validate` **Success** for
  both `aws/` and `kubernetes/`

That last one matters: this is the **first time** `-199`'s module upgrade
(`rds` v6→v7, `security-group` v5→v6, `aurora` v9→v10, `msk` v2→v3) has met the
catalog decorators. The branch already contained `-199`; it was `-227` it was
missing, and both sides had done the same rename independently, so the merge
conflicted on one hunk in `terraform.auto.tfvars`. Resolved by keeping the branch
side — the same `@param` path plus `-206`'s metadata, a strict superset, with
every `@param` path checked against `main` to confirm none was dropped.

## Not in this PR

The frontend does not read the catalog yet in production: `USE_RUNTIME_CATALOG`
is off in `openprime-app` `1.20.0`. Merging this changes the *generated output*
(decorators, trimmed) and the *catalog the backend can serve*, not the wizard.
`-209` parity cutover and `-210` static-config decommission are still open.

author: edkerk
body:
## Summary
Fixes [raven-gecko-parity#71](https://github.com/SysBioChalmers/raven-gecko-parity/issues/71).

The post-loop refinement pass in `flexibilize_enz_concs` previously pinned `bio_rxn.lower_bound` to `exp_growth` exactly and minimized protein-pool usage. MATLAB's `flexibilizeEnzConcs.m` instead uses RAVEN's `setParam('var', bioRxn, expGrowth, 0.5)` for the same solve — a soft ±0.25% band, not a hard pin. Since minimal protein-pool usage is non-decreasing in growth rate near the optimum, that band's minimiser settles at its **low edge** (~0.25% below `exp_growth`), not at `exp_growth` itself.

Both sides were internally consistent with their own stated contract — MATLAB genuinely finds "minimal protein cost for growth within 0.25% of target," geckopy genuinely found "minimal protein cost for growth at least at target" — so this isn't a bug fix so much as a reconciliation, decided in raven-gecko-parity#71: geckopy now uses the same soft band, so both implementations produce the same final growth rate and the same flexed enzyme bounds given the same inputs.

Confirmed against `raven-gecko-parity`'s own `flexibilize_concs_ectestgem` scenario, which had already pinned down the exact numbers by direct execution (growth 2.49375 vs 2.5, `flexConcs` 0.173177 vs 0.173611 for the one enzyme both sides flex) — updated its comment now that both sides agree.

## Test plan
- [x] Three existing tests updated to expect the band's low edge (`exp_growth * 0.9975`) rather than `exp_growth` exactly, since the refinement now genuinely produces a different (band-edge) growth rate and enzyme bound, not just a different code path to the same answer
- [x] Full suite: 1329 passed, 0 failed related to this change (1 pre-existing, unrelated failure in `test_save_ec_model.py` — a `date.today()` metadata check, confirmed unaffected by this change)

author: srahsrah
body:
## What

Same latent bug as #29 (FR-30 notice), on FR-18's unavailability line: `unavailability_line()` strings were handed to the model inside the structured payload's `unavailable` list in both `synthesize()` and `_quarantine_and_recompose()`, with a verbatim `if line not in text` safety net after. A live model that paraphrases the line defeats the exact-string check, and the reader gets the notice twice — once reworded, once canonical.

## Fix

The FR-18 line never enters the model payload. `_structured_payload` now carries only `lines`; the canonical unavailability line is appended after composition, unconditionally — same pattern as #29's FR-30 fix.

**Provenance verified before deciding:** `check_provenance`'s `missing_unavailability_line` check (trace.py) only requires the digest to *name* the failed beat (case-insensitive substring), not the exact line. `unavailability_line()` always names the beat, so the appended line satisfies it — the regression test asserts `check_provenance(trace.path).ok` on the reworded run.

## Tests

- New `test_the_unavailability_line_appears_exactly_once_even_if_the_model_rewords` (rewording `FakeAgentClient` subclass, same pattern as #29's test). Verified it **fails against the pre-fix synthesizer** with exactly the double-notice digest, and passes with the fix.
- `test_the_model_is_never_handed_a_gap_to_fill` updated: the failed beat is now absent from the payload entirely (no gap, and no pre-written line to reword).
- `test_the_model_phrases_and_never_originates` updated: payload keys are now `{lines}`.
- `uv run pytest -q`: **624 passed**.

## Note

**Stacked on #29** (`fix/fr30-notice-once`) — both fixes edit the same lines in `_quarantine_and_recompose`. Merge #29 first and this PR's diff shrinks to just the FR-18 change; merging this one first lands both. Do not merge without Sarah's say-so.

author: rwlove
body:
Four hardening fixes from the cross-component adversarial review — the "green but dead" class, where a wedged capture/pipeline sat behind a hardcoded `{"status":"ok"}` `/healthz`.

## F2 — RTSP read-stall watchdog
A half-open stream leaves `cap.read()` parked in its worker thread forever (no exception, no EOF), so the reconnect path never fired and capture died silently behind a green probe. The consumer now waits on the frame slot with a timeout (`pose.read_stale_seconds`, default 15s); a stall raises and the outer `poses()` loop reconnects. Pairs with the FFmpeg `stimeout` added to `OPENCV_FFMPEG_CAPTURE_OPTIONS` in home-ops (build-independent belt-and-suspenders).

## F1 — `/healthz` asserts real progress
Now returns 503 once ready if no **live** camera (file sources ignored) has produced a frame within `health.frame_stale_seconds` (default 120s — generous so a camera reboot doesn't flap the pod). New `pump_cv_last_frame_age_seconds` gauge for pre-flip alerting.

## F3 — model load inside the retry loop
`_ensure_model()` ran once *before* the loop, so a cold PVC / GPU contention / CUDA-init failure crashed the process into CrashLoopBackOff instead of backing off. A poisoned CUDA context now drops the model so the next attempt rebuilds it.

## F6 — retention size cap
Age-only sweep had no floor against a heavy training month filling a small cache PVC; now deletes oldest-first until under `PUMP_CV_RETENTION_MAX_BYTES` (default 5Gi). Previously-swallowed unlink failures are now logged.

## Tests
New `test_hardening.py` (stall→reconnect, freshness gate ignores file sources, size cap deletes oldest). Full suite 62 pass, ruff clean. Env vars documented. No schema change.

author: theactualdev
body:
A signed-in student could not open a real lesson. This makes the loop work end to end, verified against a live account rather than asserted.

## The chain

Four findings that were one fault. The lesson route resolved a two-entry mock registry and `notFound()` on everything else — so Home shipped its live cards with `href: null` on purpose, the Lessons tab stayed on fixtures, and nothing a child did was ever written down.

- **Lesson route reads live first.** New adapter maps `GET /api/content/lessons/{id}` onto the player's shape. Mock ids still resolve for the designed walkthrough; a real 404 is a 404, and a failed load is a retry, not "your lesson was deleted".
- **Home's cards link.** The `href: null` branch is gone.
- **Lessons tab shows the student's own assignments**, from `students/me/dashboard` — not `content/lessons`, which is the school's whole library and the teacher's view of the world. Status filters now filter on the student's real progress instead of a fixture's invented state.
- **Progress is written.** `POST /lessons/{id}/session` on open, `PUT /lessons/{id}/progress` on advance and completion, and the player resumes where the child left off. "Your progress is saved" on the completion screen was previously untrue; it now reports, and says so plainly when the write did not land.

## Signals were never reaching the backend

Separate, and larger. Every `POST /api/signals` returned **422**. Both `session.sessionId` and `events[].sessionId` are `format: uuid`; the player passed a string it built itself (`lesson-<id>-<random>`), so every batch was rejected before a field was read — time on segment, scroll depth, replays, modality switches, comprehension responses, breaks. It stayed invisible because a 4xx is deliberately not re-queued and the failure has no user-facing effect.

Signals now carry the id `POST /session` issues, which is the same id `PUT /progress` requires — the backend's own model is one session, not two. Events captured before it arrives are held (capped, newest kept) rather than thrown at a validator that will refuse them.

## PIN length

The contract is `^\d{4,8}$`, design frame 00 draws four boxes, and the screens were fixed at exactly 4 — so an account issued a 6-digit PIN had its first four digits submitted on the fourth keystroke and was told the PIN was wrong. Now one constant, `STUDENT_PIN_LENGTH`, set to 6 to match the accounts currently being issued, honoured by both login and PIN creation. Design and backend disagree here and one has to move; when that lands it is a one-line change.

## Verified live

Signed in as a seeded student against `api.nevolearning.com`:

- Real assignments render on Home; fixtures gone
- A real lesson opens and plays (`GET /content/lessons/{id}` 200)
- `POST /session` **201**, `PUT /progress` **200**
- Progress reads back — the "Pick back up · About halfway in" card appears
- Reopening resumes at the right segment, on client navigation and on a hard page load
- `POST /api/signals` **202 Accepted**

Signed-out path unchanged: the authored mock lessons still play with full density and modality treatment, and the Lessons tab still shows the designed fixtures with subject grouping. `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean.

## Assumptions worth challenging

- **Live lessons play as text only.** The five per-modality payloads are `Record<string, unknown>` in the spec, so nothing can be read out of them honestly. The adapter reads none of them and builds the text modality from `body`. Audio is excluded for a second reason: narration assets do not exist and playback is simulated.
- **Density toggles are hidden when a segment has no reshapes.** Parsed content carries one body, and a toggle that re-renders identical prose is the player claiming an adaptation it did not make.
- **Subject and description are omitted on live lessons** rather than invented — assignments carry neither.

## Not covered — needs backend

- Onboarding, profiling and SSO signal streams have no lesson session; both ids are required UUIDs, so they now hold silently instead of 422-ing. Still unsent. This includes the baseline profiling run.
- Student → teacher messaging: `recipientType` is `^(student|class)$`.
- Progress tab has no endpoint at all.
- Account provisioning: the device still derives `login_identifier` from the child's typed name.

author: jaysbeekay
body:
## Summary

Closes #3169.

The AI status page (#3145, PR #3155) proves only that the `web` process resolved a valid-looking configuration and can reach the configured provider from its own network context. Most AI workloads — assistant responses, PDF processing, embeddings, auto-categorization, and merchant detection — actually run in Sidekiq `worker` processes, which can differ from `web` in environment, DNS, proxy rules, network policy, or even loaded credentials (workload-specific overrides, an updated Secret without a pod restart, `web` recreated without `worker`). A passing web check says nothing about whether a worker can do the same.

## What this adds

`WorkerAiHealthCheckJob`, queued on demand from a new **Verify worker configuration** button on **System health → AI status**. It runs the same bounded, non-destructive probes `AiHealth` already runs, but from inside whichever Sidekiq worker process dequeues it, and records the result via `WorkerAiHealth`: process identity (`hostname:pid`), checked-at time, a non-secret configuration fingerprint (effective provider, model, redacted endpoint, vector-store adapter/embedding config), and probe outcomes.

The AI status tab lists every recorded result — most recent first, kept for `WorkerAiHealth::RETENTION` (15 minutes) — each labeled with a status pill (`Passing` / `Failing` / `Stale`, the last once older than `STALE_AFTER`) and a configuration pill comparing it against the web snapshot (`Matches web` / `Differs from web`), with a failure-reason list reusing the existing failure-code translations when a probe failed.

## Implementation constraints from the issue, addressed directly

- **Cannot reuse a web-cached probe result, or vice versa.** `AiHealth.new` gained an injectable `probe_cache:` (default `Rails.cache`, matching today's behavior). The worker job passes a fresh `ActiveSupport::Cache::NullStore` instead, so every worker check is a live call that neither reads a web-cached entry nor leaves one behind.
- **A single job only verifies one worker.** Documented on the button (`coverage_notice`) and in the docs: with multiple replicas, a passing result names one process, not the fleet. Queuing again samples another.
- **Never persists or displays a raw credential.** `WorkerAiHealth::Snapshot` only carries redacted endpoints (`AiHealth` already redacts these before they reach the job) and provider/model/status fields — there is no field for a token to occupy. A structural test asserts this stays true.
- **Failures land in both places an operator already checks.** Same destinations as `AiHealth::Probe`'s own failures: `Rails.logger` and `DebugLogEntry` (new `ai_health_worker` category), tagged with the process identity.
- **Results carry a clear status**, including the "no result yet" case (explanatory empty state) and `stale` for a result whose process may no longer reflect current state.
- **DB-backed vs ENV-backed settings are labeled.** A new info block next to the worker results explains which UI settings propagate automatically (`rails-settings-cached` invalidates the shared cache on write) versus which require restarting/recreating both `web` and `worker`.

## What this deliberately doesn't do

Full-fleet coverage (every process publishing a periodic fingerprint) — the issue lists this under "Other options to consider," not the acceptance criteria, and Sidekiq's normal dispatch doesn't target every process without an explicit per-process coordination mechanism. This PR implements the on-demand, single-check design the acceptance criteria actually describes ("An administrator can request an asynchronous worker-side check", "does not imply full-fleet coverage"); periodic fleet-wide publishing is a natural follow-up if operators need it.

## Testing

- `WorkerAiHealth`: recording/reading, same-process replacement vs. cross-process coexistence, `MAX_RESULTS` bounding, staleness, status derivation (failure codes / component statuses / function-calling refusal), `matches_web?` comparison, and the credential-field structural guard.
- `WorkerAiHealthCheckJob`: records a passing/failing snapshot naming this process, writes failures to `Rails.logger` + `DebugLogEntry` (and only on failure), never leaks the access token, and — the defining property — is proven to construct `AiHealth.new` with an isolated `NullStore` rather than the shared web-facing cache.
- `Admin::SystemHealthController`: empty state, a rendered result with matching/mismatched configuration, a failing result's failure reason, a stale result, the `verify_worker_ai` action enqueuing the job and redirecting with a flash notice, and that non-super-admins and unauthenticated requests cannot trigger it.

## Test plan

- [ ] `bin/rails test test/models/worker_ai_health_test.rb test/jobs/worker_ai_health_check_job_test.rb test/controllers/admin/system_health_controller_test.rb`
- [ ] `bin/rails test`
- [ ] `bin/rubocop -f github -a`
- [ ] `bundle exec erb_lint ./app/**/*.erb -a`
- [ ] `bin/brakeman --no-pager`
- [ ] Manually verify: open System health → AI status, click "Verify worker configuration", confirm a result appears with process identity, a status pill, and a configuration-match pill; confirm credentials never appear in the rendered page

> **Note:** I could not run the Rails test suite in this environment (no working Ruby/Bundler toolchain locally — system Ruby is 2.6 vs. the project's required 3.4.9, no sudo/Docker access to install). Every file was checked with `ruby -c`, YAML files with `YAML.load_file`, the ERB view with `ERB.new(...).src`, plus careful manual tracing of each test against the production code paths it exercises — but CI should be treated as the first real run of this suite.

author: laruss
body:
From a report written by an agent driving the browser against a live SPA. Nine
items, each one something a capable surface still got wrong.

## What was wrong, and where it landed

| Report item | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `--help` worked only at the top level | One `BROWSER_CLI_COMMANDS` table feeds `patcher --help` metadata, each command's own `--help`, **and** which flags that command reads |
| 401 named neither the variable nor the path | `apps/cli/src/app-credential-hint.ts`, wired into all three places that print a 401 |
| No `wait` — the biggest one | `wait --text\|--selector\|--url\|--network-idle`, exit 124; **plus** every acting/navigating command settles before answering |
| `open --background` | `tabs.open({activate:false})` and a hidden view that actually loads |
| Scroll only via `mousewheel`, under "Direct control" | `scroll` in Acting: `--page`/`--top`/`--bottom`/`--by`/a ref, reporting offset · height · viewport |
| `text --selector` silently ignored | Implemented for real: new `readPageIn` shell channel |
| Tab ids dragged through every call | `--tab 3`, `--tab x.com`, `--tab active`; `tabs` is numbered |
| `status` answered `{connected, windowCount}` | Active tab with its URL, and a next step when nothing is connected |
| `generation 0` explained nothing | Says what to pass it to |

Two bugs of the same class the report did not reach: the `browser_snapshot`
**agent tool** accepted `selector` and dropped it, and `open --tab X --new-tab`
silently ignored `--tab`.

## The two that needed more than the CLI

**`text --selector`.** The unscoped read's request carries `tabId` and nothing
else *on purpose* — any knob would be a caller's value spliced into a privileged
snippet inside an untrusted page. So the scoped read takes the shape `snapshotIn`
established: its own shell channel, feature-detected, with the selector
travelling as a `DOM.querySelector` parameter over the debugger and a constant
function called on the node that comes back. It resolves into the automation
world, so a scoped read is no more forgeable than an unscoped one. It costs a CDP
attach the unscoped read does not, hence `debugger_unavailable`,
`invalid_selector` and `no_match`. An older shell is refused rather than allowed
to read the whole document and call it a success.

**`open --background`.** `tabs.open({activate: false})` existed, but the deck
mounts a view only for the active tab — deliberately, so restoring twenty tabs
does not load twenty pages. That rule is about *restore*, and it made a
background open useless: no live page, so the next read failed `tab_not_live`. A
background open now attaches its own hidden view and waits for it, registered
under the identity the deck will use when the user later selects that tab. Its
bounds are deliberately not zeroes — a hidden view is still laid out, and layout
is what `innerText`, `scrollHeight` and every actionability check read.

## Two decisions recorded rather than left implicit

Both are in `docs/architecture/browser-automation.md` under a new Stage G:

- **`scroll` rides `control.evaluate`** with four fixed expressions, which costs
  `page.inject` — the arbitrary-JS permission — for something that should cost
  `page.interact`. Nothing a caller supplies reaches the page (`--by` is an
  integer by then), so it is safe, but a plugin wanting `scroll` would have to
  declare `page.inject`. A wire-level interaction on its own channel is the right
  home; that is a follow-up, not a blocker.
- **`wait --selector` resolves through the scoped read, not a scoped snapshot.**
  A snapshot replaces the tab's ref table, so waiting for an element to appear
  would silently invalidate the refs the caller is holding. Waiting must cost
  nothing but time.

## Quiet is measured by fingerprint, not by clock

Network entries are stamped by the machine running the desktop app; this code
runs in the server process, which on a remote install is a different machine.
Two samples of the newest entries, an interval apart measured locally, say
"nothing finished in between" without the two clocks having to agree. And a
settle can never fail a command that already succeeded — a tab with no live page
reports "still busy" on stderr and leaves the exit code alone.

## Behaviour changes worth knowing at review time

- Acting and navigating commands now cost ~500ms on a quiet page (500ms quiet
  window, 3s budget). `--no-settle` opts out.
- A flag a command does not read is now **refused by name** instead of ignored,
  and the refusal names the commands that do read it. `patcher browser url
  --json` errors where it used to be silently accepted.
- The settle puts `page.network` polls into `tracing-start` traces.

## Verification

- browser-tools 130, app 3114, desktop 641, cli 426, plugin-sdk 125, domain 176,
  desktop-contract 15 — green. `turbo run typecheck lint`: 55/55, 0 errors /
  152 warnings (the repo's documented baseline).
- **15 mutations of the new behaviour, each one turned a test red** — none
  missed, none skipped.
- `apps/server`'s plugin suite fails 25/634 in a fresh worktree. Verified
  pre-existing by restoring every file this branch touches to `HEAD` and
  re-running: identical 25 failed / 609 passed on both sides.
- Not run locally: `tests/integration` (boots a real server and daemon).

body:
Previously, when the `autoit3.installDir` or `autoit3.userDefinedLibraries` settings changed,
already-resolved `#include`s were kept from the old configuration, leaving stale include
resolutions and diagnostics until the document itself was edited.

Fixes #75

## Changes

- `server/src/autoit/Script.ts`
  - Added `Script.refreshIncludes()`: releases all cached includes, clears the include
    cache, re-runs `analyze()` (re-resolves includes without re-parsing the document text),
    and triggers diagnostics.
- `server/src/autoit/Workspace.ts`
  - `onDidChangeConfiguration` now compares old vs. new `installDir` and
    `userDefinedLibraries`; if either changed, `refreshIncludes()` is called on every
    script in the workspace.
  - Extracted the dependency-graph update logic from `createOrUpdate()` into a new
    `Workspace.updateDependencies(script)` method, reused after include refreshes so
    dependency edges stay consistent with the newly resolved includes.
- `server/src/autoit/Workspace.test.ts`
  - Added tests: `installDir` / `userDefinedLibraries` changes trigger `refreshIncludes()`,
    and unchanged/reapplied configuration does not.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Includes are now automatically re-checked when the installation directory or user-defined library settings change.
  - Updated library settings refresh dependency information and diagnostics across open scripts without requiring text reparsing or manual reopening.
  - Unchanged configuration updates no longer trigger unnecessary include refreshes.
  - Prevented outdated include results from overwriting dependency information after files are refreshed.
  - Removed stale unresolved-include diagnostics when newer include analysis supersedes previous results.

author: g-f307
snehaa006
body:
The transcript already lined up against the questions; nothing read it. A teacher had the conversation under each question and still had to write both observed columns from memory.

So the recording is read. Per student turn, markers — eliminated, gave a reason, self-corrected, second-guessed, misread the stem, named the rule, said outright she did not know a word — and per question a verdict off them. The verdicts exist because four of them are invisible in the answers: a tick is a tick whether the student explained it or shrugged, and the teacher asks for the reasoning on the right ones precisely because of that.

Findings roll up per domain and are offered as buttons under the boxes they belong to, each naming its questions and showing the line it came from. The teacher clicks one, edits it, or ignores it. Nothing writes itself in — the numbers are computed, the words stay the teacher's.

Two patterns had to be tightened against the real recording. self_correction first matched "wait" and "actually", which is how anyone talks; it fired on two questions in three and meant nothing. talked_out_of_it fired on any wobble and swallowed the concept gaps, so it now needs the student to have been the one doing the talking. With both, the verdicts land on the teacher's own diagnosis chips for all five misses.

Alignment stays a lookup. Find it sets the offset by trying each one and keeping what leaves fewest questions with nobody talking; who is who is a control, because attributing the teacher's explanation to the student would be wrong silently.

And the report leaves the app: Save as PDF prints it as it appears, heading and all, minus the sidebar and the buttons. There is no second document to hold in step with the data.

0022 seeds the recorded paper as a test to sit, in the order the hour works through it. The transcript is deliberately not seeded — pasting it is the step being rehearsed.

author: lei-tzuy
body:
## Summary

- prevent an in-flight Reporting API request from recreating a delayed retry after the same concrete endpoint URL has already been removed by a prior `410 Gone`
- apply endpoint-removal state after each completion batch, then prune any retry just produced for a completed batch whose endpoint is already removed
- preserve retries for unrelated collectors
- retain ownership of already-dispatched requests in the network backend; they may settle normally, but their retryable failure cannot resurrect a removed endpoint
- add deterministic integration coverage for completion ordering across separate event-loop turns

## Why

PR #232 prunes delayed retries that already exist when a 410 removal is observed. One lifecycle hole remains when another request to the same URL is still in flight at that moment: if that request later completes with 503 or a network error, the runtime can schedule a brand-new retry after the endpoint is already removed.

This PR makes endpoint removal authoritative across later in-flight settlements too. The completion is still surfaced to the caller, but any retry it creates is immediately discarded when its endpoint is already marked removed.

## Tests

New `tests/reporting_post_410_inflight_retry.rs` covers:

1. 410 arrives first; a same-endpoint in-flight 503 arrives on a later completion turn and must not recreate a retry
2. a backup endpoint's later 503 remains retryable after the primary endpoint was removed

## Validation

- final head: `96b996f24b3c577191c3b26252bbcecf5cad2153`
- relative to #232: 2 commits, 2 changed files, +124 / -16
- GitHub Actions `Tests` #1591 / run `33431874551`: **completed / success**
- full workflow `cargo test --locked`: **success**
- PR is open, mergeable, and unmerged

## Stack

Based directly on PR #232 / `agent/reporting-prune-410-retries`.

Reporting tail: `#226 → #229 → #231 → #232 → #233`

No PR is merged by this change.

author: jeremydmiller
body:
Closes #178, #182, #183, #184. **Stacked on #188** (`gh-181-event-model-edges`, itself on #186) — they all touch `EventModelView.vue`. Merge downwards and each retargets cleanly.

Four commits, one per issue, all in `@jasperfx/event-model-vue` (**0.7.0**) so both consoles inherit one answer. Verified against the real 106-slice CritterWatch model in the running console, which is also what exposed two of the fixes below.

## #183 — bound-specification count

A badge on every slice header. Until now the only way to learn whether a slice had a spec at all was to click it. `no spec` is spelled out rather than rendered as `0`, because zero is the drift case the canvas already colours orange and it should read as a finding. Where the host passes `sliceOutcomes` the badge carries the verdict, so a failing slice says so at the same glance it says it has three specs. A slice the evidence did not name stays unmarked rather than defaulting to green.

## #184 — trigger kind, and routes that stop eating the card

A 12px glyph per `triggerKind` (globe, envelope, clock, person, paired arrows, box-with-arrow) with `triggerOrigin` on its tooltip — which is where the route lives now that wolverine#4181 stopped the HTTP source claiming `TriggerLabel`. Inline path data, not an icon dependency: this component ships to two consoles with different icon sets and a shared third is the one thing neither host wants.

A trigger card whose label *is* a route renders its verb as an outlined badge and the path beside it. Outlined rather than filled because fill means the element **kind**, and a badge painting over it would spend the one channel this package guards. `parseRoute` matches the label rather than reading `triggerOrigin`, because the label is what the card actually renders — and prose that merely starts with a word is not a route: *"An agent claims ready work"* stays a sentence.

## #178 — a source disagreement is a finding

The producer makes the hotspot's *text* the element label, so the card led with the role name and a truncated sentence. Reviewing the Stoat canvas you read it as a malformed events list and asked what it was supposed to show — and that reading is the finding: nothing on the card said two sources disagreed.

It now renders structure — what kind of finding, then the role and both claims with their rungs, kept above dropped and the dropped one struck through — all from the typed `role` / `winningClaim` / `losingClaim`. A disagreement whose pair did not survive the wire degrades to its text rather than to half a finding with one side missing.

Promoting findings out of the lanes into a strip above the canvas — the other candidate on the issue — stays unbuilt: position is what says which slice a finding belongs to, and a strip would have to repeat that in words. Worth reopening if the header turns out not to be enough.

## #182 — zoom and pan

Zoom is a CSS transform on a wrapper, deliberately **not** a scale factor threaded into `layoutEventModel`: layout is a pure function of the descriptor, and letting the viewport change it would put the two viewers' agreement at the mercy of how wide someone's window happens to be. The wrapper carries its own scaled box, because a transform does not change layout size and the scroller would otherwise still think the canvas was its 100% self.

Stops (25%–200%) so a reader can return to a zoom they had, the level doubling as reset; **Fit** is the one non-step zoom because "all of it on screen" is a measurement, and it never zooms *in* to fill. Drag-to-pan on the background, never on a button. Ctrl/⌘+wheel for the trackpad pinch. The canvas chrome measurements moved into `layout.ts` as `canvasSize()` for the same anti-drift reason the type scale did in #180.

Worth knowing: on the 106-slice CritterWatch model, Fit lands on the 25% floor and the canvas is still ~10,000px wide. That is the honest answer — the floor exists so text stays legible — but it says a very large model wants a minimap or slice filtering, which is a separate issue if you want it.

## Verification

80 tests in the package, typecheck + build green. Screenshots in the conversation: the `PUT` badge with a wrapped path, globe/envelope glyphs, `no spec` badges, and a `SOURCES DISAGREE` card showing kept vs struck-through dropped.

author: jdrumgoole
body:
Found in the documentation-reconciliation pass at session close — the pass that catches a *correct-looking* claim describing behaviour that has since been measured.

`CLAUDE.md` and `docs/indexes.md` both say per-index collation supports "strength 1/2/3 + `caseLevel`". That is accurate for what those sections describe (index entry normalisation, so collation-equal strings land at one byte key) — but it reads as collation working generally, and the 2026-08-31 differential measured that it does not:

- **matching** agreed with mongod 8.2.11 at every strength;
- **ordering** falls back to codepoint — accents sort after `z` instead of beside their base letter, and `caseFirst` / `backwards` / `numericOrdering` / the locale itself are accepted and ignored.

Both files now name which half is supported and point at `tasks/backlog.md` §5 for the measurements and what closing it would take.

`CLAUDE.md` also records the spec-validation asymmetry from #1174, because it is exactly the kind of thing a later change would "tidy up for consistency": the collation spec is validated on `find` / `aggregate` / `count` / `distinct` / `findAndModify` and **deliberately not** on `update` / `delete`, because mongod does not validate it there.

Docs only — no code change.

author: pkulijing
body:
## 1. 本批 issue 清单

- Closes #106 —— `_common` 模板的 CI 默认只跑 lint 不跑测试 —— 守护测试没有门禁就只是注释 `[标记通道]`
- Closes #128 —— react-vite 栈没有任何自动门禁：既无 pre-commit 也无 CI workflow `[标记通道]`

两条都属「模板的自动门禁」这一件事，按 Step 2 规则 2（主题同源可并批）合为一批；且都要动 `README.md` 的模板表，按落点不相交不变式本来也必须并批。每条一个 commit。

## 2. 逐条改动摘要

### #106 → `184f84f`

六份后端 CI 文件各加一个 pytest job：`python-uv` 与 `python-uv-workspace` ×（GitHub `lint.yml` + GitLab `.variant.docker` + `.variant.shell`）。

- **无用例时优雅跳过**：pytest 收集不到用例时退出码为 5，视作跳过；**其它非零退出码照常让 CI 红**（「一旦有测试就必须跑」）。
- **GitLab 侧复用一律用标准 YAML 锚点**（`&anchor` / `*anchor`），**不用** `!reference` —— 这是 issue 明确点名的坑：`check-yaml` 不认那个自定义 tag，会报 `could not determine a constructor for the tag` 让 commit 直接失败。

> **一处有意的保守取舍**：issue 提到「可顺带上 OS matrix」，**没做成默认**。GitHub 的 macos runner 对公开仓免费、对私有仓按 **10 倍分钟**计费，给每个用该模板起的项目默认开启是一笔不该由模板替人做的决定。开启方法以注释写在 `test` job 上方，两行即可打开。代价是 issue 那个「17 个用例在 macOS 上红了整整一轮而 CI 全绿」的具体故障形态，本次只堵住了「CI 根本不跑测试」那一半。

> `_common/` 下**其实没有 CI 文件**（issue 标题说的是 `_common`，实际 CI 一直在两个 python 栈的 `__root__/` 下）。按实际落点改的，没有新建 `_common` CI。

### #128 → `4a19af2`

**落点决策**（issue 明确把它留给实现者按 `MECHANICS.md` 既有约定定）：

| 目标 | 机制 | 为什么 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.pre-commit-config.yaml` | **新增 YAML fragment** | 落项目根，前后端两维都要贡献 hooks，混栈要的是**并集**不是二选一 |
| `.gitlab-ci.yml` | **新增 YAML fragment** | 同上；前端与 runner 类型正交，要的不是「再来一个变体」，而是往**已选中的那份**里加一个 job |
| `.github/workflows/` | **普通文件**，命名 `frontend-lint.yml` | 与后端 `lint.yml` 天然不同名，`__root__` 不撞车，**不需要**上 fragment 机制 |

据此 `MECHANICS.md` 新增 **§2.3「YAML 合并」**，定义两个目标各自的合并语义，以及两条硬约束：

1. **落地顺序：普通文件与变体组先落地，fragment 最后合并。**
2. **fragment 里不许用 YAML 锚点**（锚点作用域是单个文档，合并后会重名或悬空）。变体组那两份是**整份落地、不参与合并**，故它们内部照常用锚点。

**另外两处不在 issue 里、但不做就等于白做的**：

- **`bootstrap` 的 3.3.6 / 3.3.7 顺序原本是反的**（先合 fragment 再落变体），与上面硬约束 1 相反。**这是 review 报出来的**，见下节。
- **`MECHANICS.md` §5 补上「确保 pre-commit 钩子真的注册上」两步**。配置文件本身不是门禁 —— 没跑过 `pre-commit install` 就没有 `.git/hooks/pre-commit`，那份配置一次都不会被执行。混栈项目由 §4 顺带装上了，**纯前端项目走不到 §4**，不补就等于白落一个文件（正是本 issue 自己在讲的那个道理）。

**一处与 issue 给的代码不同**：issue 的钩子片段用 `npm run lint --workspaces --if-present`，那是从 split-book（npm workspaces 仓库）来的；**本模板是落 `frontend/` 的单包、没有 workspaces**，故写成 `cd frontend && npm run lint`。这同时正是 biome 按目录解析配置所要求的形式。

`playbooks/frontend.md` §1 补上那条 biome 陷阱（从根跑 `biome check <子目录>` 读不到该目录的 `biome.json`，静默用默认配置），与既有的「`biome.json` 里不能写注释否则静默回落 tab 缩进」同型。

## 3. review 情况

**扇出规格与轮数**：默认档（角度 ①②③），共 2 轮，收敛放行（非留痕放行，无遗留 finding）。**本批未降级** —— `agents/` 的类型已可用，`review-orchestrator` 与 `code-reviewer` 均真实起用。

**一处必须如实说明的编队形态**：第 1 轮的 `review-orchestrator` **未能并行起 reviewer 子 agent**（子 agent 不能再起子 agent，它在自己的工具列表里找不到 Agent 工具），故它按角度清单①②③**顺序自审**并在结果顶部注明了「reviewer 未并行」。所以第 1 轮是「一个独立 context 覆盖三个角度」而非「三个独立 context 各覆盖一个角度」。第 2 轮改由主会话**直接**并行起 `code-reviewer`（`model` 与 `effort` 均由 frontmatter 钉死），拿到了真正的逐角度独立 context。合起来两轮都在独立 context 内完成，**独立 context 这个首要属性未丢**，但第 1 轮的角度隔离不如设计意图。

**第 1 轮 finding（1 条，置信 90，已修）**

> **`skills/bootstrap/SKILL.md` 的步骤顺序与本次新增的 `MECHANICS.md` §2.3 硬约束 1 方向相反。** bootstrap 是「3.3.6 合并 fragments → 3.3.7 落地变体组」，而新约束要求变体先落地。**而本次新增的 `.gitlab-ci.yml.fragment` 正是让 `.gitlab-ci.yml` 首次同时成为变体组目标与 fragment 目标的改动**，所以这个矛盾是本 PR 亲手变得可触发的：同时选 `python-uv` + `react-vite` 时，fragment 先判定「目标不存在」而创建了 `.gitlab-ci.yml`，随后变体落地发现文件已存在、把它扔进冲突清单 —— 白白问用户一次，而用户要选的那个变体本来就该赢。

→ 对调两步并重新编号，加一句指向 §2.3 的说明，并更新**三处交叉引用**（第 68 行的「分别走 X 的合并与 Y 的落地」、3.5 的「回到 3.3.6」、marker 示例注释里的「3.3.7 用户选的 key」）。第 2 轮已逐处复核六个引用点全部一致，且确认 `needs-step-3.5` 回环在新编号下逻辑不变。

**第 2 轮 finding（2 条，均属文档准确性，已修）**

1. **【角度 ③】`bootstrap` 那段说明复述了 `MECHANICS.md` 的故障机制**，违反 `CLAUDE.md`「落地机制的单一真源是 `templates/MECHANICS.md`，**别在别处复述**」。→ 压成一句指向式引用。
2. **【角度 ①②】`README.md` 里「前后端两维**各出一份 fragment**取并集」与实际机制不符** —— 后端那份 `.pre-commit-config.yaml` 是走普通复制的**基础文件**，只有前端出 fragment 往里合。文实不符会误导后续新增 stack 的人。→ 改写为准确描述。

**第 2 轮明确未推翻的一条**：角度 ③ 被要求独立复核第 1 轮「`sync-project-config` 属遵从而非矛盾」的判断，复核后**维持原判**（它把顺序完全交给 MECHANICS，未自行断言先后）。

**运行验证（闸 A）**：本批改的是模板与指令文件，仓库自身**无对应单测**（`scripts/` / `hooks/` 未被触及）。改为跑与产物直接对应的**可执行验证**：

| 验证 | 结果 |
| --- | --- |
| 全部 11 份 YAML 用 PyYAML 解析（等价 pre-commit 的 `check-yaml`，正是 `!reference` 会挂的那道闸） | **PASS** |
| GitLab 锚点展开（`*uv_image` / `*uv_sync` / `*default_rules` 是否真的展开成期望值） | **PASS** |
| pytest 退出码逻辑在 `bash -e` 下实跑 0 / 5 / 1 / 2 | **0→过、5→跳过、1→红、2→红**，不吞真失败 |
| pre-commit `entry` 按 pre-commit 对 `language: system` 的 shlex 切法实跑 | **PASS**：cwd 确为 `frontend/`（证明 biome 能读到 `frontend/biome.json`）、非零退出码如实传播（钩子真的拦得住 commit） |
| 拆分成 2 个 commit 后与被 review 的工作树逐字节比对（13 个文件） | **全部一致** |

**一处如实记录的偏差**（与 PR #146 同）：本批采用「一次 review 覆盖整批 diff，再按 issue 拆成 2 个 commit」，而非每个 commit 各跑一轮 review。

**一条已知未覆盖**：`setup-node` 的 `cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json` 在 lockfile 尚未生成时会硬失败。reviewer 判定触发条件很窄（要求 bootstrap 的 `npm install` 已失败、用户仍提交推送），且两种情况下 CI 都会红、不构成静默通过，故未改。**如实记在这里而不是当它不存在。**

## 4. 本次跳过

（本次运行的完整跳过清单已写在**第一个** PR **#146** 的第 4 段，此处不重复。）

本批相关的一条：**5 条 `auto:take` issue 全部纳入本次运行**，没有「被标记却仍被跳过」的。

## 5. 本批触及了什么面

> ⚠ **本 PR 修改了跨项目模板，会影响后续所有 bootstrap / sync。**
> ⚠ **本 PR 同时修改了 skill（`skills/bootstrap/SKILL.md` 的步骤顺序）与指令规则文件（`playbooks/frontend.md`），请重点 review。**

取最高一档标注，但两条都点出来，因为它们的影响面不同：

- **模板改动会流向每一个未来项目**，且 `.pre-commit-config.yaml` / `.gitlab-ci.yml` 是**会被工具真实解析执行**的配置 —— 写错不是文档别扭，是每次 commit / 每条 pipeline 都在执行它。
- **`bootstrap` 的步骤顺序对调**改变的是既有落地流程。对**已 bootstrap 过的老项目无影响**（那是一次性脚手架），影响的是此后每一次新项目初始化。
- **新增的 YAML fragment 是一个新机制**，`sync-project-config` 的 normal sync 路径也会消费它。§6「迁移去重」经核对**无需改动**（本次是纯新增，没有任何旧文件被删除，不构成「同一资源换承载形式」）。

## 6. 合入方式

打 `ff-merge` label 或评论 `/ff` 即 fast-forward 合入，不留 merge commit。

> ⚠ 与 **#146** 的落点已核对**两两不相交**（#146 只碰 `skills/review-loop/SKILL.md`），两个 PR 可按任意顺序 FF 合入，互不冲突。

author: va3elina
body:
Правки Вадима по живому черновику 1357: не писать «перекос net/gross» (жаргон), не приводить голое число контрактов (читателю ничего не говорит), искать крупное простое сравнение и привязывать позицию к цене.

## Опять чиним не правилом, а тем, что лежит на столе

Модель писала «перекос net/gross» **дословно, потому что дословно так называлось поле брифа**. Третий раз за сессию один и тот же механизм.

- поле → `доля_чистой_позиции_в_ои`, отдаёт готовую фразу «чистый шорт — 8% открытого интереса физлиц»;
- `чистая_позиция_контрактов` → в `служебное_не_для_текста` с объяснением почему;
- диапазон → `эта_доля_в_рамках_N_дней`.

## Новый блок `цена_акции`

Изменение за месяц / полгода / год из `candles` (маппинг фьючерс→акция через `ticker_futures_map.futures_sectype`). При движении ≥45% отдаётся **круглым сравнением** («упала примерно в 2 раза»), иначе процентом.

«Упала вдвое» читается лучше, чем «упала на 51,3%» — и это ровно язык канала: «за 10 дней сложились в 2 раза», «с начала года потеряли около 60%».

Горизонт ряда позиций 45 → 400 дней, добавлены сравнения за полгода и за год: без них привязать позицию к годовому движению цены было нечем.

## Судья

Пункт `no_methodology_talk` расширен на жаргон (`net`/`gross`) и на голые числа контрактов. Новый пункт **не заводился намеренно** — 13 ключей в рубрике и в коде остаются прежними.

`BRIEF_VERSION` 2 → 3 в обоих местах: набор полей изменился, а судья судит только по своей версии контракта (иначе артефактные провалы, см. миграцию 059).

author: j15z
body:
## Summary

When `generate_image` declares reference files, Sim now either loads every reference or fails before calling Gemini. A missing or unreadable image can no longer be silently dropped and turn an intended image edit into an unrelated text-only generation. Text-to-image remains unchanged when `inputs` is omitted.

This supersedes #5615. The existing production `save_upload` flow already promotes uploads to canonical workspace files, so this replacement preserves that boundary instead of making `uploads/...` a second first-class media path.

Related contract and agent-guidance change: https://github.com/simstudioai/mothership/pull/465

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation-only change

## Changes

- Reject a supplied but empty `inputs.files` array.
- Reject direct `uploads/...` references with guidance to use `save_upload` and the returned `files/...` path.
- Resolve, safety-check, and read every declared image before initializing or invoking the provider.
- Abort on the first unresolved or unreadable reference instead of silently continuing.
- Update the generated tool catalog and schema with the non-empty `generate_image.inputs.files` contract.
- Preserve Sim-local table TTL catalog descriptions so the generated diff stays scoped to this fix.

## Testing

- `cd apps/sim && bun run test lib/copilot/tools/server/image/generate-image.test.ts lib/copilot/tools/server/media/model-boundaries.test.ts` — 14 tests passed.
- `bunx biome check` passed for all four changed Sim files.
- `bun run check:api-validation` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Paired code review: ready to merge, with no actionable findings.

The repository-wide typecheck is currently blocked by unrelated existing dependency drift, including missing `@sim/deployment-config` and browser-protocol packages. Filtering its diagnostics produced no errors for the changed image-generation or generated-contract files.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

- For 24 hours after deploy, search `GenerateImageTool` logs for `Failed to load reference image`, `inputs.files must contain at least one`, and `save_upload` guidance.
- Healthy behavior: image edits report `referenceImageCount >= 1`, while text-to-image calls continue succeeding with no `inputs` object.
- Failure signal: a sustained increase in image-tool failures or agents repeatedly retrying the upload-promotion sequence.
- Owner: Copilot/media on-call. If those signals regress, roll back this PR and mothership#465 together.

## Checklist

- [x] Focused tests cover empty, upload, unresolved, unsafe, unreadable, and successful multi-reference inputs.
- [x] API validation and formatting checks pass.
- [x] No database schema changes.

## Screenshots / Videos

Not applicable; this is a server-side runtime and generated-contract change.

author: robertoepifanio-byte
body:
## O problema

A copy do e-mail de boas-vindas foi escrita **antes** da estratégia de pilotos e descreve um lançamento nacional simultâneo:

> Você é o **#N°** na lista de fundadores do ShareO.
> Avisaremos você em primeira mão **quando abrirmos**.
> Um e-mail com link de acesso exclusivo **assim que o ShareO abrir**.

Mas o plano de 90 dias é um **rollout por cidade**, e a ordem de convite é definida pela cidade escolhida — a rota `/api/admin/founders/invite` convida por `state`/`cityNorm`. Na prática, **um #2 nacional pode ser chamado depois de um #300 da cidade-piloto**.

Quem não está na primeira região não conclui "é por etapas": conclui que foi esquecido. E é justamente essa pessoa de quem o programa depende para **encaminhar** o e-mail.

## A nova redação

> **Você está na lista, Roberto!**
>
> Você é o **#2°** interessado a entrar na lista de fundadores. A abertura é feita **por cidade**: as regiões com mais interessados entram primeiro, e avisamos você em primeira mão quando chegar a sua — antes de qualquer anúncio público.
>
> **O que esperar:** Um e-mail com link de acesso exclusivo quando o ShareO abrir na sua cidade. Nenhum spam até lá.

| Mudança | Por quê |
|---|---|
| "**interessado a entrar** na lista" | o número passa a descrever *quando* a pessoa entrou — segue verdadeiro depois de a cidade reordenar tudo |
| "as regiões com **mais interessados entram primeiro**" | transforma espera passiva em algo que a pessoa influencia; é o mecanismo do programa dito explicitamente |
| "quando o ShareO abrir **na sua cidade**" | remove a promessa de data única |

O número segue **global** (ordem de entrada na lista) — calcular posição por região exigiria mudar a rota, e a redação nova não depende disso.

## Rodapé

"Desenvolvido por **Pratika IA**" entra no rodapé do **e-mail** e no da **landing da campanha** — os dois únicos que ainda não traziam a assinatura (o site e o app já têm, desde o #414).

Mesma redação e mesma URL (`https://www.pratika.ia.br`) do `components/layout/AppFooter.tsx`: duas grafias da mesma assinatura envelheceriam em direções diferentes. Na landing, `text-white` opaco pelo mesmo motivo documentado logo acima no arquivo — em texto pequeno sobre aquele fundo, opacidade reduzida era a única violação de contraste da página.

## Verificação

- `npx jest __tests__/unit/lib` → **509 passando** (4 novos)
- `npx jest` em `apps/campanha` → **28 passando**
- `npx tsc --noEmit` limpo nos dois apps

Os 4 testes novos fixam o que não pode regredir: que a abertura é por cidade, que o critério da ordem é declarado, que não se promete lançamento único, e que o número descreve entrada e não acesso.

⚠️ Copy de e-mail só é verificável em envio real após deploy.

author: seonghobae
body:
## Why

Protected main already serves `POST /v1/temporal-context` on `AnalysisRunLiveService` / `tepp-loopback`, but LineageWeave operators still had to write raw HTTP/1.1. Stdout stays cutoff-safe and metric-free with `claim_boundary` `association_not_causal`. `tepp.scientific_acceptance.v1` never appears. The CLI does not infer causality.

Live slices that this PR does **not** duplicate:
- #356 `analysis_engine` scientific-acceptance library
- #358 tepp_api terminal-wire DTO
- #359 GET loopback status by id
- #360 POST running/terminal lifecycle
- #361 cancel HTTP
- #362 scientific-acceptance loopback CLI
- #368 collection GET
- #371 collection CLI `list`
- #378 cancel CLI
- #385 create CLI
- #392 status CLI
- #394 retry CLI
- #395 stored-request CLI
- #397 lifecycle CLI
- #400 retry-parent CLI
- #401 lookup CLI
- #403 retry-lineage CLI
- #406 wait CLI
- #410 export-authorize CLI
- #411 export-retrieval GET
- #287 GAP-003B persistence/Compose
- #351 Leiden
- GAP-010 Figma/export

## What

LineageWeave temporal-context CLI stacked on protected main `1bc02f580cf48e1d39da239f0e818453437c31c3`:

- `tepp-temporal-context query` client of `POST /v1/temporal-context` on `tepp-loopback`
- stdin is `TemporalContextRequest` JSON; consumer is `lineageweave` only
- no `idempotency-key` (bounded read, not a durable create)
- metric-free `association_not_causal` stdout; `tepp.scientific_acceptance.v1` never prints
- loopback-only; credential flags, empty stdin, unknown verbs, and metric keys fail closed
- ADR 0027 on protected main (distinct from GET-status ADR 0027 on other stacks)

Not an ADR 0014 scientific claim. Not persistence. Not a causal score. Not project-history CLI.

## Verification

- `cargo clippy -p tepp_api --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p tepp_api --lib temporal_context_cli`
- `cargo test -p tepp_api --test temporal_context_cli_contract`
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc -p tepp_api --no-deps`
- `python3 scripts/validate_documentation.py`
- `python3 scripts/check_docstrings.py`

Do not merge without two independent APPROVE reviews on this exact head and current Checks. Author COMMENTED is not independent APPROVE.

author: raksitnongbua
body:
The flowchart canvas answers all four canvas-edit abilities now, where it answered none. Every gesture is a **line patch** of the author's own source, so comments, blank lines and hand spacing survive one.

## ⚠️ This changes the `.alab` flowchart format

`FlowchartNode` takes an optional `position`, spelled `(x,y)` on the node line — the C4 geometry token minus the size.

**It is not a breaking change, and that was measured, not assumed:**

- A node with no `(x,y)` is solved from the arrows exactly as before. The bundled example lays out at the same `694x976` and every node's coordinates are unchanged.
- Every `.alab` flowchart already on disk or inside a share link parses and renders identically.
- A point carrying an unexpected key from a newer minor rides the `!` escape **whole**. This was a real data-loss bug — `{"x":1,"y":2,"z":3}` was being written back as `(1,2)` — found by writing the assertion rather than by reading the code.

`.alab` is beta in-product; flagging it explicitly per `.claude/rules/changelog.md` regardless.

## What each ability needed

| Ability | Was | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `move` | refused, `grammar` | **the format changed** — the one thing that moves such a refusal |
| `create` | refused, `grammar` | **the refusal was simply wrong** — see below |
| `revise` | refused, `surface` | grew the dock the canvas already opened |
| `connect` | refused, `surface` | grew a grip on the node that already had focus |

**`create` is the one worth reading.** Its cell had copied `NO_PLACE_IN_THE_TEXT` from the notations that solve their own layout — "there is no position to place a new element at." But a flowchart step's place *is* its arrows, so "between these two" was always writable: splitting `a -> b` into `a -> new` and `new -> b` needed no new grammar and would have worked a release earlier. A written-out cell can copy the wrong neighbour's sentence just as easily as a default can supply one, which is the failure the "no default cell" rule does *not* protect against. That is now in the rules file.

## Multi-select is the C4 canvas's gesture, not a second invention

It first shipped as a shift-click beside a canvas that had a Select/Pan toggle and a marquee — so learning one canvas did not teach the other (`codebase.md` habit 2). Now: the same toggle, Select as the default once unlocked, selection on **full containment**, and a bare drag still pans on a locked canvas — which is every shared link and every presentation, since the canvas locks by default.

`ViewerModeToggle` → `src/components/ui/canvas-mode-toggle.tsx` as `CanvasModeToggle`, since two features use it now. A check asserts both canvases read one definition.

## Bugs found in use, fixed with geometry measured rather than reasoned about

- **A pin was stored in solved space and read in drawn space**, so a step walked `offset.x` further right on *every* drag — 300 → 655 → 1010. Fixing it took three rounds, because each fix exposed the next coupling: the offset itself moved with the pin, then routing did, then pin-incident edge points did. **1,120 drop points across the canvas now land 0px out.**
- **Pointer capture on pointerdown retargeted the click**, so clicking a step stopped focusing it. Capture is lazy now.
- **The drag threshold was in user units** — a hair-trigger at any scale below 1:1, which is the default `fit`. Two pixels of jitter turned a shift-click into a drag, making multi-select unusable in practice.
- **Overlay chrome inside the pane ate its own clicks** — pressing Clear, or the padlock, started a marquee. Chrome is marked rather than listed, so a new overlay is covered without anyone remembering.
- **The drag now moves the real symbol at reduced opacity**, not a ghost outline, with the arrows that still describe its old place dimmed for the length of the drag.

## Decisions recorded

- **ADR 0002** supersedes **ADR 0001**. 0001 is marked, not rewritten: its argument was sound and every cost it named is still real and unmitigated — a pinned step can overlap a solved one, an arrow into it can run backwards, and a hand-written coordinate outside the solved bounds is clipped. That last one is a genuine trade-off: exact dragging and clip protection are mutually exclusive, and dragging won because a drag can never produce an off-canvas pin.
- **There is no unpin gesture.** Delete the `(x,y)` in the source pane. A gap, not a decision.

## Proof

- **98 behavioural assertions** across five harnesses — grammar round-trip, layout, gestures, drag exactness, marquee containment — all against deliberately non-canonical text.
- **839 `check:canvas-edit` assertions**, including a new section deriving flowchart gesture reachability from `FlowchartEditHandlers` the way the sequence one already did. There was no flowchart equivalent, which is why six gestures shipped with nothing asserting a control reached them.
- **Every new assertion was broken on purpose and watched fail by name.** Three of my own turned out to be unfailable and were strengthened: one counted a marker that also matched its own selector string, one matched a sibling prop, and one asked whether the derived passage mentioned a notation when a sibling clause already did.
- Two check-script bugs fixed: `canvas-chrome` windowed 400 characters and mistook a neighbouring control's `left-3` for the zoom pill's; the replacement walks back to the first `className` that states a position, verified against both markup shapes in the repo.

## Gate

`pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test && pnpm build` all pass — lint has its 3 known warnings and no fourth. 60 of 61 `check:*` scripts pass.

**`check:canvas-grid` fails, and it fails on clean `main` too** (`paper: the well is ABOVE its chrome`) — verified by checking out `main` and running it. Pre-existing, not this branch's.

body:
<!-- Write all pull request text in Simplified Technical English (ASD-STE100): short sentences, one instruction per sentence, simple approved vocabulary, and the active voice. -->

## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is the open source app people use to manage AI agents for work.
> - The issue lifecycle controls governed work and dependency order.
> - A completed blocker did not activate the next governed task.
> - The API also accepted a direct backlog-to-done transition.
> - The governed root could then close without a valid child lifecycle.
> - This pull request adds focused lifecycle guards and dependency activation.
> - The benefit is deterministic task order and safe governed closeout.

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

Related closed setup PR: #37

**What happened?**

A governed child stayed in backlog after its blocker completed. The API then accepted a direct transition from backlog to done. The API also allowed the governed root to close.

**Expected behavior**

A completed blocker must activate the newly ready child and assign its planned owner. A governed backlog task must not move directly to done. A governed root must stay open until all descendants are done.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Create a governed root with two children.
2. Make the second child depend on the first child.
3. Accept the current plan and dependency graph.
4. Complete the first child.
5. Observe that the second child stays in backlog.
6. Move the second child directly to done.
7. Close the governed root.

**Paperclip version or commit**

The bug was reproduced on commit `668e1b4d4ee41f809d4c2141de3a958fc0035c01`.

**Deployment mode**

Built from source.

**Agent adapter(s) involved**

Not adapter-specific. This is a core lifecycle bug.

## What Changed

- Activate each newly unblocked governed child once.
- Restore the planned agent assignment during activation.
- Send the normal idempotent assignment wake after commit.
- Reject a governed transition from backlog to done.
- Reject governed root closeout until every descendant is done.
- Add focused regression tests for all three paths.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @paperclipai/server exec vitest run src/__tests__/sdlc-lifecycle.test.ts`
- `pnpm --filter @paperclipai/server typecheck`
- `git diff --check`

## Risks

- The change makes governed closeout stricter. A cancelled child no longer satisfies completion.
- The activation update uses a root row lock. This keeps concurrent blocker completion deterministic.
- The wake request uses an idempotency key. A repeated completion does not create a second activation.

> For core feature work, check [`ROADMAP.md`](ROADMAP.md) first and discuss it in `#dev` before opening the PR. Feature PRs that overlap with planned core work may need to be redirected — check the roadmap first. See `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Model Used

OpenAI Codex with model `gpt-5.6-sol`. The agent used repository tools, code execution, focused tests, and TypeScript type checking.

author: ced59
shman4ik
body:
The two Nimbus marks had drifted apart in three ways that only show up when you measure them against each other. Geometry was pulled out of **both** `design/logo.af` files through the Affinity SDK and compared numerically rather than by eye.

## What was wrong

| | pgNimbus | kubeNimbus (before) | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| Light field radius | 360 (ring 152) | **380** (ring 132) | 360 |
| Broom scale | 1.0 | **×1.013916** | 1.0 |
| Clearance halo stroke | 39.451 | **40** | 39.451 |
| Layer names | `base-plate`, `base-field`, `broom-*-clearance` | `circle1`, `inner-circle`, `path3/4/5` | matched |
| Field's CSS class | `paper` | **`ink`** (rescued only by an inline style) | `paper` |
| `logo-dark.svg` | deleted | diverged path for path from its light twin | generated |

The field radius is the most visible one side by side, and 380 had no derivation behind it — 360/512 = 0.703125 is measured off pgNimbus's raster-era master.

The broom drift is the interesting one. The halo stroke had gone 39.451 → 40 by ×1.013916 and the outlines had gone by ×1.013923 — **the same factor for both**, which is the fingerprint of one resize handle rather than of two independent decisions. That is what identified kubeNimbus as the copy that had moved.

## Verification

The broom is now byte-identical to pgNimbus's — same size, same coordinates in the same 1024 grid. Both marks rendered at 2048 and diffed over regions containing broom and plate but **no mascot**:

```
plate + bristles (bottom-left)   >32/255: 0 of 68,120    max 14/255
plate + handle tip (top-right)   >32/255: 0 of 27,200    max  9/255
plate + handle mid               >32/255: 0 of 28,000    max  8/255
plate only (top-left corner)     >32/255: 0 of 67,600    max  0/255
```

Zero differing pixels; the residue is antialiasing. Path data also compared coordinate-by-coordinate: max delta 0.01px, which is the resolution of the SVG's two-decimal output.

The `.af` → SVG bridge was checked against Affinity's own render of the `.af`: **0.076%** of pixels differ by more than 32/255, against pgNimbus's already-trusted **0.073%** baseline. That equivalence is also what proves the halo is rendered at 39.451 and not 40 — the leaves here carry a *scale*, which pgNimbus's (pure translations) never have.

App builds with 0 warnings; the 16/24px marks still read correctly.

## The mascots are deliberately left alone

They differ in ink area (3.76% vs 5.28% of canvas), bounding box (586×455 vs 411×375), line weight (21.5 vs ~34) and whether they cross onto the plate (the elephant does and needs its halo there; the helm does not). That is the point: the family is the plate, the field, the broom and the rules of construction — **not a common silhouette**. Forcing one mascot's numbers onto the other would damage whichever lost the argument without making the pair read as more related.

## So it cannot drift again

`design/logo.af` becomes the master and every SVG is generated from it, the same two-step bridge pgNimbus uses:

```
logo.af → scripts/design/dump-af.js → scripts/design/af-to-svg.py
```

`af-to-svg.py` differs from pgNimbus's copy in two ways, both load-bearing: it **accumulates ancestor transforms** instead of reading only a leaf's own (Affinity puts a transform wherever the edit was made, and a leaf-only reader silently emits untransformed geometry), and it **carries stroke width through that transform**, refusing a non-uniform scale rather than guessing. It writes `logo-dark.svg` too, so "the same bytes with two values exchanged" is enforced rather than asserted.

The four **family rules** and the evidence behind them are in [`design/LOGO.md`](design/LOGO.md). A change to the base or the broom is a change to both repositories and a pair of PRs — the same discipline `shared/nimbusUi` already has.

## Paired change in pgNimbus

`pgNimbus/design/LOGO.md` carries the same four rules verbatim. **It is written but not committed** — that working tree is mid-change on `logo-vector-master`, so it is left for you rather than committed onto your in-progress branch. pgNimbus's own art is untouched by this PR.

## Known exception, unchanged and now written down

`#mascot-helm` still has the broom's clearance gap baked into its outline, so unlike `#brand-broom` it is not yet liftable onto an arbitrary background (family rule 3). Un-baking it means redrawing the helm parametrically. It is invisible in the shipped mark, and the helm does not cross the field's rim, so it needs no halo for legibility today.

author: reizuseharu
body:
The rebuild lost two events, both to #132.

### A clause is not a Duelist

`2016-sa-wcq` writes its Top 16 as a dash-delimited chain with "Versus" between the halves. The sentence reader fires on any sentence saying "against" or "versus", so it read this as a pairing:

```
'With just sixteen Duelists now remaining in the WCQ let's find out who's
 left; where they're from'      versus      'in the Top 16'
```

and the post as a **Top 16 of two matches**, which took the event out of the archive.

Both sides parsed, so the all-or-nothing guard had nothing to object to — it asks whether every pairing *found* was read, not whether what was found is a pairing. That is the flaw, and it was mine.

A side is now a name or it is nothing: two to six words, each capitalised or a particle, no separators and no digits. That post reads as no round at all, which is the right answer until somebody teaches the reader its shape.

### Two letters the wrong way round

`2016-ycs-toronto` is a different fault the same change uncovered:

```
Top 4 write-up   Alexander Dalpe
Top 8 table      Alexandre Dalpe
```

One Duelist. `misspelt` allows one letter typed wrong, and a transposition is not that — so the Top 4 held somebody who had not played in the Top 8.

A transposition is the same slip of the hand, so it now folds the same way. **Checked against the archive, not against tests** — every name set in all 166 events, folded both ways and diffed:

```
1,137,263 seated names
divergences: 2

  'Rodney Lamont Willimas'         -> 'Rodney Lamont Williams'
  'Miguel Eduardo Snachez Montero' -> 'Miguel Eduardo Sanchez Montero'
```

Both are the typo they look like. No other name in the archive moves.

### A doubled word should not cost the post

YCS Toronto writes `Michael Kyle Walters and and his Burning Abyss Phantom Knight Deck`. The doubled word leaves a conjunction on the end of the name, which the new name test then refuses — losing the round rather than the typo. Trimmed.

### Effect on the prose reader

```
before this   29 of 36 posts read, two of them wrongly
after         27 of 36, none of them wrongly
```

`sa-wcq-top-16-pairings` and `top-16-pairings-3` now read as nothing rather than as garbage. Both are dash-or-"with" delimited chains with no brackets; reading them needs a shape the reader does not have yet, and I would rather it said so.

### Tests

Three added, all mutation-checked. The fold test failed first time because my fixture had each spelling in one round — the surviving spelling has to be the one seen in more, which is the rule working. 521 tests pass.

`BUILD_VERSION` → 18.

## Summary

Closes the transcript-envelope **drift surface** (#534) by making `@nanobpm/agentic` the single source of truth for the *ACP `session/update` → on-wire transcript chunk* path, and publishes a **conformance vector** that pins the exact envelope bytes both a producer and a consumer test against.

The package already shipped **both halves** but nothing composed them, so the producer emitted a marker-as-value (`{type,v,…}`) shape the consumer's marker-as-key decoder never matched — every envelope fell back to a raw `stream-chunk` and the Cockpit Worker Terminal rendered "raw replay only".

## What changed

1. **Canonical bridge** — `acpUpdateToTranscriptChunk(update) → string | null` (`session/acp/transcript-bridge.ts`), the one pure composition of `classifyUpdate` + `encodeTranscriptEvent`. Exported from `@nanobpm/agentic/session/acp`. Resolves the two documented shape gaps explicitly:
   - tool-result `result` → transcript `content` (string / omitted), and
   - the ACP `reasoning` role folds to the `assistant` `TranscriptRole` that `deriveView` already renders.
   Returns `null` for an `ignored` update. No new envelope grammar.
2. **Published conformance vector** — `ACP_TRANSCRIPT_VECTORS` from `@nanobpm/agentic/protocol/conformance`: golden triples `(ACP update) → (exact chunk bytes) → (typed event)` covering `agent_message_chunk`, `agent_thought_chunk`, `user_message_chunk`, `tool_call`, a terminal `tool_call_update`, and an `ignored` `plan`. Both the producer (c8ctl-nano) and the consumer (transcript parser / cockpit) hold to the **same bytes**. The marker prefix is *derived* from its one canonical definition, so the transcript drift-guard stays satisfied.
3. **Drift guard + Red/Green** — a real harness-shaped `{type,v,…}` envelope proves raw-only today, then the bridge makes each ACP update round-trip through `parseTranscriptEvent`/`deriveView` to a non-raw message / tool card.

## Verification

`npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run lint`, and the full `npm test` (616 pass) are green; no `as T` assertions. Release is derived from this Conventional PR title (`feat(agentic): …`).

## Follow-up (already tracked, not in scope here)

- nano-workforce keeps a local copy of the transcript grammar — dedupe to the published package once this lands (noted in #534).
- Producer adoption: **jwulf/c8ctl-plugin-nano#127** must emit canonical envelopes via this bridge (gated on this issue's release).

Closes #534

author: jjwren
body:
Implements the "capped event" story end to end — custom RSVP options, attendee limits with a waitlist, and a close-early cutoff — across API, bot, and web.

Closes #120

## Custom RSVP options
- `RsvpOptionSpec` in Contracts; `CreateEventRequest.RsvpOptions` / `UpdateEventRequest.RsvpOptions` carry structured specs. Defaults (✅/❌/🤔) apply when unspecified — including poll conversion and pre-existing events.
- **Attending flag**: `RsvpOption.IsAttending` (exactly one per event; default the first). Every consumer of "Going" semantics resolves through it — attendee roles, thread member adds, availability (bot + web), live-list and event-card counts, embed role note — via `RsvpPolicy.AttendingOption` server-side and `EventDto.AttendingOption` client-side, both with a min-SortOrder fallback. The migration backfills the flag onto each existing event's first option, preserving exact prior behavior.
- Bot syntax: `/create rsvp-options:"⚔️ Raider x10, 🛡️ Standby, ❌ Out"` — comma-separated `[emoji] label [xN]`, trailing `*` picks the attending option (default first). Parsed by `RsvpOptionSyntax` (pure, unit-tested); the API stays the validator of record (1–10 options, unique labels, one attending, lengths).
- Web: a row editor on the event form (emoji / label / capacity / attending radio).
- **Edits with existing RSVPs**: options match by label (case-insensitive) so RSVPs follow; an option with RSVPs can't be removed (409); new labels append; moving the attending flag re-syncs roles exactly like a role change (revoke-all old, grant-all new) and seats the old option's now-meaningless waitlist.

## Attendee limit + waitlist
- The existing `RsvpOption.Capacity` is surfaced at create/edit: bot `attendee-limit:` (shorthand for the attending option, works with default buttons) or per-option `xN`; web per-row capacity. The two conflict explicitly (400) rather than silently overriding.
- RSVPs past the attending option's cap **queue in RSVP order** (`Rsvp.Waitlisted`; `CreatedAt` doubles as queue position and no longer moves on same-option re-clicks). Other full options still 409 — there's nothing to wait for on a decline.
- Waitlisted users hold no seat: no role grant, no thread add, excluded from availability and every count. They're told their queue position (ephemeral reply / web note).
- **Promotion**: when a seat frees (drop, switch-away, raised or cleared cap), `RsvpPolicy.PromoteAsync` seats the earliest waitlisted user in the same transaction; the role grant, thread add, and a channel ping (new `WaitlistPromotion` delivery type 15) ride the outbox, so notifications are crash-safe and the role arrives on promotion, not while waitlisted. End-of-event revoke fan-outs skip waitlisted rows.

## Close RSVPs early
- `rsvp-close:` accepts **relative** text ("2h before", stored as `RsvpCloseMinutesBefore` so it tracks start-time edits and is inherited by series occurrences as a template field) or **absolute** natural language ("friday 5pm", occurrence-only). `EventDto.RsvpClosesAtUtc` carries the resolved instant.
- After the cutoff, PUT and DELETE RSVPs both 409 with a clear message (the frozen list is the point); the bot surfaces it as the ephemeral error, the web disables the buttons and says so.
- The scheduler sweep re-renders the embed **once** when a cutoff passes (`RsvpCloseSynced` one-shot, reset by time/cutoff edits): buttons disabled, "🔒 RSVPs are closed".

## Compatibility
- EF migration `RsvpV1` adds the columns and backfills `IsAttending`; existing events keep the default three options and identical semantics.
- Series occurrences clone the latest occurrence's option set forward (fresh ids, no RSVPs) — custom options and caps persist across recurrences without new schema.
- Poll conversion, ICS/native-event mirroring untouched; every event mutation site keeps its `SyncLiveList` trigger (Live List #127).
- README command table/features and the web Docs page updated.

Out of scope (#125): role-restricted signup, multi-RSVP, per-option roles.

## Tests
Full suite green: **395 passed** (290 API incl. 24 new RSVP-v1 integration/unit tests, 46 bot, 59 web) — capacity/waitlist/promotion FIFO, cutoff parsing and 409s, option-edit rules, attending-flag moves, series roll-forward, embed closed/waitlist rendering, button-row chunking, web form/button behavior.

author: zhouhufeng
body:
#Third and last of the MPRA tools from Max Schubach / BIH (kircherlab, MIT). Adds `igvfagent mpralib`: the three barcode outlier detectors from Rosen et al. (2025), replicate agreement, and per-barcode activity.

  global            barcode extreme for the whole replicate (|z|>3)
  oligo             barcode extreme for its own oligo (|z|>3 within)
  large_expression  activity >5 log2-units ABOVE the oligo median

Ported stdlib-only. Upstream materialises a barcodes x replicates AnnData matrix; the 240K libraries have 20M barcodes, where that costs several GB, so this streams instead. pandas' ddof=1 std and NaN-skipping are reproduced explicitly (population SD would shift every z-score), as is upstream's transform("std").fillna(0).replace(0, 1) for single-barcode and zero-variance oligos.

Benchmark extended to three published claims, all reproduced:

  8K-neurons    1,444,480 barcodes / Lincoln 1,523,572   EXACT
  80K-neurons   5,459,247 barcodes / Lincoln 6,243,618   EXACT
  12K-cardiop   outlier replicate consistency 7.8%       EXACT

The consistency metric's denominator is easy to get wrong and worth recording: the paper's "percentage of barcodes consistently identified as outliers across all three replicates" is flagged-in-all divided by the MEAN PER-REPLICATE count, not by the union. Over the union the same data reads 3.0% where the paper reports 7.8% -- a plausible-looking number that is simply the wrong statistic.

Outlier rates also fall inside the paper's published lentiviral ranges for both datasets in its outlier panel (12K-cardiop global 1.06%, 80K-neurons global 1.46%, 12K-cardiop oligo-specific 1.75%).

Not exact: 80K-neurons consistency is 49.0% against a published 49.6%. Both published NGN2 file versions give 49.0%, and applying the paper's stated pre-filters (zero RNA CPM, DNA CPM below the 5th percentile, oligos with >=20 barcodes) moves it further away to 48.6% -- so the residual is not the filtering step as written. Documented in the benchmark README rather than tuned away.

Note the paper concluded that outlier removal changes variant effects very little (r>0.95), so these are reported as diagnostics; the skill does not filter by default and the playbook says why.

author: copilot
body:
The assets bucket in `infra/main.tf` was world-readable over plaintext HTTP: `acl = "public-read"`, no public access block, a policy granting `s3:GetObject` to `*` with no `aws:SecureTransport` condition, no encryption at rest, versioning disabled, and no access logging.

## Assets bucket

- Removed the `public-read` ACL; added `aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block` with all four settings `true` and `BucketOwnerEnforced` ownership so ACLs cannot be used at all.
- Replaced the `PublicReadGetObject` allow with a single TLS deny. Public objects are expected to be served through a CDN origin access identity, not by opening the bucket.
- Added `aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration` (AES256, bucket key on) and flipped versioning to `Enabled`.
- Added `aws_s3_bucket_logging` writing to a separate bucket under `assets/`.
- `assets_bucket_domain` now emits the regional domain, since the bucket is no longer a public website origin.

```hcl
{
  Sid       = "DenyInsecureTransport"
  Effect    = "Deny"
  Principal = "*"
  Action    = "s3:*"
  Resource  = [aws_s3_bucket.assets.arn, "${aws_s3_bucket.assets.arn}/*"]
  Condition = { Bool = { "aws:SecureTransport" = "false" } }
}
```

## Log bucket

- New private bucket with the same public access block, SSE, versioning and TLS deny.
- Because ACLs are disabled, log delivery is granted to `logging.s3.amazonaws.com` in the bucket policy, scoped by `aws:SourceArn` and `aws:SourceAccount`.
- Both policies `depends_on` their public access block so a `*`-principal policy is not evaluated as a public grant during apply.

## Regression test

`tests/unit/infra.test.ts` reads `main.tf` and asserts each control: no public ACL, all four block settings on both buckets, no allow-to-`*`, the `aws:SecureTransport` deny, versioning `Enabled`, an SSE resource, and logging pointed at the log bucket. All eight assertions fail against the previous file.

`infra/README.md` now documents the controls in place of the defect table.

## Scope

The diff is confined to `infra/` and `tests/`. `infra/` is code-owned, so this needs a human approval before it can merge — which is the behaviour the demo is meant to show.
